title: The Seventh Bell · revision 7
summary:
Revision 7 of The Seventh Bell, for Waypoint 1.35. It installs over the original campaign or over revision 6, and keeps any world state you have recorded.

- **Tongues are now Hearts.** The bells' clappers are called Hearts (Ossa's Heart, the Heart-Hound), which is easier to say at the table. One review item renames the word in your own wiki pages, session notes and saved cards too; your chronicle keeps its words.
- **Built for your table: four characters starting at level 3.** Every encounter is rebudgeted with the 2024 XP rules for four players at the level each chapter expects, from Low skirmishes in Pellmoor to High fights at the Strike, the summit and the Seventh Bell.
- **A real finale.** Acts IV and V now have full sets of prepared plays, and every ending can be reached and recorded: the Hush Shrine, Oum's waking, and the table's own choice to stop resisting. A new stat block for Maudrin as Keeper of the Seventh (CR 12, legendary actions).
- **Nothing gets stranded.** Every place a Heart, the Key or a person can end up has a play that moves it on, and "Down the line" notes point at the sessions that deliver them, so Waypoint can bring them back in your prep brief.
- **Fixes from a full audit:** timeline slips (the Stilled have been frozen since 2 SS), state that the fiction hadn't earned, 2024 rulings for the spells a level-3 to 11 party actually has, and stat block arithmetic.
- **Corvane in the Realms,** as in revision 6: the Stormwall and the Seam, Pellmoor Landing as a port, memory as money.
- **Foresight playbook.** 429 prepared plays across 32 chapters and 75 anytime plays; 66 tracked world-state facts; 32 session prep briefs; 51 encounters; 23 Corvane stat blocks built on the 2024 Monster Manual; and an ending forecast.

Your notes, IsoForge map kits, chronicle and any world state you have recorded are kept. Replaced wiki text moves to each page's revision history.

edits.find: Corvane is a world that was once rung like a great cathedral.
edits.replace: Corvane is a land far out in the Trackless Sea of the Forgotten Realms, a world of its own that was once rung like a great cathedral.

edits.find: They trade memories for coin. They have forgotten what the bells sounded like.
edits.replace:
They trade memories as money, and lately for gold. They have forgotten what the bells sounded like.

For four centuries a wall of storm at sea hid Corvane from the rest of the world. Thirty years ago a passage opened, and ships from Faerûn's Sword Coast began to arrive. They anchor at Pellmoor, on the still waters of the Mute Mere, now the busiest port in Corvane.

edits.find: > "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long grey ribbons, and the village of Pellmoor comes into sight: reed roofs, leaning docks, nets like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell is silent. A girl stands on the ferry-dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the heart, or for the bell?'*"
edits.replace: > "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long gray ribbons, and Pellmoor Landing comes into sight: forty masts standing over water so still the ships look painted on it, and beneath them, just under the surface, the rooftops of a drowned town. On the Quays, a dozen languages argue over the price of a memory. Past the last warehouse, the old reed-roofed ferry village still leans toward the water as if none of this were happening. A girl stands on the oldest dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the heart, or for the bell?'*"

locked.replace: Source canon: the v6 pages (CORVANE IN THE REALMS, MEMORY AS MONEY, PELLMOOR LANDING) and then Part 3.3 win conflicts within the manuscript. Corvane is part of the Forgotten Realms; the Seam opened in 382 SS (1462 DR); Pellmoor is a busy port; memory is money alongside gold; rules are D&D 2024.

plays.title: They speak gently to Ila
plays.why: Ila is fourteen, alone on the old dock, and asks the first question; most tables answer kindly.
plays.readAloud: "It's warm. Not like a hot pan. Like something alive that's been asleep. When it hums, the water on the far shore ripples in the shape of a bell. I've seen it. Nobody believes me except Mother Sallow, and she only believes me because she's scared."
plays.response: Ila unwraps the oilskin for whoever asked respectfully. The Heart hums while she holds it and fades when she sets it down. She answers one plain question per kindness, then asks: "Did you hear it too?" Mother Sallow is watching from the net-racks and walks over once Ila smiles.
plays.consequence: Ila trusts this person. She will show them the Heart again and tell them when the Hushmen come.
plays.fallback: If the table freezes, Ila counts the masts on the Quays out loud and asks which ship they came on.
plays.tells: A player crouches to her level, offers food or a coat, or answers her question honestly.
plays.rules: No check: Ila is willing (2024 Influence). A Bell-Touched character recognises the hum at once.
plays.later: S2: Ila sings the response beside whoever was kind to her. S3: Ila insists on a say in what happens to the Heart, and her trust decides whether she will travel (s03-take-ila-along). S28: she remembers who was kind first.
plays.keywords: ila, girl, dock, kind, gentle, talk, heart, hum, show, child

plays.title: They brush Ila off or demand the Heart
plays.why: Some characters arrive on business and treat the strange child as a nuisance.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow's voice cuts across the dock like a dropped oar. "She's a child. You can be a child too, or you can be useful."
plays.response: Ila turns away and pockets the bundle. Mother Sallow plants herself between them and gives the party one chance: find the eastern-marsh ferry that has been missing a week, and she'll believe they mean well. She never raises her voice twice.
plays.consequence: Ila will not show the Heart today. The missing ferry (H-02) becomes the party's way back in.
plays.fallback: If nobody takes the ferry job, a ferry-folk widow begs them at the Shuttered Bell instead.
plays.tells: Players talk over her, laugh at the question, or ask what she's hiding.
plays.rules: Mother Sallow starts Indifferent (2024 Influence). Charm moves her nowhere; blunt honesty makes her Friendly.
plays.later: S2: Sallow's help costs more: she asks them to speak a dead person's name on the Memory Shore before she teaches the hymn (s02-sing-response). S3: Ila argues against handing them the Heart.
plays.keywords: rude, ignore, demand, push, threaten, mother sallow, sallow, ferry job

plays.title: They try to take or steal the Heart from Ila
plays.why: A rogue sees a humming relic and a child holding it.
plays.readAloud: Ila's hand closes on empty oilskin. She doesn't scream at first. She just looks at you, and then the whole Old Shore goes quiet, the way water goes quiet before something surfaces.
plays.response: Check the session-zero Off-limits list first; nothing is done to Ila, who is fourteen. A lifted bundle is noticed because a ferry-folk witness is always watching the dock: Brannagh Wick sends a runner to the Pilots' Hall and Mother Sallow demands it back. If the party keeps it, the Old Shore goes cold: no skiff, no pilot, no hymn from anyone, until amends are made. That is a social closing, not a wall: the Quays still hire boats, and s02-make-amends is the way back.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Heart and has lost the ferry-folk. Quill hears of it by evening.
plays.fallback: If they return it within the day with an honest apology, Mother Sallow lets it be known they did, and nothing is lost.
plays.tells: A player asks where Ila sleeps, how she carries it, or rolls Sleight of Hand.
plays.rules: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) DC 17 against Ila's Passive Perception 15 (+5 near water); a Rogue's Fast Hands or Cunning Action can try it as a bonus action, and a ferry-folk witness spots it unless the roll beats 20. Invisibility or Pass without Trace give Advantage but the Heart still hums when it leaves her hand.
plays.later: S2: until they make amends, the Cantor treats them as the forgetful and the Night Song is dangerous (s02-make-amends reopens the Shore). S3: Mother Sallow still names Eld, but coldly, and says so. S4: the Gate Clerk raises Persuasion DCs by 2 (quill is Suspicious).
plays.keywords: steal, take, grab, snatch, pickpocket, sleight of hand, rob, ila

plays.title: They accept Mother Sallow's three-day bargain
plays.why: Sallow offers what the party wants (answers) for something easy to promise (keep the Heart safe).
plays.readAloud: "Keep it safe for three days. Not from thieves. From the Court. Do that, and I'll tell you what the water knows. And learn this, before the dark comes: when they sing, you sing back."
plays.response: Over bitter reed tea she explains that the Mere holds the dead and the Heart belongs to Ossa, the Bone Bell. She cannot say why she has no memory of her husband's face. She teaches the response to the Night Song: a two-line call and answer. Ask each player, "What do you want from Mother Sallow?" She answers honestly but not fully; she knows the Drowned are her ancestors.
plays.consequence: The party has a promise to keep and the response hymn. Record the bargain.
plays.fallback: If they dither, she hands Ila the tea and says, "Then I'll keep it, and you can watch me fail."
plays.tells: Players ask what she knows about the Drowned, the bell, or Ila's father.
plays.rules: Learning the hymn takes a few minutes and no check. Singing it later quiets the Drowned for one hour (v5 2.11).
plays.later: S2: the hymn calms the Night Song for an hour. S3: if they kept the Heart from the Court for three days, Mother Sallow opens the ledger without being asked (s03-search-eld).
plays.keywords: mother sallow, bargain, deal, three days, tea, hymn, response, night song, keep it safe

plays.title: They hand the Heart to Quill
plays.why: Quill is polite, official, and offers an easy way out of trouble.
plays.readAloud: Quill takes the bundle in both gloved hands, and the hum stops dead, as if someone had put a palm on a bell. "Thank you. The Court remembers its friends." He writes in his ledger without looking down.
plays.response: Quill gives a grey-wax receipt and a Tithe-exemption chit for one mote, records every face, and leaves for the Landing House that night. Ila does not cry. She walks to the end of the old dock and sits there until dark.
plays.consequence: The Court holds Ossa's Heart and knows the party's faces.
plays.fallback: If a player regrets it at once, Quill is still on the Quays for an hour, haggling with a Coster clerk.
plays.tells: Players ask whether giving it up would protect Ila, or what the Court pays.
plays.later: S3: returning it to the Mere now means recovering it first. S4: Maudrin already holds it; ask for it back with s04-ask-ossa-back or take Ila's exemption instead. Concord: Ossa needs the Heart back (the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer once the party holds it again).
plays.keywords: quill, give, hand over, surrender, court, heart, receipt, comply

plays.title: They lie to Quill
plays.why: Most parties protect the child and bluff the official.
plays.readAloud: Quill nods along, then asks one quiet question and waits. "Where did the child's coat go?"
plays.response: Quill is not a fool. He asks exactly one specific question and lets the silence work. If the party can't answer, he says, "Then I'll look myself," and searches the Old Shore that night with his guard. He finds the Heart unless it has been moved; a hiding place on the Quays or aboard a foreign ship is outside his warrant.
plays.consequence: Quill is suspicious. A search happens tonight unless the lie holds.
plays.fallback: If the scene stalls, Quill's guard spots Ila's oversized ferry coat on a peg.
plays.tells: A player says they know nothing about any humming, or offers a cover story.
plays.rules: Charisma (Deception) DC 16, or contested against Quill's Insight +5 if the player prefers a roll-off. Quill asks the coat question with Advantage if anyone has lied to him before. Hold Person on Quill is a Wisdom save and works, but his next report names the caster (every spell hums); Suggestion works the same way (see any-l3-hold-suggest-charm). On a success he leaves suspicious but without cause to search.
plays.later: If he finds it: as handing it over, and S4's Gate Clerk raises Persuasion DCs by 2 (s04-refuse-courtesy-memory reads quill). If the lie holds: S3 Quill returns with a second Hushman (s03-quill-returns).
plays.keywords: lie, bluff, deceive, cover story, deny, quill, hide, coat

plays.title: They attack Quill
plays.why: A Hushman threatening a child is an easy villain for a level-3 party that can now do something about it.
plays.readAloud: Quill steps back so neatly it looks rehearsed. His gloves come up grey and silent. "You've made yourselves a Tithe-case. I do hope you understand what that means."
plays.response: Run Quill's patrol. Quill wants an arrest, not a killing; his guard fights while Quill retreats toward the Landing House shouting for witnesses. Foreign captains on the Quays will not interfere with the Court. Ila's house becomes the first place the Hushmen search.
plays.consequence: The party is a Tithe-case. The Landing House's six Hushmen now watch the Old Shore.
plays.fallback: If a PC drops, Quill has them bound, not killed, and offers them back for the Heart.
plays.tells: Hands on weapons; a player asks how many Hushmen are in Pellmoor.
plays.rules: Encounter: Quill's patrol. Silence-glove strikes make no sound and can't be sensed by Tonework. Hold Person on Quill or the Sergeant ends the fight quickly: let it, and note the caster is named in the report.
plays.later: Tonight: the Hushmen raid Ila's house (run it). S3: Quill's report reaches Hallowmere, but the Chancellor's invitation still comes; the Court prefers to buy before it threatens. S4: the Gate Clerk already has their names (s04-refuse-courtesy-memory, +2 DC).
plays.keywords: attack, fight, kill, hit, quill, hushman, guard, violence, combat

plays.title: They bribe Quill
plays.why: Quill is short on quota and visibly open to an arrangement.
plays.readAloud: Quill looks at the gold the way a man looks at a fine meal he isn't allowed to eat. "Gold I can't put on a shelf, friend. But I'll take it. And one more thing. A name."
plays.response: Quill pockets gold for himself, but his quota needs memories. He asks for one favor: a name of someone 'not keeping the Court's quiet.' If they give Mother Sallow's, he writes it down. If they refuse, he keeps the coin and says, "Then I'll remember you were generous."
plays.consequence: Quill is bribed. He leaves the Heart alone for now.
plays.fallback: If they won't name anyone, Quill suggests the quota itself: 'Three memories, freely given. I'm not particular whose.'
plays.tells: A player jingles coin, asks what his quota is, or offers a 'gift'.
plays.rules: No check for the bribe. A Charisma (Persuasion) Influence check, DC 15, talks him out of the name if they offer something else useful.
plays.later: If they named Mother Sallow: Hushmen are at her door in S3 (s03-quill-returns) and her ledger is at risk. If they refused: in S4 Quill's letter vouches for them (Gate Clerk DCs drop by 2 at s04-refuse-courtesy-memory).
plays.keywords: bribe, pay, gold, coin, buy off, deal, quill, money

plays.title: They fill the village's memory quota themselves
plays.why: H-03 makes the quota a problem. Memory is the honest answer; gilding (s01-gild-the-quota) is the illegal one.
plays.readAloud: "Three memories," Quill says, already uncapping a keep-glass. "The Court is not particular whose. That's rather the point of the Court."
plays.response: The honest way to meet a Corvanese quota is memories, and nothing stops the party giving some of their own on the villagers' behalf. Quill draws each one with a tuning fork in about a minute. The three villagers he was hounding are Bellwright sympathisers, and they will not forget this.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor's quota is met. Quill leaves satisfied. Three households owe the party.
plays.fallback: If the party offers gold instead, Reckoner Sela Maunt quietly explains why that is gilding, what it risks, and how it is done (s01-gild-the-quota).
plays.tells: Players ask why villagers won't pay, or offer to cover the shortfall.
plays.rules: Each giver names the memory and its weight (mote, keep or heartkeep) in the Memory Ledger. The DM may award Heroic Inspiration for a memory given freely to someone who needs it.
plays.later: S3: those households warn the party when Hushmen move and can hide Ila (s03-households-warn). S4 (siege): they shelter villagers. S6: Wren's Bellwrights already know who paid, so Wren's confession needs no Insight.
plays.keywords: quota, tithe, pay the quota, give memories, gilding, villagers, h-03, sacrifice, keep, mote

plays.title: They take the Heart to the Quays to learn what it's worth
plays.why: A port full of Reckoners and foreign buyers invites appraisal.
plays.readAloud: Sela Maunt doesn't touch it. She taps one tuning fork on the counter and the fork goes silent mid-note. "That's not a memory, love. That's a bell. Put it away before someone who isn't me sees it."
plays.response: Sela refuses to appraise it and warns them to hide it. Too late: Master Orsolo Venn, two stalls over, heard the fork die. He introduces himself warmly, offers 600 gp and a berth home on the Coster ship Gilded Heron, and gives them three days to think.
plays.consequence: Venn knows the Heart exists and wants it. He pays Quill, so Quill will hear by evening.
plays.fallback: If they avoid Venn, he sends a polite note to the Shuttered Bell with his offer in writing.
plays.tells: Players ask who in Pellmoor would know about relics, or head for the Reckoning House.
plays.later: S1: Quill arrives on the first evening instead of the second. S3: Venn's offer becomes a real option (sell it abroad); his polite note arrives at the Shuttered Bell.
plays.keywords: appraise, sell, worth, value, reckoner, reckoning house, sela, venn, merchant, quays, buyer

plays.title: A Stormborn character asks to travel inland
plays.why: Faerûnian characters arrive under the Landing Charter and will soon want to leave Pellmoor.
plays.readAloud: The Landing House clerk stamps your papers without reading them. "Landing due, five gold. Pellmoor and the Mere road only. Anywhere else needs a writ from Hallowmere. They take about a season. Next."
plays.response: Explain the Landing Charter plainly: foreigners trade freely here but need a Court writ of passage to go inland. Quill can 'expedite' one for a heartkeep and means it (s01-expedite-writ). A forger on Strangers' Row sells a counterfeit (s01-forged-writ). Brannagh Wick knows ferry routes that skirt the Mere road checkpoints. Don't block the plot: the Chancellor's letter at the end of Session 3 counts as a writ.
plays.consequence: The party understands the Court controls movement, and that a writ is worth something.
plays.fallback: If a player feels trapped, Dorra Pell mentions that 'writs have a way of arriving for interesting people.'
plays.tells: A player from the Sword Coast asks about Hallowmere, roads, or the rest of Corvane.
plays.later: S3: the Chancellor's invitation sets the writ to 'invited'. S4: the Hallowmere gate reads the writ (s04-stormborn-at-gate). A forged writ works until someone checks the grey wax (DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation) for a Hushman).
plays.keywords: writ, passage, papers, landing house, travel, inland, hallowmere, faerunian, stormborn, charter, customs

plays.title: They cast Detect Magic or Identify on the Heart
plays.why: Casters reach for Detect Magic or Identify the moment something hums.
plays.readAloud: The spell doesn't find an aura so much as an answer. The Heart hums back at you, one clean note, the way a glass rings when you speak near it.
plays.response: Detect Magic shows a faint aura that belongs to no school. Identify (or a minute's Study) reveals: 'Ossa's Heart. It belongs to a bell under water.' Nothing about Tolls, and nothing about the Key. A Bell-Touched character recognises it without magic.
plays.consequence: The party knows what it is and where it belongs.
plays.fallback: If no one has the spell, Mother Sallow simply tells them.
plays.tells: A wizard, cleric or bard asks to cast a ritual on it.
plays.rules: Detect Magic (ritual) or Identify. Study action, Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) DC 14, for the same answer without a spell. Locate Object on the Heart gives a direction by its hum (see any-l3-locate-and-scry).
plays.later: S2: they may think to bring it on the dive. S3: returning it to the Mere becomes an informed choice.
plays.keywords: detect magic, identify, arcana, study, what is it, magic, aura, spell, ritual

plays.title: They defend Ila's house during the night raid
plays.why: v5 ends Session 1 with a Hushmen raid on the Harrow house if Quill suspects anything.
plays.readAloud: No knock. Just the door, opening very quietly, and two grey gloves catching the lamplight.
plays.response: Four Hushmen under a Sergeant (the night raid). They want the Heart and the child's father's papers, and they withdraw when one drops or the alarm rouses the Old Shore. Ila can be hidden: under the net-racks, or with Brannagh at the Pilots' Hall. Ila is a child: check session-zero Off-limits; she is never harmed on-screen, and if she is taken it is Off-screen and handled by s01-raid-takes-ila.
plays.consequence: The Court's first move has failed or succeeded in front of the whole Old Shore.
plays.fallback: If the party is elsewhere, Ila hides on her own and finds them before dawn, shaking and furious.
plays.tells: The party keeps watch at the Harrow house, or asks where Ila sleeps tonight.
plays.rules: Encounter: the night raid. Hiding Ila: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 14 with the Hide action's rules; the ferry-folk help (Help action) without being asked. A Rogue can Hide as a bonus action (Cunning Action).
plays.later: If the raid fails: S3 Quill brings reinforcements and the ferry-folk start to trust the party. If Ila is hidden at the Pilots' Hall, set ila to Hidden by playing s03-hide-ila.
plays.keywords: raid, night, defend, protect, hushmen, harrow house, ila, guard, ambush

plays.title: The raid takes Ila
plays.why: The party is elsewhere or loses the doorway, and the Hushmen leave with the child.
plays.readAloud: By dawn the door of the Harrow house hangs open and the oilskin is gone from its peg. Dorra Pell says only, 'Grey wax on the step. They took her for questioning.'
plays.response: Check session-zero Off-limits before this scene: Ila is taken Off-screen, held in a lamp-lit room at the Landing House with Dorra Pell's soup, and never harmed or described in danger. The Court cart leaves for Hallowmere at the next dawn. The party has one day to act: the Mere road cart (s02-intercept-ila-cart), a bribe through Quill, or Brannagh's pilots.
plays.consequence: Ila is under Court arrest. The Old Shore is angry at the Hushmen.
plays.fallback: If the party stalls, Brannagh Wick sends a runner with the cart's route and hour.
plays.tells: Nobody guards the Harrow house, or the raid scene ends with the Hushmen holding the door.
plays.rules: No check. Give the party the cart's route and hour (telegraphed): the Mere road, second checkpoint, an hour past dawn.
plays.later: S2: a rescue on the Mere road (s02-intercept-ila-cart). S4: if she reaches Hallowmere, she is held in the Hall of Tithes and Maudrin offers her release as a bargain (s04-exemption-releases-ila). S6: rescue her alongside Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa-with-ila).
plays.keywords: ila taken, arrested, raid, child taken, kidnapped, hushmen take ila

plays.title: They gild the village's quota with gold
plays.why: Gold is the party's strongest resource, and the canon's way out of the quota is gilding: illegal and common.
plays.readAloud: Sela Maunt does not look up. 'I can stamp a grey-wax mote for a silver piece and not ask whose it was. Quill can look at the stamp and not ask either. That is gilding. If anyone writes it down, it is a crime.'
plays.response: Sela will stamp stand-in motes for the three households (about 40 gp in all, which includes her 10 percent). Quill must look away: automatic if he is bribed, otherwise Influence DC 15. He accepts it once. A Sergeant who sees it writes it down.
plays.consequence: The quota is met without memories, and Quill is in the party's pocket. The Court clock rises by one.
plays.fallback: If Quill refuses, Sela offers to take the gold as a deposit and stamp the motes in a week, when the Landing House changes shift.
plays.tells: A player offers Quill coin for the three villagers, or asks Sela Maunt how locals really pay.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion or Deception) DC 15 on Quill (Indifferent, Intelligence 11, so DC 15). Failure: Quill writes the party down and the households pay double next quarter. Gilding twice raises the Court clock.
plays.later: S3: the three households owe the party and warn them (s03-households-warn). S4: Quill's letter vouches for them at the gate (DCs drop by 2). Repeat gilding is in any-gild-a-tithe.
plays.keywords: gild, gilding, gold for tithe, pay quota gold, sela stamp, bribe quill gold

plays.title: They buy a true writ from Quill
plays.why: A Faerûnian wants to leave Pellmoor before the Chancellor's letter arrives.
plays.readAloud: Quill folds the grey paper in thirds. 'Expedited. It will say your name, your ship, and the date I wrote it. The Court remembers all three.'
plays.response: One heartkeep, or 50 gp, buys a true writ in two days. It names the bearer, so the Court has the name. Quill is polite and will not bring it up again unless the party asks about the Heart.
plays.consequence: The bearer holds a true writ and the Court holds the bearer's name.
plays.fallback: If the price is too steep, the Chancellor's letter arrives anyway at the end of S3.
plays.tells: A Stormborn player asks how fast a writ can be had.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 to lower the price to a keep. No check for the writ itself. The writ gets past the Hallowmere gate without the grey-wax check.
plays.later: S4: the gate reads the true writ (s04-stormborn-at-gate) and the Gate Clerk is polite.
plays.keywords: writ, passage, quill expedite, papers, travel permit

plays.title: They buy a forged writ on Strangers' Row
plays.why: The Row has a back room for every kind of paper.
plays.readAloud: The forger's room smells of hot wax. 'Grey is hard,' she says. 'The seal is easy. The ash in the wax is the part Hushmen know.'
plays.response: A forged writ costs 40 gp and a day. It carries no real name. It passes a Blank clerk but not a Sergeant who checks the grey wax. The forger asks for a small favour later, never named.
plays.consequence: A character carries a forged writ.
plays.fallback: If the party has no gold, the forger will take a keep.
plays.tells: A player asks the Brass Lantern's bartender who 'sorts out paper', or wants no name on record.
plays.rules: Intelligence (Investigation) DC 17 for a Hushman to spot it. Thieves' Tools or a Forgery Kit proficiency lets a PC improve it to DC 18.
plays.later: S4: a failed forgery is arrest for landing past the Charter (s04-stormborn-at-gate). S9: a forged writ is stopped at the north gate unless they leave under Rook's escort or a smuggling route.
plays.keywords: forged writ, forge, counterfeit, papers, zhentarim, forger, fake writ

plays.title: They visit the Dawn Mission on Strangers' Row
plays.why: The Row is a short walk away, and a healer's house is where hurt or devout characters go.
plays.readAloud: The Mission is a narrow house with a gilt sunburst over a door that has been painted yellow four times. A woman in a dawn-coloured mantle looks up from a washing-bowl. 'When the sun comes back,' she says, 'I would like to be standing somewhere it can see me.'
plays.response: Sister Aurelie Dawnmantle (Priest) tends anyone who comes in and asks for nothing. She wants a writ for Hallowmere; the Court has refused her four times. Tell her about Vaer's bell and her eyes light; she asks, carefully, whether it can be rung. She is bright and a little reckless. She gives the party a letter of introduction ('the Mission's first friend in Hallowmere').
plays.consequence: Aurelie is met. She is the seed of the Stormborn ally.
plays.fallback: If nobody goes, a Mission acolyte brings the same letter to the Shuttered Bell.
plays.tells: A cleric or paladin asks where the Faerûnian temples are, or a PC is hurt.
plays.rules: No check. A Lathander cleric or paladin is Friendly at once. Healing Word and Lesser Restoration are available to the party at the Mission (ends Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed or Poisoned only).
plays.later: S4: bringing her into Hallowmere is the party's call (s04-bring-aurelie). S9: if Vaer rings, she goes to the terraces to sing (s09-aurelie-on-the-terraces). S22: a free Aurelie is the core of the Stormborn ally.
plays.keywords: aurelie, dawn mission, lathander, strangers row, morninglord, healer, priest, temple

plays.title: A Harper at the Brass Lantern asks about the Tithe
plays.why: The Brass Lantern is where Faerûnians drink, and a lute-player is working the room.
plays.readAloud: A woman with a lute plays something that is not quite a drinking song. Between verses she asks, very lightly, 'And what do you make of the Tithe? Asking for a friend who has lost his mother's face.'
plays.response: She is a Harper and will not say so. If the party answers honestly and is kind about the Old Shore, she gives them a coin-sized silver brooch and a rendezvous: a cellar under the clockmaker's shop. The Harpers sympathise with the Bellwrights and distrust the Tithe. Zhentarim hands at the next table watch everything.
plays.consequence: A Harper contact knows the party's names kindly.
plays.fallback: If nobody bites, the Harper leaves the brooch on a bar-towel with a cellar address.
plays.tells: The party drinks on Strangers' Row, or a player asks what outsiders think of the Court.
plays.rules: Insight DC 14 to see the lute-player is working. Influence DC 15 to learn her aim without giving more than a rumour. A Bard recognises the Harper pin at once.
plays.later: S9: a detour to Pellmoor can reach the Harpers (s09-detour-pellmoor). S22: exposing the memory trade to the Harpers makes them the Stormborn ally.
plays.keywords: harper, brass lantern, lute, strangers row, stormborn, ally, tavern

plays.title: They ask Ila about her mother
plays.why: Ila talks about her father; a player notices there is no mother in the house.
plays.readAloud: 'Mum went north when I was little,' Ila says, still looking at the water. 'Kell's Crossing, Dad said, where the fields are ash. He said she sold the day I was born and then couldn't remember why she was crying.'
plays.response: Ila has never met her. She has only her father's story and a name, Nessa. She does not ask the party to find her. If anyone offers, she goes quiet and says 'Maybe.' Do not make the offer for her.
plays.consequence: The party knows Ila's mother is alive and in the ash fields.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, Dorra Pell mentions Nessa to the next stranger who sits at the bar.
plays.tells: A player asks who else lives in the Harrow house.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S9: Nessa Harrow lives at Kell's Crossing and comes out when Calla rings (s09-ring-calla). S28: Ila can meet her, if anyone tells her.
plays.keywords: ila mother, nessa, harrow, kells crossing, family

plays.title: They kill Quill
plays.why: A Hushman who threatens a child is an easy target, and the party can now hit hard enough to do it.
plays.readAloud: Quill's gloves open and his keep-glass rolls across the boards without a sound. Along the Quays, no one says anything, and the nearest foreign captain turns his back.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' A downed Quill can be bound instead (2024: a creature at 0 HP can be knocked out). If he dies, the Landing House's six Hushmen close the Old Shore within the hour, and a Sergeant from Hallowmere arrives in three days with a Tithe warrant for the killers. Pellmoor's Hushmen are afraid of the Old Shore, not the other way round. Say plainly that no one resurrects him.
plays.consequence: Quill is dead. The party are named murderers in the Court's records.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Quill begs for the Tithe-exemption chit in his pocket, which is a bribe, not a plea.
plays.tells: A player says 'finish him' over a downed Quill, or waits for him alone on the Quays.
plays.rules: Quill is a Hushman (Tough). Hold Person, then a coup de grace on a Paralyzed creature, is murder in front of witnesses: the ferry-folk saw. No check.
plays.later: S3: Hallowmere sends a Sergeant (s03-quill-returns no longer applies; the Court escalates). S4: the Gate Clerk has their names, and Maudrin starts the bargain colder. S28: Ila remembers whether anyone killed for her.
plays.keywords: kill quill, murder, execute, hushman dead, assassinate

edits.find: > "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long gray ribbons, and the village of Pellmoor comes into sight: reed roofs, leaning docks, nets like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell is silent. A girl stands on the ferry-dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the heart, or for the bell?'*"
edits.replace: > "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long gray ribbons, and Pellmoor Landing comes into sight: forty masts standing over water so still the ships look painted on it, and beneath them, just under the surface, the rooftops of a drowned town. On the Quays, a dozen languages argue over the price of a memory. Past the last warehouse, the old reed-roofed ferry village still leans toward the water as if none of this were happening. A girl stands on the oldest dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the heart, or for the bell?'*"

edits.find: **DO:** Let the party respond. Whatever they say, Ila answers with a plain question: "Did you hear it too?"
edits.replace: **DO:** First ask each player how their character arrived: off a ship through the Seam this morning, down the Mere road, or from a house in Pellmoor they've lived in for years. Then let the party respond to Ila. Whatever they say, Ila answers with a plain question: "Did you hear it too?"

edits.find: **Scene 3: Hushman Quill Arrives.** On the second evening, Hushman Tobias Quill arrives with one guard to collect the village's memory quota and inspect for "unlicensed bell-work."
edits.replace: **Scene 3: Hushman Quill Arrives.** On the second evening, Hushman Tobias Quill walks over from the Landing House with one guard to collect the Old Shore's memory quota and inspect for "unlicensed bell-work." Pellmoor pays its way in gold now, and gold cannot pay a Corvanese subject's Tithe, so his quota is short every season. If Master Venn has heard about the humming Heart, Quill comes on the first evening instead.

edits.find: Pellmoor is short on its quota this season. Several villagers have declined to give memories.
edits.replace: Pellmoor is short on its quota this season. Several villagers have offered me gold, which I can't put on a shelf.

edits.find: **Session 1 end:**
edits.replace:
**The port (v6).** Pellmoor is Corvane's only lawful landing for foreign ships. Use the Quays, the Reckoning House and Strangers' Row as background and as places the party can go: Reckoner Sela Maunt explains memory money; Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick knew Tam; Master Orsolo Venn will want the humming Heart the moment he hears of it. See the wiki pages PELLMOOR LANDING and MEMORY AS MONEY, and Foresight's prep brief for this session.

**Session 1 end:**

sessions.summary: A port of forty masts on a drowned town, a girl on the oldest dock, and a bronze heart that hums.

plays.title: They sing the response to the Night Song
plays.why: Mother Sallow taught it for exactly this, and the whole village does it.
plays.readAloud: Up and down the shore, people hum back at the water, the way you'd hum to a child who won't sleep. When you join them, the voice under the Mere hesitates, and for a while the names stop.
plays.response: The Night Song quiets for one hour. The Drowned do not attack the grieving or the singing. A character who sings with a dead person in mind feels the water listen; mark them, because the Cantor will ask about it.
plays.consequence: One safe hour on or near the water.
plays.fallback: If nobody learned it, Ila sings it, badly, and the Mere listens anyway.
plays.tells: Players ask what the villagers are humming, or if anyone remembers Sallow's hymn.
plays.rules: No check. A sincere attempt works; a Charisma (Performance) roll is flavour only and cannot fail. Silence the spell does not end it: the Drowned hear grief, not sound. If the party has not made amends for stealing the Heart (s02-make-amends), Mother Sallow will not teach it.
plays.later: S2: the Cantor greets a singer more gently. S3: safe passage to the belfry is easier for anyone who has sung the response.
plays.keywords: sing, hymn, response, night song, hum, choir, drowned, calm, quiet

plays.title: They stay on the Memory Shore all night
plays.why: Curious characters want to hear the whole song.
plays.readAloud: Somewhere before dawn the cold stops mattering. You are standing on a ferry in fog, and your hands are someone else's hands.
plays.response: Each character who stays the full night makes the save. On a failure, roll on the Mere Memory table (v5 Part 11.4). If the party is investigating Tam, replace the roll for one character with Tam's last night: grey gloves, an emptied gaze, a boat drifting with no cargo.
plays.consequence: Someone carries a stranger's memory, possibly Tam's.
plays.fallback: If nobody fails, Ila wakes them at dawn and says she dreamed of her father again.
plays.tells: A player asks what happens if they don't go inside.
plays.rules: DC 12 Wisdom saving throw. Mere Memories are borrowed impressions, not losses; record them as 'Mere' in the ledger.
plays.later: Tam's memory is one of the four sources (Eld's papers S3, the Cantor S2, Brannagh Wick). Any two establish the Court's responsibility.
plays.keywords: night, shore, stay, sleep, camp, memory shore, mere memory, dream, wait

plays.title: They row out to find the missing ferry
plays.why: Mother Sallow asks them to; it is the session's clear objective.
plays.readAloud: Below the skiff, rooftops slide past like the backs of sleeping animals. A drowned weathervane points the way you came. Ahead, a ferry sits crooked on a sandbank, and someone is sitting in it.
plays.response: Brannagh Wick lends a skiff and a pilot if asked; without one, the drowned town is a maze of roofs just under the surface. On the sandbank: the ferry, and its dead ferryman, face peaceful, a dripping oar in his hands. That is the Tidewarden's old body; don't name it yet. Memory-eels circle.
plays.consequence: The ferry is found. The eels are between the party and the body.
plays.fallback: If they won't go, the Tidewarden's ferry drifts in to the Old Shore on its own at dawn, its ferryman still holding the oar.
plays.tells: Players ask for a boat, a pilot, or directions to the eastern-marsh route.
plays.rules: Without a pilot: Wisdom (Survival) DC 14 to read the drowned streets. On a failure the skiff scrapes a roof, ships water, and wakes the eels early.
plays.later: S3: the Tidewarden appears to anyone who treated the body with respect, and offers safe passage to the belfry.
plays.keywords: ferry, missing ferry, boat, row, sandbank, skiff, pilot, brannagh, eastern marsh, h-02

plays.title: They fight the memory-eels
plays.why: The eels guard the sandbank and bite anyone who wades.
plays.readAloud: The water around the sandbank thickens into grey ropes, and the ropes have mouths.
plays.response: Run the eel encounter. A bite that deals damage can take a memory; the player chooses which minor memory goes, and it comes back after their next long rest. The eels flee when reduced to two. Don't add the Drowned Singers to this fight; let the party breathe on the sandbank first.
plays.consequence: The sandbank is clear. Someone may be missing a small memory until morning.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, the dead ferryman's oar rises and the eels scatter.
plays.tells: Weapons out at the waterline; someone jumps in.
plays.rules: Encounter: memory-eels. Bite: DC 13 Wisdom save or lose a minor memory until the next long rest (record as 'Eel'). Swimming in the cold Mere: 2024 Frigid Water (minutes equal to Constitution score, then DC 10 Constitution save each minute or 1 Exhaustion level). A Druid can Wild Shape into a swimming beast and ignore the breath clock but not the bite.
plays.later: S2: the missing memory comes back after a long rest. S3: the Tidewarden notes who fought them. No level is given here: the party stays level 3 until S6.
plays.keywords: eels, memory-eels, fight, attack, bite, water, swim, combat, sandbank

plays.title: They slip past the eels
plays.why: Cautious parties avoid a fight in deep water.
plays.readAloud: You drift with the oars up. The grey shapes rise, taste the air above the water, and sink again.
plays.response: Each character in the boat attempts the check. If at least half succeed, the eels never notice and the party reaches the ferry quietly. If not, the eels attack from below with the party in the boat (they can't reach anyone who stays seated for the first round).
plays.consequence: The ferry and body are reached without a fight.
plays.fallback: If the group fails, give the boat one round of grace before the first bite.
plays.tells: Players ask about the eels' behaviour, or ship their oars and drift.
plays.rules: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 15 for each character; succeed as a group if at least half succeed. Pass without Trace gives +10.
plays.later: No eel-thefts to track. The Tidewarden notes their care in S3.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, quiet, drift, avoid, eels, slip past

plays.title: They dive to the drowned belfry
plays.why: The bell is visible on calm nights and someone always wants to see it up close (H-07).
plays.readAloud: In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's bell-tower stands like a finger pointing at the sky. Pale figures wait among the arches. One of them turns, and her eyes are too bright.
plays.response: The belfry's top is about forty feet down. The Cantor does not attack unless the party touches the bell. If the Tidewarden has met them kindly, he offers an air pocket around the divers for the length of one conversation. Otherwise, breath and cold are the clock.
plays.consequence: The party meets the Cantor.
plays.fallback: If a diver runs out of air, a drowned hand pushes them gently up to the surface.
plays.tells: A player asks how deep it is, or ties a rope to the skiff.
plays.rules: 2024 Suffocation: hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds); out of breath, 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn, removed when breathing again. Frigid Water applies to long dives. A Druid in a swimming Wild Shape has no breath clock, but the Cantor reads an animal shape as a lie unless it is named. Water Breathing (3rd level) arrives with level 5; before then the Tidewarden's air pocket is the only breath-free route.
plays.later: S2: her question follows. S3: the belfry route is known.
plays.keywords: dive, swim, underwater, belfry, bell, drowned bell, cantor, deep, h-07, breath

plays.title: They answer the Cantor truthfully
plays.why: "Tell me, who are you grieving?" is hard to dodge, and players love a true answer.
plays.readAloud: "You have come down to the bell. Good. Tell me, who are you grieving? Do not lie to me. The dead can tell."
plays.response: The Cantor sings the name back to them, and the water warms. She teaches a verse of Ossa's hymn. Ask her about Ila's father and she says he came to find a safe path to her and never arrived. The full release verse needs a sincere memory of a dead person (s02-grieve-to-cantor); a true answer about anything else earns the hymn verse only.
plays.consequence: The party has one more source on Tam's death and the verse of Ossa's hymn.
plays.fallback: If no one has a loss to name, the Cantor accepts someone grieving on Ila's behalf.
plays.tells: A player names a real loss from their backstory.
plays.rules: The verse grants Advantage on the next saving throw against a Drowned Singer.
plays.later: S3: the Choir is calmer toward whoever answered truly. The release verse is in s02-grieve-to-cantor.
plays.keywords: cantor, ondra, grieving, truth, answer, verse, hymn, release, name, dead

plays.title: They lie to the Cantor, or refuse her question
plays.why: Guarded characters won't share grief with a ghost.
plays.readAloud: The Cantor's eyes go dark. The singing stops, and in the silence something long and pale lets go of an arch and comes toward you.
plays.response: Two Drowned Singers attack. The Cantor keeps singing from the water and does not join the fight at this level; her Dirge of Names is pressure, not damage. The Singers stop pursuit at the surface and treat the response hymn as a ceasefire. Give the divers a clear way up.
plays.consequence: The Choir marks them as the forgetful.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, the Tidewarden's oar breaks the surface and the Singer withdraws.
plays.tells: A player deflects, jokes, or gives a name they don't mean.
plays.rules: Encounter: two Drowned Singers, underwater. Melee attackers without a Swim Speed have Disadvantage underwater unless using a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear or trident. Turn Undead on a Singer works (see s02-turn-the-singers).
plays.later: S3: the ferry-stair route to the belfry is guarded; they'll need the Tidewarden or the hymn. The Cantor will still bargain if they come back honest.
plays.keywords: lie, refuse, cantor, attack, drowned singer, fight, flee, underwater combat

plays.title: They ask the Cantor about the Heart
plays.why: The Heart is the reason anyone is here.
plays.readAloud: "The heart was taken from us. Ask the ferry-folk what they owe the dead."
plays.response: That is all she says about it. If they brought the Heart down with them, she goes very still and asks whether they mean to return it. Returning it earns safe access to the bell.
plays.consequence: The party knows the Heart belongs to the Mere and that the ferry-folk carry a debt.
plays.tells: A player mentions the humming bundle, or brought it with them.
plays.later: S3: Mother Sallow's ledger explains the debt (Tam stole it back from the Court in 392 SS, and the Choir asked for it). She can rebuild the release verse from the ledger (s03-sallow-rebuilds-verse).
plays.keywords: heart, ask, cantor, bell, owe, debt, ferry-folk

plays.title: They bring the Heart down and ring Ossa tonight
plays.why: If the party has the Heart and reaches the bell, nothing in the rules stops them.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings from under the water. It is deep and slow and it makes the whole Mere ripple. Every grey face on the shore lifts toward the sound. One voice, very old and very clear, speaks a single name.
plays.response: Before anyone fits the Heart, state the Toll and wait for consent: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. If they say no, the bell does not ring. Ila may not be the Ringer: she is fourteen and has just lost her father, so offer the Toll to an adult in the party. If they agree, the Drowned fall silent and stop hunting; Mother Sallow, on the shore, suddenly remembers her husband's face and the night of the Wrongweather. The Court will hear of it by the next evening.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The Choir rests. Session 3's Heart decision is already made.
plays.fallback: If the Toll gives the table pause, let them surface and decide tomorrow; the bell will wait.
plays.tells: The Heart is in the boat, and a player asks what happens if they fit it.
plays.rules: The Ringer must be at the bell with the Heart. Record the Toll (kind: Toll, bell: Ossa).
plays.later: S3: run the ledger and Eld; skip the Heart choice. S4: Maudrin skips her Heart bargain and is colder (s04-assembly-after-ossa). Concord: 1 of 6. With the verse, the Cantor can be released now (s03-sing-release).
plays.keywords: ring, ossa, bell, toll, early, fit heart, ring the bell, now

plays.title: They deal with Brother Hadrik's blessing of the Mere
plays.why: A Kelemvorite on Strangers' Row has decided the restless dead are an abomination, and he means to act tonight.
plays.readAloud: "The dead are owed rest, not songs," Brother Hadrik says, uncorking the vial. "Kelemvor's judgment is mercy. Stand aside, or kneel."
plays.response: If Hadrik pours holy water into the Mere during the Night Song and calls on his god, the Choir rises angry and a Drowned Singer comes ashore for him (s02-hadrik-pours). Talk him down by arguing his own dogma: Kelemvor's dead are meant to be judged and remembered, not erased. Or restrain him; the ferry-folk will thank you, the Court will not care.
plays.consequence: Hadrik is talked down or held, and the Night Song stays quiet.
plays.fallback: If the party ignores him, play s02-hadrik-pours.
plays.tells: Players notice a grey-robed foreigner with a censer and a vial of holy water heading for the Memory Shore.
plays.rules: Influence, Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15; he's Indifferent. A successful DC 14 Intelligence (Religion) Study check about Kelemvor's teachings first grants Advantage. Hold Person or Zone of Truth also stop him; the former makes him Hostile when it ends.
plays.later: S3: he blesses the Ringer before Ossa rings and can be an ally in Pellmoor later. S3: his forced blessing (s02-hadrik-pours) is the version where the belfry gets a fourth Singer.
plays.keywords: hadrik, kelemvor, priest, holy water, bless, exorcise, turn undead, foreigner, censer

plays.title: They ask the Pilots' Hall about Tam Harrow
plays.why: Tam was a pilot; his colleagues know things the family doesn't.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh Wick coils her sounding-line slowly, twice, before she answers. "Tam took her out the night he died. No cargo. No ship to bring in. No pilot does that, lad. Not unless he's going somewhere he can't write down."
plays.response: Brannagh told the Landing House nothing. She thinks Tam was going to the drowned belfry, and she's right. She'll say so if Ila vouches for the party or if they've helped the ferry-folk.
plays.consequence: One more source on Tam's death.
plays.tells: Players ask who Tam worked with, or where he took his boat.
plays.rules: Influence, Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15; automatic success if Ila vouches for them or they filled the quota.
plays.later: S3: with any second source (Eld's patrol entry, the Cantor, a Mere Memory of Tam) the Court's responsibility is established. Brannagh can also delay any ship from leaving the Mere (s03-delay-heron): no pilot, no departure.
plays.keywords: brannagh, pilots hall, pilot, tam, harrow, father, boat, how he died, investigate

plays.title: They share a sincere memory of someone who has died
plays.why: The Cantor asks whom they grieve, and a player has someone real to name.
plays.readAloud: The Cantor goes still. 'That one is real,' she says. 'Hold it a moment longer. I will give you what I can.'
plays.response: If the memory is sincere, she teaches the full release verse: four lines that let a spirit set down its song. Sharing the memory does not erase it. The player may keep the detail private and describe only the feeling. If the table is shy, the Cantor accepts someone grieving on Ila's behalf.
plays.consequence: The party knows the release verse.
plays.fallback: If nobody offers, Ila names her father for the party.
plays.tells: A player names a lost parent, friend or companion, with a detail only the character would know.
plays.rules: No check. The verse grants Advantage on the next saving throw against a Drowned Singer.
plays.later: S3: after Ossa rings, singing the verse releases Ondra and the remaining Choir (s03-sing-release). If never learned: s03-sallow-rebuilds-verse.
plays.keywords: cantor, grief, dead, release verse, ondra, sincere, memory of the dead

plays.title: Hadrik pours holy water into the Mere
plays.why: Nobody stops him, or the attempt fails, and the Night Song breaks.
plays.readAloud: The holy water goes in without a sound. A moment later the whole shore feels it, like a plate dropped in a quiet house.
plays.response: The Choir rises angry and a Drowned Singer comes ashore for Hadrik. The party can save him (Singers stop when the response hymn is sung) or let the ferry-folk drag him back. Mother Sallow steps between them and gets hurt if no one moves. The Old Shore blames the Loud Quarter.
plays.consequence: The Choir hunts harder. The Old Shore resents the Loud Quarter.
plays.fallback: If it goes badly, the Tidewarden's oar breaks the surface and the Singer withdraws.
plays.tells: The party ignores Hadrik, or his Persuasion check fails.
plays.rules: One Drowned Singer on land; the response hymn is a ceasefire. Mother Sallow takes 5 (1d10) damage if she is not covered.
plays.later: S3: the belfry stair is guarded by an extra Singer (enc-s03-belfry-guard).
plays.keywords: hadrik pours, holy water, kelemvor, choir angry

plays.title: They make amends for taking the Heart
plays.why: The party took the Heart in S1 and the Old Shore has gone cold; most tables want it back.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow is mending a net when you set the bundle on the dock. She does not look up. 'Say a name,' she says. 'Someone who is gone. Out loud, to the water. Then we will see.'
plays.response: Amends are two acts: give the Heart back to Ila by hand, and speak a dead person's name on the Memory Shore. Ila takes it without a word, then sings the response hymn beside whoever apologised. Brannagh reopens the Pilots' Hall within the hour. If the party wants to keep the Heart, they cannot have the Old Shore's help but may still hire a Quays skiff (5 gp) and face the Night Song without the hymn.
plays.consequence: The Shore reopens. Ila holds the Heart again.
plays.fallback: If nobody offers, Ila walks over and holds out her hands for the bundle, and that is enough.
plays.tells: A player asks how to put it right, or asks Dorra Pell why nobody will meet their eye.
plays.rules: No check. The hymn is taught once amends are made. Without it the Night Song is dangerous: the Drowned treat unsung travellers as the forgetful.
plays.later: S2: the hymn calms the Night Song for an hour. S3: Sallow opens the ledger as before.
plays.keywords: amends, apology, return heart, give back, sorry, reconcile, ferry-folk

plays.title: They stop the Court cart on the Mere road
plays.why: The raid took Ila and the cart's route and hour are known.
plays.readAloud: The cart is a covered ferry-wagon with a grey stripe on its tail-board. The driver wears gloves. Behind the canvas, someone is humming the response hymn very quietly.
plays.response: Four Hushmen and a Sergeant escort a covered cart. Check session-zero Off-limits: Ila stays inside, in a closed cart behind a ferry-folk driver, unharmed and not described in danger. Three plans work: a pilot's false checkpoint that turns the cart onto a drowned causeway (Deception DC 15), an ambush at the ford, or Brannagh's pilots refusing the crossing so the cart must wait. The Sergeant yields the cart rather than die.
plays.consequence: Ila is free again. The Court has a reason to be angry.
plays.fallback: If the ambush fails, the Sergeant stops at the next ferry and Brannagh's pilots take the cart by agreement for a keep.
plays.tells: The party asks Brannagh Wick for the road, or begins to plan an ambush.
plays.rules: Encounter: the Mere road cart (Sergeant and three Hushmen). Deception DC 15 for the false checkpoint. Area spells stay clear of the cart: describe the canvas before anyone casts.
plays.later: S3: Quill brings reinforcements (s03-quill-returns). S4: the Gate Clerk knows the party.
plays.keywords: rescue ila, cart, mere road, ambush, free ila, intercept

plays.title: A cleric or paladin turns the Drowned Singers
plays.why: The Singers are undead and a level-3 cleric or paladin has Turn Undead.
plays.readAloud: The holy symbol flares, and the Singer's wail cracks off key. It lets go of the arch and drifts backward with its hands over its ears.
plays.response: Turn Undead (Wisdom save) works on a Drowned Singer, which flees for a minute. It does not work on the Cantor, who is a Ghost singing from the grave with her own will; she is not forced and treats the attempt as an insult. Divine Smite on a Singer is as written. Kelemvor's clergy do the same thing with less reverence, so Hadrik will approve.
plays.consequence: The Singers are driven off, but not released. The Choir marks the party.
plays.fallback: If the save succeeds on a Singer, it comes back in a minute, angrier.
plays.tells: A cleric asks if the Singers count as undead, or a paladin readies a smite.
plays.rules: Turn Undead (2024): Wisdom save against your spell save DC; failed targets are Frightened and flee for 1 minute. The Cantor is immune to Frightened and Charmed (statblock). Radiant damage helps.
plays.later: S3: the belfry guard remembers who turned it. The release verse is the gentler answer.
plays.keywords: turn undead, smite, cleric, paladin, singers, undead, holy

plays.title: They take the dead ferryman home
plays.why: A body on a sandbank is a debt, and ferry-folk have a cold-house for exactly this.
plays.readAloud: The ferryman's face is peaceful. His hands are cold and light. When you lift him, the oar stays in his fingers, and the Mere is very still.
plays.response: Brannagh Wick lends a skiff and a pilot to take the body to the ferry-folk cold-house. This is the Tidewarden's old body: the Choir let it be borne. The Tidewarden's gratitude is quiet; he will offer the air pocket in S3 without being asked. Whether this is Tam or someone else is Sallow's to say; the Choir returned Tam, not this man.
plays.consequence: The ferry-folk see the party honour a dead man.
plays.fallback: If nobody moves, the ferry drifts in to the Old Shore at dawn with the ferryman still holding the oar.
plays.tells: A player asks what happens to the body, or lifts the oar.
plays.rules: No check. A Wisdom (Survival) DC 14 to carry it through the drowned streets if there is no pilot.
plays.later: S3: the Tidewarden appears to the party at the ferry-stair and offers peaceful passage (s03-return-heart).
plays.keywords: body, ferryman, burial, cold-house, tidewarden, honour the dead

plays.title: They skip the Mere and attend the Night Song at the Shuttered Bell
plays.why: Cautious tables rest, shop and listen before they go out on the water.
plays.readAloud: In the Shuttered Bell, no one speaks. The whole room hums back at the water, the way you'd hum to a child who won't sleep. Dorra Pell puts a mug in front of you without asking what you want.
plays.response: The Night Song rises at dusk and passes, and the village's attention is on the water. Quill writes his report. Use the evening to buy gear, learn the hymn, and hear the villagers' rumours (Tam, the missing ferry, the page). A character who sits through the whole night makes the DC 12 Wisdom save (s02-stay-the-night).
plays.consequence: The party has the hymn and a rumour or two; the missing ferry waits.
plays.fallback: If it gets slow, Brannagh Wick comes in at last call and says the ferry has been gone eight days.
plays.tells: A player asks if the village sings together, or says they will take the night off.
plays.rules: No check. Short rest in the inn; a long rest is safe in the Old Shore. Every spell hums: casting inside the Bell draws looks.
plays.later: S3: the missing ferry drifts in by itself at dawn.
plays.keywords: rest, skip, shop, inn, shuttered bell, night song, dorra pell

edits.find: - The ferry for the eastern marsh has not returned. Mother Sallow asks the party to find it.
edits.replace: - The ferry for the eastern marsh has not returned. Mother Sallow asks the party to find it. Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick lends a skiff and a pilot; without one, the drowned rooftops just under the surface make the crossing a maze (DC 12 Wisdom (Survival)).

edits.find: - In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry stands like a finger.
edits.replace: - In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry stands like a finger, its top about forty feet down. Use the 2024 Suffocation rules (hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes) unless the Tidewarden grants an air pocket.

edits.find: **Session 2 end:**
edits.replace:
**Complication (v6, optional): Brother Hadrik Voss.** A Kelemvorite priest from Strangers' Row means to "lay the dead to rest" by blessing the Mere during the Night Song. If he does, the Choir rises angry and a Drowned Singer comes ashore. He can be argued down from his own faith: Kelemvor's dead are owed judgment and remembrance, not erasure.

**Session 2 end:**

sessions.summary: The Night Song, a missing ferry on a sandbank, memory-eels, and a question from the deep: who are you grieving?

plays.title: They search Brother Eld's desk
plays.why: Mother Sallow names him, and the page has to be somewhere.
plays.readAloud: The desk is very neat. Too neat. The drawer that sticks has been oiled.
plays.response: Once they have access, the page is found without a roll. If the three-day bargain with Mother Sallow held, she brings Eld's chapel key and says nothing. A good search also turns up the matching Court forms and a recent patrol entry recording Tam Harrow's interrogation. Failure only costs time and brings Eld in from the vestry, frightened.
plays.consequence: The party holds the missing page, with Ila's name on it.
plays.fallback: If they won't search, Eld brings them the page himself the next morning, unable to sleep.
plays.tells: Players ask when the chapel is empty, or how to get Eld out of it.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 16 finds it quickly, with the forms and the patrol entry. The essential clue is never lost to a failed check. Locate Object on 'the page' needs a sample; Detect Thoughts on Eld shows a man frozen in fear (see any-l3-truth-and-minds).
plays.later: The patrol entry is a source on Tam's death. S4: if they took the forms, Rook (S6) values them as evidence.
plays.keywords: eld, desk, search, chapel, page, ledger, find, investigate, steal, forms

plays.title: They confront Eld privately and take the page
plays.why: A quiet confrontation protects the children and lets Eld save face.
plays.readAloud: "The page is in my desk, Mother. The Court asked me to keep it. I didn't read it, because I didn't want to. But I know what it says. I copied the names onto the Court's forms myself."
plays.response: Eld asks for absolution before anything else. He gives them the name of one child on the list whose family can still be warned, and then he leaves Pellmoor on the next ferry for the ash fields of Kell's Crossing, to pray among the dead fields.
plays.consequence: Eld is gone. One family is warned in time.
plays.tells: Players wait until Eld is alone.
plays.later: S4: Eld is not at the Assembly; use an unnamed Court chaplain. S9: he can be found at Kell's Crossing, in the ash, if the party goes there (s09-ring-calla).
plays.keywords: confront, eld, private, page, absolution, forgive, leave

plays.title: They expose Eld in front of the village
plays.why: The page names children. Some parties want justice in public.
plays.readAloud: Nobody shouts. That is the worst of it. The ferry-folk just look at him, one family at a time, until he can't stand it.
plays.response: The village turns on him. Eld flees to Hallowmere that night in shame and becomes a Court chaplain. Mother Sallow says nothing kind and nothing cruel.
plays.consequence: Eld is in Hallowmere, humiliated and useful to the Court.
plays.tells: Players gather the Old Shore, or read names aloud at the chapel door.
plays.later: S4: Eld is at the Assembly as a Court chaplain and will not meet their eyes. The Court learns what the party knows about the page.
plays.keywords: expose, public, accuse, shame, eld, village, crowd, justice

plays.title: They forgive Eld
plays.why: Eld is pliant, sorry, and offers help; mercy is a real option.
plays.readAloud: Eld cries like a man who has been holding it in for two years. When he stops, he asks what he can do, and he means it.
plays.response: Eld cries like a man who has been holding it in for two years. When he stops, he asks what he can do. The Court wants a chaplain at the Hallowmere masque and has written to him; he will go and be the party's inside ear. He still writes to the Court, and tells the party what he writes. His loyalty depends on how they protect him and the children. Foreshadow any renewed Court pressure before he wavers.
plays.consequence: The party has a source inside the Church, and Eld travels to Hallowmere.
plays.tells: A cleric or a kind character responds to his request for absolution.
plays.later: S4: Eld meets their eyes at the Assembly and slips them a note about Haldric's armory (s04-eld-at-assembly). S6: he can testify at the oath-duel if protected.
plays.keywords: forgive, absolve, mercy, eld, informant, redemption, spare

plays.title: They tell Ila the truth about her name on the list
plays.why: Ila recognises her own name and begins to cry; someone will speak to her.
plays.readAloud: Ila reads her own name twice. Then she says, very quietly, "That's why he was scared. Not of the water. Of them."
plays.response: Ila trusts people who tell her the truth about hard things. If they explain what the list means, she asks to decide the Heart's fate with them, and asks whether she can come. If they say "don't worry about it," she stops talking to that character.
plays.consequence: Ila's trust is earned or lost here.
plays.tells: A player turns to Ila instead of Eld.
plays.later: S3: she argues for returning the Heart to the Mere. Taking her along keeps her close and in danger (s03-take-ila-along); hiding her with the Pilots' Hall keeps her safe (s03-hide-ila). If the party does neither and the Heart goes to the Court, she is arrested (s03-ila-arrested).
plays.keywords: ila, comfort, truth, list, name, cry, tell her, father

plays.title: They work out how Tam Harrow died
plays.why: By now the party likely holds two of the four sources.
plays.readAloud: It isn't a mystery anymore. It's a ferry with no cargo, a patrol in grey gloves, and a man who couldn't remember the way home.
plays.response: Confirm it when any two sources agree: a Court patrol took Tam's memory of the route to the belfry and left him on the water; he fell in and drowned; the Choir kept his body, but did not kill him. Let Ila hear it from whoever she trusts most.
plays.consequence: The Court is responsible for Tam's death, and the party knows it.
plays.fallback: If they have only one source, Mother Sallow supplies the second from the ledger: Tam's name, with a Court mark beside it.
plays.tells: Players line up the patrol entry, the Cantor's words, Brannagh's story, or a Mere Memory.
plays.later: S6: Wren's confession (she gave the Court Tam's name) lands hard. Ila's anger shapes her choices for the rest of the campaign.
plays.keywords: tam, death, murder, how he died, clues, solve, patrol, route, memory taken

plays.title: They return the Heart to the Mere
plays.why: Ila, Mother Sallow and the Cantor all point this way.
plays.readAloud: The Tidewarden is waiting at the end of the old dock, oar dripping. He doesn't ask where you're going.
plays.response: The ferry-stair is safest, and the Choir guards it. The Tidewarden holds a pocket of breathable air around anyone who accepts peaceful passage; Mother Sallow's hymn earns that passage without any memory price. Diving magic or a sound alternative plan also works. Ila is fourteen: she may come to the stair, but she stays in the ferry with an adult and never goes down with the divers, so check session-zero Off-limits. At the belfry, the Cantor asks whether they mean to ring it.
plays.consequence: The Heart is home. The Choir is quieter while it stays there.
plays.fallback: If they hesitate at the water's edge, Ila holds out her hands for the bundle, and the Tidewarden's ferry waits for whoever carries it.
plays.tells: Players ask how to reach the drowned belfry safely.
plays.rules: If not using the Tidewarden: 2024 Suffocation and Frigid Water apply.
plays.later: Ringing is a separate choice with a Toll (next play). The Court still wants the Heart (S4).
plays.keywords: return, give back, mere, belfry, tidewarden, choir, cantor, put back

plays.title: They ring Ossa
plays.why: With the Heart at the bell, the question is only who pays.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings from under the water. It is deep and slow and it makes the whole Mere ripple. Every grey face on the shore lifts toward the sound. The Drowned fall silent, and one voice, very old and very clear, speaks a single name. Then the Mere is only water again, and the reeds bend in a breeze that smells of rain.
plays.response: State the Toll first and wait for a yes: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. Ila may volunteer; she is fourteen and has just lost her father, so offer the Toll to an adult instead and let her stand beside them. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. If they ring it, the Choir rests, and Mother Sallow remembers her husband Davin and the night of the Wrongweather. If anyone sings the Cantor's release verse afterward, Ondra speaks her own name and goes quiet.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The dead of the Mere may rest.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer is unsure, the Cantor waits. A bell that waited four hundred years can wait a night.
plays.tells: A player asks what ringing would do, or what it costs.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (kind: Toll, bell: Ossa). The deceased person need not be a loved one (v5 2.11). Ila may not be the Ringer.
plays.later: Concord: 1 of 6. S4: no Heart bargain at the Assembly. The Court withdraws collectors from the newly quiet Mere for a while (Court clock +1). S27: the Choir can sing at the summit if released.
plays.keywords: ring, ossa, toll, bell, ring the bell, memory of the dead, ringer

plays.title: They sing the Cantor's release verse after Ossa rings
plays.why: If they learned the verse in Session 2, this is the moment it was for.
plays.readAloud: The verse is short. When it ends, the Cantor sings her own name, Ondra Sallow, in a voice nobody has heard for two hundred and sixty years. Then she goes quiet, and so does everyone else under the water.
plays.response: The singer must sincerely commemorate a dead person. Ondra and the remaining Choir are released. Released spirits may return once, willingly, as allies; they are never compelled back.
plays.consequence: The Drowned Choir is released.
plays.fallback: If nobody learned the verse, Mother Sallow can rebuild it from the restored ledger (s03-sallow-rebuilds-verse); the Cantor will wait.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Choir can be freed now.
plays.later: S22/S27: the Cantor may return once as an ally. S28: Mother Sallow sings the last verse with Ila.
plays.keywords: release, verse, sing, cantor, ondra, free the choir, choir, rest

plays.title: They carry the Heart to Hallowmere
plays.why: Some parties want allies (the Dawn Order, the Bellwrights) before deciding.
plays.readAloud: The bundle hums all the way to the edge of the Mere road, and then, as the reeds give way to grey hedges, it goes quiet, as if it knows where it's going.
plays.response: Act II begins early. Brannagh can ferry them across the Mere (three days to the capital instead of six) and knows a landing that skips the first checkpoint. Faerûnians need the Chancellor's invitation or a writ: the grey-sealed letter reaches them at the first checkpoint by the Court's own rider, and they can accept it there (s03-accept-invitation). Ila's place in this trip is s03-take-ila-along or s03-hide-ila.
plays.consequence: The party is on the road to Hallowmere with Ossa's Heart.
plays.tells: Players ask who in the capital opposes the Court.
plays.later: S4: the Gate Clerk already has their names (+2 to Persuasion DCs). Maudrin's bargain targets the Heart they carry. Concord: Ossa still needs a return to the Mere (the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer once they hold it again).
plays.keywords: hallowmere, capital, carry, take it, dawn order, bellwrights, travel, leave pellmoor, road

plays.title: They keep the Heart in Pellmoor and defend the village
plays.why: A protective party won't let the Court take anything from the Old Shore.
plays.readAloud: Quill comes back with every Hushman the Landing House has, and a written deadline nailed to the chapel door. Behind him, forty foreign masts stand very still on the water and do nothing at all.
plays.response: Act II begins as a siege. Quill issues a deadline; villagers prepare shelter and an evacuation route; the party negotiates, resists a patrol, or leads an escape. The foreign ships stay neutral, but Brannagh can close the Mere to Court boats: no pilot, no crossing. Intercepted orders point to the Hallowmere vault.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor is under Court pressure and will be changed by it.
plays.fallback: If the siege drags, the Pilots' Hall offers to smuggle the Heart out by night.
plays.tells: Players ask about defences, the Landing House's strength, or who would fight.
plays.rules: Use the siege patrol (enc-s04-siege-patrol) scaled for four level-3 characters. Show retreat routes and the deadline before any fighting.
plays.later: S4: a short siege outline replaces the gate scene; the intercepted orders lead to Hallowmere. The Old Shore's trust is earned for the rest of the campaign. Faerûnian traders note which side the party took.
plays.keywords: keep, defend, protect, siege, stay, fight the court, village, pellmoor, barricade

plays.title: They send the Heart to the Chancellor
plays.why: Greedy or desperate parties take the Court's reward.
plays.readAloud: The order comes back with the receipt, sealed in the same grey wax: the arrest of one Ila Harrow, listener, for questioning.
plays.response: Show the arrest order to the players before anyone acts on it. Give them a chance to warn, hide, or escort Ila (s03-take-ila-along, s03-hide-ila). Check session-zero Off-limits: Ila is arrested Off-screen, held in a room with a lamp and a bowl of soup, never harmed. If the party does nothing, the Hushmen come at dawn (s03-ila-arrested).
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Heart and wants Ila.
plays.tells: Players ask what the Court would pay, or want to end the danger quickly.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin is delighted and offers Ila's Tithe-exemption instead of a bargain (s04-exemption-releases-ila if she was taken, s04-exemption-for-ila if not). If Ila is taken, she is held in the Hall of Tithes (rescue alongside Tessa in S6). Concord: Ossa needs the Heart recovered (s04-ask-ossa-back).
plays.keywords: give, maudrin, court, chancellor, sell to the court, reward, surrender

plays.title: They sell the Heart to Master Venn
plays.why: A Faerûnian buyer offers real gold and a way out of Corvane's problems.
plays.readAloud: Venn counts the gold onto the table himself, coin by coin, smiling. "The Gilded Heron sails in three days. Your relic will be admired in Athkatla by people who have never heard of a Toll. Isn't that a kindness?"
plays.response: Venn pays 600 gp (Influence, Persuasion, DC 15 raises it to 900; his buyer pays 5,000). The Heart goes aboard the Gilded Heron, which needs a pilot to leave the Mere and a day to cross the Seam. Ila learns within the hour. Brannagh Wick can delay the ship one day by refusing a pilot.
plays.consequence: The Heart is on a foreign ship. The clock is three days, maybe four (s03-delay-heron adds one).
plays.fallback: If the players regret it, Venn will sell it back for 1,200 gp or a heartkeep, and enjoy the profit.
plays.tells: Players ask what Venn would pay, or whether selling abroad keeps it from the Court.
plays.rules: Record the sale. The Heron leaves in 3 days; Brannagh can add 1; the Seam crossing takes 1 more.
plays.later: If it clears the Seam (s03-heron-sails): Ossa can't be rung and Concord is impossible until it is recovered. The safety valve is any-heron-wrecks. S4: the Court is furious with Venn, and with the party. S28: Ila never forgives it.
plays.keywords: sell, venn, merchant, gold, coster, gilded heron, ship, abroad, athkatla, profit, buyer

plays.title: They board the Gilded Heron and take the Heart back
plays.why: If the Heart was sold, regret (or Ila) arrives quickly.
plays.readAloud: The Gilded Heron rides at anchor beyond the last pier, lamps lit, a drowned church spire just under her keel.
plays.response: Three ways: board her at night past two Coster guards and a mate; persuade Brannagh to deny her a pilot until Venn deals (s03-delay-heron); or buy it back (s03-buy-back-from-venn). Venn prefers money to trouble and folds once a guard drops or the Pilots' Hall turns against him. Invisibility, Misty Step and Pass without Trace make boarding easier but the Heron's lamps pick up a shimmer on the water; the mate has Passive Perception 14.
plays.consequence: The Heart is recovered, or it sails.
plays.fallback: If they fail, the Heron's first mate, a Baldurian who toasts the Gull's Wager, offers to 'lose' it overboard for 100 gp.
plays.tells: Players ask where the Heron is anchored, or who pilots her out.
plays.rules: Boarding: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 15 per character, or the encounter. Venn is Indifferent; he becomes Hostile only if humiliated in public.
plays.later: Recovered by force or theft: Venn holds a grudge and pays Quill to watch the party (S4 Court knows them). If they sail before it is done: s03-heron-sails.
plays.keywords: recover, steal back, board, ship, gilded heron, venn, buy back, pilot, retrieve

plays.title: They accept the Chancellor's invitation
plays.why: The letter arrives whatever they chose, and it promises safety and answers.
plays.readAloud: "To those who carried the Heart of Ossa from Pellmoor: the Quiet Court extends its gratitude and its invitation. The Chancellor would be honoured by your presence at the Quiet Assembly in Hallowmere, in ten days. You will be safe. You will be remembered. Nothing you carry will be asked of you that you do not wish to give. M. Vesk, Quiet Chancellor, Warden of Silence."
plays.response: The grey seal makes the letter a writ of passage for everyone named in it, Stormborn included. Brannagh offers the Mere crossing. The party is still level 3; level 4 comes after the Hallowmere investigation in S6.
plays.consequence: The party is expected at the Quiet Assembly.
plays.tells: Players read the letter twice, or ask whether it's a trap.
plays.later: S4: the gate accepts the letter as a writ. Maudrin has read Quill's report and knows their faces.
plays.keywords: invitation, letter, assembly, accept, go, hallowmere, writ, chancellor

plays.title: They refuse the invitation
plays.why: A letter from the people who killed Tam is easy to burn.
plays.readAloud: The letter curls in the fire. The grey wax doesn't melt. It sits in the ashes, perfectly round, until someone picks it up.
plays.response: Don't force the trip. Captain Rook or Wren Caddock brings the investigation to them instead (a Dawn Order rider, or a Bellwright courier asking for help). The wax seal still works as a writ if they keep it.
