plays.consequence: The Court takes note of the refusal.
plays.tells: Players call it a trap, or burn it.
plays.later: S4: start with Rook's or Wren's request instead of the Assembly; Maudrin's bargain comes later, by letter. The Court's clock ticks.
plays.keywords: refuse, burn, decline, ignore, trap, invitation, letter, no

plays.title: They take Ila with them
plays.why: Ila asked whether she could come, and the party does not want her alone with Hushmen at the door.
plays.readAloud: 'I'll carry my own bag,' Ila says. 'And I'll tell you when the water's wrong. That's all I'm good for, so far.'
plays.response: Mother Sallow allows it only if an adult promises to bring her home. Ila is fourteen: she travels with the party and is never put in combat or described in harm; check session-zero Off-limits and give her a quiet place at every scene's edge. She keeps the Harrow house key and sings the response hymn at the Gate when asked.
plays.consequence: Ila is in the party's care, which makes her a lever for the Court.
plays.fallback: If the party hesitates, Sallow says 'She is safest with people who are looked for.'
plays.tells: A player says 'you're coming with us', or asks Mother Sallow's leave.
plays.rules: No check. Brannagh gives a pilot-letter for the Mere crossing.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin notices her at the masque and offers her exemption as a bargain. S6: Ila can reach the Hall of Tithes, which Wren's plan uses. S28: Ila grew up in the party's shadow.
plays.keywords: take ila, bring ila, travel, companion, child, escort ila

plays.title: They hide Ila at the Pilots' Hall
plays.why: The Court wants her; the Pilots' Hall is the safest roof in Pellmoor.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh looks at Ila over the sounding-line on her shoulder. 'Pilots' Hall has a loft nobody climbs. She'll have a hammock, a bell to ring if the gloves come, and a pilot on the stair.'
plays.response: Brannagh keeps Ila in the loft with a pilot on the stair, and the ferry-folk close ranks. Ila stays hidden until the party returns or the Court escalates. She argues, but accepts it if the party explains why; if they say 'don't worry', she stops speaking to that character.
plays.consequence: Ila is safe, and the Court's cart finds only an empty house.
plays.fallback: If nobody has a plan, Brannagh does it anyway.
plays.tells: A player asks Brannagh Wick where a child could sleep out of sight.
plays.rules: No check. The households that owe the party (s01-fill-the-quota) also offer a hiding place.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin's bargain is for the Heart, not Ila. S6: if the party told Maudrin where she was (s04-tell-where-ila), Hushmen go to the Pilots' Hall within two days. S28: Ila is hidden but angry.
plays.keywords: hide ila, pilots hall, safe house, protect ila, loft

plays.title: Hushmen come for Ila at dawn
plays.why: The Heart went to the Court and nobody sheltered her.
plays.readAloud: Grey wax on the Harrow door. Dorra Pell says it flatly: 'They came at first light. She went with her coat on and her head up.'
plays.response: Off-screen. Check session-zero Off-limits. Ila is taken by a Hushman Sergeant and two escorts and carried to Hallowmere, where she waits in the Hall of Tithes, a clean room with a bed. A courier from Brannagh's pilots can reach the cart before it leaves the Mere (s02-intercept-ila-cart applies on the road). Maudrin's offer will use her.
plays.consequence: Ila is under Court arrest.
plays.fallback: If the party reacts in time, Brannagh's pilots delay the cart one day.
plays.tells: A party that sold the Heart to Quill or the Chancellor leaves Ila in her father's house.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin offers Ila's release for a favour (s04-exemption-releases-ila). S6: rescue alongside Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa-with-ila).
plays.keywords: ila arrested, dawn, hushmen, taken, child arrested

plays.title: Quill returns with a second Hushman
plays.why: The lie held, or the party named Mother Sallow to him; either way Quill's report is out.
plays.readAloud: Quill stands in the chapel door with a second Hushman behind him. 'Good morning,' he says. 'I was reviewing my notes and found a gap in my notes, and I thought you'd want to help me fill it.'
plays.response: He asks the coat question again, and if Mother Sallow's name was given, he asks for her ledger. He is polite; the second Hushman is not. He wants a reason to search. Persuasion DC 16 on Quill buys a week. Hold Person or Suggestion on Quill works but the Landing House reads the hum as a confession.
plays.consequence: The Court's pressure rises one notch.
plays.fallback: If the party fights him, run s01-attack-quill.
plays.tells: The party has lied to Quill or named a villager to him in S1.
plays.rules: Influence DC 16 on Quill (Intelligence 11, Insight +5). If bribed, he takes more gold and complains less.
plays.later: S4: the Gate Clerk raises Persuasion DCs by 2 if Quill is Suspicious (s04-refuse-courtesy-memory).
plays.keywords: quill returns, second hushman, search, ledger, mother sallow

plays.title: The three households warn the party
plays.why: The party filled the quota, so three Bellwright-sympathising households owe them.
plays.readAloud: A boy slips a folded net-tag under your door: a thread tied in three knots. Downstairs, the woman whose quota you filled says only, 'Not tonight. They're at the chapel.'
plays.response: The households warn the party when Hushmen move, offer a hiding place for Ila or the Heart, and later shelter villagers during a siege. They will not fight; they will lie. They do not ask for anything. Heroic Inspiration for a player who thanks them by name.
plays.consequence: The Old Shore has a back door.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, the households send a child with a loaf.
plays.tells: Hushmen move in the village, or the party asks who can be trusted.
plays.rules: No check. A hiding place gives Advantage on Stealth checks to hide a person or bundle on the Old Shore.
plays.later: S4 (siege): they shelter villagers. S6: Wren already trusts the party.
plays.keywords: households, quota, warn, villagers owe, sympathisers

plays.title: They kill Brother Eld
plays.why: Eld wrote down the names of children for the Court.
plays.readAloud: Eld does not run. 'I knew it would be someone,' he says. 'I'd like to ask only that you tell Mother Sallow I tried to keep the page.'
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' A downed Eld can be bound. If he dies, the ferry-folk say nothing and the chapel stays shut. Say plainly that the only living witness to the Court's patrol entries is gone; the page and the forms still point at Quill and Hallowmere. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Eld is dead. The Church notes it.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Eld offers the Heart's page and a name of a child to warn.
plays.tells: A player lifts a blade in the chapel, or waits for Eld on the Mere road.
plays.rules: Eld is a Priest Acolyte (CR 1/4) and can cast Silence once per day. A downed Eld can be knocked out instead of killed.
plays.later: S4: use an unnamed chaplain at the Assembly. S28: Mother Sallow knows who did it.
plays.keywords: kill eld, murder, chaplain, execute

plays.title: Brannagh denies the Heron a pilot
plays.why: The Heron needs a pilot to leave the Mere, and Brannagh runs the Pilots' Hall.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh counts the tide out loud and shakes her head. 'No pilot leaves this hall for the Heron today. She'll sit till Venn's patience runs out.'
plays.response: Brannagh can delay the ship one day by refusing a pilot; a second day costs the Pilots' Hall a favour and Venn a fine. The delay buys the party time to board or buy back the Heart. It also tells Venn exactly who is against him.
plays.consequence: The Heron's sailing is delayed by one day.
plays.fallback: If Brannagh refuses, a Baldurian mate offers to 'lose' the Heart overboard for 100 gp.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Heron can be stopped without a fight.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Brannagh (Friendly if Ila vouches). Each day of delay adds one to clock_ferry. At 6 the Hall suspends a crossing.
plays.later: S3: s03-heron-sails runs the clock out if the Heart is not recovered. Venn remembers.
plays.keywords: delay ship, pilot, pilots hall, brannagh, heron

plays.title: The Gilded Heron sails with the Heart
plays.why: Three or four days pass and the Heart is still aboard.
plays.readAloud: The Heron slips her lines at the turn of the tide, a Pilots' Hall skiff ahead of her, and the last you see of her is a plum-coloured sail going into a wall of grey weather.
plays.response: Brannagh counts the days honestly. The Heron crosses the Seam in a day. The Heart is beyond Corvane. Ossa cannot be rung until it returns. Tell the table plainly what this closes (the Concord) and what stays open (the Second Dawn). Offer the safety valve if the table wants it: the Heron wrecks in the Wall and the Mere returns the Heart weeks later (any-heron-wrecks).
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is gone through the Seam.
plays.fallback: If the table is stunned, the Tidewarden says only: 'The Mere remembers what is taken from it.'
plays.tells: The party has not recovered the Heart by the end of the third or fourth day.
plays.rules: No check. Three days after the sale, four if Brannagh delayed once.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin hears of it from Quill's replacement (s04-tell-where). S28: Ila never forgives the sale. Any time: any-heron-wrecks, or any-ossa-written-off if the table moves on.
plays.keywords: heron sails, ship leaves, heart gone, seam, abroad

plays.title: They buy the Heart back from Venn
plays.why: They sold it in haste, or Ila found out.
plays.readAloud: Venn spreads his ringed hands. 'Twelve hundred, friend, or a heartkeep. You see I am a reasonable man. I paid six, I lose nothing, and I was so looking forward to Athkatla.'
plays.response: Venn sells it back for 1,200 gp or a heartkeep and enjoys the profit. He remains Friendly; the party now owes him nothing and he thinks well of them. Persuasion DC 15 brings it to 900 gp. A heartkeep is a defining memory, chosen by the player.
plays.consequence: The Heart returns without a fight; Venn is a smiling creditor.
plays.fallback: If the party cannot pay, Brannagh offers to guarantee a loan.
plays.tells: A player asks what Venn wants for it, or counts out gold.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 for the discount.
plays.later: S4: the Court hears of the sale from Quill but Venn is not exposed.
plays.keywords: buy back, venn, pay, heartkeep, 1200 gp, heart

plays.title: Mother Sallow rebuilds the release verse
plays.why: They missed the Cantor's verse, but Sallow's ledger can rebuild it.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow reads from the restored ledger in a low voice. 'It was a funeral verse, once. They sang it in my grandmother's time. I lost it with the rest.'
plays.response: Sallow reads the verse from the ledger and teaches it. It takes an hour. The verse is the same as the Cantor's: four lines and a sincere commemoration.
plays.consequence: The party knows the release verse.
plays.fallback: If the ledger is damaged, Ila hums the tune and Sallow supplies the words.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Choir can be freed without the Cantor's help.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S3: the verse is sung after Ossa rings (s03-sing-release).
plays.keywords: verse, ledger, rebuild, mother sallow, choir release

**DO (v6):** The letter's grey seal is a writ of passage for everyone it names, Stormborn included.

sessions.summary: A missing ledger page, a frightened friar, and the choice of what to do with the Heart before the Court decides for you.

plays.title: They give the courtesy memory at the gate
plays.why: It is presented as a formality, the clerk is pitiable, and refusing looks like trouble on the first day.
plays.readAloud: The clerk touches a tuning fork to a vial of grey glass and holds it near your temple. It feels like forgetting a word you were about to say, and then not minding. He writes your name in the book without looking up. “Welcome to Hallowmere. You won't miss it.”
plays.response: Each player chooses the memory and writes one line in the Memory Ledger; you never choose it. Log it as a Tithe, not a Toll: it sits in a labelled jar in the Tithe-Ledger Room and its owner can redeem it by opening the jar. Clerk Oswin Tell is a Blank; asked why he works here, he says “Someone must,” and looks frightened that he cannot say who. If anyone offers gold he stares at the coin as if it were a pebble: the courtesy memory is a registration, not a fee, and the Hallowmere gate takes no gold for it.
plays.consequence: The party is in the Tithe-system. Any Hushman can look up their names and what they gave.
plays.fallback: If a player can't pick, offer a mote: last Ossday's supper, a stranger's coat, the second verse of a song.
plays.tells: Players ask “What happens to it?” or start choosing something small.
plays.rules: No check. Record as a Tithe (redeemable), not a Toll. A Reckoner's draw takes about a minute and needs consent.
plays.later: S5: each courtesy jar sits on the vault's newest shelf, near the character's older earliest-memory jar. S7 and S9: Hushmen at the line and the north gate know their names on sight.
plays.keywords: gate, courtesy memory, register, registration, tithe, clerk, give memory, entry, gold, pay, oswin

plays.title: They refuse the courtesy memory
plays.why: Players who spent three sessions learning what the Tithe costs will balk at feeding it.
plays.readAloud: The clerk's pen stops. He looks past you, at the two grey-gloved men by the arch, and says in a small voice, “Sergeant? These ones won't.”
plays.response: Refusing needs Influence (Persuasion) DC 15 on Sergeant Mabry Cole, or a bribe: Cole takes 10 gp a head, Tithes a mote of his own to fill the line, and pockets the gold. If that fails, Cole calls his men (Gate Hushmen). The party can run into the lamp-lit lanes (DC 13 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) each) or talk their way out (DC 15 Charisma (Deception): 'the Chancellor promised us exemption'). Anyone who fails spends a day and a night in a cell in Vaer's Belfry, and Captain Rook hears of it by evening and visits the cell herself.
plays.consequence: The party stays outside the Tithe-system, and the gate remembers their faces as refusers.
plays.fallback: If it bogs down, the Assembly's carriage arrives for 'the Chancellor's guests' and Cole steps back, furious.
plays.tells: A flat “No,” or a player asks what happens if they don't.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Cole's Intelligence is 14). Athletics or Acrobatics DC 13 to flee; Deception DC 15. Quill's modifiers: add +2 to these DCs if quill is Suspicious, Tithe-case or Dead (the Gate Clerk has their names; if Dead, Cole names them murderers); subtract 2 if quill is Bribed (Quill's letter vouches for them). Add +2 more if the party carried the Heart to Hallowmere early in S3. A night in the Belfry is a night in a Court city (Tithe Clock +1).
plays.later: S6: a jailed character meets Rook early; she opens the commission in the cell. S9: Cole is on the north gate on the day they leave and remembers refusers (+2 to any bluff there).
plays.keywords: refuse, no, won't give, bribe guard, run, flee, gate, hushmen, deception, belfry, jail, cell, cole, sergeant

plays.title: A Stormborn character shows their papers
plays.why: Under the Landing Charter, Faerûnians need a writ of passage beyond the Mere road, and the Hallowmere gate checks.
plays.readAloud: Sergeant Cole holds the grey-sealed letter to the lamp and reads the signature twice. Then he hands it back very carefully, as if it might bruise. “Guests of the Assembly. Loudfolk too, it seems.”
plays.response: Read the writ. The Chancellor's invitation (writ Invited) counts for everyone it names, Stormborn included. A true writ (bought from Quill) passes without a question. A forged writ gets past the Blank clerk but not Cole, who checks the grey wax (DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation)); a failed forgery is arrest for 'landing past the Charter' unless they talk or run as above. With no writ at all, a Faerûnian is turned back to the Mere road; a Corvane Venture cloth wagon gets them in by night (DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth)). Inland, nobody speaks Common: Faerûnians without Hesk need a companion to translate, or Comprehend Languages to understand what is said; a Hesk speaker still has to speak for them.
plays.consequence: Stormborn characters are inside Hallowmere, lawfully or not. Hushmen stare at dragonborn, tieflings and gnomes, and whisper that aasimar are bell-touched.
plays.fallback: If a player feels locked out, a palace clerk arrives with a fresh writ 'for the Chancellor's guests', which also shows how closely Maudrin watches them.
plays.tells: A Sword Coast character produces papers, or asks whether foreigners are allowed in.
plays.rules: Investigation DC 17 (Cole vs a forgery). Stealth DC 16 to ride in under cloth. Add Quill's modifier from s04-refuse-courtesy-memory. Comprehend Languages lets you understand Hesk but not reply in it; Hearts is a level-5 spell.
plays.later: S9: a forged-writ character is stopped at the north gate unless they leave under Rook's escort or a smuggling route. Act IV: if Thrane rings, the Charter collapses and writs stop mattering.
plays.keywords: writ, passage, papers, faerunian, stormborn, loudfolk, foreigner, forged, seal, grey wax, charter, hesk, language, hearts, translate

plays.title: They bring Sister Aurelie into the city
plays.why: The Court has refused Aurelie's writ four times; a party with the Chancellor's invitation looks like her chance.
plays.readAloud: Sister Aurelie lowers her hood at the edge of the marsh road and looks up at the grey disc of the sun. “When the sun comes back,” she says, “I'd like to be standing somewhere it can see me.”
plays.response: The invitation does not name her. Passing her off as the party's scribe is Influence (Deception) DC 15 against Cole; hiding her in a cart is DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) for her, with advantage if someone Helps. Inside, she cannot stay quiet: within two days she wants to sing a dawn-hymn on the Terraces of Grief. If caught, play s04-aurelie-caught.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is in Hallowmere: a healer, an ally, and a liability.
plays.fallback: If smuggling her stalls, she gives the party a letter for 'the Dawn Mission's first friend in Hallowmere' and goes back to Pellmoor to wait.
plays.tells: The party met Aurelie at the Dawn Mission (s01-dawn-mission), or a cleric or paladin of Lathander asks about her.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Cole). Stealth DC 15; Help gives advantage. Aurelie uses Priest stats (Healing Word, Lesser Restoration, Dispel Magic: she is an NPC, so her 3rd-level spells are not available to the party).
plays.later: S9: if Vaer rings while she is in the city, she goes to the terraces to sing (s09-aurelie-on-the-terraces). S22: a free Aurelie is the core of the Stormborn ally.
plays.keywords: aurelie, dawnmantle, lathander, dawn mission, morninglord, smuggle, sneak in, cart, cleric, priest, disguise

plays.title: They stayed to defend Pellmoor
plays.why: A party that kept the Heart in Pellmoor (S3) opens Act II under siege instead of at the gate.
plays.readAloud: The notice is nailed to the chapel door in Quill's neat hand: 'By the Office of Tithes. Surrender all unlicensed bell-work by Hushday dusk. Thereafter the Old Shore will be searched house by house.'
plays.response: Run it short: Quill gives three days. The villagers want a shelter (the ledger-house) and an escape route (Brannagh Wick's pilots can take the Old Shore across the Mere in two nights). The households who owe the party (s01-fill-the-quota) shelter villagers without being asked. The party negotiates, resists one patrol (Siege Patrol), or leads the evacuation. Whatever happens, the patrol's Sergeant carries orders in grey wax: 'Ossa relic to the Tithe-Ledger Room, Hallowmere, by Vaerday.' The siege takes three days and the road to the capital three more; the Assembly is ten days after the letter, so they arrive with a day to spare. The marsh road out is cordoned (DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth) as a group). The outcome is s04-evacuate-old-shore or s04-siege-holds.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor is under siege. The party chooses how it ends.
plays.fallback: If the siege drags, Quill accepts a parley: one memory 'for the quota' from a volunteer, and he withdraws for a week.
plays.tells: The Heart is still in Pellmoor and Quill's notice is on the chapel door.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 16 past the cordon; Pass without Trace gives +10. Influence DC 15 on Quill (Indifferent, Hostile if the party is a Tithe-case).
plays.later: S9: the party can come back to Pellmoor instead of going north. S22: defended ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day (no pilot, no departure).
plays.keywords: siege, defend pellmoor, quill, deadline, evacuate, cordon, marsh road, patrol, orders, old shore, stay

plays.title: They refuse the invitation or never go to the Assembly
plays.why: Some tables smell a trap and stay away from the Chancellor entirely.
plays.readAloud: A broad woman in a dawn-coloured cloak gone grey sits down across from you without asking and sets a Dawn Order seal on the table. “You turned down the Chancellor. Good. Then you might be the only people in this city who'll listen to me.”
plays.response: Bring the investigation to them. Captain Dessa Rook finds them at their lodgings and opens her commission early (S6, Scene 1); or Wren Caddock, sewing on a bench outside the Bone Archive, asks too many friendly questions and mentions that Lysse Carrow 'needs someone brave'. Maudrin is not offended: she sends a single grey rose to their lodgings with no note, and two Hushmen follow them for the rest of the Act.
plays.consequence: No bargain is offered, so no favor is owed. The Court watches them closely.
plays.fallback: If they wander, Lysse Carrow drops a bone-bound book at their feet in the street and asks them to carry it back to the Archive.
plays.tells: “We're not going to her party.” Or they head straight for the Bone Archive or the Dawn Order.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 to shake the Hushmen for a day.
plays.later: S8: Maudrin's last word still comes, through Isolde. S23: with no favor owed, Maudrin runs the Strike normally.
plays.keywords: refuse invitation, skip assembly, don't go, avoid maudrin, stay away, rook, wren, investigation, lysse

plays.title: They accept Maudrin's bargain for Ossa's Heart
plays.why: Safe passage, a pension and a protected memory are a real offer, and some players are tired of being hunted.
plays.readAloud: “Safe passage. A Court pension. And one memory of your choosing that no Tithe will ever touch.” Maudrin folds her grey gloves. “All I ask is the thing your friend is carrying, which was never yours to carry.”
plays.response: Maudrin keeps her word about exactly what she promised. Each character names one memory on a grey card she signs: no Court Tithe can take it (Tolls, the stairs of the Hush and eel bites are not Tithes). She calls Ser Haldric, 'my dear' — and corrects it to 'Ser' before the word is finished. Haldric carries the Heart to the Dawn Order armory beside Vaer's Heart, so the party sees a Dawn Order knight take the Chancellor's orders. The pension is 5 gp a month for Stormborn (she knows they prefer gold) or 5 keeps for Corvanese.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is in the Dawn Order armory. The party owes Maudrin one favor.
plays.fallback: If the table splits, Maudrin gives them until the end of the masque and dances with Isolde while they argue.
plays.tells: A player asks exactly what the exemption covers, or looks at the bundle and then at the others.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 (Maudrin's Intelligence) to haggle a better term, such as Ila's exemption too. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S6: if Rook wins the hearing, she takes the armory and hands Ossa's Heart back to the party (s06-rook-returns-ossa). S9: or they steal it with Vaer's (s09-steal-ossa-too). S23: Maudrin calls the favor in on the ridge: 'One favor, dear, and I am calling it in now. Go, before I change my mind.'
plays.keywords: accept, bargain, deal, maudrin, exemption, pension, safe passage, hand over, give heart, favor, ossa

plays.title: They refuse Maudrin's bargain
plays.why: Most tables have decided by now that the Court is the problem.
plays.readAloud: Her smile does not move at all. “Then the Assembly will go on without you. Enjoy the city.”
plays.response: She does not threaten. Two Hushmen follow the party for the rest of the Act at a polite distance; a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) group check loses them for a day, and they are back next morning. Isolde Drave finds the party within the hour, delighted: people who refuse Maudrin are the most interesting people in the room. A locket at her throat holds a boy's portrait; she closes it when someone looks. For one true story about the Mere, Isolde trades one true secret: 'The Tithe-Ledger Room has a service passage, and a Hushman named Ilam Bray walks past it every evening.' She also mentions, idly, that Ironhorn bronze is cheaper this year.
plays.consequence: No favor is owed. The Court watches them, and Isolde is curious.
plays.fallback: If they freeze, Maudrin answers the question nobody asked: 'Yes, I know about your Heart. Everyone does.'
plays.tells: Players answer with a question about the Tithe, or say no outright.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 to shake the tail (once a day). Isolde: Influence DC 15, Indifferent; clever talk makes her Friendly. Record in the Bargain Log: refused.
plays.later: S5: the Ledger shows Isolde's Ironhorn sales (s05-take-ledger). S7: the Ilam Bray lead pays off. S8: Maudrin's last word is warmer than they expect, and Isolde can be turned (s08-turn-isolde).
plays.keywords: refuse, no deal, decline, reject bargain, maudrin, hushmen follow, tail, isolde, gossip

plays.title: They tell Maudrin where the Heart is
plays.why: The party no longer carries Ossa's Heart, so Maudrin changes the bargain: “Then tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded.”
plays.readAloud: “Then you don't have it.” Maudrin smiles as if you have passed a test. “Tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded. Lie to me and I'll know by morning, which would be a waste of both our evenings.”
plays.response: She wants a place, not a promise, and the truth costs whoever holds it. On Venn's Gilded Heron or gone through the Seam: the Court seizes Venn's cargo at the Landing House, and Venn learns who told. Telling her earns the pension and exemption, and the favor. If the Heart is with Ila, play s04-tell-where-ila.
plays.consequence: The party owes Maudrin a favor, and whoever holds the Heart is in danger.
plays.fallback: If they won't say, play s04-bargain-refuse.
plays.tells: The Heart is with Master Venn or beyond the Seam, and a player starts weighing the pension.
plays.rules: Deception against Maudrin's Insight (+4); anything the Court's records contradict fails automatically. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in on the ridge. If they named Venn, he treats them as enemies on their return to Pellmoor.
plays.keywords: tell, reveal, where is it, location, inform, maudrin, ila, venn, dawn order, armory, reward

plays.title: They take Maudrin's exemption for Ila
plays.why: Maudrin already holds Ossa's Heart (S3), so she bargains for the girl who heard it.
plays.readAloud: “I have the Heart. You were very sensible.” Maudrin turns her glass in her fingers. “The girl who heard it, though. Ila. My office has an order for her. I could lose it, and give her the same exemption I'd give you. For a favor.”
plays.response: This is the only bargain she has to offer. Ila is free or hidden, so Maudrin tears the arrest order in half in front of them. The party owes the favor. If they refuse, the order stands and Hushmen move on Ila within two days.
plays.consequence: Ila is safe from the Court's Tithe for now. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.fallback: If the party argues morality with her, she agrees with every word and keeps the order in her hand.
plays.tells: Players ask about Ila, or whether the arrest order can be withdrawn.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to add anything to the deal. Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in, and Maudrin reminds them who it was for. S28: Ila, untithed, grows up to keep the ledger and to ring the ferry-folk's bell.
plays.keywords: ila, exemption, arrest order, release, protect ila, maudrin, favor, bargain, child

plays.title: Ossa's Heart went back to the Mere
plays.why: The Heart is at the Ossa Belfry (S3), so there is nothing to bargain for, and Maudrin knows it.
plays.readAloud: “You put it back.” Maudrin says it gently, as if she were sorry for them. “Every glass in my palace hummed that night. I had them all wrapped in cloth.”
plays.response: Skip the bargain. She asks, with real curiosity, what the bell sounded like, and listens to the answer. She offers one smaller deal from Part 9: a Court pension in exchange for their silence about what they found under the Mere; accepting it means they owe her the favor. If Ossa was rung, she says the Court will 'revisit Pellmoor's quota in the spring', which means the collectors have withdrawn for now.
plays.consequence: No Heart changes hands. Maudrin has measured them.
plays.fallback: If the table wants a fight with her, she introduces them to Isolde and leaves.
plays.tells: Maudrin greets them without asking for anything.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 if they want anything else from her. Insight DC 15: she is relieved the Heart is not in the city.
plays.later: S23: a favor is owed only if they took the pension. Act V: Ossa's resonance persists for the Concord whatever the Court does to Pellmoor.
plays.keywords: returned, belfry, mere, ossa rung, no heart, assembly, pension, silence, maudrin

plays.title: They find Brother Eld among the guests
plays.why: An exposed or forgiven Eld came to Hallowmere and serves as a Court chaplain at the masque.
plays.readAloud: A tall, round-shouldered man in chaplain's grey stands by the punch with his mask slightly crooked. Ink still on his fingers. He sees you, and his face does the sad thing it was trained to do.
plays.response: If Eld fled in disgrace, he will not meet their eyes; cornered behind a pillar, he begs them not to tell anyone what he did, and buys their silence with the name of the Court's new Pellmoor informer, a ferry-boy called Coll who owes the Landing House money. If they forgave him, he meets their eyes and slips a folded hymn-sheet into a pocket as he passes: 'Your names came up the river in Quill's report. Ser Haldric carried it to the palace, not to the Order.'
plays.consequence: The party has an informant (forgiven) or a frightened man who owes them his secret (fled).
plays.fallback: If they ignore him, a forgiven Eld finds them at the door with the same note; a disgraced one avoids them all night.
plays.tells: A player scans the room for familiar faces, or asks who the chaplain is.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15: Friendly if forgiven, Hostile with fear if exposed. Intimidation works on a frightened Eld and sends him running to Haldric.
plays.later: S6: Eld's note is a corroborating witness that Haldric serves the palace, though not proof of payment. S28: Eld confesses publicly, dies in the Mere, or leaves forever, following how they treat him now.
plays.keywords: eld, brother eld, chaplain, priest, informant, ledger page, pellmoor, mask, note, haldric

plays.title: They threaten Maudrin at the masque
plays.why: A frustrated or bold player decides the villain is right there and lightly guarded.
plays.readAloud: She laughs, softly, delighted. “Oh, you're adorable. Haldric, please see to our guests.”
plays.response: Ser Haldric Mose arrives with four palace guards: a Dawn Order knight answering the Chancellor's call is the surprise. Maudrin says 'Haldric, please see to our guests' and, as he passes, touches his sleeve: 'my boy', and then 'Ser'. He asks them to leave, courteously, twice. If they fight, use Haldric's Escort; Maudrin leaves by a side door and casts only if someone casts at her (Counterspell). Nobody dies at the masque: guests scream, guards grapple, and anyone dropped wakes in Vaer's Belfry.
plays.consequence: The party is a named enemy, and they have seen Haldric take the Chancellor's orders.
plays.fallback: If it starts to go badly, Isolde steps between them with a fresh glass and a joke, and the guards take the hint.
plays.tells: Hands on hilts, a raised voice, a spell component in a fist.
plays.rules: Haldric's silence-stone shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day. Maudrin: Counterspell (3/day). Grappled, Prone. A knock-out is the default for every Court combatant.
plays.later: S6: 'Who called you to the masque, Ser Haldric?' is a fair question on the Dawn Steps, though not proof of payment. S6: Rook says Haldric came to the Order at twelve with a palace letter. S23: Maudrin remembers this evening when she makes her offer on the ridge.
plays.keywords: threaten, attack maudrin, kill, assassinate, fight, masque, haldric, guards, violence, intimidate

plays.title: They mention a key that can ring the Seventh
plays.why: Players who picked up rumours from Eld's papers, a Mere Memory or a Bellwright may test Maudrin with it.
plays.readAloud: Her face goes still for half a second, the way the Mere goes still. Then she says, quite pleasantly, “I have no idea what you mean,” and turns to thank the musicians.
plays.response: The Assembly ends early: the music stops, Hushmen open the doors, and guests are thanked for coming. Maudrin does not look at the party again tonight. By the time they reach their lodgings, two Hushmen stand at the door and their Tithe records are flagged.
plays.consequence: The party is the Court's enemy.
plays.fallback: If nobody pushes further, Isolde catches them on the stairs and says, 'Whatever you said, say it to me next time.'
plays.tells: A player asks about 'the Key' or 'the Seventh Bell' by name.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 catches the half-second: she was afraid, not angry.
plays.later: S8: her last word mentions the Key outright; she has stopped pretending. S13: the Sexton will tell them what she was afraid of. Part 9, Situation 4: the Key stays in her palace vault until she leaves Hallowmere.
plays.keywords: key, tuning key, seventh bell, ysh, mention, reveal, accuse, maudrin, secret

plays.title: They read Maudrin with Insight, Detect Thoughts or Zone of Truth
plays.why: She is the antagonist, and casters reach for mind magic the moment she speaks.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums behind your teeth. Across the table Maudrin's eyes flick to you, then to your lips, and she smiles as though you had complimented her dress.
plays.response: Every spell in Corvane hums as it is cast, and Maudrin hears it. Detect Thoughts on her surface mind gives: 'Four of them. Ossa's. Not yet.' If the caster probes deeper she saves at +4; on a failure the caster sees a grey case on a chain, hears a lullaby, and feels her fear, and either way she knows, says “That was rude,” and ends the conversation. Zone of Truth fails near her chair: two silence-stones sit in the plinths of the dais, and the dimmed light shows the boundary before anyone casts. Insight DC 15 without magic tells them she means every promise and is leaving something out.
plays.consequence: They know she fears something she carries. She knows they read people.
plays.fallback: If no one has the spell, Insight alone gives the same last sentence.
plays.tells: A player asks “Is she lying?” or quietly names a spell.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts (2nd level; Maudrin's Wisdom save +4). Silence-stone field, 10 feet (Part 2.6 house rule). Insight DC 15. Maudrin's Counterspell is an NPC ability. See any-l3-truth-and-minds for the campaign-wide ruling.
plays.later: S22: the grey case and the lullaby make sense. S23: her first Counterspell goes to whoever cast Detect Thoughts on her tonight.
plays.keywords: detect thoughts, zone of truth, insight, read her, mind, lie, spell, probe, truth, silence-stone, dais

plays.title: Cole arrests Aurelie at the gate
plays.why: The smuggling failed, or she sang where she was told not to.
plays.readAloud: Cole turns Aurelie's papers over, then her face. 'No Charter, no writ, no dawn. Take her to the Belfry.'
plays.response: Aurelie is held in Vaer's Belfry as a Charter-breaker, unharmed. The Court offers to trade her for something the party has. Rook hears of it by evening and visits the cell; she will let Aurelie go if the party asks and gives her a reason (Influence DC 15, Rook Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent).
plays.consequence: Aurelie is under arrest. The Court has a bargaining chip.
plays.fallback: If nobody acts, a Mission acolyte sends a letter for the party's first friend.
plays.tells: The gate check fails, or Aurelie hums a dawn-hymn within earshot of a Hushman.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Rook. Aurelie can be broken out with the same methods as Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa) and s09-free-aurelie.
plays.later: S9: s09-free-aurelie frees her. Rook can ask for her release in S6.
plays.keywords: aurelie arrested, gate, belfry, charter-breaker, dawn mission

plays.title: They evacuate the Old Shore
plays.why: Fighting a Court siege is hard, and ferry-folk have boats.
plays.readAloud: Forty skiffs go out under the grey dawn, the ferry-folk poling across the drowned roofs with their children in the bows. Behind them the Old Shore stands empty and every door is open.
plays.response: Brannagh's pilots take the Old Shore across the Mere in two nights. The Hushmen find an empty village and a notice nailed to the chapel door: 'Search it.' Quill leaves a guard and burns nothing. The ferry-folk will remember who led them.
plays.consequence: The Old Shore is empty and unharmed.
plays.fallback: If the plan stalls, Sallow insists on being the last off.
plays.tells: The party asks Brannagh Wick how many boats she can find.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 16 past the cordon. Brannagh's help is automatic if Ila vouches.
plays.later: S22: the ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day. S28: who keeps the ledger now depends on who came back.
plays.keywords: evacuate, escape, ferry-folk, boats, old shore, siege end

plays.title: They hold the Old Shore against the siege
plays.why: A protective party will not hand over the village.
plays.readAloud: Quill reads the deadline twice. When he reaches the end the ferry-folk are still standing in the lane, saying nothing, and none of them are afraid.
plays.response: After the siege patrol, Quill accepts a parley: one memory 'for the quota' from a volunteer, and he withdraws for a week. The Court remembers. The Old Shore is changed: windows boarded, the chapel door nailed shut.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor stood, and is changed by it.
plays.fallback: If the party loses, Brannagh's pilots take the wounded across the Mere by night.
plays.tells: The party barricades the lanes or fights the patrol.
plays.rules: Encounter: Siege patrol (enc-s04-siege-patrol). Influence DC 15 on Quill for the parley.
plays.later: S9: Hushmen watch the Mere road. S22: defended ferry-folk keep Court ships on the Mere for a day.
plays.keywords: defend, siege, hold the line, old shore, quill parley

plays.title: They tell Maudrin where Ila hides the Heart
plays.why: The party no longer carries the Heart, and the pension is real.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin does not smile. 'Thank you. That is exactly what I needed, and I will not forget who said it.'
plays.response: Hushmen ride for Pellmoor within a day. Check session-zero Off-limits: Ila is taken Off-screen, never harmed. The Court cart is two days behind, so there is no way to beat it except a courier boat tonight (Brannagh's fast pilot-skiff, 5 gp; play s04-warn-ila). Telling her earns the pension, the exemption and the favor.
plays.consequence: The party owes Maudrin a favor, and Ila is under arrest unless they warn her.
plays.fallback: If they won't say, play s04-bargain-refuse.
plays.tells: The Heart is with Ila, and a player weighs the pension against the girl.
plays.rules: Deception against Maudrin's Insight (+4) if they lie; the Court's records contradict a lie.
plays.later: S6: Ila is in the dormitory with Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa-with-ila). S23: the favor is called in on the ridge.
plays.keywords: tell maudrin, betray ila, location, informer

plays.title: A pilot-skiff reaches Pellmoor first
plays.why: The party sent word ahead after naming Ila.
plays.readAloud: The skiff slides in under the drowned spire at midnight. Ila is already on the dock with her coat on. 'Brannagh said you'd send,' she says.
plays.response: Ila is hidden at the Pilots' Hall before the Hushmen arrive. They find the Harrow house empty and Quill furious. The Heart is wherever Ila keeps it.
plays.consequence: Ila is hidden and safe.
plays.fallback: If the courier is late, the Hushmen arrive and Ila hides with the households.
plays.tells: A player asks Brannagh Wick for the fastest boat on the Mere.
plays.rules: No check if the courier leaves tonight; DC 14 Survival to read the Mere in the dark.
plays.later: S6: no Ila in the dormitory. S28: Ila learns who told and who warned.
plays.keywords: warn ila, courier, skiff, brannagh, hide

plays.title: They take Maudrin's offer to release Ila
plays.why: Ila is in the Hall of Tithes and the Chancellor holds the key.
plays.readAloud: 'The girl is well,' Maudrin says. 'She has not been harmed, and she will not be. She can go back to her river. For a favor.'
plays.response: Maudrin offers Ila's release to Pellmoor with the same exemption she would give the party. A Hushman escort takes her to the ferry-stair at dawn. The party owes the favor. If they refuse, the order stands and Ila stays in the Hall of Tithes (rescue alongside Tessa).
plays.consequence: Ila is free in Pellmoor. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.fallback: If the party argues morality with her, she agrees with every word and keeps the order in her hand.
plays.tells: The party asks where Ila is, or whether the arrest can be withdrawn.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to add anything to the deal (Maudrin's Intelligence). Record in the Bargain Log: one favor owed.
plays.later: S23: the favor is called in, and Maudrin reminds them who it was for. S28: Ila, untithed, grows up to keep the ledger and to ring the ferry-folk's bell.
plays.keywords: release ila, exemption, favor, hall of tithes

plays.title: They ask Maudrin to give Ossa's Heart back
plays.why: The Court holds the Heart and the party needs it for the Concord.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin looks at her glove, then at you. 'Take it. It hums when it is near me, and Quill's reports say it does not hum in the dark. I would rather know where it is.'
plays.response: She returns it for the favor and the silence she asked for. She wants the party to gather the Hearts for her to take at the Strike; she does not say so. Accepting makes her an owed favor. Refusing leaves the Heart in the Hall of Tithes (s05-take-ossa-from-vault is the theft).
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is with the party. The party owes Maudrin a favor.
plays.fallback: If they refuse, she says 'Then it stays where it is safe', and means it.
plays.tells: A player says 'we want it back', or asks Maudrin what the Court plans to do with it.
plays.rules: Influence DC 17 to haggle (Maudrin's Intelligence); Insight DC 15 catches that she is relieved to have it out of the vault.
plays.later: S9: they can ring Ossa after the detour (s09-ring-ossa-later). S23: Maudrin calls the favor and wants every Heart they carry.
plays.keywords: ossa back, return heart, favor, bargain, court vault

plays.title: They charm, disguise or put the gate to sleep
plays.why: Level-3 casters have Charm Person, Disguise Self, Sleep and Hold Person, and the gate is a short, dull scene.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and Cole turns toward the sound before he stops turning. 'Interesting,' he says. 'You'll be wanting to explain that.'
plays.response: Charm Person on Cole works (Wisdom save), but he knows he was charmed when it ends and reports it at the Gate Office. Sleep puts the Gate Hushmen down but not the lamplit lanes beyond: someone will find them within the hour. Disguise Self gets past a clerk but not a Reckoner's tuning fork (Investigation DC 15 to see through it). The Blank clerk cannot be charmed: nothing is there to hold.
plays.consequence: The gate is passed, and the Court's record has a flag on the caster.
plays.fallback: If the spell fails, Cole calls the Gate Hushmen (enc-s04-gate-hushmen).
plays.tells: A caster asks whether Cole or the Blank clerk can be charmed, or whether the Hushmen can be slept.
plays.rules: Charm Person: Wisdom save; target knows afterward. Sleep: HP pool; works on Hushmen. Disguise Self: Investigation DC 15 to see through. Every spell hums within 30 feet, so Cole hears the cast.
plays.later: S9: Cole is on the north gate and remembers the caster. Court clock +1 if a spell was used.
plays.keywords: charm person, sleep, disguise self, gate, cole, hold person

plays.title: They skip the Assembly and go straight to Rook or the Bellwrights
plays.why: Some tables know the Court is the enemy and want allies first.
plays.readAloud: The Dawn Order's barracks is a long grey building with a yellow door painted over twice. Rook looks up from a map of the Terraces and says, 'You're early. I haven't decided whether I like that.'
plays.response: Rook opens her commission early (S6, Scene 1) and offers a Dawn Order writ for one day. The Bellwrights send Wren Caddock, sewing on a bench outside the Archive, with a friendly question. Maudrin sends a grey rose without a note and two Hushmen follow the party. If the party holds the Heart, Rook asks what they intend; she will trade a seat at the armory for it.
plays.consequence: No favor to Maudrin is owed. The Court watches.
plays.fallback: If they wander, Lysse Carrow drops a bone-bound book at their feet.
plays.tells: A player asks where the Dawn Order sits, or whether the Bellwrights have a safe house.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 to shake the Hushmen for a day. Influence DC 15 on Rook (Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent).
plays.later: S6: Rook's commission opens early. S23: with no favor owed, Maudrin runs the Strike normally.
plays.keywords: rook, bellwrights, skip assembly, barracks, dawn order, wren

plays.title: They pay the Librarian for the diary's label
plays.why: The Librarian offers the answer outright for one true memory, and Edda's diary is the Act's prize.
plays.readAloud: The pages show your own face, then fill with handwriting that is almost yours: “You have asked a question with a memory behind it. Edda Thorne's diary is not on any shelf of this archive. Ask me the label, and I will tell you it, for one true memory.”
plays.response: The price is a memory the player is willing to give; the player names it and writes it in the ledger as a trade with the Librarian (not a Toll, not a Tithe, never redeemable). Never from an absent player's character. The answer is true: MIREL, LOST. Each further question costs another memory and gets a true but partial answer. If nobody will pay, the clue is not lost: Lysse cross-checks the Archive's accession lists and finds a Court receipt for 'one diary, relabelled'.
plays.consequence: They know what to look for in the vault: a cloth-wrapped book labelled MIREL, LOST.
plays.fallback: If the table stalls on the price, Lysse offers to pay it herself, and does; she has very little left to lose, and that should sting.
plays.tells: A player opens the wordless book, or asks Lysse where to look.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 for Lysse's shortcut in an hour; on a failure she finds it by morning. Record Librarian trades as their own kind in the ledger.
plays.later: S5: they find the diary in a minute once inside. S22: if every other source is gone, the Librarian reads the Quiet Night page aloud for one true memory.
plays.keywords: librarian, sealed book, sealed stacks, question, label, diary, edda, mirel lost, memory, price, lysse

plays.title: They bargain for Mirel's Heart
plays.why: The Librarian holds Mirel's Heart and will trade it now, which saves the courier's bargain at Vael Tor.
plays.readAloud: A page turns by itself. “I keep the dream-bell's heart because it belongs to whoever read it last. Give me a dream you have never told anyone, and you will be the last.”
plays.response: The price is a dream the giver has never told anyone; it is gone for good, and the player tells you (privately if they like) what it was. Never from an absent player's character. If they refuse the dream, the Librarian accepts a Gift instead (Part 2.7): something the giver values, given freely and never returned. The Heart is a honey-coloured bronze clapper the length of a forearm, warm, and anyone who holds it yawns.
plays.consequence: The party carries Mirel's Heart.
plays.fallback: If they refuse both prices, tell them plainly that the courier will repeat the offer at Vael Tor.
plays.tells: A player asks what else the Librarian keeps, or whether it would trade for a Heart.
plays.rules: Record the dream as a Librarian trade, or the Gift as a Gift. Neither is Mirel's Toll: a Fear for one day is still owed when Mirel rings.
plays.later: S16B or S20: they can ring Mirel as soon as they reach the Sleeping Hall, and the Librarian's courier never comes. S9: a cart search at the north gate is now a real danger. S23: Maudrin wants every Heart they carry.
plays.keywords: mirel, heart, dream, librarian, trade, gift, bargain, dream bell, sleeping hall, buy

plays.title: They steal Mirel's Heart from the Sealed Stacks
plays.why: A dream nobody has told is a steep price, and rogues like a reading stand with nothing guarding it.
plays.readAloud: The Heart rests on a reading stand between two shelves, under a page that has written, very small: 'Do not.'
plays.response: Lifting it unseen is DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth) to reach the stand, or DC 16 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools to free it from the stand's clasp. Success: they have it, and the Librarian writes 'Then you are the last who read me' and closes; it answers no more questions this visit. Failure: the book slams, every warm spine in the Archive goes cold, and the Librarian fights only if someone keeps grabbing (The Librarian). The reading-room keepers fetch Hushmen in ten minutes, not three rounds.
plays.consequence: On a success the party holds Mirel's Heart and the Librarian is cold to them; on a failure the Heart stays.
plays.fallback: If they fail and flee, Lysse covers for them with the keepers, and asks what on earth they were thinking.
plays.tells: A player asks where exactly the Heart sits, or whether the book can see.
plays.rules: Stealth or Thieves' Tools DC 16. The Stacks are not silence-stone: spells work, but hum loudly in the quiet, and the Librarian hears them.
plays.later: S16B: if the theft failed, the courier still comes with the same offer. S22: even a cold Librarian keeps its word and reads the Quiet Night page for one true memory.
plays.keywords: steal, mirel, heart, sealed stacks, sleight of hand, stealth, thieves tools, grab, librarian, snatch

plays.title: They bribe Ansel Quay for the vault door
plays.why: Ansel holds the key, wants to retire to the coast, and is obviously nervous: the easiest door in the book.
plays.readAloud: Ansel takes off the spectacles he doesn't need and polishes them. “I don't know what you mean,” he whispers. “And if I did, the service passage is unlocked between the second and third lamp-lightings. Hypothetically.”
plays.response: Ansel wants enough to retire to the coast, and the coast takes gold: 50 gp, or a Gift (something they value, freely given), or a believable promise of safety, meaning getting him and his cat out of the city when this is over. He opens the door, waits outside with his back turned, and gives them a quarter of an hour. For another 25 gp he sells the copy of the Tithe-Ledger he has been making for the Bellwrights; taking the copy sets off nothing. If anyone threatens him, he agrees to everything and tells Wren Caddock that night.
plays.consequence: The party is in the vault without a roll, and may hold Ansel's copy of the Ledger.
plays.fallback: If they can't afford him, he accepts a promise in writing, which he will hold them to.
plays.tells: Players ask who has the key, or Lysse mentions 'the steward who never needs his spectacles'.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Ansel starts Indifferent; a Gift or a safety promise makes him Friendly). Intimidation works and costs Wren's trust.
plays.later: S6: Ansel's copy contains the armory-payment entry that can win Rook's hearing, and Wren already knows who the party is when she approaches. Act IV (Part 9, Situation 4): Ansel knows Maudrin's routes from the palace to the Tor.
plays.keywords: ansel, quay, bribe, steward, archivist, key, vault, service passage, copy, ledger, gold, pay

plays.title: They break into the vault with tools or spells
plays.why: Lockpicks and Knock are the first tools most parties reach for.
plays.readAloud: The vault door is grey stone banded in iron. Ten feet out, the lamplight dims and there is a pressure in your ears like diving. Whatever hums behind your teeth goes quiet.
plays.response: The lock is DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools; a failure costs a minute. A Hushman passes every ten minutes (DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) to wait in shadow). Fixed silence-stones in the frame and walls cover the door and the whole room: Knock fails, Invisibility and Pass without Trace are suppressed inside (they resume outside if concentration holds). Prying a frame stone loose (AC 12, 10 HP) ends the field at the door, but stone cracking on stone sets off the alarm.
plays.consequence: They are in, and no Tonework works anywhere in the vault.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, Ansel comes out of the service passage with a lamp and a very guilty look.
plays.tells: A player asks about the lock, guards, or whether Knock or Invisibility will work.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17. Stealth DC 15. Silence-stone house rule (Part 2.6): no spell can be cast in the field or produce an effect inside it. A fixed stone: AC 12, 10 HP. Misty Step cast from outside lands you at the edge of the field, not inside; Disguise Self and Invisibility drop at the threshold. Dispel Magic (an NPC's, or Aurelie's) cannot target a stone because it is not a spell.
plays.later: S7: Ilam Bray's service-passage key makes a second visit easy. Act IV (Situation 21): coming back for anything left on these shelves means this door again, with the Tithe Clock running.
plays.keywords: break in, lockpick, pick lock, thieves tools, knock, invisibility, pass without trace, dispel magic, silence-stone, vault door, sneak

plays.title: They open a memory jar of their own
plays.why: A character who grew up under the Court has a childhood jar with their name on it; others have the S4 courtesy jar.
plays.readAloud: The jar has a name on it in a clerk's tidy hand. It is warm. When you lift the stopper, the vault fills with a smell you had forgotten you knew.
plays.response: Ask the player first whether their character grew up under the Court. If so, their earliest-memory jar is here: describe it from the character's earliest years and ask the player to add one detail; it is theirs again. Offer a clue as a question, not a fact: the clerk who drew it wore a Hushman's grey glove, and the date is a Tithe-raid year. Ask whether the character's family ever spoke of it. Never invent a backstory loss without the player. A Stormborn character, or one who arrived this week, has no childhood jar: they have only the S4 courtesy jar, which opens the same way. Ansel's office tallies the jars each morning, so the empty one tells the Court who has been in.
plays.consequence: The memory is restored. The Court knows they opened it.
plays.fallback: If no player wants to, one jar hums louder until someone looks.
plays.tells: A player searches the shelves for their name.
plays.rules: Opening one's own jar restores the memory (Tithe, redeemable). Opening another person's jar only witnesses it and fades it; after three strangers it is spent. The S4 courtesy jar is on the newest shelf.
plays.later: S9: the Hallowmere Ledger asks what was in it. S24: Maudrin uses it: 'I gave you that back, you know. I could have broken it.'
plays.keywords: jar, own jar, my name, memory, open, earliest memory, restore, tithe, courtesy jar

plays.title: They take Edda Thorne's diary
plays.why: Lysse asked for it, the Librarian pointed to it, and it is the true account of the Quiet Night.
plays.readAloud: “The seventh is not a bell. It is a lullaby with a voice, and the note beneath the note is the sound of something dreaming. Imber came to the Tower tonight with the Key, meaning to tune the seven into one long spring.”
plays.response: The diary is cloth-wrapped on the MIREL, LOST shelf: one minute to find if they know the label, ten minutes of searching if not, never missed. Read the full Quiet Night entry aloud (S5 box). Tell them plainly what else it holds, as the reveal-early rule requires: its later pages say six restored bells, each in its own voice, could hold the lullaby steady without waking anything. Taking it sets off no alarm; the Court knows it has gone by morning. If they would rather not risk it, they can read it and leave it: set the diary to 'Read and left behind', and the Court never learns.
plays.consequence: The party holds the true account of the Quiet Night and the first hint of the Concord.
plays.fallback: If they can't read bell-script or old Hesk, Lysse can; give her the moment.
plays.tells: A player asks for the shelf marked MIREL, LOST.
plays.rules: Search, Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 if they don't know the label; a failure only costs time.
plays.later: S13: the Sexton's confession matches it line for line, and he weeps to hear Edda's words. S22: it is a source for the truth of the Key. S24: Maudrin knows they have read what she read.
plays.keywords: diary, edda thorne, mirel lost, quiet night, read, take, steal, book, imber, lullaby, key

plays.title: They take Calla's Heart from HARVEST, WITHHELD
plays.why: It is right there, warm, smelling of bread, and it is the only way to ring the Old Granary.
plays.readAloud: The moment the weight leaves the shelf, somewhere above you a bell-pull jerks, and a handbell with felt wrapped round its clapper starts thudding against its frame. Thud. Thud. Thud.
plays.response: The alarm is mechanical, not Tonework, so it works inside the silence-stone: the shelf is weighted, and any lift pulls the bell. A clever swap (an equal weight, DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) delays it by ten minutes instead of three rounds, but it still sounds. Hushmen arrive in three rounds (Vault Alarm), so the party should be moving by round two. For the next two days, four Hushmen search every cart leaving the city.
plays.consequence: The party carries Calla's Heart and the Court is hunting it.
plays.fallback: If they freeze when the alarm sounds, Ansel's voice from the service passage hisses, “This way. Now.”
plays.tells: A player unwraps the cloth on the HARVEST, WITHHELD shelf.
plays.rules: Alarm: Hushmen in 3 rounds. Sleight of Hand DC 15 for a weight-swap (delay, not prevention). Searching the shelf first shows the bell-pull without a roll.
plays.later: S9: Calla can be rung at Kell's Crossing, three days north; Bet Ostrow is the natural Gift. S9: cart searches at the gate for two days. S15: Isolde asks for Calla's Heart too. S23: Maudrin wants every Heart they carry.
plays.keywords: calla, heart, harvest withheld, take, steal, alarm, shelf, bread, granary, kell's crossing

plays.title: They take the Tithe-Ledger or Ansel's copy
plays.why: Rook wants it, and the master book of who gave what is the strongest evidence in the city.
plays.readAloud: The Ledger is as thick as a doorstep, chained to its stand with a plain iron chain. The newest pages are still damp at the edges.
plays.response: Lifting the original pulls the same alarm as Calla's Heart. Ansel's copy (sold for 25 gp) sets off nothing and is just as good as evidence. Finding one entry takes ten minutes without a roll. Worth finding: Ser Haldric's armory payments ('for H.V., at the Chancellor's pleasure: three heartkeeps, quarterly'); Mara Bray, Tithed of 'her son', 408 SS; Lysse Carrow, twice, under other people's names; Lady Isolde Drave, selling twelve heartkeeps to I.C. (the Ironhorn Compact) in 411 SS and never recording the gap; each party member's jars.
plays.consequence: The party holds the evidence that can break Haldric, and a map of whose memories are where.
plays.fallback: If they skip it, Ansel's copy can still reach Rook through Wren before the hearing, for a price.
plays.tells: A player goes to the reading stand, or asks Ansel about copies.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 finds an entry in a minute; otherwise ten minutes, no roll. Taking the original: alarm, Hushmen in 3 rounds, cart searches for two days.
plays.later: S6: the armory-payment entry wins Rook's hearing, and 'H.V.' is a question for later. S7: Mara Bray's entry says Jonah's mother is alive and a Blank. S8: the Ironhorn entry is a lever on Isolde (s08-turn-isolde). S9: with Ilam's roster as well, they can name every Hushman at the north gate.
plays.keywords: ledger, tithe-ledger, book, copy, evidence, haldric, payment, entry, records, names, steal, ansel

plays.title: They find the EXPORT — VENNMARK column
plays.why: Anyone reading the Ledger closely, or a Stormborn who reads Common, will notice a column in the wrong language.
plays.readAloud: The last column on each page is narrower than the rest and ruled in newer ink. Its heading is in Common, not Hesk: EXPORT — VENNMARK. Beside some names, a tick and a ship: Gilded Heron. Saltglass. Gilded Heron again.
plays.response: The Court sells 'surplus' Tithed memories to Master Orsolo Venn's coster, and they are shipped through the Seam to Athkatla: heartkeeps, mostly, the red-wax weights. Blanks' memories may be sitting in an Amnian noble's cabinet right now. Reckoner Sela Maunt in Pellmoor could confirm the weights from the stamps, and Venn's own counting-house ledgers would prove the trade.
plays.consequence: The memory trade is not only the Court's crime. The party has a reason to go back to Pellmoor.
plays.fallback: If nobody notices, Lysse does, and asks what 'Vennmark' means.
plays.tells: A player asks where the Tithed memories go, or reads the Ledger page by page.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 12 to notice it if nobody asks about exports; a character who reads Common notices it without a roll.
plays.later: S7: telling the Blanks is a spark. S9: a detour to Pellmoor can confront Venn (Venn hostile, Landing clock moves). S22: exposing the trade to the Harpers or the Dawn Mission earns the Stormborn ally. Act V: in the Empty Choir, the export trade grows.
plays.keywords: export, vennmark, venn, coster, athkatla, amn, ship, gilded heron, column, trade, smuggle, heartkeeps, faerun

plays.title: They take other people's memory jars
plays.why: Players who care about Bet, Lysse or the Blanks will want their memories back.
plays.readAloud: The shelves go on further than the lamp reaches. OSTROW, B. 340 SS. BRAY, M. 408 SS. Each jar hums a different note, like a choir that has lost its place.
plays.response: Jars are not weighted like the Calla shelf; a few can leave in a satchel without the alarm, and Ansel's morning tally finds the gaps. Only the owner can restore a memory: Bet must open her own jar to remember ringing Calla at nine, and Mara Bray hers to know her son. Mother Sallow's jar, her wedding day (SALLOW, M.), is here too: she has been losing her husband ever since, and opening it herself would give her Davin back. Anyone else who opens a jar only witnesses it and fades it, and a dropped jar scatters the memory for good. Lysse's two jars are filed under other names (MORROW, T. and HADE, E.); Study DC 17 matches her hand in the 'reason given' column.
plays.consequence: The party carries other people's memories, and the responsibility that comes with them.
plays.fallback: If they hesitate over whose jars to take, Lysse asks quietly whether hers are here.
plays.tells: A player searches for a friend's name rather than their own.
plays.rules: Witnessing another's jar fades it (three times and it is spent). Destroying a jar scatters the memory; it does not restore it. Study DC 17 for Lysse's jars.
plays.later: S6: Bet, given her jar, remembers the Last Ringing and asks to ring Calla again (S9). S7: Mara opening her jar lets her know Jonah. S28: Mother Sallow opens her wedding-day jar at the Memory Shore. S30: Lysse recovers her memories and writes the true history.
plays.keywords: jars, other people, bet, ostrow, mara bray, lysse, steal jars, free memories, blanks, return

plays.title: They set off the alarm without taking anything
plays.why: A careless lift, a cracked stone or a dropped jar is easy in a dim room.
plays.readAloud: Thud. Thud. Thud. Above you, boots on stone, and someone shouting for lamps.
plays.response: Hushmen arrive in three rounds (Vault Alarm). They want arrests and an intact vault; they block the doors rather than fight among the jars. The party can surrender, fight out through the service passage, or bluff that Ansel let them in (DC 15 Charisma (Deception); Ansel will not thank them). Nothing is missing, so nobody searches carts afterward, but the Court knows faces were in its vault.
plays.consequence: The Court tightens its watch on the vault; the party may be identified.
plays.fallback: If capture looks certain, Ansel throws the service-passage bolt from the far side and pretends he never did.
plays.tells: A failed check near the Calla shelf, the reading stand, or a frame stone.
plays.rules: Hushmen in 3 rounds. Deception DC 15. Grappled. Tonework fails inside the vault, so casters must fight their way to the door first.
plays.later: S6: Haldric uses the break-in to argue on the Dawn Steps that Rook's 'evidence' is stolen. S7: Ilam's key still opens the service passage if they need another try.
plays.keywords: alarm, caught, hushmen, fight, escape, surrender, bluff, vault, service passage, trapped

plays.title: They take Ossa's Heart from the vault
plays.why: The Court holds Ossa's Heart in the Tithe-Ledger Room, and the party needs it back for the Concord.
plays.readAloud: The Heart lies on a shelf marked SURRENDERED, BELL-WORK. It is cold. When you close your hand on it, it hums once, as if it knew your voice from the Mere.
plays.response: The shelf is weighted like Calla's: lifting it pulls the bell-pull (Hushmen in three rounds). A weight-swap (DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) delays it ten minutes. Four Hushmen search every cart for two days afterward. Ansel will not talk about it.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is with the party and the Court is hunting it.
plays.fallback: If they freeze when the alarm sounds, Ansel hisses 'This way. Now.'
plays.tells: A player asks what the sealed shelf behind the Ledger holds, or reads the siege orders ('Ossa relic to the Tithe-Ledger Room').
plays.rules: Alarm: Hushmen in 3 rounds. Sleight of Hand DC 17 for a weight-swap. A Heart in a silence-stone-lined box doesn't hum.
plays.later: S9: cart searches at the north gate (s09-smuggle-out). S9: ring Ossa after a detour (s09-ring-ossa-later). S23: Maudrin wants every Heart they carry.
plays.keywords: ossa vault, steal heart, tithe-ledger room, court holds ossa

plays.title: They go in as clerks, or bring Lysse
plays.why: Disguises and a friend on the inside are the oldest vault plan.
plays.readAloud: The clerk's apron is two sizes too big and smells of damp paper. Lysse straightens your collar. 'Walk like you're late,' she says. 'Nobody looks at late people.'
plays.response: Lysse can walk a party into the vault as a clerical squad. Mundane disguises (aprons, a Disguise Kit) work; Disguise Self drops at the threshold because the field suppresses it. Misty Step through a wall is stopped at the edge of the field. Ansel's morning tally still shows the gap. Lysse is old and breathes badly in the cold; she stays at the door.
plays.consequence: The party is inside without a fight, and Lysse knows what they take.
plays.fallback: If the disguise fails, Ansel comes out of the service passage and takes them to the kitchens.
plays.tells: A player asks about grey aprons, or whether Lysse could walk them in.
plays.rules: Disguise Kit: Charisma (Deception) DC 15 per character; Lysse gives Advantage. Disguise Self, Invisibility and Misty Step are suppressed inside the field.
plays.later: S6: Lysse tells Rook what she saw. S9: Lysse can meet them at the gate.
plays.keywords: disguise, clerks, lysse, aprons, misty step, disguise self, invisible

plays.title: They kill Ansel Quay
plays.why: Ansel is the only man who can sound the alarm, and a threatened party might silence him.
plays.readAloud: Ansel's spectacles fall and he does not pick them up. 'I wanted a cat and a coast,' he says. 'That is all I ever wanted.'
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' A downed Ansel can be bound; Wren Caddock will find out and take it hard. If he dies, the vault has no keeper, the Hushmen close it for a week, and Wren stops trusting the party. Ansel's Ledger copy and his knowledge of Maudrin's routes (Act IV) are gone. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Ansel is dead. The Court closes the vault.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Ansel agrees to everything and walks out.
plays.tells: A player corners Ansel in the service passage with a blade.
plays.rules: Ansel is a Commoner-grade clerk. Intimidation does not require death.
plays.later: S6: Wren breaks with the party. S7: Ilam's key still opens the service passage if the party goes back. Act IV: Maudrin's routes must come from somewhere else (Isolde, Edda's Notes).
plays.keywords: kill ansel, murder, vault steward

plays.title: They read the diary and leave it where it lies
plays.why: Taking it is a theft the Court will feel; reading it costs a few quiet hours.
plays.readAloud: You read by one stub of candle. When you close the cloth, the jar beside it is still humming the note it hummed when you came in.
plays.response: The diary stays on the shelf. The Court never learns. They have the Quiet Night entry and the hint of the Concord in memory only; a Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 search finds it. They cannot read it to Imber in S13 without the diary.
plays.consequence: The Court does not know the diary was read.
plays.fallback: If they change their minds, the diary is still on the shelf.
plays.tells: A player says 'we read it here' or worries about the Court noticing.
plays.rules: Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 if they do not know the label; a failure costs time only.
plays.later: S13: Imber weeps but the page is not in hand. S22: the Librarian reads the entry aloud for one true memory.
plays.keywords: read diary, leave diary, quiet night, edda thorne

plays.title: They take Captain Rook's commission
plays.why: Rook is honest, desperate and offers protection; she is the first authority in Hallowmere who asks rather than takes.
plays.readAloud: “I don't have time for pleasantries. The Court is rotten, and I'm not allowed to say so, because the men who could say it have been Tithed. So I'm asking you. Will you help me find out what's in the Tithe-Ledger? Not for the Court. For the people who've forgotten their own children.”
plays.response: Rook wants a copy of the Ledger or the original before the oath-hearing in two days. In return she gives one day of protection (a Dawn Order writ that Hushmen must honour until dusk) and an escort of two knights. She is honest and she is using them, and says so if asked. She mentions that Haldric came to the Order at twelve with a palace letter and no name but Mose. If they already hold the Ledger or Ansel's copy (S5), she reads the payment entries in silence and then says, 'We.'
plays.consequence: The party works for the Dawn Order's captain. Haldric knows by evening.
plays.fallback: If they won't commit, Rook says the hearing goes ahead regardless and they can watch her lose.
plays.tells: Players ask what she needs, what she offers, or whether she can be trusted.
plays.rules: Rook starts Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent. Influence DC 15 to keep the escort a second day.
plays.later: S6: the hearing turns on what they bring. S9: if Rook wins, she lends Vaer's Heart and the chain-key. S22: Rook and her knights are an ally only if she won.
plays.keywords: rook, dessa, captain, dawn order, commission, job, ledger, protection, escort, hire

plays.title: They present Haldric's payments at the oath-duel
plays.why: The party holds the Ledger, Ansel's copy or a witness, and the Dawn Steps are where it counts.
plays.readAloud: The Dawn Steps are crowded to the lamps. Rook and Haldric stand three steps apart in the grey light, swords laid sheathed at their feet. A herald calls for the first question from the crowd.
plays.response: Each knight swears 'I have not sold this Order's protection to the Court' and answers three questions chosen by the players. Rook admits small compromises and denies selling protection. Haldric denies payment smoothly until he is confronted with the armory-payment entry, Ansel's copy, or a corroborated witness (Eld's note plus the party's testimony counts as one). Shown the entry, he looks once toward the palace, then refuses to answer, and refusing loses: he is stripped of his sword and his knights step away from him. If Ossa's Heart is in the armory, Rook hands it back (s06-rook-returns-ossa).
plays.consequence: Rook wins. Haldric is disgraced; Rook holds the armory and Vaer's Heart.
plays.fallback: If the players fumble the questions, Rook asks the last one herself: 'Ser Haldric, what does the line for H. in this book mean?'
plays.tells: A player asks how the duel works, or rehearses their three questions.
plays.rules: Finding the entry: ten minutes, no roll; Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 to have it ready before the hearing starts. A failure means a recess or another witness, never lost evidence.
plays.later: S9: Rook opens Vaer's Belfry and gives them the chain-key, and the Dawn Order will not enforce a Silence Warrant. S22: Rook and her knights hold the ridge. S23: Haldric and both Dawn Order knights are absent from the Strike, leaving Maudrin and four Hushmen (a much smaller fight than the full Strike).
plays.keywords: oath-duel, duel, hearing, evidence, ledger, haldric, rook, dawn steps, questions, prove, payment, win

plays.title: The hearing goes ahead without proof
plays.why: The vault went badly or the party never went in, and Rook will not postpone.
plays.readAloud: Haldric answers every question beautifully, with a little bow to the crowd after each one. When it is over, he offers Rook his hand. She doesn't take it.
plays.response: Rook's accusation fails for now; Haldric keeps his office and is gracious about it, which is worse. Tell the players this door stays open: Dawn Order law allows a second hearing with new evidence within a month. Haldric now knows exactly who stood with Rook.
plays.consequence: Rook's case fails for now. Haldric holds the armory.
plays.fallback: Rook buys them a drink afterward and says, 'Get me the book. I'll call it again.'
plays.tells: The party arrives at the Steps empty-handed, or with only suspicion.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 on Haldric: relief, not confidence.
plays.later: S9: Rook can still be talked into a quiet loan of Vaer's Heart (s09-rook-loans-vaer, Influence DC 15), but the armory is Haldric's. If they bring the Ledger later in Act II, rerun the hearing and set the duel to 'Rook won'. S23: if it is never reopened, Haldric and his knights ride with Maudrin.
plays.keywords: no evidence, lose, fail, hearing, duel, haldric wins, rook loses, reopen, recess

plays.title: They support Ser Haldric
plays.why: Haldric is charming and offers alliance; a table that distrusts Rook, or wants Court favour, may take it.
plays.readAloud: Haldric catches you on the stair afterward, polishing a gauntlet that is already clean. “For the good of all, I'd be grateful for friends who see clearly. The dawn will come. It only needs the right hands.”
plays.response: With the party behind him, Haldric wins, and the Dawn Order accepts the Court's control of the city. Then he asks for one thing: Bellwright names. Only names the party actually gives are endangered; each one is a Hushman raid within three days. He keeps his promises exactly as long as no better offer arrives.
plays.consequence: Haldric wins the duel. Rook is humiliated. The Bellwrights learn who helped.
plays.fallback: If they waver, Haldric offers them the armory's 'safekeeping' of any Heart they carry, which is the Court's armory in all but name.
plays.tells: Players warm to Haldric's courtesy, or ask what he can offer them.
plays.rules: Haldric starts Friendly to allies. Record in the Bargain Log what he promised and what they gave.
plays.later: S9: the Dawn Order enforces any Silence Warrant and Vaer's Belfry is shut to them (s09-warrant-arrest). S18A: Corin Aldeth knows who gave names and is cold. S23: Haldric and two knights ride in the Strike at full strength; even so, if the party holds the Key there, Haldric hesitates, and that still breaks the line.
plays.keywords: support haldric, side with haldric, betray rook, alliance, bellwright names, informer, court favour

plays.title: They stay out of the duel
plays.why: It looks like Dawn Order business, and the party has its own goals.
plays.readAloud: By the evening lamps the news is everywhere: the Captain's accusation failed. By morning there are Hushmen at every door of the Archive.
plays.response: Rook's unsupported accusation fails. Court patrols tighten: Hushmen at the Archive doors and a checkpoint on the Hall of Tithes steps. Rook does not blame them aloud. She remembers.
plays.consequence: Rook's case fails for now and the city gets tighter.
plays.fallback: If the players want back in, Rook will reopen it the day they bring her the book.
plays.tells: “That's their fight.” Or the party is busy elsewhere on the day.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 (up from 13) to move unseen in the upper city for the rest of the Act.
plays.later: S7: the Hushmen line forms faster. S9: Rook might still help if asked (s09-rook-loans-vaer, Influence DC 15), but she has nothing else to give. S23: Haldric and his knights ride with Maudrin unless the case is reopened.
plays.keywords: stay out, ignore, not our business, skip duel, neutral, avoid

plays.title: They use Zone of Truth or Detect Thoughts on the knights
plays.why: Clerics and bards at level 3–4 have exactly the spells a lie-hearing seems to call for.
plays.readAloud: Two heralds in faded dawn-yellow stand at the top of the Steps holding grey stone rods. Around each knight the lamplight is a shade dimmer than it ought to be.
plays.response: An oath-court allows no Tonework: by Dawn Order law each knight stands in a herald's silence-stone field (10 feet), so Zone of Truth and Detect Thoughts on the knights fail, visibly, and casting at them is contempt (the caster's side loses one question). Off the Steps, magic works. Detect Thoughts on Haldric is negated by his silence-stone shield the first time each day; a second casting shows him thinking 'She won't let them break me. She promised.'
