Zone of Truth on a willing witness (Eld, Ansel or Wren) before the hearing counts: the herald accepts a witness who stood in a Zone as corroboration.
plays.consequence: Magic can find and support evidence. It never replaces it.
plays.fallback: If the caster feels cheated, let the herald say aloud why the rods exist: 'A knight's word is weighed by men, not tones.'
plays.tells: A player asks whether Zone of Truth is allowed, or casts it from the crowd.
plays.rules: Silence-stone field, 10 feet (house rule). Haldric's shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day; area spells are unaffected. Zone of Truth: Charisma save.
plays.later: S23: Haldric remembers who tried to read him, and keeps his shield raised toward that caster.
plays.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, spell, magic, lie, truth, oath, herald, rods, silence-stone, shield, read mind

plays.title: They attack Haldric on the Dawn Steps
plays.why: Haldric is smug, the party may know he's guilty, and the evidence isn't landing.
plays.readAloud: The herald drops his rod with a crack like a bell that cannot ring. “Order! Order on the Steps!” Haldric's knights close around him in a wall of grey steel.
plays.response: Violence at an oath-court voids the hearing: the herald calls it, Haldric's knights close ranks, and Rook roars at the party to stand down. If they keep going, use Dawn Steps Brawl. Haldric fights to disarm and arrest, then plays the wronged man perfectly to the crowd. Killing him is a separate choice (s06-kill-haldric).
plays.consequence: The hearing is void. The party is a named enemy, and Rook is furious.
plays.fallback: If it turns deadly, Rook steps in front of the party with her sword sheathed and her arms wide, and nobody on the Steps will strike her.
plays.tells: Weapons drawn in the crowd, or a spell readied at the herald.
plays.rules: Knights: Parry reaction. Haldric's shield negates the first spell that targets only him each day. Grappled, Prone.
plays.later: S9: Rook lends them nothing until they make amends (a public apology on the Steps, Influence DC 15). S23: Haldric and his knights ride with Maudrin.
plays.keywords: attack haldric, fight, kill haldric, brawl, violence, dawn steps, knights, duel fight

plays.title: They hear Wren's confession
plays.why: Wren chooses them in Bet's bakery; what they do with a spy who gave up Tam Harrow is a real choice.
plays.readAloud: “I'm sorry. I have to tell you something you won't like. I've been giving the Court names. Bellwright names, and one from Pellmoor: a ferryman called Tam Harrow. Two years now. I'd stop if I could, but they've got my daughter.”
plays.response: Wren has also warned the Bellwrights of several raids, which is why some survived. She asks nothing for herself, only that Tessa be taken out of the city. She says the Court's watchers reported Tam by Bellwright courier channels: Tam Harrow ran messages between the Old Shore and the Tower, so his name crossed her desk. If they listen or forgive, she gives the dormitory room, the evening shift change (third lamp-lighting), and Ilam Bray as the Hushman who knows the service entrance. If the households who owe the party (s01-fill-the-quota) are known to her, she trusts them without a roll. If they hand her to the Hushmen, play s06-hand-wren-over.
plays.consequence: The party knows who gave up Tam Harrow, and has a way to Tessa.
plays.fallback: If the party is cold, Wren leaves the dormitory plan on the counter wrapped in a loaf and walks out.
plays.tells: A freckled woman with sewing in her lap asks to sit down, then can't start.
plays.rules: Insight DC 12: she is telling the truth and terrified. No Influence is needed; she is Friendly to anyone who isn't cruel, and breaks if someone is.
plays.later: S7: Ilam Bray's name ties Wren's plan to Jonah. S28: whether to tell Ila is the party's call; Ila trusts people who tell her hard truths. Act IV: Ansel is loyal to Wren, not Maudrin, and knows Maudrin's routes. S29: Wren is forgiven, or is not.
plays.keywords: wren, caddock, confession, spy, informer, tam harrow, betrayal, forgive, daughter, tessa, bakery

plays.title: They get Tessa out of the Hall of Tithes
plays.why: A rescue with a known room and shift change is the kind of plan players love.
plays.readAloud: The clerks' dormitory smells of ink and boiled cabbage. Two grey-gloved men lean on either side of a door at the end of the corridor, bored, counting the minutes to the shift bell.
plays.response: Three good routes: a forged transfer order (DC 16 Charisma (Deception) on the guards, or DC 16 Intelligence check with a Forgery Kit to make one that needs no talking); a negotiated exchange through Ansel, who 'misfiles' Tessa as a kitchen girl for 25 gp; or a kitchen evacuation (a grease fire, smoke, a well-placed Prestidigitation). Failure alerts the guards and starts a chase through the lanes, never an automatic Tithe (Tessa's Guards). Bet Ostrow hides Tessa overnight above the bakery and Wren has a cart out at dawn.
plays.consequence: Tessa is out. Wren is free of the Court's hold and becomes the party's ally.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Ilam Bray, on the corridor shift, looks at Tessa, looks at the party, and opens the service door.
plays.tells: The party asks Wren for the layout, or starts forging papers.
plays.rules: Deception DC 16, or Forgery Kit DC 16. Stealth DC 15 in the corridor; Pass without Trace works (no silence-stones here). One night in the city: Tithe Clock +1. If your table has no child peril, Tessa is Wren's adult sister.
plays.later: S9: Wren's Bellwright route can carry a Heart past the cart searches. S18A: Corin trusts the party because the Bellwrights trust Wren. S29: 'Wren gets her daughter out.'
plays.keywords: tessa, rescue, hall of tithes, dormitory, forge, forgery, transfer order, kitchen, fire, distraction, child, wren

plays.title: They are kind to Bet Ostrow
plays.why: Bet feeds anyone who looks hungry, and players adopt her on sight.
plays.readAloud: Bet presses a heel of warm bread into your hands before you've asked. A child at the counter jingles something in a pocket, a little brass bell, and Bet goes perfectly still with the knife in the loaf.
plays.response: Bet chatters, then stops mid-sentence and cries without knowing why; she freezes at any small bell. Her hands still know the harvest-bell's tune: if anyone hums a few notes of a harvest-song, her fingers tap the rhythm on the counter. If the party brought her jar from the vault (S5) and she opens it herself, she remembers ringing Calla at nine and asks, very quietly, whether she could do it again.
plays.consequence: Bet trusts them, and her bakery becomes a safe house.
plays.fallback: If nobody engages, Bet sends a loaf to their lodgings with a note: 'You looked hungry.'
plays.tells: A player accepts the bread, asks her name, or asks why she is crying.
plays.rules: Heroic Inspiration: giving Bet back her own memory freely earns it (v6 generosity rule).
plays.later: S9: Bet is the natural Gift-recipient when Calla rings, or the Ringer herself if she remembers. Act IV (Situation 21): Bet knows which carts leave the city unsearched. S30: Bet cries when she hears a bell, and this time she knows why.
plays.keywords: bet, ostrow, baker, bakery, bread, kind, bell, cry, calla, harvest, jar

plays.title: Rook hands Ossa's Heart back
plays.why: Maudrin stored Ossa's Heart in the armory, and Rook now holds it.
plays.readAloud: Rook sets the Heart on the table between you. 'It hummed all night,' she says. 'I'd rather it hummed in the right hands.'
plays.response: Rook gives it freely and asks nothing. She warns them that Maudrin will want it back and knows exactly where Rook keeps it.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is with the party.
plays.fallback: If the party leaves it, Rook keeps it safe until S9.
plays.tells: The party asks Rook what is on the armory shelves.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S9: ring Ossa with a detour (s09-ring-ossa-later). S23: Maudrin wants every Heart they carry.
plays.keywords: ossa heart, armory, rook, return

plays.title: They kill Haldric
plays.why: The party believes he is guilty and the hearing is going nowhere.
plays.readAloud: Haldric's sword hits the stone. He looks at the palace, not at you. 'She'll hate this,' he says, and does not finish.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' He can be knocked out instead. If he dies, the Steps go quiet and Rook steps in front of the party with her arms wide, furious and heartbroken. The Dawn Order splits. Say plainly that Haldric is dead and that a letter in the palace names him 'my son'. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Haldric is dead. The Strike has two knights and no hesitation.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Haldric yields his sword and kneels.
plays.tells: A player takes the coup de grace or aims a killing blow at Haldric on the Steps or in the barracks.
plays.rules: Haldric is a Knight (CR 3). His silence-stone shield negates the first spell targeting only him each day.
plays.later: S23: Maudrin's line has no Haldric to break; she arrives colder. S24 and S26: Maudrin carries the grief.
plays.keywords: kill haldric, murder, execute knight, dead

plays.title: They capture Haldric and question him
plays.why: Rook cannot prove the payments; a bound Haldric might talk.
plays.readAloud: He sits very straight on the stable bench, his sword gone, his hands bound in front of him. 'You can't make me say it. And she can't make me stop.'
plays.response: Haldric will not talk about Maudrin. He says 'I serve the dawn' and asks to be killed cleanly. Detect Thoughts is negated by his shield the first time each day; a second casting shows him thinking 'She promised she would come.' Zone of Truth: he declines to answer, which is a tell. Holding a knight is kidnapping in the Dawn Order's law, and Rook will not forgive it.
plays.consequence: The party holds Haldric for a night. The Court knows.
plays.fallback: If the plan fails, Rook arrives with six knights.
plays.tells: The party follows Haldric after the hearing, or ambushes his escort in the barracks yard.
plays.rules: Haldric: Intimidation DC 17 only moves him to anger. Influence DC 17 if the party shows him the entry.
plays.later: S23: Haldric remembers who held him. If he is released, Rook demands a public apology.
plays.keywords: capture haldric, interrogate, kidnap, question knight

plays.title: They steal Vaer's Heart while the city watches the duel
plays.why: Every Dawn Order knight is on the Steps, and the armory is a grille and a lock.
plays.readAloud: The barracks yard is empty. Somewhere a long way off a herald is shouting 'Order, order,' and inside the armory a bronze clapper hangs on its peg.
plays.response: The armory grille is DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools. One young knight stands watch; he is a Rook loyalist and 'misses' the party if they look like they are on her side. The theft is noticed the moment Haldric checks the armory that night.
plays.consequence: The party holds Vaer's Heart, and Haldric knows.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, the young knight forgets to lock the yard gate.
plays.tells: A rogue asks where the armory guards are during the hearing.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17. Stealth DC 15 through the yard. If Ossa's Heart is here too, s09-steal-ossa-too.
plays.later: S9: ring Vaer (s09-ring-vaer). S23: if Haldric holds his office, he rides with Maudrin to get it back.
plays.keywords: steal vaer, armory, duel day, sleight of hand

plays.title: They hand Wren to the Hushmen
plays.why: She sold Tam Harrow's name; some players want justice.
plays.readAloud: Wren does not resist. She holds out her hands. 'I would have done it too,' she says. 'Tessa. Please.'
plays.response: Tessa is moved to a Tithe-house that night and Wren is Tithed within a week. The Bellwrights learn who gave her up. The party loses the Bellwright route and Ansel's loyalty. A rescue is still possible, harder: s06-rescue-tessa-hard.
plays.consequence: Wren is exposed to the Court and Tessa is moved.
plays.fallback: If the party hesitates, Wren steps back before they do.
plays.tells: The party takes Wren to a Hushman, or tells the Court her name.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S18A: Corin Aldeth knows who handed Wren in and is cold. S29: Wren cannot be forgiven because she is Tithed.
plays.keywords: hand over wren, betray, expose, hushmen

plays.title: They get Tessa and Ila out of the Hall of Tithes
plays.why: Ila was arrested, and the same dormitory holds Tessa.
plays.readAloud: The dormitory door at the end of the corridor is open a hand's breadth. Inside, two girls sit on the same bunk. One of them has an oilskin bundle; it is Ila, and she is humming the response hymn.
plays.response: Same plan as Tessa's, with two children and one closed door: Ila is held, never harmed, and the guards are bored. A forged transfer order covers both. Bet's attic holds both overnight, and Wren's cart takes Ila home. Check Off-limits: both stay behind the party's shield, never described in danger.
plays.consequence: Tessa and Ila are out. Wren is the party's ally.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Ilam Bray opens the service door.
plays.tells: The party asks Wren for the layout, and learns Ila is in the next room.
plays.rules: Deception DC 16 or Forgery Kit DC 16; Stealth DC 15. One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: Wren's Bellwright route carries Hearts past the carts. S28: Ila remembers who came for her.
plays.keywords: rescue ila, rescue tessa, hall of tithes, dormitory

plays.title: They break Tessa out of the Tithe-house
plays.why: Wren was handed over and Tessa has been moved.
plays.readAloud: The Tithe-house is a narrow building with grey shutters and a single lit window. A clerk's apron hangs on the line outside.
plays.response: Ansel (if he is alive) knows where Tessa went; Bet Ostrow hears from the clerks. The Tithe-house is lightly guarded by two Hushmen and a Blank. Same options as before, harder: no inside shift-change, no ally on the other side.
plays.consequence: Tessa is out; Wren is gone.
plays.fallback: If the plan fails, Tessa is moved again and the trail goes cold.
plays.tells: The party asks Ansel where the children went.
plays.rules: Deception or Forgery Kit DC 19; Stealth DC 17. One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S29: Wren's fate is the Court's; Tessa is with Bet.
plays.keywords: tessa, tithe-house, rescue, moved

plays.title: They calm the crowd (it works)
plays.why: Hundreds of grieving people and a line of Hushmen: most parties try words first.
plays.readAloud: The Hall of Tithes is surrounded. Hundreds of people, grey-faced, holding up old drawings and wooden toys, shouting names they cannot quite remember. They do not riot. They only stand and ask, over and over, “Who was she? Who was I?” The Hushmen are forming a line.
plays.response: The Blanks follow anyone who promises to help them recover their memories, and they hold that person to it. Calming them is Influence (Persuasion) DC 16 by one speaker, with Help from others; a promise backed by something real (jars from the vault, the Ledger's names) gives advantage. On a success the crowd sits down on the steps in silence, which the Hushmen have no procedure for, and Sergeant Orla Gaunt orders the line to hold. If the roll fails, play s07-calm-crowd-fails.
plays.consequence: The Blanks trust the party, and expect them to keep their promise.
plays.fallback: If the speech stalls, a Blank at the front asks the speaker their name, forgets it, and asks again; the crowd laughs, and the tension breaks a little.
plays.tells: A player climbs onto something to be seen, or asks who leads the crowd.
plays.rules: Influence DC 16 for the crowd; Help gives advantage. Calm Emotions or Thaumaturgy can also give advantage (see s07-spells-crowd).
plays.later: S22: the Blanks march. S23: they break the Hushmen's line by numbers. S28–30: every promise made on these steps is asked about by name.
plays.keywords: crowd, blanks, calm, speech, persuade, promise, help, protest, hall of tithes, steps

plays.title: They fight the Hushmen line
plays.why: The line moves on unarmed grieving people; many tables will not stand by.
plays.readAloud: Six grey gloves come up together. Where they strike, there is no sound at all, and that is the worst part.
plays.response: The Hushmen want arrests, not deaths, and so do the Blanks: area damage near the crowd hits Blanks too (Commoners, 4 HP each). Use the Hushmen Line. Give the party a way to end it fast: Sergeant Gaunt withdraws when half her line is down or the party holds the Hall's doors. Afterward the steps belong to the Blanks, and to the party.
plays.consequence: The party is the Blanks' champion and the Court's named enemy.
plays.fallback: If it turns bloody, Captain Rook's knights arrive on the far side of the square and the Sergeant decides she has been outnumbered.
plays.tells: Weapons out, or a player steps between a Hushman and a Blank.
plays.rules: Hushmen: Pack Tactics, grapple. Silence-stone gloves silence only their own strikes. Blanks are Commoners (4 HP).
plays.later: S9: the north gate is reinforced (Gate Sweep at every gate). S22: the Blanks march. S23: they break the line by numbers.
plays.keywords: fight, attack hushmen, line, protect, combat, battle, defend blanks, sergeant

plays.title: They reunite Jonah and Ilam Bray
plays.why: A boy with a wooden bird and a Hushman who stops when he sees it: the scene asks to be finished.
plays.readAloud: “That's my carving. I made it for my son. I don't know his name anymore. I've tried. I don't know why I can't remember. Is he in there? In the crowd? Please. I need to see him.”
plays.response: Bring Jonah to the edge of the line, or Ilam to the boy. Neither remembers the other's name. The bird does it: Ilam turns it over, finds the notch where his knife slipped, and Jonah says, very literally, “You made that.” Ilam takes off his silence-stone gloves on the spot and drops them on the stones. He gives the party a key to the Tithe-Ledger Room's service passage and the Hushman roster: every name, post and shift.
plays.consequence: Ilam deserts the Hushmen. The party holds a vault key and the roster.
plays.fallback: If the party misses the moment, Jonah walks to Ilam by himself and holds up the bird.
plays.tells: A player notices Ilam staring at the bird, or asks Jonah where he got it.
plays.rules: No check if Jonah trusts the party (he attaches to whoever is kind). Stealth DC 13 to get Ilam out of the line before his Sergeant notices.
plays.later: S9: the roster says which gate and shift to avoid. S22: Ilam holds the Tor's southern road. S23: Ilam stands between Jonah and the fight, and Jonah sees his father clearly. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.
plays.keywords: jonah, ilam, bray, reunite, father, son, wooden bird, carving, family, hushman, desert

plays.title: They attack Ilam Bray
plays.why: A gloved Hushman walking toward a child looks like a threat to a table that has learned to hate Hushmen.
plays.readAloud: The crowd's murmur stops dead. Jonah screams a word you don't know, and somewhere in the crowd a woman's voice says it too.
plays.response: The crowd turns on the party: they are now the villains of the Blanks. Ilam does not fight back beyond covering his face. Jonah runs into the crowd and is taken into Court custody by nightfall unless someone else reaches him first. Killing Ilam is a separate choice (s07-kill-ilam).
plays.consequence: The Blanks turn against the party and Jonah is in custody.
plays.fallback: If the player hesitates mid-swing, let Ilam drop his gloves first; nobody attacks a man with bare hands raised.
plays.tells: A player readies an attack as Ilam steps out of the line.
plays.rules: Ilam: Hushman (Tough). The crowd will not fight, but it blocks, shouts, and remembers faces.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks will not march, and some inform on the party. S23: if Jonah is in custody, Maudrin brings him to the ridge as a hostage, and freeing him costs one Heart or the Strike.
plays.keywords: attack ilam, kill hushman, strike, mistake, wrong person, fight, ilam bray

plays.title: They leave Jonah in the crowd
plays.why: The party has bigger aims, or simply doesn't notice one boy among hundreds.
plays.readAloud: Later, you remember the bird: a small wooden shape held up above the heads, going away from you toward the carts.
plays.response: The sweep takes Jonah into Court custody as a Blank. He goes quietly, holding the bird. Ilam watches the cart go and says nothing; his Sergeant tells him to hold the line, and he does.
plays.consequence: Jonah is in Court custody. Ilam stays a Hushman.
plays.fallback: If a player asks later, Ilam can be found drinking alone at the Shuttered Lamp, asking strangers whether they've seen a boy with a bird.
plays.tells: The party heads for the vault, the Archive or the gate while the sweep begins.
plays.later: S9: Jonah is in the Hall of Tithes until then; a rescue like Tessa's still works (s09-free-jonah: same guards, same shift change). S23: Maudrin brings him to the ridge as a hostage; freeing him costs one Heart or the Strike.
plays.keywords: leave, ignore, abandon, jonah, custody, sweep, cart, walk away

plays.title: They take Jonah somewhere safe without his father
plays.why: Saving the child is obvious; trusting the Hushman isn't.
plays.readAloud: Jonah holds your hand and the bird in the other, very tightly. “Is the man with the gloves coming?” he asks. Then, a street later: “Is he coming?”
plays.response: Jonah goes with whoever is kind. Bet Ostrow's attic, the Dawn Mission's lodging (if Aurelie is in the city) or Rook's barracks will take him. He asks every hour whether the man with the gloves is coming. Ilam keeps looking, and a reunion can still happen before they leave the city.
plays.consequence: Jonah is safe. Ilam is still a Hushman, searching.
plays.fallback: If nobody knows where to take him, Bet does: 'Attic's warm. He can have the cat.'
plays.tells: A player picks Jonah up and heads away from the line.
plays.rules: One night in the city: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: Ilam finds the bakery; play the reunion there (s09-jonah-bakery). S23: a safe Jonah is no hostage. S30: his mother still needs finding.
plays.keywords: hide jonah, protect, safe house, bakery, take him, child, shelter, bet

plays.title: They look for Jonah's mother
plays.why: The Ledger or Ilam's roster names Mara Bray, and players want the family whole.
plays.readAloud: Mara Bray sits on the steps with an empty frame in her lap. She is very polite. She asks your names, forgets them, and asks again.
plays.response: The Ledger (S5) or Ilam names her: Mara Bray, Tithed of 'her son' in 408 SS, in this crowd. She does not know Jonah and he does not know her; the meeting is gentle and painful, and nothing more. Her memory is a red-wax heartkeep jar in the vault, unless the EXPORT — VENNMARK column has a tick by her name, in which case it sailed on the Gilded Heron last season. Only Mara opening her own jar brings Jonah back to her.
plays.consequence: The family is three people on paper, and one jar away from three people in fact.
plays.fallback: If they don't look, Ilam asks them to, the night before they leave.
plays.tells: A player asks “Where's his mother?”
plays.rules: Lesser Restoration and Remove Curse do nothing for a Blank: a Tithed memory is not a condition or a curse. Only the owner opening the jar restores it.
plays.later: S9: a second vault visit with Ilam's key can bring her jar out (s09-second-vault-visit). Act V or beyond: if her jar was exported, it is in Athkatla, through the Seam. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.
plays.keywords: mara, bray, mother, jonah's mother, blank, jar, family, find, ledger, heartkeep

plays.title: They use magic on the crowd or the line
plays.why: Calm Emotions, Suggestion and Silence are all on level 3–4 lists and all look made for this square.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums across the square, and every grey glove in the line turns toward the sound.
plays.response: Calm Emotions on the crowd's front ranks gives advantage on the DC 16 Influence and ends Frightened in the area. Suggestion on Sergeant Gaunt ('send your men home; there's nothing to arrest here') works if she fails her Wisdom save; she obeys and is furious afterward. The Silence spell over the line is sacramental here: the Hushmen hesitate for one round, because nobody has ever turned the Court's holy quiet against them. Thaumaturgy lets one speaker be heard across the whole square.
plays.consequence: Magic can win the crowd a night. The caster is marked.
plays.fallback: If a spell fails, the hum alone makes the front rank of Blanks turn and look at the caster with hope, which is pressure enough.
plays.tells: A caster asks how many people a spell can cover, or whether the Sergeant can be charmed.
plays.rules: Calm Emotions (Charisma save, unwilling only). Suggestion (Gaunt's Wisdom save +2). Silence the spell is not silence-stone: Tonework works outside its sphere. Lesser Restoration does not restore Tithed memories. Every spell hums, so the line knows who cast.
plays.later: S9: the caster's description is at every gate, with +2 to the DC of any bluff there.
plays.keywords: calm emotions, suggestion, silence, thaumaturgy, spell, magic, crowd, charm, sergeant, hushmen

plays.title: They tell the Blanks their memories are shipped abroad
plays.why: A party that found the EXPORT — VENNMARK column (S5) has a truth that answers 'Who was I?' in the worst way.
plays.readAloud: It goes through the crowd like a dropped lamp through dry reeds. “Sold?” “Across the sea?” Somebody starts to scream a name, and doesn't stop.
plays.response: Half the crowd surges for the Hall's doors and the line moves at once (Hushmen Line, with Blanks in the way). The other half turns to any Stormborn in the party: “Your people have them?” A Faerûnian character is mobbed, not hurt, and must answer. The Court hears what was said within the hour.
plays.consequence: The Blanks know about the export trade, and the Court knows the party knows.
plays.fallback: If the surge gets dangerous, Ilam Bray drops his gloves and starts helping people off the steps, and others follow.
plays.tells: A player mentions Venn, Athkatla, or 'the ships' in front of the crowd.
plays.rules: Influence DC 18 to calm them after this (raised from 16).
plays.later: S9: a detour to Pellmoor to confront Venn becomes a promise to keep. S22: the Blanks march, but some want to march on Pellmoor's quays instead.
plays.keywords: export, vennmark, venn, ships, athkatla, sold, tell crowd, reveal, riot, faerun, stormborn

plays.title: The speech fails and the crowd surges
plays.why: The Blanks are afraid and a bad promise sounds like a lie.
plays.readAloud: The front rank steps forward. Somebody drops a drawing. A Hushman's glove closes on a shoulder, and the crowd stops being a crowd.
plays.response: The crowd surges, the Hushmen arrest anyone who interferes, and the party must pick a side now: the Blanks (s07-fight-the-line) or the line (leave, or help restrain). Nobody dies in the crush if the party steps in. A Blank at the front asks the speaker's name, forgets it, and asks again, and the surge slows.
plays.consequence: The Blanks do not trust the party yet, and the Court records the speaker.
plays.fallback: If the surge gets dangerous, Ilam Bray drops his gloves and starts helping people off the steps.
plays.tells: The Influence check fails, or the speaker offers something the Blanks know is empty.
plays.rules: Influence DC 18 to try again after the failure; the second attempt has Advantage if the speaker says sorry.
plays.later: S9: the speaker's description is at the north gate. S22: the Blanks will not march unless a promise is kept.
plays.keywords: crowd fails, surge, failed speech, blanks

plays.title: They kill Ilam Bray
plays.why: A Hushman walking toward a child looks like a threat to a table that has learned to hate Hushmen.
plays.readAloud: Ilam falls without a sound. The wooden bird rolls from his pocket and stops against Jonah's shoe.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' He can be knocked out. If he dies, the crowd screams, Jonah is taken into custody by nightfall, and the Blanks turn on the party. Say plainly that Ilam is dead and that Jonah has lost his father without knowing his name. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Ilam is dead. Jonah is in custody.
plays.fallback: If the player hesitates mid-swing, let Ilam drop his gloves first.
plays.tells: A player follows through on the attack.
plays.rules: Ilam is a Hushman (Tough). Child peril: Jonah is not harmed on-screen.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks will not march. S23: Jonah is a hostage on the ridge. S30: Jonah remembers only his mother's face.
plays.keywords: kill ilam, murder hushman, father, jonah

plays.title: They smuggle Blanks out of the city
plays.why: The sweep takes hundreds, and the party has a safe route.
plays.readAloud: Bet's flour cart goes out under the north gate with sacks and six quiet people in the false bed. The Hushmen wave it through because she feeds them.
plays.response: Bet's flour cart, Wren's drains and Ilam's roster can smuggle a few at a time to Pellmoor, the Dawn Mission or Bet's attic. Each night is a Tithe Clock tick. The Blanks remember the promise, and some go to Pellmoor to work the quays with Sela Maunt.
plays.consequence: A handful of Blanks are out of the sweep and the Blanks trust the party.
plays.fallback: If the party has no cart, Bet offers hers.
plays.tells: A player asks Bet or Wren how carts leave the city, or counts the Hushmen at the gate.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 at the gate. Each night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S22: the Blanks march. S28: some Blanks keep the ledger at Pellmoor.
plays.keywords: smuggle blanks, cart, bet, drains, pellmoor, escape

plays.title: They read the Hushmen's roster aloud to the line
plays.why: Ilam's roster names every Hushman, post and shift. A voice that says their names aloud can break a line.
plays.readAloud: 'Sergeant Gaunt,' you say, reading from Ilam's list. 'North gate, third shift. Your sister Orla lives on Cutler's Lane and has not seen you since the Tithe.' The line goes very still.
plays.response: A reading of names to a line of Tithed Hushmen is the cruellest and most effective thing the party can do here. Gaunt withdraws when half her line hesitates. Every Hushman named wonders who else knows. Gaunt will not forgive it.
plays.consequence: The line wavers and the Court's patience thins.
plays.fallback: If the speech stalls, a Blank reads the next name.
plays.tells: Ilam deserts and gives the roster; a player holds it up to the line.
plays.rules: Intimidation or Persuasion DC 16 to hold the line's attention; the roster gives Advantage.
plays.later: S9: the Gate Sergeants know the party has the roster (Gate Sweep +2 DC for bluffs). S23: Gaunt is a Court agent against the party.
plays.keywords: roster, read names, hushmen, ilam, intimidate

plays.title: They trace the courier
plays.why: A shaking one-line letter from 'I.V.' begs the question who carried it.
plays.readAloud: The courier is a trapper in reindeer hide with frost-burn on both cheeks, and he will not sit near the fire. “Not mine to explain,” he says. “I was paid to carry it. The sister wrote it. The voice said it.”
plays.response: He is Edrin Moss, a Glassreach trapper. A DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) check, or a drink and Influence DC 15, gets the rest: he was paid by Wyn Talla, an old woman at the forest's edge whose family has watched the glass for four hundred years. They call the woman in it 'the sister'. A voice in the glass told Wyn what to write, called itself 'I.V.', and promised the sister would move again. On a failure Edrin leaves at dawn and they can follow his tracks north. That afternoon two Hushmen and a Court agent try to take Edrin off the street (Courier Snatch): Isolde wants to read the letter too.
plays.consequence: They know where to start in Glassreach (Wyn Talla's hut, beside Yara's camp) and that the Court is interested.
plays.fallback: If they don't ask, Edrin asks them, on his way out, whether they know what year it is up north. He's never sure.
plays.tells: A player asks where the courier went, or who paid him.
plays.rules: Investigation DC 15, or Influence DC 15 (Edrin is Indifferent; Friendly if paid or warmed).
plays.later: S10: Wyn waits at Yara's camp and asks them to free the woman in the glass (s10-meet-wyn). S11: Maren Talla is one of the Stilled adults; waking her gently is the kind route. S15: if Maren wakes, Wyn is first to bring the Stilled bread.
plays.keywords: courier, letter, trace, investigate, trapper, edrin, who sent it, i.v., glassreach, wyn talla

plays.title: They question Isolde about Maudrin's last word
plays.why: Isolde delivers Maudrin's message in person, and it raises more questions than it answers.
plays.readAloud: “Thank you for your curiosity. It is, after all, why I invited you. When you come back from the north, I will be waiting, and so will the Key. Give my regards to the Glass Sexton. He was once family, and he will not thank you for disturbing him.”
plays.response: Isolde reads it word for word and watches what it does to their faces. Asked what it means, she gives the truth as she knows it: the Glass Sexton is Imber Vesk, High Sexton on the Quiet Night, and 'once family' means exactly that. She does not know what the Key is, and that bothers her. She mentions, idly, that the North Road is cold and that she has never liked the cold.
plays.consequence: They know the Sexton is a Vesk, and that someone will follow them north.
plays.fallback: If they ignore her, she leaves the message pinned to their door with a silver hairpin, which is worth 5 gp and is clearly a test.
plays.tells: Players ask what 'he was once family' means, or what the Key is.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15: she is going north herself, and isn't pleased about it. Influence DC 15 (Isolde's Intelligence 12) to learn when: within a day of their leaving.
plays.later: S9: Isolde follows with a Hushman escort (s09-isolde-follows). S12: the Sexton asks who rules the Court, and the answer is his own blood. S15: Isolde arrives at the thaw.
plays.keywords: isolde, drave, maudrin, message, last word, key, glass sexton, family, vesk, question

plays.title: They turn Isolde into an informant
plays.why: Players who learned about her son, or her quiet sales to the Ironhorn, have leverage on the Court's best gossip.
plays.readAloud: Isolde sets her glass down for the first time all evening. “Careful. People who say that to me usually want something. What do you want, and what will you give my son?”
plays.response: Two levers work: her son's safety (a place outside the city, such as Pellmoor under Brannagh Wick's pilots, or Rook's protection) and her secret (she sells Tithed memories to the Ironhorn Compact; the Ledger entry in S5 shows the gaps). Either moves her to Friendly; then Influence DC 15 seals it. She will still be sent north, because refusing would expose her, but she brings only two Hushmen and warns the party what the Court wants.
plays.consequence: Isolde is their informant inside the Court, for as long as it protects her son.
plays.fallback: If they push too hard, she laughs, agrees to nothing, and remembers they tried.
plays.tells: A player brings up her son, or what she sells and to whom.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15, only after a real offer or real leverage. Record in the Bargain Log: Isolde's son's safety.
plays.later: S9: she follows anyway, leaving a note at the first waystation naming her escort (s09-isolde-follows-ally). S15: she asks for the Frost Heart in front of her Hushmen, then offers a private way to 'lose' it (s15-isolde-informant). S21: she warns them a day before Maudrin leaves Hallowmere.
plays.keywords: isolde, informant, turn, blackmail, leverage, son, ironhorn, deal, spy, double agent

plays.title: They ignore the letter
plays.why: Some tables refuse the hook, or want Brassfall, Vael Tor or Pellmoor first.
plays.readAloud: A week later, the same blue wax. The same shaking hand. One word under the first line: 'Please.'
plays.response: Let them; Corvane is big. The letter comes again a week later. Meanwhile the Sexton's sermon spreads south: two travelers at Kell's Crossing stop speaking. The Frost Heart stays in his crown and the Concord needs Hieme, so tell the players plainly that this is where the winter bell is.
plays.consequence: Glassreach waits. The silence spreads down the North Road.
plays.fallback: If they waver, Edrin Moss offers to guide them for nothing: he wants to see what happens.
plays.tells: “We're not going to Glassreach.” Or the party plans another road.
plays.rules: The Tithe Clock resets once they have been out of Court cities for a week.
plays.later: Act IV: run whichever branch they reach first; Glassreach can follow. S15: with nobody to follow north, Isolde waits in Hallowmere. S22: without Hieme rung, the Concord is closed until they go north; the Second Dawn stays open.
plays.keywords: ignore, refuse, not going, skip, elsewhere, brassfall, vael tor, letter, hook, decline

plays.title: They leave Hallowmere tonight
plays.why: The letter says 'before the winter takes the last of me', and the Tithe Clock is ticking.
plays.readAloud: The city's lamps burn the same at midnight as at noon. Only the Hushmen change: fewer, colder, and more awake.
plays.response: Run Session 9 now, on the road. Ask the Hallowmere Ledger questions as they pass the gate. Anything left behind stays: Calla's Heart on its shelf, Vaer silent, Jonah wherever he is. If they carry Calla's Heart or the Ledger, the cart searches are still on (Gate Sweep); a night departure gives advantage on the group Stealth check.
plays.consequence: They are on the North Road with whatever they carried out.
plays.fallback: If they'd rather settle accounts first, play Session 9 in the city instead.
plays.tells: “We go now.” Players pack before the scene is over.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15 at the north gate, with advantage at night.
plays.later: Act IV (Situation 21): Calla's Heart is only in the Court's vault; coming back for it is a clear choice with a cost. S22: if Vaer and Calla are unrung, the Concord needs a return to Hallowmere, where a Silence Warrant or a tighter Tithe Clock may be waiting.
plays.keywords: leave, depart, tonight, go now, rush, north road, exit, flee city, hurry

plays.title: They ask the Librarian or Lysse who 'I.V.' is
plays.why: The letter is signed with initials, and the Archive knows every name.
plays.readAloud: The Librarian's page turns by itself. 'Imber Vesk,' it writes, in your own hand. 'High Sexton of the Quiet Night. He is not dead. He is waiting.'
plays.response: For one true memory the Librarian names him and says he has been in the glass since 32 SS. Lysse suggests the Archive's Court receipts for the Quiet Night, which are incomplete. The answer is true, and the Librarian adds nothing more.
plays.consequence: The party knows I.V. is Imber Vesk, a Vesk and a Sexton, before they leave.
plays.fallback: If nobody pays, Isolde's message names him anyway.
plays.tells: A player asks Lysse who I.V. might be, or carries the letter to the Stacks.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 16 for Lysse's shortcut in an hour. Never from an absent player's character.
plays.later: S12: they know what to ask him. S13: the Sexton's confession is not a surprise.
plays.keywords: who is iv, imber vesk, librarian, lysse, letter

plays.title: They read Edrin with Detect Thoughts or Suggestion
plays.why: A frightened courier with a secret invites mind magic.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums behind your teeth. Edrin goes pale. 'Don't,' he says. 'Please. I've been paid not to remember.'
plays.response: Detect Thoughts on Edrin shows the name Wyn, the cold of the glass, and a voice in a chapel singing. He is not hiding anything he would not share if asked kindly. Suggestion ('tell us everything') works if he fails his Wisdom save, and he knows afterward. Edrin trusts the party less; the Hushmen hear the spell hum at two streets' distance and the agent arrives sooner.
plays.consequence: They learn the same facts at the cost of Edrin's goodwill.
plays.fallback: If the save succeeds, Edrin still answers because the party has already been kind.
plays.tells: A caster asks whether Edrin is hiding something.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts: Wisdom save to probe deeper. Suggestion: Wisdom save. Every spell hums within 30 feet.
plays.later: S8: the Court agent reaches Edrin early (Courier Snatch). S10: Edrin will not guide them unless asked kindly.
plays.keywords: detect thoughts, suggestion, edrin moss, interrogate courier

plays.title: They waylay Isolde's carriage or forge a reply
plays.why: Isolde carries Maudrin's orders, and a party that wants the Court's plans has a target.
plays.readAloud: The carriage rolls into the yard with grey curtains drawn. The driver is a Hushman. Inside, a small locked case sits beside a pair of silver-rimmed gloves.
plays.response: The case holds the Court's orders to follow the party north: Isolde, two Hushmen, a Sergeant at the waystation. Isolde is not in it. Taking it is a crime against the Court, and the carriage's escort fights to keep it. A forged reply (Forgery Kit DC 16) can send her the wrong way for two days.
plays.consequence: The party knows Isolde's escort and route; the Court knows they were here.
plays.fallback: If the plan fails, Isolde invites them to dinner and gives them the orders for free.
plays.tells: A player asks where Isolde's carriage rests, or whether her seal can be copied.
plays.rules: Stealth DC 15 to reach the case. Forgery Kit DC 16 for the reply. Hold Person and Sleep can disable the driver but the Court notes the hum.
plays.later: S9: Isolde follows with fewer Hushmen (the case is empty), or follows the wrong road. S15: she arrives angry.
plays.keywords: waylay, carriage, forge reply, orders, isolde, stealth

plays.title: They hire Edrin as a guide
plays.why: Edrin knows the North Road, wants a reason to return, and will guide for nothing if he is curious.
plays.readAloud: 'The road past the second waystation is not on any map,' Edrin says. 'I'll take you as far as the forest edge. After that the ice does the guiding.'
plays.response: Edrin guides them to Yara's camp; he will not enter the glass. He is a trapper, not a fighter, and he flees if Hushmen appear. He knows the sermon's voice and warns against arguing.
plays.consequence: A guide who knows the road to Glassreach.
plays.fallback: If the party refuses, Edrin goes anyway and they can follow his tracks.
plays.tells: A player offers a drink and a fee, or notices Edrin's frost-burn.
plays.rules: No check. Perception DC 14 on the road to notice Isolde's carriage.
plays.later: S10: Edrin leaves them at the edge. S12: his warning about the sermon is a free chance to stop arguing.
plays.keywords: edrin guide, trapper, north road, hire guide

plays.title: They ring Vaer
plays.why: They hold Vaer's Heart and stand under the only thing in Hallowmere that isn't grey.
plays.readAloud: The bell cracks the grey like a knife through glass. For one heartbeat the cloud tears open, and a line of gold falls across the terraces. Every person in the city looks up. The opening widens. For this one day, sunlight reaches every terrace.
plays.response: First the silence-stone chains must come off: Rook's chain-key opens them, or DC 17 Thieves' Tools, or breaking three chain-stones (AC 12, 10 HP each), which is loud. Then state the Toll and wait for a yes: a memory of a dawn you loved; a Corvanese character raised in Hallowmere who never saw one may offer a memory of a hoped-for beginning instead. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. When it rings, the Court marks the Ringer with a Silence Warrant. If Sister Aurelie is in the city, she is on the terraces singing to Lathander within the hour (s09-aurelie-on-the-terraces).
plays.consequence: Hallowmere has one real day of sun. The Ringer is wanted in every Court city.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, Rook says, 'I've waited my whole life. I can wait one more minute.' And she does.
plays.tells: A player asks what Vaer would do, or what it costs.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Vaer). Silence Warrant: any Hushman may arrest the Ringer on sight in a Court city; the Dawn Order enforces it only if Haldric won the duel or Rook's case failed. One day of true sunlight; dawn-based abilities at full strength; Hushmen and Blanks look up.
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S9: the Warrant follows the Ringer (s09-warrant-arrest). S22: a freed Aurelie and her Dawn Mission are the Stormborn ally. S23: the Strike's Hushmen go for the Ringer first. Act V: Vaer's dawn lasts one day unless the final rite sustains it (Concord or Second Dawn).
plays.keywords: ring, vaer, dawn, bell, belfry, toll, sun, sunrise, warrant, chains, ringer

plays.title: They steal Vaer's Heart from the armory
plays.why: Rook didn't win, or they don't want to owe her, and the armory is only a grille and a lock.
plays.readAloud: The armory is a long room of racked spears and dawn-yellow pennons gone grey. Behind an iron grille, a long bronze clapper hangs on a peg, the colour of sunlight in a country that has none.
plays.response: The grille's lock is DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) with Thieves' Tools. Two Dawn Order knights guard the chain-room above, not the armory, so a quiet job never meets them unless the party climbs straight up to ring (Chain-Room Knights). Haldric checks the armory each dawn, so by the second hour the theft is known. If Ossa's Heart hangs beside Vaer's, take both (s09-steal-ossa-too).
plays.consequence: The party holds Vaer's Heart (and perhaps Ossa's), and the Dawn Order is hunting it.
plays.fallback: If the lock beats them, a young knight on night watch, a Rook loyalist, 'forgets' to lock the yard gate behind him.
plays.tells: Players ask where the armory is and who watches it.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17. Stealth DC 15 through the barracks yard. Pass without Trace (+10) and Invisibility make the yard easy but the lock is still a lock.
plays.later: S9: ring at once (past the chain-room knights, s09-ring-vaer) or carry it out past the gate searches. S23: if Haldric still holds his office, he rides with Maudrin to get it back.
plays.keywords: steal, vaer, heart, armory, theft, grille, lock, dawn order, haldric, ossa

plays.title: They ring Calla at Kell's Crossing
plays.why: Calla's Heart is in their pack and the Old Granary is on the North Road, three days out.
plays.readAloud: The sound is warm and round, and it smells of baking bread. The ash on the fields stirs. Somewhere a child laughs, and a woman begins to cry without knowing why. For one season, the grain comes up green across the plain.
plays.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a Gift, something the Ringer values, given freely to someone in need and never returned. Bet Ostrow is the natural recipient if she is with her own free choice (she is eighty and decides for herself whether to travel three days); otherwise the innkeeper of the Empty Sheaf has six children and one coat. Nessa Harrow, Ila's mother, lives here: she comes out to look at the green fields, and if anyone says Ila's name, she sits down in the ash. Afterward, Court Tithe-men raid the Crossing for the rest of the season and try to capture the Ringer; play that out, don't assume it.
plays.consequence: One harvest season: bread for everyone. The Court's collectors are coming.
plays.fallback: If nobody wants to pay, Bet (if she remembers) asks to ring it herself; she has paid before.
plays.tells: The party stops at the fork, or asks what the Gift Toll means.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Calla: Gift). At Kell's Crossing a character who gives a Gift gains Heroic Inspiration once per session. After ringing, decide where the Heart goes: in the frame ('Left at the Old Granary') or on with the party.
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S15: if they still carry Calla's Heart, Isolde asks for it too. S28: Ila can meet her mother here, if anyone tells her.
plays.keywords: ring, calla, harvest, kell's crossing, granary, gift, toll, bread, bet, nessa harrow

plays.title: They smuggle a Heart or a wanted Ringer past the gate
plays.why: Cart searches follow a vault theft for two days, and a Silence Warrant follows a Vaer ringing.
plays.readAloud: At the north gate four grey-gloved men are unloading every cart onto the road: grain sacks slit, barrels sounded, a coffin opened and closed again with an apology.
plays.response: Good routes: Bet's flour cart, which the Hushmen never search because she feeds them; Wren's Bellwright route through the Seaward Market drains (DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) as a group, one wet hour); Ilam's roster, which names the shift whose Sergeant takes gold; Pass without Trace for a night crossing. Bluffing a search is DC 17 Charisma (Deception), +2 if Sergeant Cole remembers them from S4. Failure means the Gate Sweep encounter, never instant loss of the Heart.
plays.consequence: They are out with what they carry, or they have a fight at the gate.
plays.fallback: If every plan fails, Captain Rook rides out of the gate 'on patrol' with the party in her escort, if she won the duel.
plays.tells: Players ask how carts leave the city, or who doesn't get searched.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 15. Deception DC 17. Pass without Trace (+10). A Heart in a silence-stone-lined box doesn't hum, but the box itself is contraband. Locate Object finds a Heart by its hum within 1,000 feet unless it is lined (see any-l3-locate-and-scry).
plays.later: S15: if they fought their way out, Isolde's escort has two more Hushmen. S23: Maudrin knows exactly which Hearts they carry.
plays.keywords: smuggle, gate, search, cart, sneak out, hide heart, escape city, bet's cart, drains, wren, warrant

plays.title: Isolde follows them north
plays.why: Isolde failed to keep them in the city; the Court sends her after them.
plays.readAloud: Two days out, a carriage with grey curtains stops at the same waystation you do. Nobody gets out. In the morning it is a mile behind you, and it stays a mile behind you.
plays.response: Isolde follows with two Hushmen (four if they fought their way out) to see what they find in the north. Spotting her is DC 15 Wisdom (Perception or Survival). They can confront her (she is charming and admits everything except her orders), lose her (Pass without Trace and a DC 15 group Survival check off the road), or ignore her. Losing her only delays her: she knows from the letter where they are going. Capturing her is s09-capture-isolde.
plays.consequence: The Court has eyes on the party all the way to Glassreach.
plays.fallback: If nobody looks back, Isolde sends a bottle of warm wine to their table at the second waystation, with her compliments.
plays.tells: The party notices the same carriage twice, or a player asks if they're being followed.
plays.rules: Perception or Survival DC 15 to notice. Group Survival DC 15 to lose her for two days.
plays.later: S15: Isolde arrives at the thaw with her escort; if they lost her, she arrives two days late, cold and angry, after the Spire is rung. If they capture her on the road, the Court sends Tristan Vesk in her place.
plays.keywords: followed, tail, isolde, carriage, spy, chase, lose her, ambush, confront, north road

plays.title: They lie low until the searches stop
plays.why: Waiting out a two-day search is the sensible option, if the city lets them.
plays.readAloud: Two days of grey light through an attic window, and boots in the street below at odd hours. Bet brings up bread and doesn't ask.
plays.response: Two nights in Bet's attic, the Dawn Mission's cellar, or Rook's barracks. The cart searches end after two days. Each night is a Tithe Clock tick; at 6 the Court sweeps the city and puts a checkpoint on every road, which makes the wait self-defeating. Use the time: the Hallowmere Ledger questions, a last visit to Lysse, Ilam finding Jonah.
plays.consequence: The searches end. The Court's clock moves.
plays.fallback: If the clock is already near 6, Bet says plainly, 'You can't stay. They're counting.'
plays.tells: “We hide for a couple of days.”
plays.rules: Tithe Clock +2. At 6: Hushmen sweep, checkpoints on every road (Gate Sweep at every gate). Rest in an attic is safe; Misty Step is blocked by silence-stone streets once the clock hits 12.
plays.later: S10: the Tithe Clock resets after a week outside Court cities. If it hits 12 before they leave, silence-stones go into every street; they stay even after the party is gone, waiting for any return in Act IV.
plays.keywords: hide, lie low, wait, rest, attic, safe house, searches, delay, tithe clock

plays.title: They go back to Pellmoor before heading north
plays.why: Ila, Ossa's bell, Venn's export trade or Aurelie's mission pull some tables back to the Mere before Glassreach.
plays.readAloud: The Quays are louder than you remember. Forty masts, no gulls, and on the Tally's slate the day's rate: 1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. Someone has chalked underneath it: HOW MUCH FOR A MOTHER?
plays.response: Pellmoor is three days by ferry and road, and Glassreach is then about two weeks away. With Ossa's Heart in hand, the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer to the Ossa Belfry and his air pocket gets them down (s09-ring-ossa-later). Water Breathing is a 3rd-level spell they will not have until level 5. Venn's counting-house holds the other half of the EXPORT column, and confronting him in public makes him their enemy and moves the Landing (any-confront-venn). The Harper cellar (s01-brass-lantern) and the Dawn Mission (s01-dawn-mission) are a short walk away. Reckoner Sela Maunt can tell exported keeps by their wax stamps.
plays.consequence: The north waits. Pellmoor's threads tighten.
plays.fallback: If the detour stalls, Brannagh Wick tells them the Seam is narrowing for the season and Venn's last ship sails in four days.
plays.tells: Players talk about Ila, Venn, or ringing Ossa with a recovered Heart.
plays.rules: Ossa's Toll: a memory of someone who has died. Holding breath lasts 1 + Constitution modifier minutes. Set Venn to 'Exposed, now hostile' if they confront him publicly.
plays.later: S22: the Stormborn ally (Harper agents, the Dawn Mission, or a Baldurian crew) is earned here if they exposed Venn or protected the ferry-folk. S15: Isolde follows them to Pellmoor and north again; only the days change.
plays.keywords: pellmoor, return, detour, ila, venn, export, ossa, ring ossa, tidewarden, sela maunt, aurelie, mere

plays.title: They settle accounts before the road
plays.why: Every Act II choice needs to be on record before Act III, and the players enjoy the recap.
plays.readAloud: The North Road runs up out of the city between grey hedges, and the Dawn Order's watchtower falls behind you. Ahead, the land rises toward the Ninefold hills. Somewhere behind, a single bell tolls once, muffled by the cloud, and then falls silent.
plays.response: Ask the seven Hallowmere Ledger questions aloud and let the players answer: the jar, Rook or Haldric, Jonah and Ilam, Maudrin's bargain, the diary, the Hearts, Tessa. Set the matching flags in Foresight as they answer. Then ask which unfinished promise they carry north, and write it as a Bargain Log line.
plays.consequence: Your state is correct before Act III.
plays.fallback: If the players don't remember something, it didn't happen; don't punish a forgotten thread.
plays.tells: The party reaches the north gate, or asks 'What did we leave undone?'
plays.rules: Level the party to 5 once Hallowmere is resolved.
plays.later: Every answer is a later: S15 (Isolde, Hearts carried), S22 (allies: Dawn Order, Blanks, Ilam), S23 (Haldric present or absent, Jonah hostage or safe, Maudrin's favor).
plays.keywords: recap, summary, ledger, promises, questions, leave city, north road, level up, unfinished

plays.title: They take Ossa's Heart from the armory as well
plays.why: Maudrin stored it beside Vaer's, and the lock is already open.
plays.readAloud: A second clapper hangs beside Vaer's, grey and cold and water-stained. When you lift it, it hums once, very low.
plays.response: No further roll if the grille is already open. Ossa's Heart goes into the pack with Vaer's. The Court knows both are gone by the second hour.
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is with the party.
plays.fallback: If the party leaves it, Rook's loyalist guard hides it for them.
plays.tells: A player looks at the second peg.
plays.rules: Thieves' Tools DC 17 if the grille is not yet open.
plays.later: S9: ring Ossa with a detour (s09-ring-ossa-later).
plays.keywords: ossa armory, take both, steal heart

plays.title: Rook lends Vaer's Heart quietly
plays.why: Rook's case failed, but she wants the dawn rung and the armory is Haldric's.
plays.readAloud: Rook sets the key on the table and does not let go. 'One night,' she says. 'If it goes wrong I never saw you. If it goes right I will be the one standing under it.'
plays.response: Rook cannot give Vaer's Heart away, but she can 'misplace' the key. She loans it for the night and brings her knights out of the chain-room. Influence DC 15 (Rook starts Friendly to anyone who protects the innocent). If the party apologised after s06-attack-haldric, she softens. Rook will not be the Ringer; she wants to hear it.
plays.consequence: The party holds Vaer's Heart on loan, and Rook's loyalty is tied to the ringing.
plays.fallback: If Rook refuses, the armory remains a theft (s09-steal-vaer).
plays.tells: A player asks Rook whether she can open the armory for one night.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15. Rook is alive (rook).
plays.later: S9: ring Vaer (s09-ring-vaer). If a Silence Warrant follows, Rook is quietly compromised. S22: Rook is an ally.
plays.keywords: rook loan, vaer, chain-key, quiet loan

plays.title: The Warrant: Hushmen close on the Ringer
plays.why: Vaer rang, and a Silence Warrant means any Hushman may arrest the Ringer on sight.
plays.readAloud: The sun is still on the terraces when the first Hushman steps out of an alley. His gloves are silent. His eyes are on one face.
plays.response: Run it as a pursuit: Gate Hushmen close on the Ringer, grapple, and try to get a hand on the Heart. The Dawn Order stands aside if Rook won; if she lost, Dawn Order knights join. The party can fight (Gate Sweep, scaled), hide, or leave by Wren's drains. Nobody dies in the street: capture is a cell, not a Tithe.
plays.consequence: The Ringer is hunted in every Court city.
plays.fallback: If it turns grim, Rook rides across the terraces with six knights and the Hushmen back away.
plays.tells: The Ringer is seen on the terraces after dusk, or at the gate.
plays.rules: Encounter: Gate Sweep. Warrant description: +2 to any Court bluff DC about the Ringer. Hide in a crowd: Stealth DC 15 as a group.
plays.later: S9: the north gate is the choke point. S23: the Strike goes for the Ringer first.
plays.keywords: silence warrant, arrest, ringer, hushmen, pursuit

plays.title: Aurelie sings on the terraces and they get her out
plays.why: Vaer rang, and a dawn-priestess is standing under the sun she has waited for.
plays.readAloud: Aurelie stands on the Terrace of Grief with her hood back and her arms open, singing in a voice that carries to the river. 'When the sun comes back,' she says, to nobody, 'I would like to be standing somewhere it can see me.'
plays.response: She is devoted to the party now and she is a liability. The Hushmen will arrest her by dusk. The party can hustle her out through Bet's flour cart, the Dawn Mission's cellar or Rook's barracks (Deception DC 15 or Stealth DC 15 as a group). She tends the wounded on the way.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is free and devoted. She becomes the core of the Stormborn ally.
plays.fallback: If the party is slow, she walks into the cart herself.
plays.tells: A player looks for Aurelie in the crowd, or Rook's knight points to a woman singing.
plays.rules: Deception or group Stealth DC 15. Aurelie uses Priest stats (Healing Word, Lesser Restoration).
plays.later: S22: the Dawn Mission is the Stormborn ally (stormborn). S23: Aurelie heals the wounded on the ridge.
plays.keywords: aurelie, sing, terraces, vaer, free aurelie, lathander

plays.title: The Hushmen arrest Aurelie at dusk
plays.why: Nobody got her out in time.
plays.readAloud: They take her at the last of the light, still singing. She does not resist. The hymn stops in the middle of a line.
plays.response: Aurelie is held in Vaer's Belfry as a Charter-breaker, unharmed. She will be freed by Rook's word, a rescue (s09-free-aurelie), or after a night's pressure from the Dawn Mission. The Court offers to trade her for the Ringer.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is under arrest.
plays.fallback: If the party tries at once, the Belfry door is guarded by two knights who 'forget' the key.
plays.tells: The party leaves the terraces and Aurelie keeps singing.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S9: s09-free-aurelie. S22: a free Aurelie is the Stormborn ally; if she is never freed, the ally is the Harpers or a crew.
plays.keywords: aurelie arrested, dusk, belfry

plays.title: They free Aurelie from the Belfry
plays.why: She is in a Belfry cell because of them.
plays.readAloud: The cell is clean and cold. Aurelie sits on the bunk with her hands folded. 'I expected to be afraid,' she says. 'Mostly I'm hungry.'
plays.response: Rook's word opens the door if she won; otherwise a forged release (Deception DC 15) or Wren's drains. Aurelie is unharmed. When freed she is devoted and embarrassed.
plays.consequence: Aurelie is free and devoted. The Dawn Mission is the Stormborn ally.
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Rook ties the keys to the cell door with a ribbon.
plays.tells: The party asks Rook about the cells, or plans a rescue.
plays.rules: Deception DC 15, or Influence DC 15 on Rook. One night in the city: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S22: a free Aurelie is the core of the Stormborn ally. S23: she heals the wounded.
plays.keywords: free aurelie, rescue, belfry cell, dawn mission

plays.title: Ilam finds the bakery, and Jonah
plays.why: Jonah has asked every hour whether the man with the gloves is coming.
plays.readAloud: Bet opens the door a hand's width and looks past you. 'There's a man here,' she says. 'He took off his gloves on the doorstep. He says he made a bird.'
plays.response: Bring Jonah to the door. Ilam turns the bird over, finds the notch where his knife slipped, and Jonah says, very literally, 'You made that.' Ilam deserts the Hushmen on the spot and gives the party the roster and a key to the service passage. Jonah goes to bed with the bird and the cat.
plays.consequence: Jonah is reunited with Ilam; Ilam is an ally.
plays.fallback: If the party misses it, Jonah walks to Ilam himself.
plays.tells: Ilam has been seen on the Terraces asking for a boy with a wooden bird.
plays.rules: No check if Jonah trusts the party. Check Off-limits for child peril; no harm on-screen.
plays.later: S22: Ilam holds the Tor's southern road. S23: Ilam stands between Jonah and the fight. S30: Jonah remembers his mother's face, if she is found.
plays.keywords: jonah, ilam, reunion, bakery, bird, father

plays.title: They free Jonah from the Hall of Tithes
plays.why: They left him in the sweep, and a rescue like Tessa's still works.
plays.readAloud: The dormitory smells of boiled cabbage. At the end of the corridor, a boy sits on a bunk holding a wooden bird and humming a tune he has forgotten the name of.
plays.response: Same guards, same shift change as Tessa's rescue. A forged transfer order (Deception DC 16) or Ilam's key (if he is an ally) gets the party in. Jonah goes with whoever is kind. Check Off-limits: Jonah is never described in danger.
plays.consequence: Jonah is safe. Ilam may reunite with him (s09-jonah-bakery).
plays.fallback: If the plan collapses, Ilam opens the service door.
plays.tells: A player asks Ilam, Wren or Bet where the Blanks were taken.
plays.rules: Deception or Forgery Kit DC 16; Stealth DC 15. One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: reunion at the bakery. S23: a safe Jonah is no hostage.
plays.keywords: free jonah, custody, hall of tithes, rescue

plays.title: A second visit to the vault with Ilam's key
plays.why: Ilam's service-passage key makes a second visit easy, and there are jars to bring out.
plays.readAloud: The service passage smells of old brick. At the end, the vault door stands ajar and a single lamp burns on the newest shelf.
plays.response: With Ilam's key and the Hushman roster, the party reaches the vault shelves without the front-door alarm. Mara Bray's jar (BRAY, M. 408 SS) can leave in a satchel; only she can open it. Bet's jar, Mother Sallow's and any others the party left behind can go too. Ansel's morning tally finds the gaps.
plays.consequence: The jars are out. The Court knows the vault was entered.
plays.fallback: If the key fails, Ansel (if he is alive) unlocks the door.
plays.tells: A player asks Ilam about the service passage, or asks where Mara Bray's jar is.
plays.rules: No roll for entry with the key. Witnessing another's jar fades it. Hushmen pass every ten minutes (Stealth DC 15 to wait in shadow). One night: Tithe Clock +1.
plays.later: S9: Mara can open her own jar and know Jonah. S28: Mother Sallow opens her wedding-day jar.
plays.keywords: second vault, mara jar, ilam key, service passage

plays.title: Isolde follows, as the party's informant
plays.why: The party turned Isolde in S8; she still has to go north.
plays.readAloud: A silver hairpin is pinned to the waystation door. Under it, in her hand: 'Two Hushmen, a coach with a squeaking axle, and my deepest apologies. Be seen to ignore me.'
plays.response: Isolde follows with two Hushmen and leaves notes. She is their informant and a risk: the Hushmen will report what they see. Do not let the party forget that she is not on their side.
plays.consequence: The Court has eyes on the party; the party has a reader inside them.
plays.fallback: If the party loses her, she finds them at Yara's camp.
plays.tells: A note at the first waystation names her escort.
plays.rules: No check. Perception DC 15 to catch her second note.
plays.later: S15: she asks for the Frost Heart in front of her Hushmen, then offers a private way out (s15-isolde-informant).
plays.keywords: isolde follows, informant, hairpin, notes

plays.title: They capture Isolde on the North Road
plays.why: She is alone with two Hushmen and she knows too much.
plays.readAloud: The carriage stops in the dark. Isolde's glass falls and does not break in the mud. 'Oh, you clever people,' she says.
plays.response: Isolde fights one round then tries to Disengage into the trees. If she is grappled or dropped, she is captured. She will talk about her son, the Ironhorn sales and the Court's plan if treated kindly, and spit if not. Her Hushmen surrender when she is down. The Court sends Tristan Vesk in her place.
plays.consequence: Isolde is captured. Tristan Vesk will come north in S15.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes long, her Hushmen walk away from the coach.
plays.tells: The party doubles back on the road, or ambushes the carriage.
plays.rules: Isolde: Spy base, Cunning Action. Grappled, Restrained. A captured creature at 0 HP can be knocked out.
plays.later: S15: Tristan Vesk meets the party instead (s15-isolde-wants-imber). S23: a captured Isolde is a bargaining chip.
plays.keywords: capture isolde, ambush carriage, grapple

plays.title: They ring Ossa on a Pellmoor detour
plays.why: They recovered Ossa's Heart in Hallowmere and the bell is a few days away.
plays.readAloud: The Tidewarden waits at the end of the old dock with his oar dripping. He does not ask where you are going.
plays.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. Ila may not be the Ringer. The Tidewarden ferries the Ringer to the belfry and holds an air pocket. If they ring it, the Choir rests and Mother Sallow remembers Davin. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The Choir rests.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, the Cantor waits.
plays.tells: A player says 'we have it, let's ring it', or asks the Tidewarden for passage.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Ossa). Ringer must be at the bell with the Heart.
plays.later: Concord: 1 of 6. S15: Isolde's escort may follow them to the Mere. S27: the Choir can sing at the summit if released.
plays.keywords: ring ossa, pellmoor detour, tidewarden, toll, belfry

plays.title: They push into the glass without proper gear
plays.why: Parties rarely pack for a winter that has lasted four hundred years.
plays.readAloud: The cold here doesn't bite. It waits. After an hour your fingers stop telling you where they are, and your breath falls from your mouth as tiny stars that ring when they hit the ground.
plays.response: Glassreach is Extreme Cold. At the end of each hour, each creature makes a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gains 1 Exhaustion level; Resistance or Immunity to Cold damage means automatic success, and so does a warm cloak or other cold-weather gear (house rule kept from v5). Each Exhaustion level is −2 to every d20 Test and −5 feet of Speed; a long rest removes one. Yara sells warm cloaks at her camp for 10 gp or a keep each, or trades one for a good tool. Telegraph it: the first failed save is a character's hands going white.
plays.consequence: Gear matters, and so does Yara.
plays.fallback: If a player is sliding toward a third level, Yara throws a cloak at them and puts it on their tab.
plays.tells: Nobody mentions cloaks, or a player asks how cold it really is.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold (DMG 2024): DC 10 Constitution save hourly or 1 Exhaustion level. Warm cloak or Cold Resistance: automatic success. Exhaustion: −2 per level to d20 Tests, −5 ft Speed; long rest removes 1.
plays.later: S11–S14: every hour in the glass is another save for anyone without a cloak; climbing the Spire at two Exhaustion levels is −4 on each Athletics check. S15: the woken Stilled need cloaks too.
plays.keywords: cold, extreme cold, freeze, freezing, exhaustion, warm cloak, gear, frostbite, constitution, winter, glassreach

plays.title: They befriend Yara Thenn
plays.why: She sells what they need, knows every safe path, and is funny.
plays.readAloud: “I'll tell you where the safe paths are. You tell me why you're going to the Sexton. Nobody goes to the Sexton for a pleasant chat. And if you're going to die, I'd like to know what for, so I can sell the story.”
plays.response: Yara sells glass-cutting tools (5 gp), warm cloaks and maps; she haggles constantly and prefers favours or good tools to coin. Befriending her needs honesty about the Sexton (Influence DC 15, with advantage if they tell her the truth). Friendly, she gives them the map of safe paths: advantage on Survival in Glassreach and no wandering Glass-Wolves on the marked paths. What she wants most is a map of the Frost Spire, because nobody has ever drawn one.
plays.consequence: The party has safe paths and a guide who will come as far as the Stilled Clearing.
plays.fallback: If they insult her, she still sells them cloaks, at double price, and the map stays in her pocket.
plays.tells: Players haggle, joke back, or ask about the Sexton.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Yara starts Indifferent). Survival with her map: advantage.
plays.later: S14: a friendly Yara shows them the old Sexton's stair on the north face (one fewer climbing check). S15: a sketch of the Spire drawn at the top earns her loyalty (s15-yara-map). S30: Yara finally opens her brother's glass-flower.
plays.keywords: yara, thenn, scavenger, camp, map, safe paths, guide, haggle, buy, tools, cloaks

plays.title: They ask about the flower Yara won't sell
plays.why: Players notice the one thing a merchant refuses to price.
plays.readAloud: It sits in a felt-lined box: a single glass rose, and inside it something moves like a laugh caught in a jar. “That's not for sale,” Yara says, and shuts the box before you can see the colour.
plays.response: It holds a moment of her dead brother Teo's laugh, and she has never opened it because she is afraid it will shatter. It cannot be bought or stolen: if anyone tries, she closes the camp to them. If someone shares a true memory of their own grief with her, freely, she tells them about Teo and the winter that took him, and the giver earns Heroic Inspiration. A Bell-Touched character can tell her it will not shatter; that is true, and she does not believe it yet.
plays.consequence: Yara trusts them with the one thing she owns that matters.
plays.fallback: If they push, she says, 'Some things you keep because you can't afford what they cost,' and changes the subject to cloaks.
plays.tells: A player asks to buy it, or asks why she keeps it.
plays.rules: Heroic Inspiration for a memory given freely to someone who needs it (v6 generosity rule).
plays.later: S15: as the thaw spreads, glass-flowers soften, and Yara has to decide whether to open hers before it melts. S30: she opens it.
plays.keywords: glass-flower, flower, rose, brother, teo, laugh, not for sale, yara, buy, steal, grief

plays.title: They free the Stilled child
plays.why: A frozen child in a clearing is the clearest call to act in the forest.
plays.readAloud: “The man in the tower was sad. He sang to us so we wouldn't be afraid. Then he stopped singing, and the winter kept going, and we couldn't move anymore. Is it still winter out there?”
plays.response: The deer, the fox and the child stand mid-step in the Stilled Clearing. Cutting her free with glass-cutting tools is DC 14 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) and harms nothing; smashing it is DC 17 Strength and sends cracks into the deer and fox, which shatter and die. Any 20 Fire or Lightning damage to the glass melts it safely. She wakes, says her one true sentence, and freezes again within a minute; she does not attack. If child peril is Off-limits at your table, she is an old woman who was a child when the winter came.
plays.consequence: They know the Sexton once sang to the Stilled, and that the winter kept going when he stopped.
plays.fallback: If they won't touch her, Wyn Talla asks them to, because the woman in the glass she has kept watch over is three trees away and she needs to know it can be done.
plays.tells: A player kneels by the child, or asks whether she is alive.
plays.rules: Sleight of Hand DC 14 with glass-cutting tools, or Strength DC 17 to smash. 20 Fire or Lightning damage at the glass melts it.
plays.later: S12: 'The man in the tower was sad' tells them he can be talked to. S15: after Hieme rings, she is among the first to wake for good, and she asks for her mother.
plays.keywords: child, stilled child, girl, wake, free, break glass, cut, clearing, deer, fox, frozen

plays.title: A Faerûnian character recognises a Stilled sailor
plays.why: Some of the Stilled are Sword Coast sailors from before the Quiet Night, and a Stormborn character will know the cut of their coats.
plays.readAloud: Among the Stilled at the clearing's edge stands a man in a sea-coat cut four hundred years out of fashion, a brass badge on his breast: a ship under three stars, the old arms of a Tethyrian merchant house.
plays.response: A Sword Coast character recognises the badge with a DC 10 Intelligence (History) check; a sailor knows it outright. He is Bosun Corran Vell of the carrack Brightwater, out of Zazesspur, Stilled in 2 SS. Melted gently (fire at the glass, or Yara's tools), he wakes Hostile from shock but not violent at once; Influence DC 15 in Common calms him. He speaks an old dialect of Common, asks what year it is ('Is it still ten hundred and eighty-two?'), and says the Brightwater's crew are somewhere in these trees.
plays.consequence: The Stilled include Faerûnians. Someone from the Sword Coast came looking for the Ringing Land four centuries ago and never went home.
plays.fallback: If no one is Faerûnian, Yara points at the badge: 'Loudfolk. Old ones. There's a dozen of them by the stream.'
plays.tells: A Faerûnian or a sailor looks closely at the Stilled at the clearing's edge.
plays.rules: History DC 10. Influence DC 15 (Indifferent after a calm word). Comprehend Languages or Tongues helps with the old dialect, but any Common speaker gets the gist.
plays.later: S15: the Brightwater's crew wake with the thaw and want passage home through the Seam; getting them to Pellmoor earns a Stormborn ally for S22. S11: if not woken gently, Vell is one of the Stilled in the ambush.
plays.keywords: faerunian, stormborn, sailor, tethyr, zazesspur, badge, ship, brightwater, corran vell, old common, sword coast, year

plays.title: They leave the safe paths or split up
plays.why: The forest is beautiful, the Spire is visible, and the shortest line is never the safe one.
plays.readAloud: A crack like a whip, somewhere to your left. Then a howl that rings, high and pure, the way a wineglass does when you run a wet finger round its rim.
plays.response: Off Yara's paths the glass is thin and the Glass-Wolves hunt by sound. Telegraph first with the crack and the howl, then run Off the Path: every wolf that shatters cracks the glass around nearby Stilled, and two of them wake. If the party split, cut between the groups and bring them together at the Stilled Clearing when the howling starts.
plays.consequence: The wolves are a warning; the woken Stilled are the real cost.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, Yara's whistle from the path draws the wolves off; glass-wolves hate a high, steady note.
plays.tells: A player cuts across the glass, or the party splits to cover more ground.
plays.rules: Survival DC 15 to keep to a path without Yara's map. Extreme Cold saves continue through the fight.
plays.later: S11: the two Stilled who woke angry remember who cracked them, and the ambush has two fewer sleepers in it. S15: Stilled harmed now are slower to trust.
plays.keywords: off path, shortcut, split up, wander, explore, wolves, glass-wolves, lost, separate, scout ahead

plays.title: They use fire, Shatter or Thunderwave in the glass
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Fireball, and a forest of glass looks like a problem fire solves.
plays.readAloud: Yara grabs your wrist before the last word. “Not here. Not near them. You don't know what's inside the glass.”
plays.response: Be firm and say it before they cast: fire and lightning melt winter-moments, thunder shatters them. A Fireball in the clearing melts the glass around every Stilled in its area at once: the animals die, adults wake Hostile and in pain (they take the damage), and the child wakes and runs. Shatter or Thunderwave on a Stilled's glass breaks it with the person inside, who takes the damage and wakes screaming. Check session-zero Off-limits before the child is in the area. Every spell hums, so Yara hears it coming.
plays.consequence: Magic can wake the whole forest at once, but not gently.
plays.fallback: If they cast anyway, the waking adults run before they fight; give the party one round to choose calm or steel.
plays.tells: A caster asks what fire does to the glass, or starts the incantation.
plays.rules: Fire or lightning damage to a winter-moment melts it; 20 damage over the scene frees someone peacefully, more than that hurts. Thunder damage shatters it and the Stilled inside takes the damage. Tell the player before they commit.
plays.later: S11: an early Stilled Ambush. S15: the Stilled remember who woke them with fire, and their trust comes slower (stilled_trust is Wary).
