plays.keywords: fireball, fire, burn, melt, shatter, thunderwave, thunder, spell, glass, area spell, explode

plays.title: They meet Wyn Talla at Yara's camp
plays.why: The letter led here, and Wyn is waiting by the fire.
plays.readAloud: The old woman by the fire has a trapper's hands and a weaver's patience. 'My family has sat with her four hundred years,' she says. 'We call her the sister. The voice in the chapel is the first thing that ever answered us.'
plays.response: Wyn is Maren Talla's descendant; the Tallas have kept the vigil and the thaw song since the Quiet Night. The voice called itself I.V. and promised Maren would move again. Wyn asks them to wake her gently and is terrified they will use a hammer. She carries the family lullaby and will sing it when the glass warms.
plays.consequence: The party knows who they are freeing and why.
plays.fallback: If nobody goes to her, Wyn comes to them.
plays.tells: The party asks Yara who sent the letter, or looks for the old woman from Edrin's story.
plays.rules: No check. Wyn is Friendly to anyone who asks about Maren first.
plays.later: S11: Maren is one of the Stilled adults; the gentle route is s11-wake-gently. S15: Wyn leads the waking Stilled to Yara's camp.
plays.keywords: wyn talla, maren, family, descendant, vigil, sister, camp

plays.title: They rest at Yara's camp
plays.why: Extreme Cold punishes a long rest outside, so tables ask where it is safe.
plays.readAloud: Yara's camp is a ring of lashed tents around a banked fire. The stars here ring faintly, as if the sky were a glass left on a table.
plays.response: A long rest in Yara's tents is safe and warm if the party has cloaks or pays for a place (5 gp each or a keep). Outside, a long rest in Extreme Cold gains no benefit unless the character has warm gear or a fire; ask for a Constitution save at DC 10 and apply Exhaustion on a failure. Yara's whistle keeps the wolves off.
plays.consequence: The party is rested and the camp is a base for S11-S15.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, Yara charges them for the bed anyway.
plays.tells: A player asks where they can sleep, or how cold the night is.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold: DC 10 Constitution save each hour without gear. Long rest at camp removes one Exhaustion level as normal.
plays.later: S15: the camp becomes a hall for the waking Stilled.
plays.keywords: rest, camp, long rest, tents, sleep, warmth

plays.title: A character sees themselves in the glass
plays.why: This is the seed v5 plants for Act V; it happens to someone whether they look for it or not.
plays.readAloud: In a sheet of glass as tall as a door you see yourself. Older. Grey at the temples. Holding a small dark key in both hands, and smiling.
plays.response: Choose the character whose story is most tied to the bells, or the player who looked first. Do not explain it. Ask the player, “What does your character feel?” and write the answer down word for word. If they break the glass, every shard shows the same thing.
plays.consequence: A seed for Act V. Nothing changes now.
plays.fallback: If nobody looks, the glass shows it to the character on watch that night.
plays.tells: A player looks into a tall sheet of glass, or lingers alone.
plays.rules: No roll. Detect Magic shows nothing: it is not a spell.
plays.later: S26: the same figure stands at the foot of Ysh, older, holding the Key and smiling; read back what the player said here. S27: whether it was the Concord's Ringer or something else is the player's to decide.
plays.keywords: vision, reflection, glass, older self, key, smiling, mirror, future, winter-moment, h-18

plays.title: They damage the glass around a Stilled adult
plays.why: Waking the child worked; players try the same on the adults, or crack one by accident.
plays.readAloud: A crack runs up the glass like frost on a window. Inside, an eye moves. Then a hand. The man inside is screaming, and you cannot hear it until the glass breaks.
plays.response: Waking in pain and terror, an adult attacks whoever is closest, and the noise cracks the glass of others. Run the Stilled Ambush: they wake one or two a round, not all at once, so the party can see it growing and leave. A Stilled child does not attack; she speaks once and freezes again unless threatened. A Stilled who is spoken to mid-fight (Influence DC 15 as an action, in Hesk or old Common) stops, shaking, and becomes Indifferent.
plays.consequence: Some Stilled are hurt or broken; some may be calmed.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns grim, Maren Talla (if awake) stands in front of the next one and says its name.
plays.tells: A hammer raised to an adult's glass, or a fight near the Stilled.
plays.rules: Stilled Person (Gargoyle base): slow to start, hard to hurt through glass. Influence DC 15 as an action to calm one.
plays.later: S15: Stilled who were calmed rather than shattered are the first to trust the party. S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor only if that trust is earned.
plays.keywords: crack, break, hammer, wake, stilled, adult, ambush, attack, glass, fight

plays.title: They wake a Stilled adult slowly and kindly
plays.why: Wyn Talla wants her sister freed, and patient tables look for a way that isn't a hammer.
plays.readAloud: You wrap the glass in two cloaks and wait. It takes an hour. Water runs down the inside like tears, and then Maren Talla takes her first breath in four hundred and ten years.
plays.response: Melting with warmth over an hour (cloaks, a campfire, a held Produce Flame) or with glass-cutting tools (DC 14 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)) wakes a Stilled without pain. They wake confused and Indifferent, not hostile; give them a name to hear and they listen. Maren asks what year it is. Wyn, her descendant, tells her, kneeling in the ash, and sings the family's thaw song; Maren knows the tune. Maren knows one useful thing: the Sexton's chapel is past the second frozen stream, and he cannot bear to be argued with.
plays.consequence: One Stilled is free and grateful. Wyn has Maren back.
plays.fallback: If nobody has the patience, Wyn sits down by the glass to do it herself, and the party has to decide whether to leave her there.
plays.tells: Players ask whether warmth or time would do it.
plays.rules: An hour of warmth. Rescuers who gave up their cloaks make Extreme Cold saves. Sleight of Hand DC 14 with tools.
plays.later: S12: Maren's warning gives the party a free chance to stop arguing before the glass cracks. S15: Maren and Wyn lead the waking Stilled to Yara's camp, which counts toward the Stilled's trust.
plays.keywords: gentle, melt, warm, slow, wake, maren, wyn, talla, sister, kind, careful, produce flame

plays.title: They slip past the Stilled without waking them
plays.why: Stealthy parties avoid fights with victims.
plays.readAloud: You move between the frozen people like guests at a sleeping house. A wolf lifts its glass head somewhere in the trees, listens, and lowers it again.
plays.response: The Stilled act only when glass cracks; the Glass-Wolves are the danger. A group DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check gets everyone through; Yara's map gives advantage and Pass without Trace gives +10. On a failure, one wolf's howl cracks one Stilled's glass: a single adult wakes, not the full ambush, and the party can still leave.
plays.consequence: No fight, and no Stilled harmed.
plays.fallback: If they fail, describe the single waking adult as confused first and angry second, and let them choose.
plays.tells: Players ask which paths avoid the clearing, or cast Pass without Trace.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 13; advantage with Yara's map; Pass without Trace +10.
plays.later: S14: the Spire's guard pack is the same pack; if it never saw them, the party has surprise at the Spire.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, avoid, slip past, pass without trace, quiet, careful, bypass

plays.title: They shatter Stilled or question the dead ones
plays.why: Treating the Stilled as monsters is quick, and a cleric with Speak with Dead wants answers.
plays.readAloud: The glass comes apart in a sound like a chandelier falling. What was inside does not get up.
plays.response: Shattering a Stilled kills it; there is no reforming. Say so plainly the first time. Speak with Dead works on a shattered Stilled, since it is dead now: it remembers 2 SS, the first night of the winter, and a man in a tower singing so nobody would be afraid. The Stilled who remain remember who did the shattering.
plays.consequence: Lives ended, a little knowledge gained.
plays.fallback: If the table didn't realise the cost, let the next Stilled they approach flinch away from them.
plays.tells: A player goes for killing blows, or casts Speak with Dead on a broken body.
plays.rules: Speak with Dead (3rd level; the party is level 5): five questions; the corpse knows only what it knew in life. A living Stilled is not a valid target. Hearts lets the speaker understand the old dialect.
plays.later: S15: the Stilled don't trust the party if they shattered more than they saved (stilled_trust is Wary). S22: without that trust, the Stilled do not walk.
plays.keywords: shatter, kill, destroy, break, stilled, speak with dead, question, corpse, dead

plays.title: They talk the waking Stilled down
plays.why: The Stilled wake terrified and the party has just seen Maren.
plays.readAloud: The man in the glass is shouting at you with his mouth wide open and no sound. When it breaks, he is already speaking: 'The river! The river is cold!' You say his name.
plays.response: A Stilled who hears their name or a calm voice stops, shaking. Influence DC 15 as an action calms one (Indifferent); Calm Emotions calms a group. Hearts lets a caster answer in their dialect. A calmed Stilled stands behind the party and refuses to fight. The ambush ends when enough of them are calm.
plays.consequence: No Stilled is shattered. The party has earned trust.
plays.fallback: If the party fumbles, Maren Talla (if awake) stands in front of the next one and says its name.
plays.tells: A player says the name of one of the Stilled, or begins to speak in old Common.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 as an action, Hesk or old Common. Calm Emotions (Charisma save, unwilling only). Hearts: understand and speak any language.
plays.later: S15: calmed Stilled are the first to trust the party. S22: they walk to the Tor only if trust is earned.
plays.keywords: calm stilled, talk down, calm emotions, hearts, name, ambush

plays.title: They fight the Glass-Wolves, not the Stilled
plays.why: The wolves are the real danger; the Stilled are victims.
plays.readAloud: The nearest wolf shatters in a bright spray, and the winter-moment beside it cracks like a plate. A hand moves inside. 'Not that one,' Yara says. 'Not near them.'
plays.response: Each wolf that shatters cracks the nearest winter-moment, so the party must choose between a clean kill and a dangerous crack. Yara's whistle drives the wolves off if the party holds out three rounds. The wolves flee when half of them shatter.
plays.consequence: The wolves are driven off. The Stilled wake in smaller numbers.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, Yara's whistle draws the wolves off.
plays.tells: A player says 'protect the glass' or aims at a wolf.
plays.rules: Encounter: Stilled Ambush, wolves only. Shards: 1d6 slashing to creatures within 5 feet of a shattering wolf.
plays.later: S14: the Spire pack is this pack; if they killed many here, fewer guard the base.
plays.keywords: wolves, glass-wolf, fight wolves, protect glass, yara whistle

plays.title: They use magic to speak to, calm or read a Stilled
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Hearts, Calm Emotions, Detect Thoughts and Speak with Dead.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and the glass answers it in the same note. The man inside blinks.
plays.response: Detect Thoughts on a Stilled shows a mind frozen at its last moment: a river, a fire, a name. Hearts lets the caster hear and answer the old dialect. Calm Emotions quiets a waking Stilled. Speak with Dead works only on the dead. Dispel Magic does not end a winter-moment: it is Hieme's silence, not a spell.
plays.consequence: The caster learns what the Stilled saw and feels.
plays.fallback: If the spell fails, the Stilled's expression is answer enough.
plays.tells: A caster asks if a Stilled can be understood or whether they are alive.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts, Hearts, Calm Emotions as written. Dispel Magic: no effect. See any-l3-third-level-spells.
plays.later: S12: they can ask the Sexton better questions. S15: the Stilled trust a caster who spoke their heart.
plays.keywords: hearts, calm emotions, detect thoughts, stilled, magic on glass

plays.title: They sit in the pews and listen
plays.why: He asks them to sit, he asks a question, and he has waited four centuries for an answer.
plays.readAloud: “Oh, look. Visitors. Children of the Court, I imagine. You carry the stink of memory-ink on your hands. Sit, please. I have waited so long to say something to someone who might understand. Who rules the Court now? I have not heard its name spoken in four centuries.”
plays.response: The Sexton does not attack unless the glass around him breaks or someone argues with him. He wants to be asked questions, and his first is his own. If they say Maudrin Vesk, he is silent a long time, then: “Vesk. Then it stayed in the family.” He will not explain until he has made his confession (S13). An hour of patient listening earns his trust: the confession begins without a check.
plays.consequence: The Sexton has an audience at last, and he is ready to confess.
plays.fallback: If no one answers his question, he answers it himself: “Still a Vesk, I suppose. It always was.”
plays.tells: Players sit, or answer his question about the Court.
plays.rules: The Sexton starts Indifferent; patient listening makes him Friendly, no roll. Influence DC 15 otherwise.
plays.later: S13: the 'listen patiently' route is already half done; he offers the Frost Heart at the end of his confession (s13-listen-confession). S13: asked about the Key, he wants to know who holds it and the party has not yet told him; he asks again.
plays.keywords: listen, sit, pews, sexton, imber, sermon, question, who rules, court, maudrin, talk

plays.title: They resist the sermon's pull
plays.why: The sermon works on everyone in the chapel, and players want to know what it is doing to them.
plays.readAloud: “Quiet is the gift of the Silence. Memory is the burden of the living. Give your burdens up. Be still. Be at rest. There is no shame in forgetting.” After a while you realise you haven't spoken in some time, and that you don't especially want to.
plays.response: Each hour in the chapel, each listener makes a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure the character does not want to speak: they act and move freely and can talk if they choose, but have disadvantage on Charisma checks against the Sexton until they leave the chapel or finish a Short Rest. It never takes control of a character. In a fight the same sermon becomes his Sermon of Stillness (Charmed until the end of its next turn, Speed 0). Lost travelers (Hobb, a Kell's Crossing carter, and his two grown sons) sit in the pews and have not spoken in days; leading them out by the hand restores their voices within an hour.
plays.consequence: The sermon is a pressure, not a prison.
plays.fallback: If the table finds it oppressive, let any character break the spell by saying a dead friend's name aloud.
plays.tells: A player asks why nobody is talking, or wants to shake it off.
plays.rules: Wisdom save DC 15, hourly. Failure: disadvantage on Charisma checks against the Sexton. Not the Charmed condition out of combat. In combat the Sermon is DC 15 and applies Charmed with Speed 0; Calm Emotions can suppress Charmed. Leaving the chapel ends the out-of-combat effect.
plays.later: S13: in a fight the sermon becomes his Phase 1 ability (DC 15 Wisdom, Charmed until the end of its next turn). S15: Hobb's family carries news of the thaw south to Kell's Crossing.
plays.keywords: sermon, resist, wisdom, silence, quiet, charm, speak, voice, travelers, mute

plays.title: They argue with the Sexton
plays.why: The sermon says forgetting is a gift; players who have seen the Blanks will say no.
plays.readAloud: The word goes up into the vaults like a stone thrown at a window. The glass of the pulpit sings, very high, and a crack runs down it like a tear.
plays.response: Arguing raises his voice and cracks the glass. Give them a clear chance: he stops and asks, “Do you wish me to go on?” They can de-escalate (an apology, or a question instead of an answer), leave, or keep pushing. If they keep provoking his unstable prison, or attack him, begin Phase 1 (the Glass Sexton encounter).
plays.consequence: The party knows exactly where the line is.
plays.fallback: If the player won't yield, Maren Talla (if awake) or Yara tugs them out of the chapel before the second crack.
plays.tells: A player answers the sermon back, or calls him a liar.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 to de-escalate: argument makes him Hostile, and one sincere apology returns him to Indifferent.
plays.later: S13: arguing again starts the fight; the listen-patiently route stays open only if they stepped back here.
plays.keywords: argue, disagree, debate, shout, contradict, liar, sermon, crack, provoke, sexton

plays.title: A character comes to agree with the sermon
plays.why: The sermon is accurate about the cost of memory; a character who has paid Tolls may find it persuasive.
plays.readAloud: “There is no shame in forgetting,” the Sexton says gently, and for a moment it is the kindest thing anyone has said to you in Corvane.
plays.response: Let it be real. The Sexton is delighted and asks what they would set down if they could. Nothing is taken: he has no Reckoner and no Tithe. The character keeps this belief as long as the player wants; ask whether it changes what they would ring, and note it. The Sexton trusts this character above the others and speaks to them first in S13.
plays.consequence: A party member sympathises with the Silence. That is a story, not a problem.
plays.fallback: If the rest of the party objects, let the argument happen between players, not with the Sexton.
plays.tells: A player says, quietly, “He's not wrong.”
plays.rules: No mechanical effect. Optionally the player rewrites one belief, as with a heartkeep sale; never a loss of control.
plays.later: S13: he confesses to this character first and offers them the Frost Heart. S26: this character's view weighs on whether Ysh is sealed, struck or tuned.
plays.keywords: agree, sympathise, convinced, persuaded, forget, peace, rest, sermon, believe

plays.title: They lead the silent travelers out
plays.why: Three mute strangers in the pews are an obvious rescue.
plays.readAloud: The carter's hand is cold and very heavy, like a child's when it is asleep. He stands when you pull. His sons stand when he does.
plays.response: Hobb and his sons follow anyone who leads them. The walk to Yara's camp is two hours of Extreme Cold and they have no cloaks. Their voices come back within an hour of leaving the chapel. Hobb asks what the man in the glass was, and whether they should go home or wait for the winter to end.
plays.consequence: Three people are free and owe the party.
plays.fallback: If nobody bothers, Yara does it the next morning and charges the party for the cloaks.
plays.tells: A player takes a traveler's hand, or asks who they are.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold for the travelers (Commoners): without cloaks, they gain Exhaustion like anyone else.
plays.later: S15: they help Yara feed the waking Stilled. If Calla rang (S9), they go home to green fields at Kell's Crossing and spread the party's name there.
plays.keywords: travelers, rescue, lead out, carter, hobb, sons, silent, mute, help, escort

plays.title: They cast Silence or plug their ears
plays.why: The sermon is sound, and the obvious counter is to stop hearing it.
plays.readAloud: The sound goes out of the chapel like a candle snuffed. The Sexton stops mid-sentence and tilts his head. 'Ah,' he says, with no sound at all. 'You are not listening.'
plays.response: Silence (the spell) or deafening works: the sermon needs to be heard, so no save is needed inside. Nobody inside can cast a spell with a Verbal component or speak. The Sexton notices and goes still. He is Hostile unless the party explains; if they drop the Silence and apologise, he returns to Indifferent. A silence-stone field would stop Hieme's winter-moments altogether, but there is none here.
plays.consequence: The party can walk the chapel unaffected but cannot talk. The Sexton is wary.
plays.fallback: If the Silence breaks his patience, he cracks a pew and asks, in a voice that carries through the glass, 'Do you wish me to go on?'
plays.tells: A caster asks whether the sermon needs to be heard, or a player stuffs wax in their ears.
plays.rules: Silence (spell, 2nd level): 20-foot sphere, no sound, immune to Thunder; no Verbal spells. A deafened creature is immune to the sermon.
plays.later: S13: his trust is lower; the listen route needs an apology (s12-argue).
plays.keywords: silence spell, earplugs, deafened, mute the sermon, plug ears

plays.title: They try to take the Heart from his crown
plays.why: The Heart is a glittering clapper in a glass crown, and Mage Hand is a cantrip.
plays.readAloud: The invisible hand closes on the Heart and the crown rings, once, a high thin note. Every pane in the chapel answers.
plays.response: The Heart is frozen into the winter-moment and part of the crown, so Mage Hand, Telekinesis or a hand-grab cannot pull it free. Forcing it cracks the glass around his head; the Sexton asks, 'Do you wish me to go on?' If they keep going, begin Phase 1. The peaceful ways remain: his confession (S13) or melting him gently.
plays.consequence: The party learns the Heart cannot be stolen quietly.
plays.fallback: If the party backs off, he forgives it with a sigh.
plays.tells: A player asks what the crown is made of, or whether Mage Hand can reach.
plays.rules: Mage Hand cannot take an object fused into a winter-moment. Strength (Athletics) DC 20 to prise it out cracks the glass and starts the fight.
plays.later: S13: the confession gives it freely (s13-listen-confession).
plays.keywords: mage hand, telekinesis, steal heart, crown, grab

plays.title: They attack the Sexton on sight
plays.why: A glass priest with a sermon is a boss to a table that wants a fight.
plays.readAloud: The Sexton rises inside his pulpit, and the glass of his body is suddenly very sharp. 'You came to my church,' he says, 'to shout?'
plays.response: Give one last chance to stop: he asks, 'Do you wish me to go on?' If they attack, run the Glass Sexton encounter (enc-s13-glass-sexton) from the stat block: frost-form 95 HP, then broken-form 45 HP. Leaving ends it; he does not pursue. The confession route stays open only if they stop and apologise.
plays.consequence: The fight begins. The shell can break (s13-sexton-shell-breaks).
plays.fallback: If the party is losing, he stops at the end of a round in which nobody struck him and asks, 'Have we finished?'
plays.tells: Weapons drawn at the pulpit before he finishes speaking.
plays.rules: Encounter: Glass Sexton. Sermon DC 15. Counterspell does nothing to his Sermon or Icicle Volley: they are not spells.
plays.later: S13: a beaten Imber still confesses, but tells what the Key is only if asked kindly.
plays.keywords: attack sexton, fight, glass priest, boss

plays.title: They lie when the Sexton asks who rules the Court
plays.why: A party wary of Vesk blood may not want to tell him it is Maudrin.
plays.readAloud: The Sexton's head tilts. 'Ilse Vesk,' you say, because it is the first name that comes. 'Then it is Ilse,' he says. 'Good. Children of the Court, you are so young. Ilse was my grandniece. She was a very small girl.'
plays.response: Four centuries out of date, he accepts a name he half-knows but notices what does not fit. Deception DC 15 against his Insight (+4); on a failure he says, 'That is not how a Vesk would answer', and trust is spent. He is Indifferent still, but the patient listen no longer works without an honest answer later.
plays.consequence: The Sexton knows he is being lied to, or believes it.
plays.fallback: If the player confesses, he nods and says nothing for a long time.
plays.tells: A player says 'nobody', 'the Church', or names a stranger.
plays.rules: Deception DC 15 (Insight +4). A sincere correction restores the listen route.
plays.later: S13: the confession needs an honest answer to 'who holds the Key?'.
plays.keywords: lie, who rules the court, maudrin, vesk, deceive sexton

plays.title: They split: one lures Hobb out while another stays
plays.why: One character can lead the silent travelers to safety while the others hold the Sexton's attention.
plays.readAloud: The carter's hand is cold and heavy. Behind you, the Sexton's voice goes on, level and kind, like water over stones.
plays.response: Cut between the two groups. The one who leads Hobb's family out faces Extreme Cold for two hours; Yara or Maren (if awake) meets them. The group that stays must keep him talking: an hour of patient listening earns trust. If the sermon takes someone, bring the others back.
plays.consequence: Hobb's family is out, the Sexton is calmer.
plays.fallback: If the split goes wrong, regroup at the chapel door.
plays.tells: A player says 'I'll take them out' while another stays to talk.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold for the travelers (Commoners). Wisdom save DC 15 hourly for those who stay.
plays.later: S15: Hobb's family helps Yara feed the waking Stilled.
plays.keywords: split party, lure hobb, travelers, divide, scout

plays.title: They listen to the whole confession
plays.why: He has waited 380 years to say it, and patient tables let him.
plays.readAloud: “I ordered her to tune them into one long spring. Edda refused, and she wrote it down for me, so that I could never say I did not know. I tuned them anyway. The Key sang against the bells, and the bells cracked on the discord. I have been sorry for four hundred years.”
plays.response: He tells the Quiet Night plainly: the order, Edda's written warning, the Key singing against the bells. He does not say what the Key truly is: 'The Key was never mine to use. I know that now.' At the end he asks someone to lift the crown from his glass head, where the Frost Heart is set; the glass gives it up to him freely. Then he asks them to end his winter and take him with them, so he can finish his sermon somewhere it can be heard (s13-free-sexton).
plays.consequence: The party holds the Frost Heart and the confession of the Quiet Night's only living witness.
plays.fallback: If the table gets restless, he skips to the end: 'Take the crown. I am too tired to wear it.'
plays.tells: Players stay seated and ask him what happened on the Quiet Night.
plays.rules: No roll for a patient audience. If they read Edda's diary to him (s13-read-diary-to-imber), he weeps and the glass fogs. His age: he has been in the glass since 32 SS, three hundred and eighty years; the Stilled around him have been frozen since 2 SS, four hundred and ten.
plays.later: S14: Hieme can be rung. S22: the confession is a source for the truth of the Key, alongside the diary and the Notes. S30: the Glass Sexton finishes his sermon.
plays.keywords: confession, listen, quiet night, imber, sexton, story, frost heart, crown, edda, patient

plays.title: They ask him about the Key
plays.why: Maudrin's last word mentioned the Key and 'family'; players will ask.
plays.readAloud: He is silent so long you think the winter has taken him. Then: “The Key passed to my daughter, Cassia, when I was disgraced. It stayed in the family's reliquary. Who holds it now? Tell me, and I will tell you what it is.”
plays.response: If they name Maudrin Vesk, he keeps his word: “It is not a tool. It is the Seventh's heart. It sings the Dreamer to sleep, and I struck the other bells with it to make the calendar behave.” He describes the Vesk reliquary as it was: a vault beneath the family chapel, now under the white palace, with a lock and a weighted tether on the case. He does not know what Maudrin intends. If they refuse to tell him who holds it, he says nothing more about it.
plays.consequence: The party learns early what the Key is.
plays.fallback: If they don't ask, he asks them, near the end: 'Who has the Key now? Someone must.'
plays.tells: A player says “the Key” or “Maudrin” out loud.
plays.rules: No roll. Session numbers are not information locks (Part 9, Situation 15): let them plan around what they learn.
plays.later: S22: the truth of the Key becomes confirmation, not revelation. Act IV (Situation 4): his description reveals the tether without a roll and gives advantage on the DC 16 lock if they rob the palace before Maudrin leaves. S24: Maudrin realises they know, and stops bargaining on that point.
plays.keywords: key, tuning key, ask, cassia, reliquary, maudrin, what is it, seventh, dreamer, oum, ysh

plays.title: They break the glass and free Imber
plays.why: He asks them to, and a man frozen for 380 years is hard to leave.
plays.readAloud: The glass runs like wax. Inside it there is only an old man in wet ceremonial robes, thin as a rake, shaking so hard his teeth click. “Oh,” he says. “It is cold.”
plays.response: A DC 15 Strength check breaks the glass, or 20 Fire or Lightning damage to it over the scene melts it without harming him (two or three Fire Bolts, one Burning Hands, a Produce Flame held for a minute). As he is freed Imber lifts the crown from his own head and presses the Frost Heart into their hands. Freed, he is old and frail (Commoner statistics) and does not attack. He needs a warm cloak at once: Extreme Cold applies to him now. He keeps confessing as they walk, and asks to see the Frost Spire before anything else.
plays.consequence: The High Sexton of the Quiet Night walks again, and he is a Vesk.
plays.fallback: If the Strength check fails, Yara's saw does it in ten minutes with no roll.
plays.tells: A player asks how to free him, or reaches for fire.
plays.rules: Strength DC 15, or 20 Fire or Lightning damage aimed at the glass. Freed Imber uses Commoner stats; Extreme Cold applies. Thunder damage shatters the glass and hurts him.
plays.later: S14: if Hieme rings while he lives, he weeps, and the thaw reaches him last. S15: Isolde sees a second Vesk with a claim to the Key, which is the thing the Court fears most (s15-isolde-wants-imber). S22: he is a living witness against Maudrin.
plays.keywords: free, break glass, melt, release, imber, sexton, rescue, fire, strength, thaw

plays.title: They argue on or attack the Sexton
plays.why: Tables that hate the Silence, or think a glass priest is a boss to beat, will push.
plays.readAloud: The pews crack one after another, like ice on a pond in spring. The Sexton rises inside his pulpit, and the glass of his body is suddenly very sharp. “You came to my church,” he says, “to shout?”
plays.response: Arguing again cracks the glass around him; give them one last chance to stop or leave. If they attack him or keep provoking, run the Glass Sexton from the stat block: frost-form with 95 HP until it shatters, then broken-form with 45 HP. When Phase 2 breaks, the Frost Heart falls from his crown onto the ice, and the Ringer can grab it before the glass reforms (free if they are adjacent when it falls, otherwise DC 12 Dexterity (Acrobatics) from up to 10 feet). At 0 HP the shell breaks and the frail Imber survives, unless someone deliberately kills him. When it does, play s13-sexton-shell-breaks.
plays.consequence: The fight is joined. Nothing about the Heart or Imber changes until the shell breaks.
plays.fallback: If the party is losing, he stops at the end of a round in which nobody struck him and asks, 'Have we finished?'
plays.tells: A second argument after the first crack, or weapons drawn at the pulpit.
plays.rules: Glass Sexton, two phases. Counterspell does nothing to his Sermon or Icicle Volley: they are not spells. Sermon: DC 15 Wisdom or Charmed until the end of its next turn, Speed 0. Shattering: DC 15 Dexterity when frost-form ends. Calm Emotions can suppress Charmed.
plays.later: S14: they can ring Hieme once the shell breaks. S15: a beaten Imber still confesses, but tells what the Key is only if asked kindly. S22: a witness who was beaten is still a witness.
plays.keywords: fight, attack, sexton, boss, combat, phase, glass, kill, argue, provoke, frost heart

plays.title: They kill Imber Vesk
plays.why: He caused the Quiet Night; some players want justice, and some want a Vesk out of the way.
plays.readAloud: He doesn't raise his hands. He only says, “I know,” and closes his eyes.
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' He is frail, unarmed and weeping, whether freed or still in the glass (shattering the glass kills him with it). If they do it, he dies and the glass around the chapel goes dull. The Frost Heart falls from the crown. Say plainly that the only living witness of the Quiet Night is gone.
plays.consequence: Imber Vesk is dead.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, he asks only that they finish his sermon for him someday.
plays.tells: A weapon raised over the frail old man after the fight, or at his release.
plays.rules: No roll. Imber has Commoner stats.
plays.later: S14: Hieme still rings, but no one weeps for the winter. S22: the truth of the Key rests on the diary, the Notes or the Librarian. S24: Maudrin hears of it and thanks them, sincerely, which should feel terrible.
plays.keywords: kill imber, execute, murder, revenge, justice, sexton, slay, vesk

plays.title: They use magic to read or free the Sexton
plays.why: Level-5 casters have Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth and Dispel Magic, and will try them on a man in a block of ice.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums in the frozen chapel, and every pane of glass answers it in the same note. The Sexton smiles. “Ah. Tonework. I had almost forgotten the sound.”
plays.response: Detect Thoughts works (he is a living mind in glass): his surface thought is a lullaby and the name Cassia. Zone of Truth is pointless and he says so: 'I have not told a lie since 32 SS; there has been no one to tell it to.' Dispel Magic does not end a winter-moment: it is Hieme's silence, not a spell, and silence-stone has no effect on it either. Fire Bolt, Produce Flame or any fire or lightning frees him gently once the glass has taken 20 damage over the scene; Shatter or Thunderwave breaks the glass and hurts him, and out of the glass he is frail.
plays.consequence: Magic can free him gently, or kill him by accident.
plays.fallback: If a spell fails, he offers the answer anyway; he has nothing to hide any more.
plays.tells: A caster asks if he's under a spell, or whether he's lying.
plays.rules: Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth: work, little gained. Dispel Magic: no effect. 20 Fire or Lightning damage to the ice melts it; thunder shatters it and damages him. See s13-free-sexton.
plays.later: S15: whoever freed him with fire is the one he asks to carry him.
plays.keywords: detect thoughts, zone of truth, dispel magic, fire bolt, produce flame, shatter, spell, magic, read mind, free

plays.title: They take the Heart and leave him in the glass
plays.why: Freeing a man who caused the Quiet Night is not obvious, and he is a Vesk.
plays.readAloud: “Then tell me when it rings,” he says to your backs. “I would like to know when the winter ends, even if I am the last to feel it.”
plays.response: He asked to be taken with them. If they refuse, he does not fight; the glass lets the Heart out of the crown when he asks it to. He asks only that they tell him when the bell rings. When Hieme rings, the thaw reaches him last: he wakes some weeks later, alone, in an empty chapel.
plays.consequence: The Sexton stays frozen for now; the Frost Heart goes with the party.
plays.fallback: If they change their minds on the way out, the glass is still warm where they touched it.
plays.tells: The party takes the crown and heads for the door.
plays.later: S15: if they leave him, Isolde finds him before the party does; a Court-held Imber is a Vesk with a claim to the Key, in Maudrin's hands (s15-isolde-takes-imber). S22: he is no witness for them unless they rescue him.
plays.keywords: leave him, abandon, walk away, frozen, refuse, don't free, sexton

plays.title: The Sexton's shell breaks
plays.why: They fought him and won, or stopped him when it broke.
plays.readAloud: The last of the glass falls away. What stands in the pulpit is an old man in wet robes, thin as a rake, shaking so hard his teeth click. The Frost Heart lies on the ice.
plays.response: The frail Imber survives unless someone deliberately kills him. He needs a cloak at once and asks, 'Have we finished?' The Ringer takes the Frost Heart from the ice. He is old, frail (Commoner statistics) and willing to confess if asked kindly.
plays.consequence: The Heart is with the party. Imber is freed.
plays.fallback: If the party hesitates, Imber holds out the crown himself.
plays.tells: Broken-form reaches 0 HP.
plays.rules: Imber uses Commoner stats; Extreme Cold applies.
plays.later: S14: they can ring Hieme. S15: Isolde sees a second Vesk (s15-isolde-wants-imber).
plays.keywords: shell breaks, defeated, imber survives, frost heart falls

plays.title: They read Edda's diary to Imber
plays.why: Edda's words are the last honest account of the Quiet Night, and the Sexton never heard them.
plays.readAloud: You read Edda's entry in a low voice. The glass fogs. When you reach the last line, the Sexton says, quietly, 'She told me. She wrote it down so I could not say I did not know.'
plays.response: He weeps, and the Frost Heart comes out of the crown into the Ringer's hand without a fight. He asks them to read the last page again, and to take him away from here afterward. The diary shows him what the Key does.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Heart and Imber's trust.
plays.fallback: If they do not have the diary, they read from memory.
plays.tells: A player takes out the diary, or asks if Edda wrote to him.
plays.rules: No roll. Requires the diary (taken in S5 or read at the vault and carried in memory).
plays.later: S14: Hieme can be rung. S22: the diary and his confession agree.
plays.keywords: read diary, edda thorne, weep, trust

plays.title: They take care of the freed Imber
plays.why: A frail man in wet robes in a glass forest is a duty.
plays.readAloud: 'It is cold,' Imber says again, wonderingly, as if the word were new. 'I had forgotten it was a thing a person could feel.'
plays.response: Imber needs a warm cloak, food and a pace he can keep. He wants to see the Frost Spire before anything else, and asks to finish his sermon 'somewhere it can be heard'. Yara allows him in the camp. His age shows: he has been in the glass for three hundred and eighty years.
plays.consequence: Imber is alive and travelling with the party.
plays.fallback: If the party wavers, Yara hands him a cloak and charges the party for it.
plays.tells: A player offers a cloak, or asks where Imber should go.
plays.rules: Extreme Cold applies. Commoner HP. Constitution save DC 10 hourly without a cloak.
plays.later: S14: he follows to the Spire and weeps when Hieme rings. S15: Isolde sees him (s15-isolde-wants-imber).
plays.keywords: imber, freed sexton, cloak, escort, care

plays.title: They climb the Frost Spire
plays.why: The bell is two hundred feet up a tower of ice, and most parties climb.
plays.readAloud: A spire of ice rises from the centre of the glass forest like a frozen fountain. Inside it the bell hangs motionless, locked in frost. Every breath you take freezes on the air. The bell is singing, so softly you hear it only in your teeth.
plays.response: About 200 feet of ice. Three DC 14 Strength (Athletics) checks get a climber to the top; a failure is a slip: the climber falls 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning) and starts that check again. A rope team lets one climber Help another (advantage) on each check. If Yara is Friendly she shows the old Sexton's stair on the north face, which removes one check. Exhaustion from the cold applies its -2 per level to every check.
plays.consequence: They reach the bell.
plays.fallback: If the climbers keep slipping, let them find the old Sexton's stair cut into the ice on the north face: slower, one extra hour of cold, no checks.
plays.tells: Players ask about rope, pitons, or how high it is.
plays.rules: Athletics DC 14, three times. Fall: 20 feet, 2d6 bludgeoning. Help gives advantage. Exhaustion: −2 per level. Extreme Cold saves continue hourly.
plays.later: S15: a sketch of the Spire drawn at the top earns Yara's loyalty (s15-yara-map). S14: anyone who reaches the bell can be the Ringer.
plays.keywords: climb, spire, frost spire, athletics, rope, ice, fall, ascend, tower, top

plays.title: They fly, levitate or Spider Climb up the Spire
plays.why: At level 6, Fly, Spider Climb and Misty Step are on most casters' lists.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and the Spire hums back, a half-note higher. At its foot, glass heads lift and turn toward the sound.
plays.response: It works. The Spire holds no silence-stones; Hieme is silent, not suppressing. Fly or Spider Climb skips the checks, Misty Step covers 30 feet at a time, and Levitate needs someone pulling a rope. The Glass-Wolves at the base hear the hum and come running, and the Stilled on the ice stairs turn their heads.
plays.consequence: A fast ascent, with the guards roused.
plays.fallback: If concentration breaks mid-air, the fall rules apply from that height; telegraph the wind before it happens (there is none, which is the point).
plays.tells: A caster asks whether anything stops magic here.
plays.rules: Fly, Spider Climb, Levitate and Misty Step as written. Every spell hums; the Spire guards notice.
plays.later: S15: whoever flew can bring the Heart down quickly if Isolde arrives.
plays.keywords: fly, levitate, spider climb, misty step, magic, spell, flight, teleport, climb

plays.title: They fight the Spire's guards
plays.why: Glass-Wolves at the base and Stilled on the stairs stand between them and the bell.
plays.readAloud: The wolves at the base of the Spire were lying so still you took them for ice. Then all of them stand up at once.
plays.response: Glass-Wolves guard the base; Stilled watch from the ice stairs and move only when glass breaks or a climber passes within 5 feet. Run the Spire Guards. Each wolf shatters when it drops (shards: 1d6 slashing to creatures within 5 feet), and each shattering cracks the ice stairs a little more. The Stilled stop fighting the moment the bell rings.
plays.consequence: The way to the bell is open.
plays.fallback: If the fight drags, the bell's hum rises and the Stilled pause, listening, for a full round.
plays.tells: The party approaches the base openly.
plays.rules: A Stilled that hits a climber forces a DC 12 Strength saving throw or the climber slips and falls 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning). Tell the climber before they pass one.
plays.later: S15: Stilled who fought here wake with the thaw and remember; spared or calmed ones count toward the Stilled's trust.
plays.keywords: fight, wolves, glass-wolves, stilled, guards, base, battle, combat, spire

plays.title: They sneak past the guards
plays.why: Parties that avoided the ambush in S11 will try the same here.
plays.readAloud: You pass so close to the nearest wolf that you can see the bubble of air frozen in its eye.
plays.response: A group DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) check gets the party to the foot of the climb; Yara's map gives advantage and Pass without Trace gives +10. If they were never seen in S11, they also have surprise if it comes to blows. A distraction works too: a thrown glass-flower, a whistle, a Minor Illusion of a running deer draws the pack for two rounds.
plays.consequence: They begin the climb unseen.
plays.fallback: If one character fails, one wolf follows them alone, and the rest sleep on.
plays.tells: Players ask about cover, wind, or a distraction.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 14. Pass without Trace +10. Surprise if undetected in S11.
plays.later: S14: climbing still hums if they use magic; a mundane climb stays quiet.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, avoid, distraction, pass without trace, quiet, hide, slip past

plays.title: They ring Hieme
plays.why: They carried the Frost Heart up two hundred feet of ice for this.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings once. The sound is high and thin and clear, like a single thread of ice pulled across the sky. The frost on the Spire cracks. The glass trees hum. Everywhere in the forest, something begins to move. The winter is going. Not all at once, but slowly, like a tide turning back.
plays.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a Memory, chosen by the Ringer. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. When it rings, the thaw begins and the Stilled wake over several weeks. If the Sexton is alive, he weeps, wherever he is, and the thaw reaches him last. A Silence spell around the bell only keeps those inside the sphere from hearing it; the ringing still works, because a bell's tone is more than sound (a silence-stone field would stop it, which is why Vaer was chained).
plays.consequence: Hieme is rung. Glassreach begins to thaw.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, the bell's hum waits with them. A bell that waited four hundred years can wait an hour.
plays.tells: A player asks what it will cost.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Hieme: a Memory). Afterward, decide where the Frost Heart goes: left in the bell or carried on.
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S15: Isolde arrives with Hushmen for the Frost Heart. S22: the thawed Stilled walk to the Tor if trust is earned. Act IV: the Court's patience ends; its clock moves.
plays.keywords: ring, hieme, bell, toll, memory, frost spire, thaw, winter bell, ringer

plays.title: They strike Hieme without the Frost Heart
plays.why: The party left the Sexton's crown behind, or lost the Heart to Isolde, and tries a hammer.
plays.readAloud: The Spire groans before you strike it. The frost on the bell thickens, and your breath freezes in the air and falls like hail.
plays.response: Telegraph it first: the bronze rings dead, the Spire groans, and Yara (or Imber) calls out that the bell has no Heart and striking it will freeze the Spire. If they swing anyway, the frost surges. For the next ten minutes, Extreme Cold saves come every minute at DC 15 (warm gear still means automatic success), and the Glass-Wolves at the base wake. Descending at once ends the effect: every minute spent climbing down is one save, no more. No Toll is asked, because nothing rang.
plays.consequence: Nothing rings, and the cold bites hard.
plays.fallback: If a player insists on trying again, the Spire itself cracks a warning down its full length.
plays.tells: A player raises a weapon or a mallet to the bell.
plays.rules: Accelerated Extreme Cold: DC 15 Constitution save each minute for up to 10 minutes; cloaks and Cold Resistance still succeed automatically. Descent ends it immediately.
plays.later: S13: the Frost Heart is still in the Sexton's crown (s13-listen-confession), or in Isolde's hands; they need it.
plays.keywords: hammer, strike, hit bell, no heart, without heart, force, improvise, weapon

plays.title: They leave the Frost Heart in the bell
plays.why: Carrying a Heart makes you a target; a bell with its Heart looks complete.
plays.readAloud: The Heart hangs in the bell where it belongs, still faintly singing. Frost is already forming on it again, softer than before.
plays.response: The resonance persists even if the Heart is later removed, so leaving it is safe for the Concord. It also means Isolde has to climb to take it, which she will not do herself.
plays.consequence: The Frost Heart stays at the Spire.
plays.fallback: If they change their minds, it comes down with one more Athletics check.
plays.tells: After ringing, a player asks whether they need to take it down.
plays.rules: A repeat ringing later needs the Heart and another Toll, and renews the effect without stacking it.
plays.later: S15: Isolde demands it; the party can say 'Go and get it', and her Hushmen spend a day failing the climb. Act IV: the Court may send climbers later; it never undoes Hieme's ringing.
plays.keywords: leave heart, keep in bell, frost heart, leave behind, safe, spire

plays.title: Nobody will pay Hieme's Toll
plays.why: After Vaer, Calla or Ossa, some characters have nothing left they want to give.
plays.readAloud: The bell keeps its one soft note in your teeth, patient as snow.
plays.response: Nobody pays, and that is a real choice: record it. Hieme can be rung later; the Heart goes with them or stays. Do not shame it.
plays.consequence: Hieme stays silent and Glassreach stays frozen, for now.
plays.fallback: If the table wants a way forward, remind them that any willing character may be the Ringer, and that the Toll is a memory, not a life.
plays.tells: A long silence when you state the Toll.
plays.rules: No Toll is taken when a ringing is declined.
plays.later: S22: the Concord needs Hieme; the Second Dawn stays open without it. S15: Isolde still comes for the Heart.
plays.keywords: refuse, won't pay, no toll, decline, don't ring, wait, later

plays.title: They help the waking Stilled
plays.why: Hundreds of people are stepping out of a four-hundred-year winter with nothing, and the party caused it.
plays.readAloud: The forest drips. Everywhere, glass is turning back into bark and leaf, and people are stepping out of their own winters with their arms still raised, asking each other's names.
plays.response: The Stilled wake over several weeks, confused, angry or grateful, and need food, shelter and a way out. A party member who organises it (Yara's camp as a hall, Wyn and Maren Talla as guides, Kell's Crossing bread if Calla rang) earns the Stilled's trust. Ask each player one thing their character does for one waking stranger. The Stilled child asks for her mother; somebody has to tell her.
plays.consequence: The Stilled trust the party.
plays.fallback: If the party is in a hurry, Yara takes charge and asks only for coin and one promise: come back.
plays.tells: Players ask what the Stilled need, or start organising.
plays.rules: Heroic Inspiration for a memory or a Gift given freely to a waking Stilled who needs it.
plays.later: S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor. S23: they stand in the Strike as living walls. Act V: they stand in the fight on the Tor.
plays.keywords: stilled, thaw, help, food, shelter, wake, refugees, care, organise, camp

plays.title: They promise the Brightwater's crew passage home
plays.why: A dozen Sword Coast sailors from 1082 DR wake up and ask the way to the sea.
plays.readAloud: “The Brightwater was moored at a river mouth, west of here, under a sky full of weather.” The bosun looks at the clear, still air. “Where did the weather go?”
plays.response: Corran Vell and eleven of the Brightwater's crew want to go home through the Seam; nobody has told them about the Stormwall. Getting them to Pellmoor means Brannagh Wick's pilots and a captain willing to carry them. Venn's agents in Pellmoor would pay well to exhibit them in Athkatla, and a letter from the Landing says so to their faces; the party can refuse for them.
plays.consequence: The party has a dozen Faerûnian sailors who owe them their lives.
plays.fallback: If nobody takes them on, they set off south on their own, and Isolde's Hushmen arrest them at Kell's Crossing as Charter-breakers.
plays.tells: Bosun Corran Vell asks which way is the harbour.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on a Baldurian factor or the Corvane Venture to find them berths; Venn will ask for nothing and want everything.
plays.later: S22: a crew who owe the party is one form of the Stormborn ally. Act IV: if Thrane rings and the Seam widens, they sail home with the first fleet.
plays.keywords: sailors, brightwater, corran vell, faerunian, stormborn, home, seam, pellmoor, ship, passage, crew

plays.title: They refuse Isolde's demand
plays.why: They paid for the thaw; they will not hand its Heart to the Court.
plays.readAloud: “What a lovely thaw. I'm told you have something of ours. The Frost Heart, let us say. Give it to us, and the Court will forget your little interference. Refuse, and the Court will remember it very precisely.”
plays.response: She smiles and leaves; no fight. On her way out she looks, once, at whatever they care about most here (Yara, the Stilled child, Imber) so they know she noticed.
plays.consequence: Isolde returns to the Court with a report.
plays.fallback: If the players want the last word, give them one; she lets them have it.
plays.tells: “No.” Or a player laughs at her.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15: she is relieved not to have to fight.
plays.later: Act IV: the Court moves against them; S23's Strike comes for the Hearts they carry. S21: Maudrin leaves Hallowmere within a day of the second Act IV ringing.
plays.keywords: refuse, no, isolde, court, envoy, demand, frost heart, reject, defy

plays.title: They give Isolde the Frost Heart
plays.why: The bell has rung, the resonance persists, and handing over the Heart may buy peace.
plays.readAloud: Isolde takes the Heart in both hands and holds it away from her body, as if it might drip. “There. Wasn't that easy?”
plays.response: She takes it. If they carry Calla's Heart, she asks for that too, sweetly, and her Hushmen step closer. The Court now holds the Frost Heart. If Hieme already rang, its resonance persists and the thaw continues; if not, the Concord needs the Heart back from Court custody. Maudrin's plan accelerates.
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Frost Heart.
plays.fallback: If they hesitate, Isolde says Hieme's resonance doesn't need the Heart any more, which is true.
plays.tells: A player asks whether they still need it after the ringing.
plays.rules: Record in the Bargain Log what Isolde promised: the Court 'forgets' their interference. It keeps that promise exactly, and nothing else.
plays.later: S21: Maudrin leaves Hallowmere sooner. S23: she wants every remaining Heart. S22: Hieme still counts for the Concord if it rang before the Heart went.
plays.keywords: give, hand over, surrender, frost heart, isolde, deal, court, peace

plays.title: They attack Isolde
plays.why: She followed them across Corvane with Hushmen; some tables end that conversation with steel.
plays.readAloud: Isolde's glass falls and does not break in the soft, thawing snow. She is already moving, and her grey lace gloves are not lace.
plays.response: She has silence-stone gloves and her escort (Isolde's Escort). Isolde retreats after one round, using Cunning Action to Disengage or Dash into the trees. If they pin her, play s15-capture-isolde.
plays.consequence: The party is the Court's open enemy in the north.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes long, the Hushmen surrender as soon as Isolde is gone; they never liked her.
plays.tells: Weapons drawn as she finishes her offer.
plays.rules: Isolde: Spy base, Cunning Action. Hushmen grapple to cover her. Grappled, Restrained.
plays.later: S23: if she escapes, she reports everything to Maudrin, and the Strike knows their numbers.
plays.keywords: attack, fight, kill isolde, capture, ambush, hushmen, envoy, combat

plays.title: Isolde recognises Imber Vesk
plays.why: A freed High Sexton is a second Vesk with a claim to the Key, which the Court fears more than any bell.
plays.readAloud: Isolde stops smiling. She looks at the old man in the borrowed cloak, at the shape of his nose, at the ring on his finger. “Oh,” she says softly. “Oh, Maudrin will hate this.”
plays.response: Isolde sees it at once. She offers to take Imber to Hallowmere 'for his safety', meaning Maudrin's; if she is their informant, she quietly tells them to hide him. Imber wants to go wherever he can finish his sermon. Let the party decide.
plays.consequence: The Court knows, or doesn't, that Imber Vesk lives.
plays.fallback: If the party says nothing, Imber introduces himself, by his full title.
plays.tells: Imber is with the party when Isolde arrives.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Isolde to make her forget she saw him (she wants something for it).
plays.later: S22: Imber can confront Maudrin with the truth in front of her own Hushmen. S24: facing her ancestor, Maudrin has nothing left to bargain with. If Isolde takes him, Maudrin silences him in the palace and the party loses a witness.
plays.keywords: imber, vesk, isolde, recognise, claim, key, witness, family, protect, hide

plays.title: Isolde comes as their informant
plays.why: The party turned Isolde in S8; she still had to come north.
plays.readAloud: Isolde makes her speech in front of her Hushmen, word for word. Then, while they water the horses, she says without moving her lips, “I need a story. Give me one I can sell.”
plays.response: She asks for the Frost Heart in front of her Hushmen, then offers a private way out: they 'lose' it in the thaw, she reports that, and she leaves. She tells them what she knows: Maudrin intends to march on the Tor the moment two more bells ring.
plays.consequence: The Court believes the Frost Heart is lost. Isolde's cover holds.
plays.fallback: If they won't play along, she takes nothing and reports that they refused.
plays.tells: Isolde's note at the waystation named her escort.
plays.rules: Deception DC 12 for the party to stage the 'loss' convincingly for her Hushmen.
plays.later: S21: the party knows Maudrin will leave Hallowmere within a day of the second ringing. S23: Isolde stays in Hallowmere 'ill' and sends word of the Strike's route.
plays.keywords: isolde, informant, ally, deal, cover story, lost heart, warning, maudrin, march

plays.title: They head east for Brassfall
plays.why: Thrane's Heart is with the Ironhorn, and the storms promise allies.
plays.readAloud: East, past the last glass trees, the sky flickers over a line of bronze-veined mountains, though there are no clouds at all.
plays.response: Six days around the Ironhorn foothills to Brassfall (Act IV, Branch A). Thrane's Heart is in Kessa's Heart-Hall. Tell the players what they know: ringing Thrane brings the storms back, and sailors say it would loosen the Stormwall.
plays.consequence: The party takes Branch A first; Vael Tor will be compressed into Sessions 20 and 21.
plays.fallback: If they can't decide, Yara says Brassfall pays better.
plays.tells: Players ask about the Ironhorn, Kessa, or the storm bell.
plays.rules: Level 7 after the Glassreach resolution.
plays.later: S16A–S19A: Brassfall. S20–S21: Vael Tor, compressed. S22: both bells are needed for the Concord.
plays.keywords: brassfall, east, ironhorn, thrane, kessa, storm, branch a, road, next

plays.title: They head for Vael Tor
plays.why: Mirel's bell, the Sleepless and the Hush are at the centre of the map, and so is the Key's destination.
plays.readAloud: South and east, the plain rises to a single hill ringed with grey stones. Even from here, if you close your eyes, you can hear something breathing in its sleep.
plays.response: Vael Tor is about a week from Glassreach by Kell's Crossing (Act IV, Branch B). If they carry Mirel's Heart (S5), they can ring it as soon as they reach the bell; otherwise the Librarian's courier waits at the Hall.
plays.consequence: The party takes Branch B first; Brassfall will be compressed into Sessions 20 and 21.
plays.fallback: If they can't decide, Imber (if alive) says, 'The Tor. It is where it ends. I would like to see it before.'
plays.tells: Players ask about the Sleeping Hall, Mirel, or the Seventh Bell.
plays.rules: Level 7 after the Glassreach resolution.
plays.later: S16B–S19B: Vael Tor. S20–S21: Brassfall, compressed. S22: both bells are needed for the Concord.
plays.keywords: vael tor, sleeping hall, mirel, sleepless, hush, branch b, road, next, tor

plays.title: They win back the Stilled's trust
plays.why: The party hurt Stilled (fire in the clearing, shattered glass) and they remember.
plays.readAloud: A woman steps out of the winter and looks at you. 'You,' she says. 'You woke my husband with fire.'
plays.response: Trust returns slowly and only for real acts: a sincere apology, a memory or Gift given freely to one Stilled, a night guarding the camp. Influence DC 17, with Advantage if a Stilled the party saved speaks for them. Wyn and Maren Talla can vouch. Heroic Inspiration for a Gift given freely.
plays.consequence: The Stilled will walk, but slowly.
plays.fallback: If the check fails, try again after a night of real work; nothing is lost.
plays.tells: A woken Stilled flinches from a character, or Maren Talla says, 'Some of us remember who held the hammer.'
plays.rules: Influence DC 17; Advantage if Maren Talla or a calmed Stilled vouches.
plays.later: S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor (stilled_trust is Yes). S23: they stand in the Strike as living walls.
plays.keywords: win back, apologise, stilled, trust, amends

plays.title: They capture Isolde at the thaw
plays.why: She came north with a small escort and the party can pin her.
plays.readAloud: Isolde's gloves hit the snow. She does not scream. 'Oh, you wonderful, wonderful people,' she says, and her eyes are on the road.
plays.response: A successful grapple or dropping her before her second turn captures her. Her Hushmen surrender at once. She will talk about her son, the Ironhorn sales and the Court's plans if treated kindly. The Court sends Tristan Vesk next (s15-tristan-envoy).
plays.consequence: Isolde is captured.
plays.fallback: If she escapes, she reports everything to Maudrin.
plays.tells: A grapple or a drop before her second turn.
plays.rules: Isolde: Spy base. Grappled, Restrained. A creature at 0 HP can be knocked out.
plays.later: S23: a captured Isolde is a bargaining chip against Maudrin (her secrets, her son).
plays.keywords: capture isolde, grapple, knocked out

plays.title: Isolde takes Imber back to Hallowmere
plays.why: The party left him frozen, or let her take him.
plays.readAloud: 'For his safety,' Isolde says, taking the Sexton's arm. 'And for the Chancellor's. She will want to meet her ancestor.'
plays.response: Isolde takes Imber under Hushman escort. In Hallowmere, Maudrin silences him in the palace and the party loses a witness. If Imber was frozen, her Hushmen carry him out in his block of ice, melting it with a lamp.
plays.consequence: Imber is in Court hands.
plays.fallback: If the party objects, Isolde shrugs and leaves him.
plays.tells: Isolde asks to see the old man in the borrowed cloak, or finds the chapel empty of party.
plays.rules: No check unless the party stops her (Influence DC 15 or a fight).
plays.later: S22: Imber cannot confront Maudrin. S24: Maudrin has nothing to fear from the diary.
plays.keywords: isolde takes imber, court custody, vesk

plays.title: Tristan Vesk comes north in Isolde's place
plays.why: The party captured Isolde on the road or at the thaw, and the Court sends the next envoy.
plays.readAloud: 'Tristan Vesk,' the young man says, offering a gloved hand. 'The Chancellor's cousin, and, I'm afraid, the one who writes her letters. I'm here about the Frost Heart.'
plays.response: Tristan offers what Isolde offered, with less charm and more threat. He negotiates for Isolde's release. He is a Spy (Court agent) and fights only if cornered. He mentions, to unsettle them, that the Court has a second Chancellor waiting.
plays.consequence: The Court knows Isolde is held and wants her back.
plays.fallback: If the party refuses, he leaves with a promise to return with Hushmen.
plays.tells: Isolde is captured, and a carriage with a Vesk crest arrives.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Tristan (Intelligence 13). Isolde's release is a bargaining chip.
plays.later: S23: Tristan is the Court's alternative Chancellor if Maudrin falls. Act V: Tristan offers the party a deal for the Key.
plays.keywords: tristan vesk, envoy, cousin, negotiate, isolde captured

plays.title: They draw Yara the map of the Spire
plays.why: She wanted it from the first night, and someone sketched it at the top.
plays.readAloud: Yara unrolls the sketch on the camp table, weighting its corners with cups. 'Nobody has ever drawn that,' she says, and for once she does not name a price.
plays.response: Yara's loyalty is earned: she offers a guide to the Stilled's camp, stores in kind and a lower price for anything the party buys. She names the Spire's second stair after the party in her notes. Heroic Inspiration for a drawing given freely.
plays.consequence: Yara is a firm ally.
plays.fallback: If nobody drew it, Yara asks them to describe it, and writes it herself.
plays.tells: A player offers Yara a drawing, or she asks what the view was like.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S30: Yara finally opens her brother's glass-flower.
plays.keywords: yara map, spire sketch, drawing, reward

plays.title: The Stilled send an emissary
plays.why: The clock_stilled threshold has been reached: the Stilled have a voice, and they have questions.
plays.readAloud: The woman who steps forward is Maren Talla, thin and upright, with the dust of four centuries in her hair. 'We have a request,' she says. 'And a debt we would like to repay.'
plays.response: Maren speaks for the Stilled: they want food, shelter, and a place to go. They offer to walk to the Tor at the party's side when the time comes (if trust is Yes), and to carry the story of the Sexton. If trust is Wary, they ask for amends first. She asks what year it is; she has been told, but she wants to hear it from the party.
plays.consequence: The Stilled have a voice in the party's plans.
plays.fallback: If the party is busy, Yara sets the meeting for the next dawn.
plays.tells: A waking Stilled asks for the party by name, or Maren Talla says she will speak for them.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 if trust is Wary; none if Yes.
plays.later: S22: the Stilled walk to the Tor (stilled_trust is Yes). S23: they stand as living walls.
plays.keywords: emissary, maren talla, stilled speak, delegation

plays.title: They go to Brassfall first
plays.why: Thrane's storms, Kessa's alliance and the lamp of a dead foreman pull east.
plays.readAloud: The mountains are veined with bronze. Old lightning-shafts drop into the earth like the throats of bells. The sky flickers above you, though there are no clouds.
plays.response: Branch A runs in full (16A–19A); Vael Tor is compressed later into Sessions 20–21. Both bells matter for the Concord.
plays.consequence: The party is on Branch A.
plays.tells: Players choose the Thrane Road at the end of Act III.
plays.later: S20–21: Vael Tor in compressed form. The Forecast tracks both bells.
plays.keywords: brassfall, east, thrane, branch a, go first, mountains

plays.title: They carry Old Garrow's lamp
plays.why: A gruff, funny ghost asks a plain favor (H-20).
plays.readAloud: "Right, lads and lasses, you look like you can carry a lamp. My girl's in the Ironhorn foothills, near the camp, with a red horse-skull on her tent. Yenna's her name. Tell her I'm sorry about the collapse. And don't drop it. It's the only thing down here that hums on purpose."
plays.response: The lamp holds the storm-stone that tethers Garrow. Carrying it lets his ghost rest near his daughter. In exchange he leads them safely through the Old Works, past the unstable shaft and, if they ask, past the Storm-stone Golems. Tell the table plainly that the lamp holds a stone, and stones attract the Thane (H-20).
plays.consequence: A safe path through the mine, and a reason to meet Yenna.
plays.tells: Players accept the lamp or ask about Yenna.
plays.rules: The lamp is a storm-stone: metal near it sparks. Old Garrow uses the 2024 Specter (CR 1) but rarely fights.
plays.later: S17A: Yenna takes the lamp, or Kessa demands the storm-stone for his Heart-Hall (see the lamp plays there). S28: Garrow's laugh is heard once more if the lamp reached Yenna.
plays.keywords: garrow, lamp, ghost, yenna, carry, favor, old works, h-20

plays.title: They refuse Garrow's request
plays.why: Some parties won't carry a ghost's tether into an armed camp.
plays.readAloud: Garrow's lamp dims. "Suit yourselves. Mind the third shaft, then. It's cracked. I'd know."
plays.response: He withdraws, disappointed, but warns them which shaft is unstable. Declining never triggers the collapse; only entering the visibly cracked passage risks it.
plays.consequence: No guide through the mine, and no lamp for the golems to recognise.
plays.tells: Players decline or ignore him.
plays.rules: Entering the cracked shaft: DC 13 Dexterity save, 3d6 Bludgeoning on a failure, half on a success.
plays.later: S17A: Yenna meets them without her father's message and is cooler; the party earns her trust by other means. S16A: the golems do not stand aside for them, so the vault is a fight or a skipped room.
plays.keywords: refuse, garrow, no, decline, lamp, ghost

plays.title: They loot the storm-stone vault
plays.why: A room of glittering storm-stones is irresistible, and guarded.
plays.readAloud: A treasure room of storm-stones, pale blue and humming. Every metal thing you carry sings back at them.
plays.response: Picking one up safely takes care; a fumbled stone discharges. Each stone lifted wakes one more Storm-stone Golem (up to three). Storm-stones are illegal to export and smuggled anyway; Mirabar dwarves in Pellmoor pay well, and the Court arrests sellers.
plays.consequence: Storm-stones in hand and golems to deal with, or a clean retreat.
plays.fallback: If the golems are too much, back out of the room: they do not leave the vault. With Garrow's lamp in hand they stand aside (next play). Without the lamp, a Bloodied golem's shard can be prised out.
plays.tells: Players ask what storm-stones are worth, or pick one up.
plays.rules: Pick up a stone: DC 13 Dexterity check; failure 3d8 Lightning. Encounter: the golems. Prising a golem's shard out (Utilize action, DC 15 Strength (Athletics), once it is Bloodied) deactivates that golem. Wooden weapons do not trigger their Storm-Stone Heart.
plays.later: Anytime: a stone sold in Pellmoor is any-sell-storm-stone (Landing clock). S17A: Kessa wants stones for his Heart-Hall and notices who carries them.
plays.keywords: storm-stone, vault, treasure, golem, loot, lightning, mine

plays.title: They notice the storm-stones hum toward the sea
plays.why: A v6 clue: the dead lightning wants to go where Thrane's storms went.
plays.readAloud: Every storm-stone in the vault hums a little louder when you turn it west, toward the sea, the way a compass needle hums toward north.
plays.response: A Stormborn character recognises the sound: the same thunder they sailed through in the Stormwall. Let them guess. Garrow says the stones "always leaned west, since before my time." Corin, later, says the storms "went to the rim and wait."
plays.consequence: The party suspects ringing Thrane will affect the Stormwall.
plays.tells: A Stormborn sailor or an Arcana-trained character studies the stones.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) DC 15, or automatic for a character who crossed the Seam.
plays.later: S19A or S21: ringing Thrane loosens the Stormwall. S28: new fleets crowd Pellmoor and the Landing Charter strains (s28-landing-fleets).
plays.keywords: stormwall, storm-stone, west, sea, thunder, clue, seam, sailor

plays.title: They examine the lamp before agreeing
plays.why: Careful players inspect a ghost's gift.
plays.readAloud: The blue flame does not flicker when you breathe on it. At its heart, pale and humming, sits a stone no bigger than a thumb.
plays.response: A Study action (Intelligence (Arcana) DC 15) shows a storm-stone inside, its dead lightning tied to Garrow. It sparks near metal. Detect Magic shows a tether of abjuration and necromancy. Dispel Magic on it frees Garrow's ghost at once, and he gives no help in the Old Works.
plays.consequence: The party knows what it is agreeing to carry.
plays.tells: A player asks what is in the lamp or tries to identify it.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Arcana) DC 15. Dispel Magic ends the tether.
plays.later: S17A: Kessa wants exactly this stone.
plays.keywords: lamp, arcana, identify, detect magic, storm-stone

plays.title: The golems stand aside for the lamp
plays.why: Garrow's lamp is the golems' kin-stone.
plays.readAloud: The great bronze shapes turn their heads toward the blue flame, and then, one by one, they step back from the door.
plays.response: With the lamp, the golems attack no one who lifts a stone carefully (the DC 13 Dexterity check still applies); they attack only if the lamp is set down or a stone is thrown. Garrow chuckles. A stone is still a stone: selling one is a crime in Pellmoor.
plays.consequence: The vault is open without a fight.
plays.tells: The party carries the lamp into the vault.
plays.rules: Lifting a stone: DC 13 Dexterity check, 3d8 Lightning on a failure.
plays.later: Anytime: selling a stone is any-sell-storm-stone.
plays.keywords: golem, vault, avoid, lamp, parley

plays.title: The party splits between Brassfall and the Tor
plays.why: Some tables send two characters down each road.
plays.readAloud: Two roads leave the crossing. One climbs toward the bronze mountains; one drops toward the marsh and the grey hill.
plays.response: Pick the branch the majority walks and run it as written; the other group's scenes are short cuts, one decision each, and the groups rejoin at the S21 report. Each group gets one Heart decision. Neither group takes a Toll the other player has not consented to. The act4 flag follows the main group.
plays.consequence: Both branches advance, thinly.
plays.fallback: If it will not stay playable, ask the table to pick one branch and give the other group's character a letter instead.
plays.tells: Players say "half of us go to the Tor".
plays.later: S21: the groups rejoin when Maudrin's march is reported.
plays.keywords: split, separate, two groups, parallel

plays.title: An Ironhorn patrol challenges them on the Brass Road
plays.why: Kessa's riders watch every road into Brassfall.
plays.readAloud: Four riders on hairy ponies cross the road ahead of you, bronze wire braided in their hair. “State your business. And your hands, rider. Show me your hands.”
plays.response: They are curious, not hostile: they want to know whether the party works for the Court. A truthful answer about the lamp gets an escort to the camp; a lie about the Court gets a shadow. The riders count how many Hearts the party carries. They do not know about Kessa's sickness; they know he does not sleep.
plays.consequence: The party arrives at the camp as guests, or watched.
plays.tells: The party travels in the open, or with a lamp that sparks.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion or Animal Handling) against attitude Indifferent; DC 15.
plays.later: S17A: Kessa has heard of them before they meet.
plays.keywords: riders, ironhorn, patrol, road, scouts

plays.title: They go to Vael Tor first
plays.why: Mirel's Heart may already be in hand, and the Tor is central.
plays.readAloud: The hill rises alone above the plain, ringed with grey stones. At night, faint lights move among the stones like fireflies. When you close your eyes, you dream of a room full of beds.
plays.response: Branch B runs in full (16B–19B); Brassfall is compressed later into Sessions 20–21.
plays.consequence: The party is on Branch B.
plays.tells: Players choose the marsh road toward the Tor.
plays.later: S20–21: Brassfall compressed. The Forecast tracks both bells.
plays.keywords: vael tor, mirel, branch b, go first, tor, dreams, sleeping hall

plays.title: They take a long rest on Vael Tor
plays.why: Travellers have to sleep, and the Tor punishes it.
plays.readAloud: You dream of a child singing in a language you almost know. When you wake, something is standing at the edge of the firelight wearing the shape of the thing you fear most.
plays.response: Warn them before they choose to sleep there. Each sleeper makes the save. Any failure brings a nightmare. At most one Sleepless forms per night, from the fear of the sleeper who failed by the most (5 or more); a character who keeps watch and does not sleep makes no save. Camp inside the Hush Cult's circle (S17B) and no Sleepless forms, at a price.
plays.consequence: Rest, at a price.
plays.tells: Players make camp among the grey stones.
plays.rules: DC 13 Wisdom save per sleeper per long rest on the Tor. Failure: Disadvantage on the first Insight check the next day. Failure by 5 or more: one Sleepless (CR 5) forms, once per night. Calm Emotions on the camp, or Protection from Evil and Good on a sleeper, gives Advantage on the saves.
plays.later: H-22: sleepers share the singing child's dream (s16b-stop-the-song). Every Sleepless dissolves into mist once Mirel rings; no new ones form on the Tor afterwards (S19B or S21).
plays.keywords: rest, sleep, camp, long rest, tor, nightmare, dream

plays.title: They fight the Sleepless
plays.why: Nightmares walk the Tor at night.
plays.readAloud: It has your mother's face. Then it has your own face, older. Then it has no face at all.
plays.response: Run the encounter. Each Sleepless takes the shape of the nearest sleeper's fear. They dissolve into mist if Mirel rings within a mile, and at dawn. The Gaze's Frightened ends on its own at the end of the target's next turn; Lesser Restoration does not end it (use Calm Emotions or Heroes' Feast for lingering dread).
plays.consequence: The night is survived; the Tor knows the party is here.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly, the Hush Cult's circle (S17B) is a retreat: the Sleepless withdraw from it.
plays.tells: A Sleepless forms, or two come out of the stones.
plays.rules: Encounter: Sleepless. Terrifying Gaze: DC 13 Wisdom or Frightened until the end of the target's next turn. Nightmare Touch lowers Hit Point maximum until a Long Rest.
plays.later: Every Sleepless stops walking once Mirel rings (S19B or S21).
plays.keywords: sleepless, fight, nightmare, fear, combat, monster

plays.title: They bargain with the Librarian's courier for Mirel's Heart
plays.why: If they didn't take Mirel's Heart in Hallowmere, the offer comes to them.
plays.readAloud: A figure in archivist's grey stands by the central bed, holding a bone-bound book that has no words. "The Librarian sends its regards. A dream you have never told anyone, and the Heart is yours."
plays.response: The price is a dream the giver has never told anyone, lost to them (the giver names it; it is a Trade in the ledger). The courier also accepts a Gift. A character never has to sell; another may pay instead. If every offer is refused, use s16b-refuse-courier.
plays.consequence: The party holds Mirel's Heart.
plays.tells: The party lacks Mirel's Heart and reaches the Sleeping Hall.
plays.rules: Record the dream as a Trade (heartkeep weight) or the Gift in the ledger.
plays.later: S19B or S21: Mirel can be rung. Concord: one step closer.
plays.keywords: courier, librarian, mirel, heart, dream, bargain, gift

plays.title: They ring Mirel as soon as they reach the bell
plays.why: If they already hold the Heart, nothing makes them wait.
plays.readAloud: The bell sings like a lullaby sung by someone who loves you. Every sleeper on the Tor sighs and turns over. The Sleepless dissolve into mist.
plays.response: State the Toll first: a Fear, chosen by the Ringer, lost for one day. Losing a fear changes a feeling, not their authority over their character or immunity to magical fear. Move later conversations around the ringing.
plays.consequence: Mirel is rung. The Sleepless stop walking. The Hush's lullaby changes key.
plays.tells: They hold Mirel's Heart on arrival.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Fear, bell Mirel).
plays.later: The Court sends Hushmen to the Tor. Concord: one step closer.
