plays.keywords: ring mirel, ring now, bell, toll, fear, dream bell

plays.title: They try to wake a sleeper in the Hall
plays.why: Hundreds of sleepers on beds invite a rescue.
plays.readAloud: The sleeper's chest rises and falls. Her eyes move beneath their lids as if reading. She does not wake.
plays.response: Noise, pain and Lesser Restoration do nothing; the Hush holds them. Greater Restoration or Dispel Magic wakes one sleeper for a minute: she speaks in a voice that is not hers, names someone she is dreaming of, and sleeps again. The names belong to real Tithed or sold memories. Nothing is lost to the caster.
plays.consequence: A name, and the knowledge that waking is temporary.
plays.tells: A healer or caster stands over a bed.
plays.rules: Dispel Magic (DC 15 check) or Greater Restoration wakes one sleeper for 1 minute.
plays.later: S28: some of the names come back to their owners (s28-return-jars).
plays.keywords: wake, sleeper, hall, restoration, rescue

plays.title: They refuse every offer from the courier
plays.why: Selling a dream is a hard thing to ask.
plays.readAloud: The courier tilts its head, closes the wordless book, and says nothing. It does not leave.
plays.response: Mirel stays unrung for now. The courier waits at the Hall, polite and patient; the Librarian's offer stays open. No penalty beyond time. The Heart can be taken later (s20-courier-bargain-quick) or stolen.
plays.consequence: Mirel's Heart waits with the courier.
plays.fallback: The courier hints that a Gift would also do.
plays.tells: Players balk at the courier's price.
plays.later: S20 or S21: the courier's offer, or another way.
plays.keywords: refuse, courier, decline, wait, no deal

plays.title: They take the Heart from the courier by force or trick
plays.why: A thin archivist holding a bell Heart looks like an easy mark.
plays.readAloud: The courier does not run. “The Librarian will remember this,” it says, and opens its hand.
plays.response: The courier is an archivist-shade (Commoner) and does not resist. They get the Heart. The Librarian remembers: S22's fallback (the Librarian reads the Quiet Night page for a memory) is closed, and the Sealed Stacks answer no one from this party.
plays.consequence: The party holds Mirel's Heart, and the Librarian is an enemy.
plays.fallback: If the table dislikes robbing a bookkeeper, the courier lets them pay a Gift afterwards.
plays.tells: Players ask how strong the courier is.
plays.later: S22: only the Notes or the diary can tell the Key's truth; the Librarian will not read it.
plays.keywords: steal, rob, courier, heart, force

plays.title: They stop humming when the child asks
plays.why: H-22: in the shared dream the singing child asks them to stop the song.
plays.readAloud: The child on the stairs has no face. “Please. When you sing along, I cannot hear myself. Can you stop?”
plays.response: If the party stops humming, the lullaby falters for a night: the Sleepless cannot form, and the Hush Cult's circle grows quiet and frightened. They have bought one safe night at the Hush's cost. Nothing is lost. If they refuse, nothing happens, and the child cries.
plays.consequence: The Hush is weaker tonight.
plays.fallback: The child asks again in the morning.
plays.tells: Sleepers share the dream, and someone hums back.
plays.later: S17B: the Cult is alarmed. S27: Oum remembers who stopped the song.
plays.keywords: child, song, hum, dream, stop

plays.title: They bring the lamp to Yenna Garrow
plays.why: Garrow asked, and Yenna is easy to find: the red horse-skull on her tent.
plays.readAloud: Yenna takes the lamp in both hands, and for a moment the blue flame steadies, and somewhere very far away an old man laughs.
plays.response: She weeps and thanks them. If they tell her what the ghost said, she gives a horse, a bow, or a bargain with her clan. She can smuggle Thrane's Heart out for a favor (s17a-yenna-smuggles) if Kessa refuses them. Garrow's laugh, very far away, is the last thing the lamp does.
plays.consequence: A friend inside the Ironhorn camp, and the lamp is where it belongs.
plays.tells: The party carried the lamp from the Old Works.
plays.rules: Yenna uses the Ironhorn Rider block (CR 3).
plays.later: S22: Yenna's riders are an ally (s22-ally-ironhorn), cutting the Hushmen's retreat at the Strike. S28: Yenna sets the lamp on her tent.
plays.keywords: yenna, lamp, garrow, daughter, red horse-skull, ironhorn, gift

plays.title: They take Kessa's steppe contest
plays.why: Kessa's guests win a wager or buy their dinner.
plays.readAloud: "Welcome, rider. You've carried a dead man's lamp into my camp. That makes you my guests, and my guests win a wager or buy their dinner. Win, and you speak to my council. Lose, and you'll leave me something to melt."
plays.response: A skill challenge: three successes before three failures. Agree a specific, nonessential stake before anyone rolls. Rotate the spotlight; a repeated skill needs a new described approach. Continue until three of either, whatever the party size. Win: Kessa opens the Heart-Hall and keeps his word. Lose: the staked item is melted and the Hall stays closed; the Champion fights only if the party tries to take the Heart by force.
plays.consequence: Win: Kessa keeps his word and opens his Heart-Hall. Lose: the staked item is melted for bronze and the Hall stays closed.
plays.tells: Players accept the wager.
plays.rules: DC 14 Strength (Athletics), Wisdom (Animal Handling) or Charisma (Performance); Help action allowed. Heroic Inspiration may reroll.
plays.later: Win: his private offer follows (s17a-accept-kessa). Lose: theft (s17a-take-thrane), Yenna (s17a-yenna-smuggles) or a duel (s17a-duel-kessa) remain.
plays.keywords: contest, wager, kessa, challenge, skill challenge, race, steppe, bet

plays.title: They accept Kessa's bargain
plays.why: He offers his Heart for a ringing, and wants Maudrin's head and a cure.
plays.readAloud: "I'm dying, rider. Thrane's Heart has been eating my hands since I took it from the Brass Road. Help me with one, and I'll help you with the rest. That's a fair bargain, isn't it?"
plays.response: Kessa lends Thrane's Heart for the ringing and asks for an oath that they will return it to the Heart-Hall afterwards. He cannot ring it himself: the Ringer is Lightning-Marked at the Shafts, and a man whose hands the Heart already blackens would not survive the first strike; his council will not follow a deaf or blind Thane in the Court's shadow either. He believes the Key can cure him because Isolde Drave sold Tithed memories to the Ironhorn, and one of them spoke of it. It cannot, and someone will have to tell him (s22-tell-kessa).
plays.consequence: The party carries Thrane's Heart under oath.
plays.tells: Kessa speaks in private about his hands.
plays.rules: Record the oath in the Bargain log.
plays.later: S19A or S21: ring Thrane. Then return the Heart (oath kept) or keep it (oath broken: the Ironhorn will not ride for the party at S22).
plays.keywords: kessa, bargain, accept, oath, thrane heart, alliance, loan

plays.title: They steal or smuggle Thrane's Heart
plays.why: If Kessa refuses them or they refuse his terms.
plays.readAloud: The Heart-Hall is a long tent of white hide. At its centre a bronze clapper hangs from a horse-skull, and it hums.
plays.response: Two routes: theft past the riders, or Yenna smuggles it out for a favor. Either way Kessa learns of it by morning. If caught, his Champion fights; Kessa offers a challenge rather than an execution. Kessa knows who took it.
plays.consequence: The party holds Thrane's Heart and has an angry Thane.
plays.tells: Players case the Heart-Hall or ask Yenna for help.
plays.rules: Theft: DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) per character. Yenna: DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) for her, Advantage if the party distracts the camp.
plays.later: S22: the Ironhorn will not ally unless the party makes amends. S23: Kessa may bring the horses to the Strike for his own reasons (s23-kessa-intercepts).
plays.keywords: steal, smuggle, thrane, heart-hall, yenna, theft, take

plays.title: They give Kessa the storm-stone
plays.why: H-20: once the lamp is in camp, the Thane sees the storm-stone and wants it for his Heart-Hall.
plays.readAloud: Kessa's black fingers hover over the lamp. “That hums like a Heart. My Hall needs a stone like that. Name your price.”
plays.response: If they give it, Garrow's tether burns away into the Heart-Hall and his ghost goes quiet with a last joke; Yenna weeps but understands. Kessa opens the Hall at once (no contest) and offers a gentler bargain. If they refuse, Kessa respects it, and the lamp goes to Yenna (s17a-lamp-to-yenna).
plays.consequence: Kessa is generous; Yenna is grieved.
plays.fallback: Yenna says quietly that she would rather he were free.
plays.tells: Kessa asks about the lamp, or the party shows it.
plays.later: S22: Yenna is not an ally unless the party makes amends (her father's tether was sold). S28: no lamp on her tent.
plays.keywords: lamp, kessa, storm-stone, hall, give

plays.title: They meet Yenna without her father's lamp
plays.why: H-20 refused: Yenna has no message from her father.
plays.readAloud: Yenna looks at your empty hands and then at your faces. “Garrow sent you?” she asks. “Then where is he?”
plays.response: She is hurt and cool. They can earn her by describing the Old Works truthfully, or by going back for the lamp (a day each way). She then helps a little: a horse. She does not smuggle the Heart unless the lamp reaches her.
plays.consequence: A cooler Yenna, and a reason to fetch the lamp.
plays.fallback: Garrow's ghost appears at the camp's edge and nudges her.
plays.tells: The lamp was refused or left behind.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion) DC 15, Advantage if they repeat Garrow's jokes.
plays.later: S22: Yenna is an ally only if the lamp reached her or the party earned her another way.
plays.keywords: yenna, no lamp, refused, cold

plays.title: They challenge Kessa to a duel
plays.why: A war-chief respects a fair fight, and a party may prefer the sword to the contest.
plays.readAloud: Kessa laughs and strips off his shirt: his chest is laced with black lightning scars. “First blood or the last? Name it, rider.”
plays.response: Run the duel as first blood: it ends when Kessa is Bloodied (Champion at his side, riders as spectators). Kessa honors a yield. If the party kills him, use s17a-kill-kessa. If he yields, the Heart-Hall opens. His Lightning-Sick trait hurts him too.
plays.consequence: A won duel opens the Hall; a lost one costs a stake.
plays.fallback: Kessa stops it the moment a fair wager is offered.
plays.tells: Players mention honor or show their weapons.
plays.rules: Encounter: Kessa, Champion and rider. Non-lethal: declare it when the melee attack drops the target to 0 HP.
plays.later: S19A: Kessa remembers whether the party fought fair.
plays.keywords: duel, fight, kessa, first blood, challenge

plays.title: They kill Kessa
plays.why: Fights end badly; Kessa will not yield if cornered.
plays.readAloud: The Thane sits down in the dust with his axe across his knees. “Tell Yenna it was weather,” he says.
plays.response: Kessa dies by the party's hand. The Ironhorn do not forget: Yenna splits the clan, and half the riders ride for the Court's Tristan. The Heart-Hall opens; the party can take Thrane's Heart. The oath, if sworn, is void.
plays.consequence: Kessa is dead; the Ironhorn are divided.
plays.fallback: Yenna can stop the fight at 0 HP if the party yields first.
plays.tells: Weapons are drawn after the duel breaks down.
plays.later: S19A: Thrane's Heart is in the party's hands; no Kessa to ease. S22: no Ironhorn ally. S28: no storm death for Kessa.
plays.keywords: kill, kessa, death, murder, thane

plays.title: Yenna smuggles the Heart out
plays.why: She owes the party for her father's lamp.
plays.readAloud: Yenna lowers her voice. “Tonight, when the third drum stops. Don't be where he looks.”
plays.response: She takes the risk herself: no skill check for the party, only a plan. The Heart is out of the Hall by morning. Kessa learns who did it and does not forgive Yenna quickly. The party owes her a favor.
plays.consequence: The party holds Thrane's Heart, and Yenna is in trouble.
plays.fallback: If it goes wrong, Yenna takes the blame and the Thane offers a duel.
plays.tells: Players ask Yenna for a favor.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 14 for the distraction; the Heart moves either way.
plays.later: S22: Yenna's riders stand with the party; Kessa does not. S19A: no oath was sworn.
plays.keywords: yenna, smuggle, favor, heart, steal

plays.title: They accept the Hush Cult's rest
plays.why: Exhausted parties on a nightmare hill find the offer kind.
plays.readAloud: "Rest, friends. You're so tired. Why not rest here, where the song is kind?"
plays.response: The Leader states the price in the offer: one night by the Hush Shrine, and the Hush takes a dream from each sleeper, who then cannot dream until the Hush is struck, sealed or tuned. Anyone may refuse; characters of absent players are away and lose nothing. A character who does not sleep (Trance, keeping watch) loses nothing and the Cult is courteous. The Hush stirs.
plays.consequence: A full rest, and a hollow where dreams were. The Hush stirs.
plays.tells: Players are tired, hurt, or tormented by the Sleepless, and the Leader has named the price.
plays.rules: Record each lost dream as Other in the ledger. Not a Toll: only a struck, sealed or tuned Seventh returns it.
plays.later: S27: the Concord, the Second Dawn and the Unbound all return dreams (s27-dreams-return); the Empty Choir does not. The Cult's secret: feeding dreams to the Hush is why it is failing.
plays.keywords: rest, sleep, cult, shrine, dreams, accept, hush cult

plays.title: They refuse the Cult and fight
plays.why: The Cult defends the shrine from anyone who would disturb it.
plays.readAloud: The humming stops. Every robed figure turns at once, and their smiles do not change.
plays.response: Run the encounter. The Cult fights to protect the shrine, not to kill; they offer rest even mid-fight. Cultists use Command only as 2024 allows (Halt, Grovel, Approach, Drop, Flee), never "Rest". The Leader drains dreams only from Charmed or Incapacitated targets.
plays.consequence: The way to the shrine stairs is open.
plays.tells: Players threaten the circle or push toward the shrine.
plays.rules: Encounter: four Hush Cultists and a Cult Leader.
plays.later: S18B: the stairs are unguarded. S22: the Cult is not an ally.
plays.keywords: fight, cult, refuse, attack, hush cult, shrine

plays.title: They tell the Cult its rest is killing the Hush
plays.why: The Cult is right about the danger and wrong about the cure; the truth can turn them.
plays.readAloud: The Cult Leader listens with her eyes closed. When she opens them, she looks very young and very tired. "Then what have we been doing?"
plays.response: With evidence (the Notes, the Librarian, Detect Thoughts on the Leader, or the Hush's own words) the Cult stops feeding the Hush and some members follow the party. Without it they are polite and unconvinced (s17b-cult-unconvinced).
plays.consequence: The Cult stops feeding the Hush; the lullaby steadies a little.
plays.tells: The party has evidence that fed dreams weaken the lullaby.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion) DC 16 against the Leader; Advantage with evidence.
plays.later: S22: the Cult is an unusual ally (s22-ally-cult): they know the shrine and quiet the Sleepless for one scene. S19B: they weep when Mirel rings.
plays.keywords: cult, truth, persuade, dreams, hush failing, convince, talk

plays.title: The Cult is not convinced
plays.why: Without evidence, a kind smile does not budge.
plays.readAloud: “That's kind of you to say,” says the Leader, and she means it. “But we have been so tired for so long.”
plays.response: The Cult remains polite. They offer rest again and do not stop feeding the Hush. The way to the stairs stays open if the party leaves them alone.
plays.consequence: No change; the Cult keeps feeding.
plays.tells: Persuasion fails or the party has no proof.
plays.later: Anytime: with evidence they listen later.
plays.keywords: cult, unconvinced, refuse, persuade, fail

plays.title: They slip past the circle to the stairs
plays.why: The Cult is tired and kind, not watchful.
plays.readAloud: The humming never stops. Nobody turns their head as you slip past the edge of the firelight.
plays.response: Group Stealth against the Cult's Passive Perception 12. Success: the party reaches the stairs unseen. Failure: the Cult notices and offers rest; they do not attack unless provoked.
plays.consequence: Access to the stairs without an encounter.
plays.tells: A rogue studies the circle.
plays.rules: Group Dexterity (Stealth) DC 13.
plays.later: S18B: the stairs are open.
plays.keywords: stealth, sneak, cult, stairs, hide

plays.title: They read the Cult with Zone of Truth or Detect Thoughts
plays.why: The Cult's kindness looks too good to be true.
plays.readAloud: The Leader answers every question with the same soft sincerity, and under each answer lies another: a dream, a name, a bed.
plays.response: Zone of Truth: the Cult believes every word; none is lying. Detect Thoughts on the Leader surfaces two things: she is dying slowly, and she feeds the Hush her own dreams first. This is the evidence for s17b-talk-cult.
plays.consequence: Evidence for the talk-cult play.
plays.tells: A caster prepares truth magic.
plays.rules: Zone of Truth (Charisma save); Detect Thoughts (Wisdom save to probe).
plays.later: S17B: Persuasion against the Leader has Advantage.
plays.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, cult, truth, evidence

plays.title: They agree to help Corin
plays.why: Corin has the Notes, a workshop and three generations of purpose.
plays.readAloud: "Ah, you've been to Brassfall. Good. My name is Corin Aldeth. My family has tried to finish a song for three generations, and I think you may be the first people in a century who can help me finish it."
plays.response: He shows them Edda Thorne's Notes, with the Quiet Night leaf, and the rite his family calls the Concord: six rung bells hold the lullaby while the Key is seated, never struck. He is honest that the Notes name a price: the Ringer's "whole name". For three generations his family read it as a bell-name, a title. Today he says: "I think it means yours. I am sorry." He asks for help and gives them the Notes. The Great Toll is always asked in private and always refusable.
plays.consequence: The party has the Notes and a Bellwright ally.
plays.tells: Players listen to his plan with interest.
plays.later: S22: the Notes tell the Key's truth (s22-read-notes), and Corin offers to pay the Great Toll himself (s22-corin-strike). S27: the Concord with Corin as the Seventh's voice is possible (s27-corin-voice).
plays.keywords: corin, bellwright, help, notes, agree, workshop, plan

plays.title: They refuse Corin
plays.why: Waking a god is a lot to sign up for.
plays.readAloud: Corin looks disappointed rather than angry. Somewhere under the workshop, something bronze begins to pace.
plays.response: He lets them go and sends a Heart-Hound to follow them. If they argue, he explains his logic for hours, passionately and without cruelty. He still wants the Concord; without the party he will try to reach the shrine and seat the Key himself.
plays.consequence: A bronze hound on their trail.
plays.tells: Players balk at the Seventh.
plays.later: S22: Corin can still be argued round (s22-corin-comes-round). S26: if he reaches the bell with the Key before all six rang, he seats it early and the lullaby cracks (s26-corin-cracks-the-lullaby). The Notes can be copied (s18a-copy-notes).
plays.keywords: refuse, corin, no, decline, hound, follow

plays.title: They fight Corin's hounds
plays.why: If talks break down, or the party tries to take the Notes by force.
plays.readAloud: The hounds ring when they bite. The whole workshop rings with them.
plays.response: Run the Bellwright ambush. Corin joins only if forced, and stops the moment someone says they have rung a bell. If the party kills him, use s18a-kill-corin; if they spare him, he stays an enemy who still wants the Concord.
plays.consequence: Corin becomes an enemy, and the Notes may be taken by force.
plays.tells: Weapons drawn in the workshop.
plays.rules: Encounter: Heart-Hounds and Corin. Non-lethal: declare it when a melee attack drops a hound or Corin to 0 HP.
plays.later: S24: an enemy Corin reaches the summit with Heart-Hounds (enc-s24-summit-corin); a spared one may come round (s22-corin-comes-round).
plays.keywords: fight, corin, hounds, heart-hound, workshop, ambush

plays.title: They argue with Corin about the price
plays.why: A name is a great deal to ask, and players test it.
plays.readAloud: “You think I do not know how it sounds? My grandmother rang a bell once. She forgot her sister's face for a week and called that the price. She was wrong. It was only the first line.”
plays.response: Corin is passionate and honest: he does not know if the Notes mean the Ringer's name in the world's memory or on the page. He asks no one to decide tonight. He explains the Deferred Toll he can offer (an hour, never cancel). Let the table argue; at the end they accept (s18a-meet-corin), refuse (s18a-refuse-corin) or fight.
plays.consequence: The party understands the price before choosing.
plays.tells: Players ask what "the whole name" means.
plays.rules: Insight DC 12: he believes every word. Influence (Persuasion) DC 15 to move him from the Concord only with a better route.
plays.later: S22: the Great Toll is asked of one volunteer in private (s27-concord).
plays.keywords: corin, argue, price, name, toll, great toll

plays.title: They copy or steal Edda's Notes
plays.why: A refusing party may still want the pages.
plays.readAloud: The pages are brittle and tight with a student's hand. The Quiet Night leaf is pinned to the back.
plays.response: DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) to take them, or a day with Forgery Kit to copy. On a failure Corin catches them: he lets them read the Quiet Night leaf at the table, but keeps the Notes. Either way the party learns the Key's truth at S22.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Notes, or has read the leaf.
plays.fallback: If the roll fails, the leaf is still read.
plays.tells: Players study the Notes on the table, or case the workshop.
plays.rules: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) DC 15; or Forgery Kit DC 13 for a full day.
plays.later: S22: the truth of the Key (s22-read-notes). Corin remembers a theft.
plays.keywords: notes, steal, copy, edda, quiet night

plays.title: They kill Corin
plays.why: A fight in the workshop can end in a death.
plays.readAloud: The tuning hammer rings once on the stone floor, a clean note, and nobody picks it up.
plays.response: Corin dies. The Notes pass to the party. The Heart-Hounds go still and cold; the Bellwrights turn against the party and the workshop goes dark. Wren, if she is an ally, says nothing for days.
plays.consequence: Corin is dead; the Bellwrights are hostile.
plays.fallback: If the table has second thoughts, a Bloodied Corin yields before the last blow.
plays.tells: The party presses a Bloodied Corin.
plays.later: S22: no Bellwright ally. S27: no Corin voice. S28: the Bellwrights are not at the epilogue.
plays.keywords: kill, corin, workshop, death, bellwrights

plays.title: They study Corin's workshop
plays.why: Unfinished bells and a lathe shaped like a Key.
plays.readAloud: On the central bench lies a plaster casting of something long and narrow, hollow where a hand would grip.
plays.response: Study, Intelligence (Arcana or Investigation) DC 14: the casting is the shape of the Tuning Key as the Notes describe it, and the lathe is for a copy Corin never dared finish. A copy is not the Key; the Seventh answers only the real one. Corin will let a Smith's Tools proficient character make a small ordinary bell (any-become-bellwrights).
plays.consequence: A clue about the Key's shape, and the Bellwright craft.
plays.tells: Players ask what the half-made bells are for.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Arcana or Investigation) DC 14.
plays.later: S22: the Key is a heart, not a tool (s22-read-notes).
plays.keywords: workshop, casting, lathe, key, bellwright, study

plays.title: They walk a few steps down to the Hush
plays.why: Curiosity pulls everyone toward the sleeping bell.
plays.readAloud: "Be quiet now. You're so close. I've held everything together for four hundred years, and I'm so tired. If you wake me, the dream will end. Do you want that?"
plays.response: They can hear the Hush, but cannot ring Ysh without the Key. The Hush speaks in the listener's own sleeping voice. State the price before the first step: the first nineteen steps cost nothing; every full twenty steps walked costs one memory, up to the campaign cap. A character makes one DC 13 Wisdom save the first time they reach step 20: on a failure their total stairs price across the whole campaign is capped at five memories, on a success at two. Count steps for each character.
plays.consequence: They know what waits below.
plays.tells: Players go to the top of the shrine stairs.
plays.rules: Record any stairs memories as Stairs in the ledger; they count toward the S25 maximum. The save is made once per character, ever.
plays.later: S25: the full descent costs only what remains of the cap.
plays.keywords: stairs, hush, shrine, visit, listen, steps, voice

plays.title: Corin comes up the shrine stairs
plays.why: On Branch B, Corin meets the party at the Tor.
plays.readAloud: "Mirel first. Mirel is the lullaby's mother. Ring her, and the Seventh's voice will carry. Ring her wrong, and the Hush will sing you to sleep before the Court can arrest you."
plays.response: Run Corin's offer here (once per campaign): the Notes, his plan, his honesty about the Toll. He wants Mirel rung first because it quiets the Tor; he wants the Concord, not a strike. Offer the three plays that follow.
plays.consequence: The party meets Corin.
plays.tells: The party hasn't met Corin yet.
plays.later: S21: accept, refuse or fight him (next plays).
plays.keywords: corin, arrives, mirel first, notes, bellwright, tor

plays.title: They agree to help Corin on the stairs
plays.why: On Branch B, Corin offers the Notes at the Tor.
plays.readAloud: “Mirel first,” Corin says again, and unrolls a map of the Tor across a step. “Then the others. Let me show you the song.”
plays.response: As s18a-meet-corin: the Notes, the Quiet Night leaf, the Concord rite, the honest warning about the price. He gives them the Notes.
plays.consequence: The party has the Notes and a Bellwright ally.
plays.tells: Players listen to his plan with interest.
plays.later: S22: s22-read-notes. S27: s27-corin-voice.
plays.keywords: corin, accept, help, notes, tor

plays.title: They refuse Corin on the stairs
plays.why: A party may not want to bring a stranger to the Hush.
plays.readAloud: Corin looks down the stairs, and then at you. “Then I will go down alone one day. Better with you.”
plays.response: As s18a-refuse-corin. He leaves, hurt but not hostile. A Heart-Hound shadows them.
plays.consequence: Corin leaves; a hound follows.
plays.tells: Players balk at the Concord.
plays.later: As s18a-refuse-corin: s26-corin-cracks-the-lullaby if he reaches the bell early.
plays.keywords: corin, refuse, decline, hound

plays.title: They fight Corin on the stairs
plays.why: A fight at the stairs risks the Hush listening.
plays.readAloud: His hammer rings on the stone, and down the stairs something stirs at the sound.
plays.response: Run as s18a-fight-corin, but every loud blow wakes the Hush a little: each round of fighting the Hush's voice grows (Wisdom save DC 13 or Frightened until the end of the next turn). Corin stops when someone says they have rung a bell.
plays.consequence: Corin is an enemy.
plays.tells: Weapons drawn at the top step.
plays.rules: Encounter: Corin, 2 Heart-Hounds. DC 13 Wisdom save per round in the stairwell.
plays.later: S24: enemy Corin at the summit (enc-s24-summit-corin).
plays.keywords: corin, fight, stairs, enemy

plays.title: They ask the Hush a question
plays.why: The Hush speaks, so players answer.
plays.readAloud: The voice is your own, half asleep. “One question. Give me a true memory of someone you loved, and I will give you a true answer.”
plays.response: The Hush answers one question per true memory offered (Trade, ledger). True but partial: it will say that someone took its voice four hundred years ago, that it is tired, and that the one who keeps the Key is afraid, not cruel. It will not lie.
plays.consequence: A true, partial answer.
plays.tells: Players speak aloud on the stairs.
plays.rules: Any Heart-less character may offer a memory; the Hush never takes without consent.
plays.later: S22: the answer prepares the Key's truth.
plays.keywords: hush, question, ask, memory, stairs, answer

plays.title: They pass the Hush Cult at the stairs
plays.why: The Cult keeps vigil at the top of the stairs.
plays.readAloud: Six robed figures sit around the top step. They look up, smiling, and one pats the stone beside her.
plays.response: If cult is ceased, they step aside and warn the party about the price. If feeding, they plead and then sit across the stairs; DC 14 Persuasion or Stealth lets the party by without a fight. Never attack the sleeping.
plays.consequence: The way down is open.
plays.tells: Players want to go down and see robed figures.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion) DC 14 or group Stealth DC 14.
plays.later: S25: the Cult is no obstacle, or has to be dealt with.
plays.keywords: cult, stairs, pass, vigil

plays.title: They walk all the way down early
plays.why: Some parties go straight to the bottom before they have the Key.
plays.readAloud: The last step is wider than the others, and at the bottom a bell the size of a house hangs in the dark, blank as a sleeping face.
plays.response: They pay the stairs price (one save, five or two memories, once per character, ever). They reach the shrine and see Ysh, but cannot ring it without the Key. The Hush speaks to them in their own voices. They can climb back up. A group that has reached the shrine can later Teleport to it, since they have seen it (any-teleport-and-gates).
plays.consequence: They have been to the bottom, lighter.
plays.tells: Players ask how deep it goes and want to see Ysh.
plays.rules: DC 13 Wisdom save at step 20, once per character; record Stairs in the ledger.
plays.later: S25: the stairs cost only what remains of the cap (nothing, if they paid in full). S26: they have seen the bell.
plays.keywords: descend, bottom, shrine, stairs, early

plays.title: They ring Thrane
plays.why: They have the Heart and stand at the Lightning Shafts.
plays.readAloud: The bell cracks like a whip. The sky above Brassfall splits open, and for the first time in four centuries a real storm rolls over the mountains. Rain falls like bronze filings. The storm-stones blaze, and every metal object you carry hums in answer.
plays.response: State the Toll first: a Sense, chosen by the Ringer, gone for one day (sight means Blinded, hearing Deafened). The Ringer is Lightning-Marked until the next dawn. Storms return; the Ironhorn celebrate; Kessa's sickness eases for a season.
plays.consequence: Thrane is rung. Storms return to Brassfall.
plays.tells: Players ask the Toll.
plays.rules: Lightning-Marked: once, when the Ringer takes Lightning damage before dawn, they can use their Reaction to deal 1d6 Lightning to a creature within 10 feet. The Sense Toll can't be ended early by magic.
plays.later: S19A: the Court sends a strike force for the Heart (s19a-strike-force). S28: within a month new fleets crowd Pellmoor and the Landing Charter starts to fail (s28-landing-fleets). Concord: one step closer.
plays.keywords: ring thrane, storm, bell, toll, sense, lightning shafts, brassfall

plays.response: The oath is kept. The Ironhorn ride for the party at the Tor.
plays.consequence: An ally for the end.
plays.tells: The ringing is done and the oath is in the Bargain log.
plays.rules: Mark the oath Kept in the Bargain log.

plays.response: The oath is broken. Kessa does not chase them; he spreads the word. The Ironhorn do not ride for them, and Yenna is torn. Kessa's reasons are his own: he can still come to the Strike for the Court's throat (s23-kessa-intercepts).
plays.consequence: The party has the Heart and has lost the steppe.
plays.tells: Players argue the Court would take it from the Ironhorn anyway.
plays.rules: Mark the oath Broken in the Bargain log.

plays.title: They read Edda Thorne's account of the Quiet Night
plays.why: The diary, the Notes or the Librarian finally tell what the Key is.
plays.readAloud: "He wants to tune the seven into one long spring. I told him the seventh is not a bell. It is the lullaby. The Key is not a tuning tool. It is the heart that sings Oum to sleep, and he has taken it to make the calendar behave. If he strikes the Seventh with it, the dream will wake or it will crack. I told him so. He did not hear me."
plays.response: Piece it together with them: the Seventh keeps Oum asleep; the Key is its only Heart; Imber struck the Key against the bells and the discord cracked the lullaby; Maudrin has known since she took the Key. The sources: Corin's Notes (with the Quiet Night leaf), the diary, or the Librarian, who reads the page aloud for one true memory (not if the party robbed the courier). One line in the Notes says Thrane's weather "will go to the rim and wait": a sharp player may connect it to the Stormwall.
plays.consequence: The party knows what every ending costs and why.
plays.fallback: If they miss every source, the Librarian's courier finds them with the page, unless they robbed it; then Corin or Wren brings a copy.
plays.tells: Players open the diary or the Notes, or ask the Librarian.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (History or Arcana) DC 13 to connect the line about Thrane's weather to the Stormwall; no roll needed for the main truth.
plays.later: S22: Telling Isolde (s22-tell-isolde) and Haldric (s24-haldric-truth) the truth can turn them. S24 to S27: the four endings are now informed choices.

The palace vault is empty: the Key goes with her. The Strike is a day or two away because the Hush frays faster with every bell: she must bring the Key near the Seventh to hold it steady (s22-why-maudrin-marches).

plays.response: Ask each player which ally they want to bring and which they trust, then run one ally play per company that agrees: each is +1 on the allies clock and takes an objective (hold the ridge, cut the retreat, break the line), not a creature count. The clock stops at 6. Ally logistics: Hallowmere to the Tor is about four days; Pellmoor is six; the Choir cannot leave the Mere, so its hymn arrives by a Mere-glass vial (Mother Sallow's message); the Stilled walk slowly and arrive at dusk.

plays.title: Corin offers to pay the Great Toll himself
plays.why: Corin's whole family has tried to finish this song for three generations, and the Notes now name the price.
plays.readAloud: “If the price is a name, then let it be mine. My grandmother died one breath into this song. Let me finish it.”
plays.response: Corin, who misread the "whole name" for years, now understands the Great Toll and offers to be the Ringer himself. He is wrong to want it for the family's sake, not evil. Let the party argue; his offer does not remove their consent for anyone else. He can defer a Toll for an hour, never cancel it.
plays.consequence: A willing Ringer is on the table that is not a PC.
plays.tells: Corin is allied and reads the Notes with the party.
plays.later: S26: if the party refuses him, he may still try to reach the bell (s26-corin-cracks-the-lullaby). S27: the Concord with Corin as the Seventh's voice (s27-corin-voice).
plays.keywords: corin, strike, ring the seventh, bellwright, argue, wake oum

plays.title: They ambush Maudrin's column on the road
plays.why: Proactive parties strike first, on ground they choose.
plays.readAloud: From the ridge you can see the column coming: grey horses, grey gloves, and one rider in dove-grey at the centre.
plays.response: Ansel knows the routes Maudrin's Hushmen take from the palace to the Tor. A good ambush gives the party Surprise and a chosen battlefield; the vanguard (not Maudrin) is hit first. Run the Strike's lead column there instead, then Maudrin arrives at the Tor.
plays.consequence: The Strike happens on the party's terms.
plays.tells: Players ask Ansel Quay or a scout for her route.
plays.rules: Surprise (2024): surprised creatures have Disadvantage on their Initiative rolls. Group Stealth: DC 14 against the column's Passive Perception.
plays.later: S23 as normal, with terrain and surprise in the party's favour: Maudrin's remaining column is smaller, and she will not underestimate them again.
plays.keywords: ambush, road, column, attack first, ansel, route, surprise

plays.title: Why Maudrin leaves Hallowmere now
plays.why: Players ask why she waited thirty-eight years and goes now.
plays.readAloud: “She has had it thirty-eight years,” Ansel says, quietly. “She never took it out of the vault. Why would she take it out now?”
plays.response: The truth, for the DM: the Court's silence-stones and gloves are tuned to the Key's hum, and a sealed Key would go quiet and end them. She kept it close to the Seventh's tune and far from any recess. Each bell rung shifts the world's key, so the Key's hum from the palace no longer holds the lullaby; she must carry it to the Tor to keep it steady. She wants the unrung Hearts (rung Hearts are worthless to her), the Key, and the Ringer, to Tithe, so no one can pay the Great Toll or strike. She will seal the stairs, not the Key.
plays.consequence: The table has a reason for her march.
plays.tells: A player asks Isolde, Ansel, a prisoner, or casts Detect Thoughts.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 (Isolde or Ansel); Detect Thoughts on Maudrin: "keep it as it is."
plays.later: S24: she negotiates a seal. S26: her last offer.
plays.keywords: maudrin, why, motive, key, silence stones, march

plays.title: Maudrin marches to take back the Key
plays.why: If the party holds the Key, she comes for it.
plays.readAloud: The scout is out of breath. “She's left the city. No case on the chain, this time. She's wearing her gloves and nothing else.”
plays.response: With the Key gone, Maudrin marches on the Tor by the party's route with every Hushman she can spare. She means to retake the Key and the Ringer. She is angrier and less patient.
plays.consequence: The Court marches.
plays.tells: The party took the Key from the palace vault.
plays.later: S23: the Strike, with the party holding the Key. Haldric hesitates if he sees it (s23-haldric-hesitates).
plays.keywords: maudrin, march, retake, key, party holds

plays.title: Tristan Vesk marches in her place
plays.why: If Maudrin is dead, her cousin takes the Key.
plays.readAloud: The man in dove-grey is not a woman, and he is not alone: Wardens, a hundred Hushmen, Dawn Order knights.
plays.response: Tristan Vesk, now Chancellor, carries the Key in the same grey case. He is cautious and clever, less frightening and less certain. He wants the Hearts and the Ringer. He knows the Key's truth only from Maudrin's papers.
plays.consequence: The Court marches under a new Chancellor.
plays.tells: Maudrin was killed before Act IV.
plays.later: S23: the Strike with Tristan (enc-s23-strike-tristan). S24: no Maudrin at the summit; Tristan or Haldric hold the stones.
plays.keywords: tristan, chancellor, march, maudrin dead

plays.title: They fight the Strike
plays.why: Most parties won't give up the Hearts.
plays.readAloud: Hushmen on grey horses come over the ridge in a long line. Their gloves catch the light and throw it back as silence. Behind them rides a figure in dove-grey. "Good evening," Maudrin Vesk says. "I'm so sorry to interrupt. But I believe you have something that belongs to me."
plays.response: Run the Strike. She wants the unrung Hearts the party carries (rung Hearts are worthless to her), the Key back if they hold it, and the Ringer. She retreats toward the Tor when Bloodied: "I'll see you at the Shrine." Track her HP and the Key's possession into the next scene. Each ally takes its objective (do not delete creatures).
plays.consequence: The Court's army is broken or holds the road.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns, the allies' actions (riders, the Stilled, the Choir) are the cavalry.
plays.tells: Weapons out on the ridge; the party refuses her offer.
plays.rules: Encounter: the Strike (pick the version for the oath-duel and for Maudrin). Surprise (2024) gives surprised creatures Disadvantage on Initiative.
plays.later: S24: Maudrin at the summit, as the Keeper, Bloodied if she was Bloodied here. Level 10 after the Strike.
plays.keywords: fight, strike, battle, ridge, maudrin, hushmen, army, combat

plays.title: They surrender to Maudrin
plays.why: Outnumbered parties sometimes yield.
plays.readAloud: "Thank you. That was wise. Now: the Hearts, please. And your Ringer will come with me to the Quiet Court."
plays.response: She takes the unrung Hearts, and the Key if the party holds it. She demands the party's Ringer come to be Tithed; the player chooses whether to accept. A saving throw never decides consent. Record each Heart handed over as Court custody in World state. Refusal leads to negotiation, escape (s23-escape-captivity) or a capture attempt. The Empty Choir needs the group's choice to end its resistance (s23-accept-tithe).
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Hearts and the Key.
plays.fallback: Offer an escape: Brannagh's pilots, Yenna's riders, or a Stormborn ship waiting off the coast.
plays.tells: Players ask her terms.
plays.later: S27: s27-empty-choir if they accept. A rescue chapter can reverse it.
plays.keywords: surrender, give up, yield, hand over hearts, captured, terms

plays.tells: The party takes the Key mid-fight and Haldric is present.

He is held off the field by a Hushman with a promise of safety; no violence on-screen; the scene has an exit (the Hushman releases him if the Heart is handed over). If it is a Line, make him an adult dependent or remove the threat. If Ilam is an ally, he goes for his son without being asked.

plays.title: They fight Maudrin at the summit
plays.why: She still holds the Key and stands between the party and the stairs.
plays.readAloud: "I'm glad you came," Maudrin says. "Shall we begin?" Behind her the Hush rises out of the stairway like a tide, so low you feel it in your ribs.
plays.response: Run the summit with Maudrin as the Keeper (sb_maudrin_keeper). She fights to slow the party and walks down the stairs when Bloodied, with Silence Step covering her; she means to seal the stairs and keep the Key. If she was Bloodied at the Strike she starts Bloodied here. Before she can act at the bell, establish her threat aloud: if they are about to take the Key, she will strike rather than lose control. Allies take their objectives (hold the stones, screen the stairs); the Cantor's vial gives Advantage on Wisdom saves against Frightened.
plays.consequence: Maudrin is beaten back down the stairs, or captured, or the party holds the Key.
plays.fallback: If the fight turns against the party, an ally's one dramatic action (the Stilled, Yenna's riders, the Cantor's hymn) opens a way past.
plays.tells: Weapons out at the stone ring; casters ready Counterspell.
plays.rules: Encounter: the summit. Her Legendary Resistance is real; Counterspell on her Counterspell works by the usual rules. Grapple and disarm work by 2024 rules; knocking the case from her hand is DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) as a Utilize action.
plays.later: S25: the stairs; the Court's sealers wait. S26: if she reaches the bell with the Key she is there with whatever HP she had left.
plays.keywords: fight, maudrin, summit, battle, attack, final battle, tor

plays.title: They take the Key from Maudrin at the summit
plays.why: A good grapple or a nimble rogue ends the race to the bell before it starts.
plays.readAloud: The case comes away in your hand, heavier than it looks, humming through the silence-stone like a heart through a wall.
plays.response: Once she has been hit this fight, a character who reaches her can take the case. On a success Maudrin stops fighting: she has nothing left to bargain with and knows it. On a failure she notices and keeps it; she escapes only by ordinary movement.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Key at the top of the stairs.
plays.tells: A player positions next to her and asks about the chain.
plays.rules: DC 17 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or win a grapple and use a Utilize action to take it. Legendary Resistance does not apply to ability checks.
plays.later: S26 runs the party-holds-the-Key version. Forecast: Concord, Second Dawn and the Unbound all depend only on the party.
plays.keywords: take the key, steal, grab, case, chain, sleight of hand, summit

plays.title: They talk with Maudrin instead of fighting
plays.why: If the party already holds the Key, she negotiates; even if not, she always offers words first.
plays.readAloud: "I'm not your enemy. I'm the last person in Corvane who understands what the silence costs. Four centuries of Tithes. Blanks. Children who forget their mothers. And you want to wake the thing that holds it all together? You're mad, or you're brave. I've never been able to tell the difference."
plays.response: Let her make her case honestly: she has kept the lullaby steady for thirty-eight years by keeping the truth from everyone. She will agree to a seal if she thinks the party won't strike. Her Final Offer (H-26): everything they want, all of it already Tithed and in her vault. She can be persuaded to surrender, or to come down the stairs as a witness; her voice-for-the-Seventh offer (s24-maudrin-as-voice) is the only way she ever pays the Great Toll.
plays.consequence: A truce at the summit, on terms.
plays.fallback: If talk breaks down, she retreats down the stairs rather than fight a party that holds the Key.
plays.tells: Someone lowers a weapon and asks her why.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion): DC 20 (her Intelligence as the Keeper), DC 18 if she is the Strike's Maudrin; automatic if the party holds the Key and offers a seal. Insight DC 15: she believes every word.
plays.later: S26: she may stand beside the bell weeping rather than fighting. S27: she can argue for her vision with Oum but never decides for the table.
plays.keywords: talk, negotiate, maudrin, persuade, surrender, final offer, parley

plays.title: They capture Maudrin
plays.why: Some parties want her alive to answer for the Tithe.
plays.readAloud: She sits down on the cold stone very carefully, like an old woman at the end of a long day, and holds out her wrists.
plays.response: A creature reduced to 0 HP by a melee attack can be knocked out instead of killed (2024). Bound, she talks: the diary, the Key, the lullaby. Her Hushmen surrender if she orders it. Haldric, if present and told she is his mother, takes her into custody himself. The Key is in the case at her chest; the party takes it.
plays.consequence: Maudrin is a prisoner; the Court is leaderless.
plays.tells: Players announce non-lethal blows or ask about manacles and silence-stone.
plays.rules: Non-lethal: declare when the melee attack drops her to 0 HP.
plays.later: S28: her fate is the party's to decide: trial, exile, or Tithe by her own office (s28-maudrin-trial, s28-maudrin-exile). Tristan Vesk moves to fill her chair (s28-tristan-chair).
plays.keywords: capture, knock out, non-lethal, prisoner, arrest maudrin, spare

plays.title: They kill Maudrin
plays.why: Thirty-eight years of Tithes makes her an easy villain to finish.
plays.readAloud: The silence-stone gloves fall open. For the first time since you met her, Maudrin Vesk makes a sound: one breath out, very long, like someone setting down something heavy.
plays.response: She dies. The Key is on her body (the party takes it). Her Hushmen scatter or surrender. If Haldric is present and knew she was his mother, he chooses what to do with her body; his fate follows play.
plays.consequence: The Chancellor is dead; the Key is free.
plays.tells: No one declares mercy; someone asks whether she's still breathing.
plays.later: S28: Tristan Vesk becomes Chancellor and wants the Key (s28-tristan-chair). Haldric finds the letters in her case (s24-letters-in-the-case).
plays.keywords: kill maudrin, death, execute, finish her, dead

plays.title: They tell Haldric he is Maudrin's son
plays.why: If they found proof (her diary, Isolde's secrets, Ansel's files), this is the moment.
plays.readAloud: Haldric stops polishing his sword. He looks at Maudrin, and she does not deny it, and that is worse than anything she could have said.
plays.response: Haldric half-suspected it. Faced with proof and her silence, he lowers his sword and steps out of the Court's line. He won't fight her, and he won't fight for her. If he fights for her, his knights fight too; this play ends that.
plays.consequence: Haldric and any knights loyal to him leave the fight.
plays.tells: Players have evidence (the letters in the case, Ansel's copied files, or Isolde's secrets) and Haldric is on the field.
plays.rules: Evidence makes it automatic; without it, Influence (Persuasion) DC 18 (his Intelligence is 12; use the higher of 15 and his Intelligence, with Disadvantage because it is his mother).
plays.later: S28: Haldric chooses his own fate (s28-haldric-rook).
plays.keywords: haldric, son, mother, maudrin, truth, reveal, parentage

plays.title: They find Maudrin's letters in the Key's case
plays.why: The case has a lining, and someone has been writing letters.
plays.readAloud: Under the Key, folded into the grey lining, lie forty years of letters, none sealed, all addressed to Haldric Mose.
plays.response: The letters tell, in Maudrin's careful hand, that Haldric is her son and that she watched him grow from across a hall. They are the evidence for s24-haldric-truth and the letters Haldric finds in the Aftermath. The letters also record that she never opened the Key's recess because the Court's stones are tuned to it.
plays.consequence: The party has proof of Haldric's parentage and a clue to her motive.
plays.tells: The party holds the Key's case and opens it.
plays.later: S24: s24-haldric-truth. S28: s28-haldric-rook.

plays.readAloud: The case is heavy in your hands. Maudrin watches it as one watches a child on a ledge.
plays.response: She takes it, gently. She will not strike. She goes down to the stairs with her Hushmen; the party is welcome to follow. The decision about what she does with it is not yet taken: it goes to s26.
plays.consequence: Maudrin holds the Key by the party's choice.

plays.title: They make a deal with Maudrin at the summit
plays.why: Her Final Offer is tempting: everything already Tithed, returned to them.
plays.readAloud: “Everything on the list,” Maudrin says. “Every jar, every name. I will sign it. And you will walk down the hill and let me seal the stairs.”
plays.response: If the group chooses this, it ends its resistance: the Court secures the Key and seals the stairs. She keeps her word about the bargain and about nothing else. This is the Empty Choir route. Do not let the dice or a clock decide it; ask the table.
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Key; the resistance ends.

plays.readAloud: “If it must be a name,” she says, “then I have more than most to give.”

plays.why: Bloodied, she heads for the bell.
plays.readAloud: She turns and goes down, one hand on the wall, and the Hush rises to meet her.

plays.title: They descend the stairs of the Hush
plays.why: The bell is at the bottom of a hundred steps.
plays.readAloud: The stairs go on for a long time. Each step has a memory carved into it, worn smooth by the feet of those who came to listen. Some are your memories. Some are strangers'. You hear a child laughing, a bell tolling, a man telling a joke to someone who isn't there.
plays.response: Disclose the full price at the first step: the first nineteen steps cost nothing; every full twenty costs one memory; each descender makes one DC 13 Wisdom save the first time they reach step 20, once per character for the whole campaign (earlier visits count). On a failure their total across the whole campaign is capped at five memories, on a success at two. A character who paid part of it at the S18B visit pays only what remains. Players may turn back. Each names their losses briefly, or keeps a private list and shares one. Losses are recollections, never class features, player knowledge or control of the character. Never make an absent player's character pay.
plays.consequence: The descenders reach Ysh, lighter.
plays.fallback: If the price stops the table cold, offer the foundry chute.
plays.tells: Players ask who goes down and who stays.
plays.rules: DC 13 Wisdom saving throw at step 20. Record each loss as Stairs in the Memory ledger. The dead pay nothing.
plays.later: S26: who stands at the bell is who paid the stairs. These losses are not Tolls and are not refunded by any ending. Allies who paid carry it in their epilogue (s28-stairs-payers).
plays.keywords: stairs, descend, hush, memories, cost, walk down, hundred steps

plays.title: They find another way down
plays.why: v5 says a route that genuinely avoids the stairs avoids their price.
plays.readAloud: At the top of the Tor, under the ring of stones, the old casting-pit drops straight down into the dark. Warm air rises out of it, smelling of bronze.
plays.response: The bells were cast at the summit and lowered to their halls; the casting chute still drops to the Hush chamber. It's a hard climb in the dark but costs no memories. Corin or the Notes can point it out. Flight or teleportation that reaches the chamber also works. Don't add a replacement punishment. Allies who cannot climb wait above.
plays.consequence: The party reaches the bell with every memory intact.
plays.tells: Players ask about the old foundry where the bells were cast, or prepare flight or Dimension Door.
plays.rules: Three DC 15 Strength (Athletics) checks to climb; a failure is a slip: 2024 Falling, 1d6 Bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen (decide the distance before rolling, usually 20 feet). A slip never stops the descent.
plays.later: S26 as normal. The chute is known after this: S27 uses the same route to get an injured Ringer out.
plays.keywords: another way, avoid stairs, foundry, chute, climb, fly, dimension door, shortcut

plays.title: Allies refuse to go down
plays.why: Some NPCs will not pay with their memories, and some will, which is the beat.
plays.readAloud: Ilam Bray looks down the stairs for a long moment, then at Jonah. "I've only just got him back," he says. "I can't lose him again."
plays.response: Let the allies choose in character. Those who stay hold the summit. Those who go pay the stairs like anyone else. Never make an absent player's character pay. Children (Jonah, Ila, Bet) are never asked to descend by an NPC and never go; they wait above with a trusted adult, and a player may not send them down. Ila is in Pellmoor unless the table brought her.
plays.consequence: The party knows who is with them all the way down.
plays.tells: Players turn to Ilam, Rook, Yenna or Corin at the top step.
plays.later: S28: an ally who paid the stairs carries it in their epilogue (s28-stairs-payers).
plays.keywords: allies, refuse, stay behind, ila, ilam, rook, yenna, go down, companions

plays.consequence: The shrine is reached.
plays.tells: The party has paid the stairs.

plays.consequence: The party reaches the shrine.
plays.tells: A caster prepares Teleport.

plays.title: They stop Maudrin striking Ysh
plays.why: If she holds the Key at the bell, the whole world hangs on one action.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin stands beside the bell with the Key raised. "Let me seal it, and the world continues. Take another step, and I will choose what follows." Her hand is shaking.
plays.response: Ask what the characters do before she acts; if combat begins, roll initiative and use the Keeper with her Wardens. Striking needs her action while adjacent to Ysh with the Key out of its case. Grappling, disarming, bargaining and blocking her route can all prevent it. She prefers to seal the stairs and hold the Key. Only a completed strike opens the Unbound; killing her afterward can't undo the sound.
plays.consequence: She strikes, seals, surrenders, or loses the Key.
plays.fallback: If the table freezes, have her hesitate one heartbeat and say a name: Cassia's, or her grandmother Ilse's.
plays.tells: Maudrin raises the Key; players shout, move, or reach for a spell.
plays.rules: Initiative; her strike is her action on her turn. Grapple (2024 Unarmed Strike option) or disarm (DC 17). Counterspell can't stop it: the strike is not a spell. Plane Shift, Banishment and Hold Monster: she has Legendary Resistance and Magic Resistance; see any-geas-dominate-hold.
plays.later: She strikes (s26-maudrin-strikes), seals (s26-maudrin-leaves-with-key), yields (s26-grapple-the-key) or dies (s26-kill-maudrin-at-bell).
plays.keywords: strike, stop her, maudrin, bell, ysh, grapple, disarm, prevent, block

plays.title: Maudrin strikes the Seventh
plays.why: If no one stops her action, she chooses what follows.
plays.readAloud: The Hush cracks. The lullaby falls silent, and the world goes quiet in a way you have never heard before: not the silence of the bells, but the silence of a held breath about to be released.
plays.response: She pays all six Tolls (Memory, Year, Sense, Name, Fear, Gift) and the Hush cracks. Oum opens an eye. The players, not Maudrin and not the DM, choose Remake or Unmake through their conversation with Oum (S27).
plays.consequence: Ysh is struck. Oum wakes.
plays.tells: She is adjacent to Ysh with the Key uncased on her turn.
plays.later: S27: the Unbound (s27-oum-answers, s27-oum-remake, s27-oum-unmake). Dreams return (s27-dreams-return).

plays.title: The party stands at the bell with the Key
plays.why: Everything ends here, and the party decides.
plays.readAloud: The bell is vast and blank, its surface like the face of a sleeping god. You stand before it with the Key in your hands. The lullaby is still there, very faint, asking you to be quiet. Your choice is the only one left in the world.
plays.response: The figure from the Session 11 winter-moment stands at the bell's foot: the character, older, holding the Key, smiling. Ask that player what they feel; don't explain. Then disclose every option and its price before anyone acts (the Forecast tab lists which are open): Concord, Unbound, Second Dawn. Take a table break before an irreversible choice. Maudrin, weeping behind them, offers no resistance.
plays.consequence: The campaign's ending is chosen.
plays.fallback: If the table can't agree, they may postpone: leave with the Key, unsealed, and keep adventuring.
plays.tells: The party holds the Key at the bottom of the stairs.
plays.rules: Concord: seat the Key without striking, a willing Ringer accepts the Great Toll (ask in private). Unbound: strike, the striker pays all six Tolls. Second Dawn: one uninterrupted minute to seal the Key in its recess, no Toll.
plays.later: S27 resolves the chosen path. S28 epilogues follow the ring ledger.
plays.keywords: choice, key, bell, ysh, ending, decide, seventh, final choice

plays.title: They take the Key from Maudrin at the bell
plays.why: A grapple or a disarm ends the race before it starts.
plays.readAloud: The Key comes away from her glove with a sound like a drawn breath. She does not reach for it.
plays.response: She strikes with her action while adjacent to Ysh with the Key uncased; interrupt her before then. Grappling her, knocking the Key from her hand (DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) as a Utilize action), bargaining or blocking her route all work. On success the party holds the Key and Maudrin stops fighting.
plays.consequence: The party holds the Key at the bell.
plays.tells: A player moves next to her and asks about the case.
plays.rules: DC 17 as above. Counterspell can't stop the strike: it is not a spell. Initiative; her strike is her action on her turn.
plays.later: S26 continues with the party's choice (s26-the-choice).
plays.keywords: take key, grapple, disarm, bell, maudrin

plays.title: They talk with Maudrin at the bell
plays.why: She talks before she fights.
plays.readAloud: “I will seal it,” she says, “and no one will wake it. Don't make me choose what comes after.”
plays.response: Let her make her case: the Court's stones are tuned to the Key, and sealing the stairs, not the Key, is her plan. She will agree to a seal and a witness. If the table freezes, she hesitates one heartbeat and says a name: Cassia, or her grandmother Ilse.
plays.consequence: A truce at the bell, on terms.
plays.tells: Someone lowers a weapon.
plays.rules: Influence (Persuasion) DC 20 (her Intelligence 20); she offers terms for the Court's survival.
plays.later: S27: whatever the table decides.
plays.keywords: parley, talk, maudrin, bell, terms

plays.title: They kill Maudrin at the bell
plays.why: The last threat to the Seventh is her.
plays.readAloud: The Key falls out of her hand and rings once on the stone.
plays.response: She dies. If she had not struck, the Key falls and the party takes it; killing her after a strike cannot undo the sound. Her Hushmen yield.
plays.consequence: Maudrin is dead and the Key is free.
plays.tells: Weapons come out at the bell.
plays.later: S27: the party's choice. S28: Tristan Vesk.

plays.response: If the group chooses to end its resistance, Maudrin seals the stairs; the Court holds the Key. This is the Empty Choir. Do not push it. If the table prefers to keep fighting, play escape or rescue.
plays.consequence: The Court secures the Key and the stairs.

plays.title: They perform the Concord
plays.why: Every regional bell rang; the Key is theirs; one person is willing.
plays.readAloud: You hear the six bells, each in its own voice: the dawn bell's clean light, the memory-bell's deep sorrow, the frost-bell's thin ice, the harvest's warm round sound, the storm's crack, the dream's soft lullaby. Together they form a chord that has not existed for four centuries. The chord rises and wraps around the Hush.
plays.response: Ask the Ringer's player in private, before the rite: the Great Toll is their name, forgotten by everyone who knew them, and they become the Seventh's new voice, retiring from ordinary adventuring. They may refuse; then no Toll is taken and the Concord doesn't happen (s27-refuse-toll). If they accept, they seat the Key unstruck and choose their final words. Read: "The Dreamer hears it, sighs, and begins to dream more gently." A willing NPC may be the voice instead (s27-corin-voice, s27-maudrin-voice).
plays.consequence: The world is restored, imperfectly. Dawns, harvests, storms, thaw, quiet dreams, and the dead remembered. The Ringer is the Seventh's voice.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer declines, offer the Second Dawn, or a postponement.
plays.tells: All six bells show as rung in the Forecast, and a player asks what the Great Toll means.
plays.rules: No ordinary Toll is paid at the rite; the six were paid when the bells rang. The Great Toll is never imposed.
plays.later: S28: every domain restored; the Stormwall thins to ordinary weather over a few years and Corvane joins the world (s28-new-world). Dreams return (s27-dreams-return). If someone sings the Cantor's verse, the Choir is released.
plays.keywords: concord, great toll, ringer, seat the key, chord, restore the world, best ending

plays.title: They strike the Seventh
plays.why: Corin's way, or desperation, or a wish to end the long unravelling for good.
plays.readAloud: The Hush cracks. Oum opens an eye, and the dream begins to unravel.
plays.response: The striker pays all six Tolls, disclosed first and refusable: refusing before the strike cancels it. Then the players talk with Oum, who asks direct questions and never lies: "Who is ringing my lullaby? Is the dream finished? Is it time to wake?" Pause for a table discussion (s27-oum-answers).
plays.consequence: Oum wakes. The world is remade from its best memories, or unmade into light.
plays.tells: A player asks what happens if they ring it, and means it.
plays.rules: Record all six Tolls for the striker (Memory, Year, Sense, Name, Fear, Gift).
plays.later: Remake or Unmake follows (s27-oum-remake, s27-oum-unmake). Dreams return.
plays.keywords: strike, ring the seventh, unbound, oum, wake, remake, unmake, ring ysh

plays.title: They seal the Key
plays.why: It costs no Toll and keeps every bell they rang.
plays.readAloud: You seal the Key into the Hush, unstruck, and the lullaby steadies. Above ground, the bells you rang are still ringing in the world. They are not enough to save everything, but they are enough to begin.
plays.response: One uninterrupted minute at the shrine's sealing recess: ten rounds, an action each round by one character. It stabilises only the domains whose bells were rung: name each one from the ring ledger. Unrung domains keep their afflictions. With no bell rung it is a stalemate: say so before they choose it. If the Sleepless gather (Mirel unrung), run enc-s27-seal-minute. Releasing the Cantor still needs the verse.
plays.consequence: Partial restoration. Oum sleeps on.
plays.tells: Players ask what sealing does and whether it keeps the bells they rang.
plays.rules: Protect the minute: if a fight is still on, it's an action each round for 10 rounds by one character.
plays.later: S28 epilogues name only what was earned. Dreams return (s27-dreams-return).
plays.keywords: seal, second dawn, recess, lock the key, stabilise, no toll

plays.title: The Court seals the shrine
plays.why: If the party is beaten or surrenders and Maudrin keeps the Key.
plays.readAloud: The Hush falls quiet again, not because you saved it, but because the Hushmen have sealed the stairs. The places you changed still bear your mark. Elsewhere, the collectors return to their rounds.
plays.response: This ending happens only if the group chooses to end its resistance. Otherwise play captivity, escape or the rescue chapter. Existing ringings still matter: the thaw, the storms and the quiet Sleepless persist; temporary blessings expire. The Court controls further ringing. Dreams stay lost.
plays.consequence: The Court rules on. The Tithe continues.
plays.fallback: Offer a rescue: the Stilled, the Choir, or a Stormborn crew comes for them.
plays.tells: The party is captured or retreating, and the Key is in Court hands.
plays.later: S28: the Court rules (s28-court-rules). Survivors may resist in a later campaign.

plays.response: Honour it completely: no Toll is taken and the Concord does not happen. The party may seal the Key, ask another willing character, postpone, or choose another course. A refused Toll cancels the ringing: nothing is rung, nothing is lost.
plays.consequence: The Concord waits for someone willing, or doesn't happen.
plays.tells: A long pause after you explain the Great Toll in private.

plays.title: They return to Pellmoor

Ila (if not Tithed; the ila flag tells you) keeps the ledger and may become the ferry-folk's Ringer; Mother Sallow reads Davin's name aloud at last if Ossa rang; Brother Eld confesses, leaves, or is gone (check the eld flag). Ansel retires to the coast; Tobias Quill is Tithed by his own office, or is a friend. Then the Landing: Brannagh, Sela, Venn. Close on: "Who keeps the ledger now?"

plays.response: Over a few years the Stormwall thins to ordinary sea. The Landing Charter can't hold; ships go wherever they like. Ask each player what their character makes of a Corvane joined to the world: a Stormborn going home, a Bellfolk seeing the sea for the first time, a Lander staying for good.
plays.consequence: Corvane joins the Forgotten Realms in earnest.
plays.tells: Players ask what happens to the ships and the trade now.
