page.title: CORVANE IN THE REALMS (v6 canon)
page.aliases: Forgotten Realms, Faerun, Faerûn, Sword Coast, Trackless Sea, Stormborn, Loudfolk, revision 6
page.body:
*Revision 6 canon. Where this page and v5 disagree, this page wins. The Canon Sheet (3.3) still governs every date and family line it lists.*

**Where Corvane is.** Corvane is a continent called **Hesk**, far out in the Trackless Sea beyond the last Sword Coast charts, part of the Forgotten Realms. A permanent band of storm circles it at sea, thirty to sixty miles deep: Faerûnian sailors call it **the Stormwall**, Corvanese who know of it call it **Thrane's Hem**. For four centuries no ship crossed it. Sword Coast sailors kept a legend of "the Ringing Land" west of the world; Candlekeep holds one water-stained portolan labelled *the Belled Coast*.

**DM truth: what the Stormwall is.** When Thrane fell silent on the Quiet Night, its storms did not end. They lost their shepherd and were pushed outward to the edge of the bells' resonance, where Ysh's lullaby stops. That is why no storm has crossed Brassfall in four hundred years: every storm Corvane should have had is in the Wall. Nobody knows this. Corin Aldeth suspects it; Edda Thorne's Notes imply it in one line ("Thrane's weather will go to the rim and wait").

**Before the Silence.** A few Faerûnian ships reached Corvane before the Quiet Night. Some of the Stilled in Glassreach are those sailors, frozen in 2 SS in Sword Coast clothes four centuries out of fashion.

**The Wrongweather (382 SS / 1462 DR).** The Ironhorn raid broke Old Garrow's sealed shafts. The dead lightning that poured out called to the storms at the rim, and for one night a storm tore up the river Pell onto the Mute Mere, the first weather the Mere had seen in 380 years. Davin Sallow drowned in it. When it passed it left a calm channel through the Wall: **the Seam**. At dawn the battered Baldur's Gate cog *Gull's Wager* drifted onto the Mere.

**Thirty years of contact.** Ilse Vesk's **Landing Charter** (384 SS) made Pellmoor the only lawful landing. Foreigners trade freely there but need a Court **writ of passage** to travel inland. Traffic has grown from one ship a year to forty or sixty a season. In come gold and silver, steel, paper, books, spices, wine, lenses and Lantanese clockwork (the Landing House removes every chime). Out go bottled memories (the richest export by far), glass-flowers, memory-pearls, reed-dye, bone-bound books and Ironhorn horses. Storm-stones and bronze are banned exports and smuggled anyway.

**Who is here.** The Vennmark Coster of Athkatla (Master Orsolo Venn), the Waterdhavian Corvane Venture, Baldurian factors, Lantanese gnome tinkers, Mirabar dwarves who want bronze, two quiet Harper agents, and Zhentarim memory smugglers. Lathander's Dawn Mission, a Kelemvorite shrine-tent and Chauntea's faithful; the Ninefold Church calls them "the loud gods."

**People and words.** Corvanese call Faerûnians **Stormborn** (polite) or **Loudfolk** (rude); Faerûnians call Corvanese **Bellfolk** or **the Quiet**; settled Faerûnians are **Landers**. Corvanese are mostly human, with halfling ferry-families, dwarven mining clans in Brassfall and very few elves. Dragonborn, tieflings, orcs, goliaths, gnomes and aasimar arrived with the ships, and Corvanese stare. Corvanese speak **Hesk**; Common is Pellmoor's second tongue.

**Magic.** Spells work by the 2024 rules. In Corvane every spell hums faintly as it is cast: that hum is Tonework, and it is how the Weave sounds here. Silence-stones suppress spells under the house rule in 2.6.

**Calendar.** 412 SS = 1492 DR.

page.title: THE STORMWALL AND THE SEAM
page.aliases: Stormwall, Thrane's Hem, the Seam, Pellmouth, river Pell, Wrongweather
page.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Ahead, the sea stands up. A wall of black cloud and white water runs from one horizon to the other, lit from inside by lightning that never stops. And in it, like a door left open, a lane of grey calm a mile wide."
- **What it is:** a permanent band of storm thirty to sixty miles deep that circles Corvane at sea. DM truth: Thrane's lost storms, waiting at the rim of the bells' resonance.
- **The Seam:** the one calm channel through it, opened by the Wrongweather of 382 SS, in line with the mouth of the river Pell. A mile or two wide; it drifts with the seasons. Crossing takes about a day with a pilot who knows its moods.
- **The river Pell:** about forty miles from the Pellmouth inland to the Mute Mere. Two days by river.
- **Dangers:** drifting off the Seam. Ships that do are rarely seen again; pilots who come back describe a warm grey light at the storm's heart (see 11.7, the Edge of the Dream).
- **If Thrane rings:** the storms come home to Brassfall. For a season the Seam widens into a broad road and new fleets arrive within a month. If an ending stabilises Thrane (the Concord, or the Second Dawn with Thrane rung), the Stormwall thins to ordinary sea weather over a few years and Corvane joins the world.
- **Voyage:** about six weeks from Baldur's Gate or Waterdeep. Sailing season is spring (Ches) to early autumn (Eleint).

page.title: MEMORY AS MONEY
page.aliases: memory currency, keep, keeps, mote, motes, heartkeep, knowing, reckoner, gilding, exchange rate, coin, gold
page.body:
Corvane traded memories long before the ships came. The Court's Tithe made it a habit and the Reckoners made it a currency. Gold arrived thirty years ago and is winning, slowly.

**How it works**
1. **Drawing.** A memory can be drawn out of a person only with their consent, by a Court-licensed **Reckoner** with a tuning fork and a small stoppered vial of Mere-glass. It takes about a minute and feels like forgetting a word on the tip of your tongue, then not minding. Drawing without a licence is *leeching*, a crime.
2. **Keeps.** A drawn, sealed memory is a **keep**: a vial of faintly luminous mist that hums one low note when held. Reckoners grade it by **weight** (how much feeling it holds) and stamp the wax. The content stays private unless someone opens it.
3. **Keeps circulate sealed,** passed hand to hand like banknotes. Their value rests on two facts: someone will always pay to witness one, and its owner can always redeem it.
4. **Opening.** If the original owner opens a keep, the memory returns whole. Anyone else *witnesses* it, as a guest in someone else's day, without acquiring the owner's identity. Each stranger's witnessing fades it; after three it is a grey, spent vial.
5. **What cannot be drawn:** skills, spells, languages, proficiencies, anything a character can do. "You can sell the day you learned to swim, but never the swimming." Nobody can sell someone else's memory.
6. **Blanks** are people who sold or Tithed so many heavy memories that they no longer recognise their own families.

| Weight | What it holds | Worth at Pellmoor | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mote** | A passing memory: last Ossday's supper, a stranger's coat | about 1 sp | Grey wax. Small change. |
| **Keep** | A memory with feeling: a good afternoon, a small win | about 1 gp (floats daily) | Plain wax. The everyday coin. |
| **Heartkeep** | A defining memory: a parent's face, a wedding day | 25 to 100 gp or more | Red wax. The Tithe prefers them. |
| **Knowing** | Knowledge: a route, a recipe, a password, a face | by usefulness | Blue wax. The seller loses the knowledge. |

**Gold, and why the Court hates it.** Old Corvanese coin was iron "ticks" and Court scrip; bronze is bell-metal. Gold cannot be Tithed, cannot fade, cannot be Reckoned. At Pellmoor nearly every stall takes either. **Court taxes on Corvanese subjects must be paid in memory; foreigners pay the landing due in gold.** Paying a local's Tithe in gold is **gilding**: illegal and common. A keep fetches about 1 gp 2 sp at Pellmoor and about 8 sp in Hallowmere. The Hallowmere gate's courtesy memory is a registration, not a fee, and the clerk refuses gold.

**Table rules (2024)**
- A character may pay in memory wherever coin is accepted in Corvane. The player chooses the memory and writes one line in the Memory ledger (Foresight → Party & ledger). The DM never chooses it.
- A Reckoner buys memories at the posted rate less a 10 percent fee.
- Motes and keeps have no mechanical effect. When a character sells a heartkeep, the player rewrites one thing the memory held up (a belief, a bond, a fear). It never removes player knowledge or control of the character.
- The DM may award **Heroic Inspiration** when a character gives a memory freely to someone who needs it.
- Once, a character who witnesses a Knowing keep has Advantage on one ability check that knowledge plainly helps.
- Keep the kinds apart: a **Toll** can never be bought back; a **Tithe** can be redeemed from its jar; a **trade** is a keep; **Mere Memories** are borrowed; **eel bites** return after a long rest; **stairs** losses follow the stairs' rule.

page.title: THE LANDING (Foreign traders at Pellmoor)
page.aliases: Vennmark Coster, Corvane Venture, Harpers, Zhentarim, Landers, foreign traders, merchants
page.body:
- **Wants:** Profit, above all from bottled memories. An end to the Landing Charter's limits (or, for the Coster, an exclusive export licence). Safe passage through the Seam.
- **Fears:** The Court closing the Seam to them. A rival house winning the Court's favour. The Wall moving.
- **Methods:** Gold, credit, gifts to officials, hiring ferry-folk pilots, and buying memories in bulk.
- **Ideal:** *Prosperity.*
- **Members:** the Vennmark Coster of Athkatla (Master Orsolo Venn; the largest memory exporter), the Waterdhavian Corvane Venture (cautious, respectable), Baldurian factors, Lantanese tinkers, Mirabar dwarves after bronze. In the shadows: two Harper agents who distrust the Tithe, and a Zhentarim smuggling ring on Strangers' Row.
- **Secret:** The Coster buys "surplus" Tithed memories from the Court and ships them to Faerûn. The Tithe-Ledger has an EXPORT — VENNMARK column. Some Blanks' memories are in Athkatla.
- **How They React:** Warmly to customers, coldly to anyone who costs them money. They will not fight the Court, and they will not fight for it.
- **Clock move (at 6):** the Coster wins an export licence, a new fleet arrives, or a Zhentarim memory-smuggling ring is exposed.

page.title: 26. PILOT-MISTRESS BRANNAGH WICK
page.body:
- **Role:** Runs the Pilots' Hall on the Quays. Every ship that crosses the drowned town does it with one of her pilots. Tam Harrow was one of them.
- **Look:** Ferry-folk, about 60. Short, wind-cracked hands, a coil of sounding-line always over one shoulder.
- **Voice:** Gruff. Counts tides out loud. Calls every ship "she" and every captain "lad."
- **Wants:** The Hall kept independent of the Court and the trading houses. Ila safe.
- **Secret:** Tam took his boat out the night he died with no cargo and no ship to pilot, which no pilot does. She told the Landing House nothing. She thinks he was going to the Ossa Belfry, and she is right.
- **2024 stat block:** Scout (CR 1/2).
- **How She Reacts:** Trusts people who keep their word on the water. Will refuse a pilot to any ship she has a reason to stop, and every ship needs one to leave the Mere.

page.title: 27. RECKONER SELA MAUNT
page.body:
- **Role:** Court-licensed memory assayer at the Reckoning House on the Tally. The person who explains memory money to newcomers.
- **Look:** Corvanese, 40s. Grey apron, three tuning forks in a breast pocket, reading lenses bought from a Lantanese tinker.
- **Voice:** Precise, kind, slightly tired. Taps a fork against the counter when she thinks.
- **Wants:** Honest weights and a quiet life.
- **Secret:** She keeps a "Lost Shelf" of heartkeeps sold in grief and quietly lets the sellers buy them back at cost, which the Court forbids.
- **2024 stat block:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How She Reacts:** Helps anyone who is kind to her: she can read a keep's weight, tell a forged keep from a true one, and explain gilding without saying the word. She will not appraise a bell's Heart: "That's not a memory, love. That's a bell."

page.title: 28. MASTER ORSOLO VENN
page.aliases: Venn, Orsolo, Vennmark Coster, Gilded Heron, merchant, Amnian
page.body:
- **Role:** Factor of the Vennmark Coster of Athkatla, the largest memory exporter in Pellmoor. A human-sized antagonist of the memory trade.
- **Look:** Amnian, 50s. Plum velvet in a grey country, rings on every finger, a silent Lantanese pocket-clock he consults constantly.
- **Voice:** Warm, fluent Hesk with an Amnian lilt. Calls everyone "friend" and means "customer."
- **Wants:** An exclusive export licence from the Court. Curiosities from the Ringing Land for his buyers in Athkatla.
- **Secret:** He pays Tobias Quill to look away from certain cargoes. A buyer in Athkatla offers 5,000 gp for "a true bell-relic of the Ringing Land." The Coster buys Tithed memories from the Court for export, and its ledgers prove it.
- **The Gilded Heron:** the Coster's carrack, anchored beyond the last pier. Two Coster guards (Tough) on watch; a Baldurian crew who won't fight for the Coster.
- **2024 stat block:** Noble (CR 1/8), with two Toughs (CR 1/2) as guards.
- **How He Reacts:** Generous, then persistent. Prefers money to trouble and folds when a deal turns violent or public. Holds grudges in ledgers, not in alleys.

page.title: 29. SISTER AURELIE DAWNMANTLE
page.aliases: Aurelie, Dawnmantle, Lathander, Morninglord, Dawn Mission
page.body:
- **Role:** Morninglord priestess of Lathander who runs the Dawn Mission on Strangers' Row. Optional ally for clerics, paladins and anyone hurt.
- **Look:** Waterdhavian, 30s. Rose-and-gold vestments faded by the Corvanese light.
- **Voice:** Bright and earnest. Says "when the sun comes back" as if it were a date in a diary.
- **Wants:** A writ of passage to Hallowmere, to bring Lathander's dawn to a city that has none.
- **Secret:** The Court has refused her writ four times. She is close to trying without one, which would get her arrested.
- **2024 stat block:** Priest (CR 2).
- **How She Reacts:** If the party tells her about Vaer's bell, she becomes a devoted ally, and a liability, in Act II. Heals for a donation, or for a true story about a sunrise.

page.title: 30. BROTHER HADRIK VOSS
page.body:
- **Role:** Kelemvorite priest with a shrine-tent on Strangers' Row. Believes the restless dead of the Mere are an abomination to be laid to rest.
- **Look:** Grey robes, a skeletal-hand pendant, a censer he never lets go out.
- **Voice:** Low and certain. Quotes the Doomguide.
- **Wants:** To lay the Drowned Choir to rest, by force if need be.
- **Secret:** His own brother drowned at sea and was never found. The Mere's unrestful dead feel like an accusation.
- **2024 stat block:** Priest (CR 2).
- **How He Reacts:** Can be argued down from his own dogma: Kelemvor's dead are owed judgment and remembrance, not erasure (DC 15 Persuasion; a DC 12 Religion Study first grants Advantage). If he blesses the Mere during the Night Song, the Choir rises angry.

page.title: PELLMOOR LANDING: THE QUAYS, THE TALLY AND STRANGERS' ROW
page.aliases: Landing House, Reckoning House, Pilots' Hall, Strangers' Row, Loud Quarter, Brass Lantern, Quays, Tally
page.body:
**The Landing House (Quays).** Court customs. A grey stone hall with a silence-stone lintel. Writs of passage, the 5 gp landing due, cargo seals, and the chime-removal bench where every imported clock is silenced. Six Hushmen and Tobias Quill's office.
> **SAY:** "The clerk stamps your papers without reading them. 'Landing due, five gold. Pellmoor and the Mere road only. Anywhere else needs a writ from Hallowmere. They take about a season. Next.'"

**The Pilots' Hall (Quays).** A long reed-roofed shed built over the water, its floor a map of Old Pellmoor's drowned streets in painted planks. Brannagh Wick's pilots wait on benches for ships.

**The Reckoning House (the Tally).** A narrow shop with a slate by the door and a counter scored by tuning forks. Sela Maunt weighs keeps under a Lantanese lens. Behind a curtain: the Lost Shelf.
> **SAY:** "The slate by the door reads, in careful chalk: 1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. MOTES AT 1 SP. HEARTKEEPS BY APPRAISAL. Underneath, smaller: NO GOLD FOR TITHES."

**Strangers' Row, the Loud Quarter.** Foreign inns, counting-houses, the Dawn Mission, a dwarven smithy, a gnomish clockmaker selling silent clocks, Brother Hadrik's shrine-tent, and music at all hours.

**The Brass Lantern.** The Faerûnian inn. Loud, warm, overpriced, and the only place in Corvane that serves Waterdhavian ale. The *Gull's Wager*'s old first mate drinks in the corner.

page.title: 2024 RULES NOTES (v6)
page.aliases: 2024, 5.5e, rules, Heroic Inspiration, Influence, Extreme Cold, Suffocation, Exhaustion, encounter budget
page.body:
- **Heroic Inspiration** replaces v5's "Inspiration."
- **Influence** (action): social plays use it. The DC is 15 or the creature's Intelligence score, whichever is higher; its attitude (Friendly, Indifferent, Hostile) decides whether a check is needed at all.
- **Study** (Intelligence) and **Search** (Wisdom) actions: clue scenes use them. Essential clues are never lost to a failed roll.
- **Extreme Cold** (Glassreach): end of each hour, DC 10 Constitution save or 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance or Immunity succeeds automatically; so does a warm cloak or cold-weather gear (house rule kept from v5).
- **Exhaustion:** each level gives −2 to d20 Tests and −5 feet of Speed; a long rest removes 1 level; level 6 is death.
- **Suffocation:** hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds); out of breath, 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn, all removed when breathing again.
- **Frigid Water:** minutes equal to the Constitution score, then a DC 10 Constitution save each minute or 1 Exhaustion level.
- **Conditions** use the 2024 definitions. A Toll of Sense uses Blinded or Deafened.
- **Encounters:** Waypoint's Foresight computes difficulty from your roster with the 2024 XP budget per character (Low, Moderate, High). Corvane creatures have full 2024 stat blocks built on 2024 Monster Manual creatures; open them from any encounter.
- **Spells that touch memory** (Modify Memory, Greater Restoration, Remove Curse, Speak with Dead, Zone of Truth and others) have rulings in Foresight's anytime plays. Search "If they…" for the spell's name.

page.title: WHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 6
page.body:
**World.** Corvane is part of the Forgotten Realms, hidden behind the Stormwall until the Wrongweather opened the Seam in 382 SS (1462 DR). Pellmoor is now Pellmoor Landing, a port of about 4,000. Memory is a working currency alongside gold (MEMORY AS MONEY). New NPCs 26–30. New faction: THE LANDING.

**Act I.** New Session 1 opening (arrival at the port). Quill works from the Landing House and is short because Pellmoor pays in gold; H-03 can be solved by giving memories on the villagers' behalf. New Session 3 option: sell the Heart to Master Venn (the *Gilded Heron* sails in three days). Optional complication: Brother Hadrik Voss blesses the Mere. Brannagh Wick is a fourth source on Tam's death; any two still establish the Court's responsibility.

**Act II.** Stormborn need a writ at the Hallowmere gate; the Chancellor's invitation counts. Optional reveal: the Tithe-Ledger's EXPORT — VENNMARK column.

**Act III.** Some Stilled are Faerûnian sailors from before the Silence. Glassreach uses 2024 Extreme Cold.

**Act IV.** Ringing Thrane loosens the Stormwall for a season. New Session 22 ally if earned: the Stormborn.

**Endings.** A stabilised Thrane thins the Stormwall for good; in the Empty Choir the Court keeps the Seam.

**Part 9.** Situation 17 now has ships home; Situation 18 has a sailor's dragon story; the Edge of the Dream lies inside the Stormwall.

**Rules.** 2024 throughout (2024 RULES NOTES). Full stat blocks and calculated encounter difficulty live in Foresight.

edits.find:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Pellmoor sits on the gray shore of the Mute Mere like a dropped lantern. Reed-thatched houses lean toward the water. The ferry-dock creaks. Nets hang from poles like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell, which should ring, is silent. Across the water, the Mere is so still it reflects the sky perfectly, except where something beneath it moves."
- **Population:** About 300, mostly Ferry-folk.
- **Key locations:** the ferry-dock, the chapel (Brother Eld), Mother Sallow's reed-hut, the Harrow house, the net-racks, the ledger-house where the old names are kept, and the Inn of the Shuttered Bell.
- **Dangers:** The Drowned Choir sings at night. Hushmen visit once a week.
- **Secrets:** The chapel's cellar holds a rope that once rang Old Pellmoor's bell, and its end is still tied to something under the water.
- **Atmosphere:** Quiet, careful, mournful. Children do not play near water.
edits.replace:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "The Mute Mere is so still that the ships look painted on it. Forty masts stand over the water where a drowned town lies just beneath, rooftops like the backs of sleeping animals. On the Quays, a dozen languages argue over the price of a memory. Gnomes shout. Gulls do not; there are no gulls on the Mere. And at the far end of the waterfront, past the last warehouse, the old reed-roofed village of Pellmoor still leans toward the water as if none of this were happening."
- **What it is:** Corvane's only lawful port for foreign ships since the Landing Charter of 384 SS. Not a Court city: the Tithe Clock does not tick here. The Court is present through the Landing House and its six Hushmen.
- **Population:** About 4,000 year-round; nearly twice that in sailing season (spring to early autumn). Ferry-folk, Corvanese who came for work, and Faerûnian Landers.
- **The Old Shore:** the original ferry village. The old ferry-dock where Ila waits, the net-racks, the chapel (Brother Eld), Mother Sallow's reed-hut, the Harrow house, the ledger-house, the Inn of the Shuttered Bell, and the Mere Memory Shore. Foreigners are tolerated, not welcomed. Children still do not play near the water.
- **The Quays:** deep-water piers driven into Old Pellmoor's drowned roofs; warehouses, chandlers, a dry-dock; the **Pilots' Hall** (Brannagh Wick) and the **Landing House** (Tobias Quill; landing due 5 gp; writs of passage).
- **The Tally:** the market square. The **Reckoning House** (Reckoner Sela Maunt) posts the day's rate on a slate: *1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. MOTES AT 1 SP. HEARTKEEPS BY APPRAISAL.*
- **Strangers' Row (the Loud Quarter):** the Faerûnian quarter. The Brass Lantern inn, the Vennmark Coster's counting-house (Master Orsolo Venn), the Corvane Venture hall, the Dawn Mission (Sister Aurelie), a dwarven smithy, a gnomish clockmaker selling silent clocks, a Kelemvorite shrine-tent (Brother Hadrik).
- **Dangers:** The Drowned Choir sings at night. Hushmen walk the Old Shore weekly and watch the Quays daily. Memory leeches and Zhentarim smugglers work Strangers' Row.
- **Secrets:** The chapel's cellar holds a rope that once rang Old Pellmoor's bell, and its end is still tied to something under the water. Every ship that leaves the Mere needs a Pilots' Hall pilot, so the ferry-folk can stop any departure.
- **Atmosphere:** Two towns in one. Loud, bright and foreign on the Quays; quiet, careful and mournful on the Old Shore.

Lathander's Dawn Mission, Kelemvor's shrine-tent and Chauntea's wandering faithful are tolerated at the Landing and forbidden in Hallowmere. **382 SS (1462 DR): The Wrongweather.** The dead lightning loosed from Garrow's broken shafts calls to the storms trapped at the rim. For one night a storm tears up the river Pell onto the Mute Mere, the first weather the Mere has seen in 380 years. Davin Sallow drowns in it. When it passes, it leaves a calm channel through the Stormwall: the Seam. At dawn the Baldur's Gate cog *Gull's Wager* drifts onto the Mere, the first Faerûnian ship in Corvane in four centuries.

**384 SS: The Landing Charter.** Ilse Vesk declares Pellmoor the only lawful landing for foreign ships and requires a Court writ of passage for foreigners travelling inland. Pellmoor begins to grow from a ferry village into a port.

**New in v6.** **Gilding:** paying a Corvanese subject's Tithe in gold; illegal. **Heartkeep:** a sealed defining memory, red wax. **Keep:** a sealed memory used as money. **Knowing:** a sealed memory that carries knowledge; the seller loses it. **Landing Charter:** the Court law that confines foreign ships to Pellmoor. **Lander:** a Faerûnian settled in Pellmoor. **Loudfolk, Stormborn:** Corvanese names for Faerûnians. **Mote:** a sealed trivial memory; small change. **Reckoner:** a Court-licensed memory assayer. **The Seam:** the one passage through the Stormwall. **The Stormwall:** the band of storm that circles Corvane at sea. **The Wrongweather:** the storm of 382 SS that opened the Seam. **Writ of passage:** the Court paper a foreigner needs to travel inland.

anytime.title: They use Hold Person, Suggestion, Charm Person or Sleep on an NPC
anytime.why: Four characters with subclasses and 2nd-level spells can solve a scene in one action.
anytime.response: They work as written, with a Corvane cost. Every spell hums within 30 feet, so any Hushman nearby hears the cast, and a held or charmed NPC knows afterward that something was done to them and who stood near. Hold Person and Sleep need a Humanoid and a failed save; a Hushman's silence-stone glove does not protect the wearer. Suggestion cannot make an NPC reveal a secret that would harm them seriously (the DM may judge the request unreasonable), and it cannot undo a Tithe or a memory. Charm Person makes the target Friendly, not obedient. The NPC's next report names the caster: raise clock_court by 1 if a Court officer is the target.
anytime.consequence: The scene is solved fast and the Court has a name.
anytime.fallback: If the save succeeds, the NPC shouts, and the encounter begins.
anytime.tells: A caster asks whether Quill, Cole, Venn, Eld or a Hushman can be held, charmed or put to sleep.
anytime.rules: Hold Person: Wisdom save each turn, ends on success. Suggestion: Wisdom save, up to 8 hours, reasonable request only. Charm Person: Wisdom save, advantage if fighting, target knows afterward. Sleep: HP pool. Blanks and the Drowned are not valid targets for Charm.
anytime.later: The target's next report puts the caster on the Court's list (court_eye). Repeated use makes the Gate Clerk and the Landing House expect it.
anytime.keywords: hold person, suggestion, charm person, sleep, command, enchant, control npc, quill, venn

anytime.title: They cast Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth or Calm Emotions on someone
anytime.why: The campaign is built on secrets; a level-3 to 6 party has the spells to ask.
anytime.response: The firm rulings: the spell hums, so the target usually hears it. At the oath-duel (S6) the knights stand in herald fields (10-foot silence-stone), so both spells fail there and casting at them costs the caster's side a question. At Maudrin's dais (S4) the plinth stones kill Zone of Truth; Detect Thoughts on her surface mind gives 'Four of them. Ossa's. Not yet.' and a probe saves at +4. Haldric's shield negates the first spell targeting only him each day. Elsewhere Zone of Truth works as written (Charisma save; creatures may refuse to answer, which is itself telling). Detect Thoughts on a Tithed person finds blank patches; on a Blank it finds only a looping 'who was I?'. Calm Emotions suppresses Charmed or Frightened (including the Sermon in a fight) but does not undo a Toll, a Tithe or a Blank.
anytime.consequence: Truth magic is a tool with edges, not a skeleton key.
anytime.fallback: If the table argues, rule it by the stones: a field stops the spell, no field means it works.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Zone of Truth before a hearing, or names Detect Thoughts at a table with Maudrin, Venn or Isolde.
anytime.rules: Zone of Truth (2nd): Charisma save, 10-minute zone. Detect Thoughts (2nd): Wisdom save to probe, concentration. Calm Emotions (2nd): Charisma save, suppresses Charmed or Frightened. Silence-stone fields stop all three.
anytime.later: S4: read-maudrin. S6: spells-on-the-steps. S13: the Sexton says he has told no lie since 32 SS.
anytime.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, calm emotions, read mind, interrogate, lie, truth magic

anytime.title: They use Locate Object, Find Familiar, Clairvoyance or Detect Magic to find a Heart
anytime.why: Five Hearts are scattered across Corvane, and a caster wants to know where.
anytime.response: Locate Object (2nd level) on a Heart the caster has seen works: the hum gives a direction within 1,000 feet. It fails if the Heart is in a silence-stone box, the Tithe-Ledger Room or the Hallowmere vault; a lined box simply shows nothing. Locate Object on 'the page', 'the diary' or 'the Key' works only if the caster has seen it. Find Familiar (ritual) can watch the Heron, Quill's office or a Hushman's door; Detect Magic shows the faint aura of a Heart, and a Bell-Touched character senses it without magic. Clairvoyance (3rd, level 5+) fails inside silence-stone and in any Court city under a raised Silence. Scrying on the Sexton fails: Hieme's silence blocks it.
anytime.consequence: They can find a Heart or watch a place, but the Court's stones block the hard places.
anytime.fallback: If the spell fails, the hum fades and Bell-Touched characters still feel a direction.
anytime.tells: A player asks whether a Heart can be tracked, or sends an owl to watch a ship.
anytime.rules: Locate Object: 1,000-foot range, concentration, blocked by lead; here also by silence-stone. Detect Magic: ritual. Find Familiar: ritual, 1 hour.
anytime.later: Hallowmere: the vault (S5) and the armory (S9) are lined and show nothing. The Heron (S3) is findable until she clears the Seam.
anytime.keywords: locate object, find familiar, clairvoyance, scry, track heart, detect magic, divination

anytime.title: They use Misty Step, Invisibility, Pass without Trace, Spider Climb or Knock
anytime.why: Heist scenes meet 2nd-level spells at level 3, and the silence-stone rule needs a clear answer.
anytime.response: They work as written outside a silence-stone field. Inside a field (the Tithe-Ledger vault, a dais, a herald's rod) no spell can be cast or produce an effect: Knock fails, Invisibility and Pass without Trace are suppressed, Disguise Self drops, and Misty Step cast from outside lands at the edge of the field, not inside. Pass without Trace gives +10 to Stealth for the group; the spell still hums when it is cast, so anyone within 30 feet hears the cast. Invisibility ends when the target attacks or casts. Spider Climb skips the chain-room climb (S9) but not the chains. On a ship (the Heron) a shimmer on the water gives the mate Passive Perception 14 a chance.
anytime.consequence: Mobility spells open the plan but not the stone.
anytime.fallback: If the player's plan needs a spell the field blocks, the Hushman passing every ten minutes gives them a mundane way through.
anytime.tells: A caster asks whether a blink, a shimmer or a lockpick spell works at the vault, the armory or the Heron.
anytime.rules: Silence-stone field: Part 2.6 house rule. Pass without Trace: +10 Stealth, concentration. Misty Step: 30 feet, bonus action, blocked into a field.
anytime.later: S5: the vault. S9: the armory and the chain-room. S3: boarding the Heron.
anytime.keywords: misty step, invisibility, pass without trace, spider climb, knock, silence-stone, heist

anytime.title: They use a level-3 class feature in a Corvane scene
anytime.why: Subclasses mean Cunning Action, Wild Shape, Turn Undead, Smite, Portent, Cutting Words and Subtle Spell all arrive at once.
anytime.response: Cunning Action and Fast Hands work in S1's theft and raid; a ferry-folk witness makes it risky. A druid's swimming Wild Shape removes the breath clock in the Mere (S2) but the Cantor reads an animal shape as a lie unless it is named. Turn Undead and Divine Smite work on the Drowned Singers; the Cantor is immune to Frightened and Charmed and is offended. Wizard Portent and Bard Cutting Words work on Stealth and Influence rolls. Sorcerer Subtle Spell hides the verbal and somatic components, so the Tonework hum is still heard within 30 feet, and Hushmen can still hear a cast. Warlock Devil's Sight sees through the Mere's dark but not through silence-stone. A Monk's Stunning Strike works on Hushmen but not on Stilled (Gargoyle) or Singers.
anytime.consequence: Class features speed the plan but do not skip the telegraph.
anytime.fallback: If a feature seems to break a scene, tell the player what the scene's real obstacle is and let them solve that.
anytime.tells: A rogue asks about Fast Hands, a druid asks about a swimming Wild Shape, a cleric about Turn Undead.
anytime.rules: Turn Undead: Wisdom save vs your spell save DC, Frightened for 1 minute. Wild Shape: swimming beasts ignore Suffocation but not eel bites. Portent: replace a roll before it is made.
anytime.later: Features that touch bells or Tolls follow the bell: nothing a class does rings a bell without its Heart and Toll.
anytime.keywords: cunning action, wild shape, turn undead, divine smite, portent, cutting words, subtle spell, class feature

anytime.title: Level 5 to 6: Dispel Magic, Counterspell, Hearts, Sending, Speak with Dead, Water Breathing
anytime.why: Third-level slots arrive at level 5 (S10). Before then these are NPC-only; after, they touch bells, silence and memory.
anytime.response: Dispel Magic ends a spell effect on a creature or object, but not a Toll, a Tithe, a Blank's state, a winter-moment (Hieme's silence), a bell's ringing, or Oum. It cannot target a silence-stone because a stone is not a spell. Counterspell stops an NPC's spell (Maudrin, Aurelie, Brother Eld's Silence) but not a bell, the Sexton's Sermon or a Hushman's glove. Hearts lets the caster understand and speak any language: it makes the old Stilled dialect and Hesk accessible but cannot read bell-script. Sending reaches anyone inside Corvane who is not in a silence-stone field; across the Stormwall it fails (the weather is in the way) unless the Seam is wide. Speak with Dead works on any corpse with a mouth for 10 days: five questions, and the corpse knows only what it knew in life (see any-speak-with-dead). Water Breathing lets a party reach the Ossa Belfry without the Tidewarden's pocket and works on the Mere's drowned streets; the Cantor treats it as a courtesy.
anytime.consequence: The party has tools for NPC casters and for the Mere, but the world's big magic stays out of their hands.
anytime.fallback: If a player is disappointed, offer the narrower thing the spell does well.
anytime.tells: A level-5 caster asks what Dispel Magic or Counterspell can do against the Court's tools.
anytime.rules: Dispel Magic (3rd): ability check DC 10 + spell level for a higher-level spell. Counterspell: reaction, 60 feet. Hearts: 1 hour. Sending: 25 words. Speak with Dead: 10 days, five questions. Water Breathing: ritual, 24 hours.
anytime.later: S10 onward: Hearts unlocks the Stilled; S11: Speak with Dead on a shattered Stilled; S13: the Sexton's Sermon cannot be countered.
anytime.keywords: dispel magic, counterspell, hearts, sending, speak with dead, water breathing, third level, fireball

anytime.title: They kill a named NPC
anytime.why: A table that has been hunted by Hushmen for ten sessions will eventually go for someone with a name.
anytime.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill them?' A creature at 0 HP can be knocked out instead (2024), and a Hold Person'd target is a murder, not a fight. If they do it, the NPC is dead; no resurrection. Record the flag if one exists (quill, eld, haldric, ilam, rook, ansel, corin, kessa, sexton, maudrin) and note the rest in the Bargain Log (Brannagh, Sela, Venn, Sallow, Lysse, Bet, Aurelie, Hadrik, Wren, Isolde, Edrin). Then show the ripple: a Court officer's death raises the Court clock and names the killers; a ferry-folk or Bellwright ally's death costs trust and a door. Never a child. If a death would end a thread the story needs (Rook dead, no Vaer loan), let another door open: Haldric, Aurelie, a theft, or the Bellwrights.
anytime.consequence: The NPC is gone and the table sees the cost.
anytime.fallback: If the table regrets it at once, it still stands: a gentle reminder that the story goes on.
anytime.tells: A player says 'finish him', ambushes a named NPC alone, or waits at their door.
anytime.rules: No check. Record the death. Court officers: clock_court +1 to +2; the Dawn Order: clock_dawn +2; ferry-folk: clock_ferry +1.
anytime.later: The NPC's later promises lapse. Their allies hold a grudge; their enemies are surprised. S28 and the endings read the death honestly.
anytime.keywords: kill npc, murder, assassinate, execute, kill quill, kill rook, kill venn, named character

anytime.title: They split the party
anytime.why: Four players, four plans: a rogue at the vault and a cleric at the Mission is how every table plays.
anytime.response: Cut between the groups in short scenes (about five minutes each) and let a timer run: Quill reaches the Old Shore on the second evening; the Tithe Clock ticks per night; Hushmen pass every ten minutes. Give each half a clear danger and a clear exit. Keep players who are not in the current scene engaged by asking them to play the NPCs. Regroup at a natural meeting point (a bakery, a chapel, a camp). Tolls, Tithes and bells need the consenting character present; an absent player's character is never charged (any-absent-player).
anytime.consequence: Parallel scenes shorten the session and raise tension.

Do not hand levels out in the Mere. 3rd-level spells arrive at level 5, which is why Fireball, Speak with Dead and Hearts appear in Glassreach. A Heart in a silence-stone-lined box does not hum, but the box itself is contraband; a lead-lined sailor's chest hides the hum from Locate Object. The ferry-folk keep it without being asked if Ila vouches. A ship's captain wants a fee, and Venn's friends notice.

anytime.why: The sale was the campaign's hardest consequence. This is the canon's safety valve, if the table wants it.
anytime.readAloud: On a still morning, a Pilots' Hall skiff comes in with a plum-coloured sail across its bows. Brannagh Wick stands in the bow, holding a wet oilskin bundle. 'The Mere remembers what is taken from it,' she says.

Tell the table honestly that this is a gift, not a reward, and that Venn is ruined and furious. Mother Sallow takes the bundle to the shore. Ila holds it first.

anytime.why: A table that refuses the safety valve, or has decided the Concord is closed.
anytime.readAloud: 'Then the Mere is quiet,' says the Tidewarden, 'and will stay quiet.' He turns his oar and does not look at you.
anytime.response: Ossa's Heart is lost beyond the Seam. The Concord requires all six bells and is closed unless a later voyage brings it back (Situation 17: leaving Corvane for six weeks). The Second Dawn stays open with fewer domains. Ila grieves. The Choir stays hunting; the ferry-folk blame the party quietly.

anytime.why: They recovered the Heart from the armory, the Court's vault, Venn or the sea, and the bell is waiting.
anytime.readAloud: The Tidewarden's ferry waits at the end of the old dock, oar dripping. The water is very still.
anytime.response: State the Toll and wait for a yes: a memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. Ila may not be the Ringer; offer it to an adult and let her stand beside them. The Tidewarden ferries the Ringer and holds an air pocket. If they ring it, the Choir rests, Mother Sallow remembers Davin, and the Cantor can be released with the verse.

anytime.why: Rook stands in the open at the oath-duel, the gate and the Strike; a table that fights the Dawn Order, or loses a protector, can lose her.
anytime.response: Play it only if it happened at the table: no NPC dies off-screen to suit the plot. The Dawn Order goes to Haldric if he is still a knight, and Vaer's Heart stays wherever it was. Her knights hold the party responsible if the party caused it, and mourn with them if not. If Rook had loaned Vaer's Heart, Haldric demands it back.

anytime.response: Let them plan; good plans get a real chance. Use the Strike (S23) or summit (S24) forces scaled to where she is. anytime.response: Allow the expedition. Ysh is at the bottom of a hundred steps and needs the Key to ring. anytime.response: Good plans should work. Ansel knows the vault schedule and can get them an audience or the service entrance. A successful plan may bypass the checks.

anytime.response: Bet Ostrow knows which carts leave the city unsearched. The Heart comes out among the grain sacks over four days, at a cost: the Tithe Clock ticks once for the night Bet's people spend in the city. In v6 a Harper on Strangers' Row can forge a writ that gets one person in.

anytime.tells: Players look at the Forecast and see Calla missing.
anytime.later: Calla is one of the six for the Concord.

anytime.title: They cast Modify Memory to restore or remove a memory
anytime.why: In a campaign about memory, the spell will come up once a bard or cleric reaches it.
anytime.readAloud: The spell finds the shape of the forgetting, a clean hollow where something was, and there is nothing in it to move.
anytime.response: Modify Memory works as written on ordinary memories (forgetting the party's faces, changing how a recent conversation went). It cannot restore a Tithed memory (that memory is in a jar in Hallowmere; only opening the jar returns it), a sold keep (it's in someone's vial), or a Toll (the bell took it). It can plant a false memory in a Blank, but not recognition of a real person. Make the limit clear before the slot is spent.
anytime.consequence: Ordinary memories bend; the Tithe, the trade and the Tolls do not.
anytime.tells: A caster asks whether magic can give Mother Sallow back her husband, or make a Hushman forget them.
anytime.rules: Modify Memory (2024): Wisdom save; the target has the Charmed condition while you work; the time window depends on spell level.
anytime.later: Planting false memories in Blanks is exactly what the Court would do. If the party does it, the Choir and the Bellwrights notice.
anytime.keywords: modify memory, restore memory, erase memory, spell, bard, cleric, wizard, forget

anytime.title: They use healing magic on a Blank, a Toll or an eel-bite
anytime.why: Players reach for Greater Restoration, Remove Curse or Heal on memory loss.
anytime.response: Rulings: Greater Restoration, Heal and Remove Curse don't restore Tithed or traded memories (those are elsewhere, in glass). A Toll can't be ended early by any magic: the bell holds it until it ends. Remove Curse or Greater Restoration does return an eel-stolen memory at once. Lesser Restoration ends Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed or Poisoned (and a disease); it does not end Frightened. Use Calm Emotions for a fear in the moment, Heroes' Feast against fear for a day. A dream lost to the Hush Cult returns only when the Hush is struck, sealed or tuned.
anytime.consequence: The table learns which losses magic can mend and which only a jar, a vial or the Remake can.
anytime.tells: A cleric offers to cure a Blank, or end a Sense Toll early.
anytime.rules: Lesser and Greater Restoration, Remove Curse and Heal work by 2024 rules except as ruled here.
anytime.later: The cure for a Blank is finding their jars, or the Remake.
anytime.keywords: greater restoration, remove curse, heal, cure, blank, toll, eel, restore, lesser restoration

anytime.title: They cast Speak with Dead on Tam Harrow
anytime.why: A level-5 cleric or bard with a drowned father's body nearby will try it.
anytime.readAloud: Tam's lips move slowly, as if the water were still in them. "Grey gloves. They took the way. I couldn't find the way home."
anytime.response: Mere-drowned bodies don't decay; the ferry-folk keep Tam in the cold-house until his name is written in the ledger. Speak with Dead works: he answers five questions from what he knew. He remembers grey gloves, a patrol, being asked about a route, and then nothing about the route at all, because it was taken from him. He wanted to return the Heart to the Choir and keep Ila safe.
anytime.consequence: A clear source on Tam's death.
anytime.tells: Players ask where Tam is buried.
anytime.rules: Speak with Dead (2024): five questions; the corpse knows only what it knew in life. Ask Ila or Mother Sallow first; doing it without asking angers the ferry-folk.
anytime.later: Counts as one of the sources on Tam's death; any two establish the Court's responsibility.
anytime.keywords: speak with dead, tam, corpse, body, cleric, question the dead, father

anytime.title: They cast Zone of Truth or Detect Thoughts on someone
anytime.why: Investigative parties reach for truth magic in a story built on lies.
anytime.response: The firm rulings for levels 3 to 6 are in the early play on truth and minds (the oath-duel's herald fields, Maudrin's dais, Haldric's shield). Later in the campaign the same rules hold: Zone of Truth works as written (Charisma save; a creature may refuse to answer, which is itself telling), and Haldric and Maudrin, who know the spell, simply refuse. Detect Thoughts on a Tithed person finds blank patches where things were taken; on Maudrin with the Key it finds one repeating thought: “keep it as it is.”
anytime.consequence: Truth magic gets answers outside the hearing, and pointed refusals from the people who know the spell.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Zone of Truth before the oath-duel or an interrogation.
anytime.rules: Zone of Truth: Charisma save; creatures can evade or refuse to answer. Detect Thoughts: Wisdom save to probe deeper.
anytime.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, lie, truth, read mind, interrogate, spell

anytime.title: They use Silence, Dispel Magic or Counterspell against silence-stones
anytime.why: Casters want to know how their magic interacts with the Court's stones.
anytime.response: Silence-stones aren't spells. Dispel Magic and Counterspell don't affect them; break one (AC 12, 10 HP) or carry it off. The spell Silence is a different thing: Corvanese find it eerie and holy, and Hushmen are amused. A bell rung inside a Silence spell still rings and still takes its Toll; its tone travels through the world, not the air. Silence does stop a Heart-Hound's ring.
anytime.consequence: Casters know stones must be broken or carried, not dispelled.
anytime.tells: A caster tries to dispel a checkpoint stone, or casts Silence around a Hushman.
anytime.rules: House rule (v5 2.6): a fixed stone suppresses spells in a 10-foot radius; a glove suppresses only its own strike.
anytime.keywords: silence, silence-stone, dispel magic, counterspell, stone, checkpoint, suppress, antimagic

anytime.title: They send a message across the Stormwall
anytime.why: A Stormborn caster with Sending can reach home.
anytime.response: It works: Corvane is on the same plane as the Sword Coast. The recipient hears a faint ringing under the words. Help sent in reply takes weeks to arrive by sea; magical travel needs a destination the caster knows, and Corvane has no permanent teleportation circles.
anytime.consequence: Faerûn knows what the party knows.
anytime.tells: A player asks whether Sending works from Corvane.
anytime.rules: Sending (2024): 25 words each way.
anytime.later: A reply can become a Stormborn ally for S22, or a complication if the Lords' Alliance decides the Seam is worth controlling.
anytime.keywords: sending, message, home, faerun, contact, harpers, teleport, scroll

anytime.title: They use Water Breathing or similar to reach Old Pellmoor
anytime.why: Diving magic makes the drowned town an explorable dungeon.
anytime.readAloud: The drowned streets of Old Pellmoor open in front of you, doors hanging, a chandelier swaying with no current.
anytime.response: It works (v5 allows diving magic). The Choir notices anyone who lingers; the response hymn keeps them calm. The drowned houses can collapse, and memory-eels nest in chimneys. Treasure: memory-pearls (v5 11.5).
anytime.consequence: Old Pellmoor becomes a place the party can explore.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Water Breathing before visiting the belfry.
anytime.rules: Underwater combat (2024): melee attackers without a Swim Speed have Disadvantage unless using a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear or trident.

anytime.title: They pay with a memory instead of coin
anytime.why: It's the everyday currency of Corvane, and players love trying it.
anytime.readAloud: The Reckoner touches a cold fork to your temple. For a moment you know exactly what you're about to lose. Then you don't, and you don't mind.
anytime.response: The player chooses the memory and its weight (mote, keep, heartkeep or knowing) and writes one line in the Memory ledger. Price it from the Reckoning House slate. Motes and keeps change nothing on the sheet. Ask the player what the character no longer remembers, and let that be a small moment.
anytime.consequence: The character has paid in the local way.
anytime.tells: A player asks what a memory is worth, or offers one at a stall.
anytime.rules: Rates at Pellmoor: mote about 1 sp; keep about 1 gp 2 sp; heartkeep 25–100 gp by appraisal. A Reckoner buying memories for gold takes a 10 percent fee.
anytime.later: Patterns of what a character sells say a lot about them; use the ledger as a spotlight prompt.
anytime.keywords: pay with memory, memory money, keep, mote, buy, sell memory, reckoner, price, coin

anytime.title: They sell a heartkeep
anytime.why: Heartkeeps pay well, and desperate characters sell them.
anytime.readAloud: Sela Maunt holds the red-waxed vial up to the light and doesn't say anything for a long moment. "Are you sure, love? This one's heavy."
anytime.response: Appraise it at 25 to 100 gp or more. Before the sale, the player names the memory and what it held up in the character (a belief, a bond, a fear); after, they rewrite that one thing. Sela will quietly offer to keep it on her Lost Shelf so they can buy it back at cost.
anytime.consequence: Real money, and a real change in the character.
anytime.tells: A player asks what a big memory is worth.
anytime.rules: No mechanical penalty. The DM may award Heroic Inspiration if the money is used for someone in need.
anytime.later: Venn's Coster pays more and ships it abroad, and then it is gone for good. A heartkeep on Sela's shelf can be bought back.
anytime.keywords: heartkeep, sell big memory, defining memory, desperate, money, sela, lost shelf

anytime.title: They try to buy back a memory
anytime.why: Someone (a PC, Mother Sallow, Lysse, a Blank) wants something back.
anytime.response: Traded keeps: find who holds the vial (Sela's Lost Shelf, a collector, a Coster crate) and buy it; the owner opens it and the memory returns whole. Tithed memories: they're jars in the Tithe-Ledger Room in Hallowmere; only theft or a Court bargain gets them. Tolls: never.
anytime.consequence: The party knows where each kind of lost memory went and what getting it back would take.
anytime.tells: A player asks where sold or Tithed memories go.
anytime.rules: Finding a sold keep: a Reckoner's records (DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation), or Sela's help) say who bought it.
anytime.later: Mother Sallow's wedding memory is a Tithe jar in the Hallowmere vault (S5). Lysse's missing memories are filed under other names there.
anytime.keywords: buy back, recover memory, get memory back, jar, tithe jar, lost shelf, restore

anytime.title: They open a stranger's keep
anytime.why: Curiosity, a clue, or an investigation can be inside a vial.
anytime.readAloud: For a moment you are someone else, on a different shore, laughing at something you'll never understand. Then the vial is a little greyer.
anytime.response: They witness the memory as a guest, without becoming its owner. Each stranger's opening fades it; after three it's spent. A Knowing gives them its knowledge for one use. Opening a keep is how investigations in Corvane find evidence: a route, a face, a password.
anytime.consequence: A stranger’s memory, and possibly a clue, at the cost of fading it.
anytime.tells: A player asks what is in a keep, or buys one to open.
anytime.rules: Once, a character who witnesses a Knowing has Advantage on one ability check that knowledge plainly helps.

anytime.title: They pay a local's Tithe in gold (gilding)
anytime.why: Faerûnian characters with gold want to spare friends their memories.
anytime.readAloud: Quill looks at the coins, then at you, then very carefully at nothing at all. "I didn't see that."
anytime.response: It is illegal and common. A bribed or tired officer looks away; an ambitious one writes it down. Quill accepts gilding once if bribed or befriended; any Hushman Sergeant reports it. Getting caught makes the payer a Tithe-case and the local pays double.
anytime.consequence: A neighbour keeps their memory; the party owes or is owed.
anytime.tells: A player offers to cover someone's Tithe with coin.
anytime.rules: Influence (Persuasion or Deception) DC 15 to get an officer to look away; automatic with Quill if he's bribed.
anytime.later: Repeated gilding advances the Court clock and raises Pellmoor's quota. The ferry-folk remember who paid.
anytime.keywords: gild, gilding, pay tithe in gold, gold for tithe, cover tithe, bribe officer

anytime.title: They make or pass a forged keep
anytime.why: Rogues will try to counterfeit the local money.
anytime.response: A forged keep is a real vial with a false or empty memory and a copied wax stamp. It passes in a busy market and fails in front of a Reckoner, whose fork rings in the wrong note. Forgery is a Court crime; the Landing's merchants take it personally.
anytime.consequence: Easy money, and enemies in the Tally.
anytime.tells: A player asks how keeps are stamped, or whether you can fake a memory.
anytime.rules: Making one: DC 15 Dexterity (Forgery Kit). Passing it: Charisma (Deception) against a merchant's Passive Insight; a Reckoner detects it automatically unless bribed.
anytime.later: Venn's Coster hires investigators; the Landing clock advances.
anytime.keywords: forge, forgery, fake keep, counterfeit, fake memory, scam

anytime.title: Someone tries to take a memory without consent
anytime.why: A player wonders if they could rip a secret out of an NPC.
anytime.response: Drawing needs a Reckoner's fork, a Mere-glass vial, training and consent; without consent the memory won't seal. Only Court Tithe-collectors and leeches force it, using tools and methods that are the Court's darkest secret. A PC cannot do it on the fly. If the table wants this thread, it is a villain's method, not a player tool.
anytime.consequence: The table knows forced drawing is the Court’s secret, not a player tool.
anytime.tells: A player asks how drawing works, intending to use it on a prisoner.
anytime.keywords: leech, steal memory, force, take memory, interrogate, without consent

anytime.title: They confront Master Venn about the memory trade
anytime.why: Once they know the Coster buys Tithed memories, Venn becomes a target.
anytime.readAloud: Venn closes his ledger gently, as if it might bruise. "Friend. Everyone in Corvane sells memories. I only pay better."
anytime.response: Venn denies nothing he can't be forced to. Evidence (the Tithe-Ledger column, a crate manifest, a bribed Quill) makes him bargain: he'll give up a crate bound for Athkatla, or betray Quill, to keep his licence hopes. Exposing him publicly turns the Old Shore against the Coster.
anytime.consequence: Venn becomes an enemy or an unwilling source.
anytime.tells: The party has seen the EXPORT — VENNMARK column, or follows a Coster crate.
anytime.rules: Influence: Venn is Indifferent; Hostile once humiliated in public. Evidence grants Advantage.
anytime.later: A recovered crate holds Blanks' memories: returning them is a powerful act (Blanks can join the S22 allies, s22-ally-blanks). The Landing clock moves.
anytime.keywords: venn, confront, coster, export, memory trade, crates, athkatla, merchant

anytime.why: Faerûnian characters know there are people in Pellmoor who distrust the Court.
anytime.readAloud: The Harper's lute has one string tuned wrong, on purpose. "You're asking the right questions. Ask them quieter."
anytime.response: Two Harper agents work Strangers' Row. They distrust the Tithe and sympathise with the Bellwrights. They can forge one writ of passage, carry a message home, or introduce the party to a Bellwright contact. In return they want the truth about the Tithe-Ledger. The Zhentarim offer the same services for money and a cut of the memory trade.
anytime.consequence: A Faerûnian contact network.
anytime.tells: A Stormborn character mentions the Harpers, the Lords' Alliance or the Zhentarim.
anytime.later: Harper help can become the Stormborn ally at S22. A Zhentarim debt comes due in Act III.
anytime.keywords: harpers, zhentarim, lords alliance, faerunian help, spies, writ forgery, contact

anytime.why: Plans against her fail more often than they work.
anytime.readAloud: The balcony door is already open. “Do come in,” says a voice in the dark.
anytime.response: The party escapes, is captured, or is allowed to leave. The Court knows their faces. Do not force a merciful Maudrin; play what the dice and the plan give. She never forgives a second attempt.

anytime.response: Tristan offers the Key's whereabouts for the Hearts the party holds, or a pension for silence about the Quiet Night. He is cautious and afraid of the Hush. He cannot be forced.

anytime.why: A fifth-level spell for a campaign about secrets.
anytime.readAloud: In the water a figure turns away, and the scene dims as if under a cloth.
anytime.response: Scrying works but is hampered: Maudrin's gloves and the Key's silence-stone case give her Advantage on the save if she knows she is watched; the Key itself cannot be seen. The shrine can be scried only by someone who has stood at the bottom (it also becomes a Teleport destination, Viewed Once). The Hush notices a scryer and speaks to them.

anytime.tells: A caster prepares Scrying.
anytime.rules: Scrying (5th): Wisdom save modified by familiarity. A silence-stone cloth blocks it entirely.

anytime.title: They Teleport, Dimension Door or Gate
anytime.why: High-level casters will try to skip the road.
anytime.readAloud: The air folds, and for a moment you smell tide and bronze.
anytime.response: Corvane has no permanent teleportation circles. Teleport works within the Ninefold Shore to places the caster knows; Hallowmere's silence-stones block arrival within 10 feet of a stone. Teleport or Gate across the Stormwall misfires: you arrive at Pellmouth in the Seam, taking 3d10 Lightning damage. Teleport or Dimension Door to the Hush chamber avoids the stairs if you have seen it (s25-teleport-to-the-shrine).
anytime.consequence: Travel has rules.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Teleport or Gate.
anytime.rules: Teleport (7th), Dimension Door (4th), Gate (9th).
anytime.later: S25: the stairs.
anytime.keywords: teleport, gate, dimension door, travel

anytime.title: They Plane Shift or leave the plane
anytime.why: A high-level escape hatch.
anytime.readAloud: The tuning fork hums, and the grey world slips away.
anytime.response: Plane Shift works (Corvane is on the Material Plane); it does not cross to Faerun because that is the same plane. Leaving Corvane's plane strands the party outside the Hush's reach: Tolls, stairs memories and the Great Toll stay with them; bells cannot be rung from another plane. Advance the Court clock by two for each month away. The Court does not follow.
anytime.consequence: The party leaves and returns later.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Plane Shift.
anytime.rules: Plane Shift (7th), Banishment (4th).
anytime.later: Anytime: the Court's clocks have moved.
anytime.keywords: plane shift, astral, leave, escape

anytime.title: They cast Wish
anytime.why: A ninth-level caster will try.
anytime.readAloud: The word is out before you finish it. The bells do not answer.
anytime.response: Wish can duplicate a spell of 8th level or lower (including Resurrection, Heal and Greater Restoration), obey the usual stress rule, and teleport a Tithe jar to its owner. It cannot pay a Toll, ring a bell, strike Ysh, undo Oum, restore a Tithed memory as if it had never been taken, or change an ending flag. The lullaby ignores wishes.
anytime.consequence: A wish is a spell.
anytime.tells: A caster has Wish and a long list.
anytime.rules: Wish (9th). Stress: Strength drops, 33% to lose the spell forever (2024).

anytime.title: They cast Revivify, Raise Dead or Resurrection
anytime.why: Parties die in Act IV and V.
anytime.readAloud: The dead are listened to in Corvane, and they take a long time to answer.
anytime.response: Player characters: Revivify (within 1 minute, 300 gp diamond), Raise Dead (within 10 days, 500 gp diamond; -4 penalty to D20 Tests that fades one per Long Rest), Resurrection (within 100 years) work. Sister Aurelie's Dawn Mission can provide Raise Dead. Bell Tolls, stairs memories and lost dreams are not restored. NPCs whose death advances the plot (Tam, Imber, Kessa, Maudrin, Corin) are not restored; offer a Mere Memory instead. A Ringer who became the Seventh's voice cannot be raised.

anytime.tells: A character drops or an NPC dies.

anytime.later: See any-pc-dies.
anytime.keywords: revivify, raise dead, resurrection, death, revive

anytime.title: A player character dies
anytime.why: Acts IV and V are dangerous.
anytime.readAloud: Your friend lies still, and the bells ring from a long way off.
anytime.response: The dead pay no Toll, stairs memory or ledger entry. Allies drag them out. Revivify within 1 minute; Raise Dead via Sister Aurelie's mission or a Tithe-free temple. A new character arrives by the next ship or road (any-absent-player). Nothing is taken from an absent player's character.

anytime.tells: A character drops to 0 HP and fails death saves.
anytime.later: S23, S24, S26, S27: s23-pc-drops, s26-help-ringer-falls, s27-ringer-dies-at-rite.

anytime.title: The Ringer dies mid-ringing
anytime.why: A bell can be struck while the Ringer is in danger.
anytime.readAloud: The Heart falls from their hand and rings once on the stone.
anytime.response: If the Ringer drops to 0 HP before the bell is struck, the ringing is cancelled and no Toll is paid. If they die after the strike, the Toll stands and the bell is rung; revival does not refund the Toll. At the Concord an interrupted rite transfers nothing. Another willing Ringer may step in and pay.

anytime.why: A player may change their mind in front of the bell.
anytime.readAloud: The bell waits. It has waited four hundred years.
anytime.response: A refusal before the bell is struck cancels the ringing: nothing is rung and nothing is lost. After the strike the Toll is owed and cannot be withdrawn. The Great Toll is asked in private and is always refusable.
anytime.consequence: The ringing is cancelled.
anytime.tells: A player hesitates with the Heart in their hand.
anytime.later: The Forecast shows what it costs the Concord.

anytime.why: Dream can reach the singing child.

anytime.response: Dream reaches the Hush, which speaks in the dreamer's own sleeping voice and answers one question per true memory. The spell costs nothing. It does not reach Oum: the Dreamer is asleep behind the lullaby, and only a struck Ysh opens that conversation.

anytime.tells: A caster prepares Dream.

anytime.title: They try Geas, Dominate, Hold Monster, Command or Banishment
anytime.why: Casters will try to control Maudrin.
anytime.readAloud: The spell takes hold of nothing, and Maudrin's gloves hum.
anytime.response: Maudrin is protected: her Silence-Stone Gloves impose Disadvantage on spell attacks within 10 feet; as the Keeper she is immune to Charmed and Frightened while she holds the Key, has Magic Resistance and Legendary Resistance (3/day). Geas and Dominate fail while she holds the Key; Hold Monster and Banishment require a save she can pass with Legendary Resistance. Command (2024) allows only Approach, Drop, Flee, Grovel or Halt: a Halt buys one round. Cultists and Hushmen are ordinary creatures and can be controlled by these spells.

anytime.title: The stairs price, in one place
anytime.why: Players ask how the stairs cost works.
anytime.readAloud: The stairs are warm, as if someone had just stood on them.
anytime.response: The first nineteen steps are free. Every full twenty steps walked costs one memory. A character makes one DC 13 Wisdom save the first time they reach step 20, once per campaign: on a failure the campaign total is capped at five memories, on a success at two. A character who walked 40 steps at S18B has paid two memories; that counts. The dead pay nothing. Children are never asked. Never make an absent player's character pay.
anytime.consequence: The price is clear before the first step.
anytime.tells: A player asks about the price.
anytime.rules: DC 13 Wisdom save at step 20, once per character.
anytime.later: S18B and S25.
anytime.keywords: stairs, price, memory, steps, save

anytime.tells: A player sees mist on the Tor.
anytime.later: S25: the stairs.
